title.rendered: Apple Researchers Discover a Simple Trick to Improve AI Models

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple tests self-checking for AI answers: Apple researchers showed that making large language models proofread their own responses can raise accuracy and reduce mistakes.
  • New RLCF training replaces vague rewards: Reinforcement Learning from Checklist Feedback (RLCF) uses detailed checklists for instructions instead of generic reward scores, making models align more closely.
  • WildChecklists dataset powers training: Apple built a dataset of 130,000 instruction-checklist pairs, mixing direct generation and candidate-based creation for training and evaluation.
  • RLCF lifts benchmark scores noticeably: The method boosted AI benchmarks, with FollowBench up by 4 points and complex reasoning tasks improving by 8.2 percent.
  • Error reduction without extra compute: Asking models to verify answers before finalizing cut coding and math errors by up to 25 percent without raising computational costs.

Large language models (LLMs) often stumble when handling complex tasks, but Apple researchers believe they’ve found a surprisingly simple way to improve them: make the models check their own work. According to a new study, this self-verification approach significantly boosts accuracy, echoing the timeless human habit of proofreading before hitting submit.

Moving Beyond Traditional Training

Today’s LLMs are usually trained with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). In that system, human reviewers judge whether a response is good or bad, and the model learns from the rewards and penalties. It works, but it’s limited. Models often learn to produce answers that look correct without fully following instructions.

Apple’s paper, Checklists Are Better Than Reward Models For Aligning Language Models, proposes a smarter approach. Instead of vague “good” or “bad” labels, Apple’s method uses detailed checklists tailored to each instruction. This is called Reinforcement Learning from Checklist Feedback (RLCF). Each response is graded against clear yes-or-no requirements, like “Is the translation in Spanish?” or “Does the answer include all requested details?”

2507.18624v1Download

The WildChecklists Dataset

To train and test this idea, Apple researchers created WildChecklists, a dataset of 130,000 instructions paired with automatically generated checklists. They tried two ways of making these lists: directly asking a model to generate them, and a more advanced candidate-based method where models first produce different answers and then list possible failure points. The candidate-based method produced far better results because it forced the model to think about what could go wrong.

Another twist was combining AI judges with small verification programs. For example, a program can quickly check whether a text includes three commas—something LLMs often miss. This mix of automated checks and AI evaluation gave more reliable training signals and cut down on reward hacking.

Benchmark Results

When Apple tested the method on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, it improved across all five major benchmarks, something no other method achieved. Results included:

  • A 4-point boost on FollowBench
  • A 6-point gain on InFoBench
  • A 3-point rise on Arena-Hard
  • Up to 8.2% improvement on complex constraint satisfaction

RLCF was particularly strong at “content” constraints, meaning it pushed models to fully cover the user’s request rather than skimming over details.

The Role of Self-Verification

Apple didn’t stop at training. Researchers also tested what happens when you simply ask a model to double-check its own answers before finalizing them. This self-verification step reduced errors by up to 25% in coding and math tasks. Crucially, it didn’t require more computing power; it just made the model pause and reflect, much like proofreading before hitting send.

Implications, Trade-offs, and What’s Ahead

For everyday people, these improvements could translate into AI assistants that better follow instructions, get details right the first time, and make fewer careless mistakes. Whether it’s planning a trip, solving a math problem, or drafting an email, the model would be more dependable.

Apple’s approach isn’t without drawbacks. RLCF relies on very large “teacher” models like Qwen2.5-72B to train smaller ones, which makes it expensive. Training on 130,000 checklist examples took about four days on eight H100 GPUs, though the team found ways to cut costs in half with only small accuracy trade-offs. Importantly, this technique is about instruction-following, not safety, so it doesn’t directly address harmful or biased outputs.

Even with these limits, Apple’s findings point to a future where simple, human-inspired techniques make AI far more reliable. As the company integrates this research into its Apple Intelligence platform, iPhone and Mac users may soon notice assistants that don’t just answer quickly, but answer correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can fake AirPods Pro connect to an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many fakes can connect via Bluetooth, but the pairing process is often clunky, and you won’t get Apple’s smooth animation or iOS features.

mainEntity.name: Do fake AirPods Pro support “Find My”?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. Real AirPods Pro integrates with Apple’s Find My network. If this feature is missing, it’s a strong sign of a fake.

mainEntity.name: Can I update firmware on fake AirPods Pro?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope. Fakes either don’t update at all or show fake firmware versions that don’t match Apple’s records.

mainEntity.name: Are all fake AirPods Pro terrible in quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Some high-end fakes mimic the look and sound decently, but they still lack Apple’s polish, features, and reliability.

mainEntity.name: How can I avoid buying a fake pair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Buy from trusted sources like Apple, Best Buy, or Amazon’s official store. Avoid deals that seem too good to be true, and always check the serial number.

keyPoints.explanation: Apple researchers found that having large language models verify their own answers significantly boosts accuracy, much like proofreading before submitting.

keyPoints.title: Moving Beyond Traditional RLHF Training
keyPoints.explanation: Instead of vague rewards, Apple's method uses detailed checklists tailored to instructions, called Reinforcement Learning from Checklist Feedback (RLCF), to improve model alignment.

keyPoints.title: The WildChecklists Dataset
keyPoints.explanation: Apple created a dataset of 130,000 instructions with checklists, using both direct generation and candidate-based methods, to train and test their self-verification approach.

keyPoints.title: Improved Benchmark Results with RLCF
keyPoints.explanation: Apple’s approach improved performance across major benchmarks, with notable gains like a 4-point boost on FollowBench and an 8.2% improvement on complex tasks.

keyPoints.title: Self-Verification Reduces Errors
keyPoints.explanation: Simply asking models to double-check their answers before finalization decreased mistakes by up to 25% in coding and math tasks without additional computing costs.

title.rendered: How to Send Large Videos and Files from iPhone Without Losing Quality

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • AirDrop is best for nearby Apple devices, offering secure, instant transfers of large files without internet or size limits.
  • iCloud links and Mail Drop support files up to 5GB, generating 30-day shareable links that work across platforms, including Windows and Android.
  • Cloud services like Google Drive or Dropbox simplify sharing, letting you upload files and share access links with anyone, regardless of device.
  • WeTransfer, Snapdrop, and similar tools work well for quick one-offs, requiring no login or cloud storage for sending large files.
  • Compressing files into ZIPs or lowering camera resolution reduces file size, saving time, bandwidth, and storage during transfers.

Sharing large videos or files from your iPhone can be frustrating—especially when you hit file-size limits in email and messaging apps or when AirDrop isn’t an option. Fortunately, Apple and trusted third-party tools offer effective ways to share large files without hassle or loss of quality—and in many cases, without needing to compress them.

Here’s a complete guide on how to send large videos and other files from your iPhone to another iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows PC, or Android device.

Table of Contents
  • Why Sending Large Videos and Files from Your iPhone Can Be a Hassle
  • Method 1: Use AirDrop (No Internet Needed)
  • Method 2: Send iCloud Links or Use Mail Drop (Up to 5GB)
  • Method 3: Use Google Drive, Dropbox, or OneDrive (Cross-Platform)
  • Method 4: Use File-Sharing Services like WeTransfer or Snapdrop
  • Compress Files Before Sending
  • Compress Large Videos Before Sending
  • Change Camera Resolution to Reduce File Size
  • Share Without Stress: Your Files, Your Way

Why Sending Large Videos and Files from Your iPhone Can Be a Hassle

Your iPhone may capture amazing 4K videos and high-res images—but sharing them isn’t always straightforward due to:

  • File size limits in apps: Messaging apps like WhatsApp, iMessage, and Instagram cap uploads between 100 MB and 2GB.
  • Email restrictions: Most services limit attachments to 20–25MB.
  • Cloud storage limits: Services like iCloud and Google Drive require available space.
  • Compression by apps: Even HD uploads often get compressed, reducing quality.

Method 1: Use AirDrop (No Internet Needed)

If the recipient is nearby and has an Apple device, AirDrop is your best bet. It’s fast, secure, and supports files of any size—no Wi-Fi required.

Steps:

  1. Open the Photos or Files app. 
  2. Select the files or videos.
  3. Tap the Share button, then select AirDrop in the Share Sheet. 

  4. Select the nearby Apple device and ask the other person to accept.

Bonus: With iOS 17, you can walk away mid-transfer and the file will continue to send using cellular data.

Method 2: Send iCloud Links or Use Mail Drop (Up to 5GB)

iCloud makes it simple to share files via link-based collaboration or Mail Drop.

iCloud Link:

  1. Open the Files app and locate the large file in the iCloud Drive.
  2. Tap and hold the file, then select Share from the pop-up menu.
  3. Now, tap Send Copy under the file name, then select the Collaborate option in the pop-up menu.
  4. Select the app you want to use to send the collaboration invite. We chose the Messages app.

  5. Tap the Send button.

Mail Drop (Files up to 5GB):

  1. Tap and hold the file or video in the Files app
  2. Tap the Share button, then select the Mail app in the Share Sheet.
  3. If the file is too large, Mail will prompt you to send it using Mail Drop.

Reminder: Links expire after 30 days.

Method 3: Use Google Drive, Dropbox, or OneDrive (Cross-Platform)

For non-Apple users, cloud platforms are perfect.

  1. Install Google Drive, Dropbox, or OneDrive from the App Store.
  2. Open the app and tap the + button, then select the Upload File option. 
  3. Select the file and tap on Upload. 

  4. After the upload is complete, tap the three–dot button next to it. 
  5. Select the Copy Link option in the pop-up menu. 

  6. Share the link via WhatsApp, email, or anywhere.

Pro Tip: Compress multiple files into a ZIP before uploading to save space and reduce upload time.

Method 4: Use File-Sharing Services like WeTransfer or Snapdrop

Need a fast, no-login, no-app method?

WeTransfer lets you send up to 2GB for free. Others like Send Anywhere or Snapdrop work across platforms with minimal steps.

Perfect for one-off transfers when you don’t want to upload to cloud storage.

Compress Files Before Sending

Combine multiple files into a ZIP archive to reduce their size and make them easier to send.

How to create a ZIP on iPhone:

  1. Open Files → Select files → Tap (•••) → Choose Compress.
  2. Send the .zip via email, iMessage, or cloud apps.

ZIPs are easily accessible across all devices—iOS, Android, Mac, or PC.

Compress Large Videos Before Sending

Unless you’re sharing professional footage, compressing videos makes sense. It saves time, bandwidth, and storage.

Recommended apps:

  • Video Compressor
  • Compress Videos & Resize

You can also reduce the size using iMovie by exporting at a lower quality.

Change Camera Resolution to Reduce File Size

Reduce file size at the source by recording at a lower resolution.

Steps:

  1. Go to Settings → Camera → Record Video.
  2. Select 1080p at 30fps instead of 4K.

This significantly reduces file size with minimal loss in quality.

Share Without Stress: Your Files, Your Way

That’s it! Whether you’re using AirDrop, cloud links, or third-party apps, sending large files from your iPhone doesn’t have to be complicated. Choose the right tool for the right situation and keep your workflow smooth.

FAQs

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. Real AirPods Pro integrates with Apple’s Find My network. If this feature is missing, it’s a strong sign of a fake.

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope. Fakes either don’t update at all or show fake firmware versions that don’t match Apple’s records.

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Some high-end fakes mimic the look and sound decently, but they still lack Apple’s polish, features, and reliability.

acceptedAnswer.text: Buy from trusted sources like Apple, Best Buy, or Amazon’s official store. Avoid deals that seem too good to be true, and always check the serial number.

title.rendered: Musk’s xAI Lawsuit Targets Apple and OpenAI Over Siri’s ChatGPT Integration

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Elon Musk sues Apple and OpenAI: Musk’s xAI and X accuse both companies of colluding to block rivals in smartphones and AI services.
  • Siri–ChatGPT integration sparks dispute: Musk argues Apple’s decision to embed ChatGPT into Siri unfairly prioritizes OpenAI while sidelining competing AI assistants like his company’s Grok.
  • App Store bias allegations surface: The lawsuit claims Apple editorial teams promote select AI apps while excluding Grok from highlights, despite it ranking competitively in charts.
  • Approval delays and data limits cited: Musk accuses Apple of slowing reviews and restricting chatbot data access, making it harder for competitors to iterate and compete.
  • Ongoing feud fuels legal push: Musk seeks court intervention against Apple’s practices, deepening his broader conflict with OpenAI over AI access and industry control.

Elon Musk has formally taken Apple and OpenAI to court, accusing the companies of colluding to shut out rivals in both the smartphone and AI chatbot markets. The lawsuit, filed in a Texas federal court by Musk’s AI firm xAI along with X (formerly Twitter), claims Apple’s recent partnership with OpenAI unfairly cements their control.

Siri Integration at the Center

At the heart of the complaint is Apple’s decision to give ChatGPT deep integration with Siri on the iPhone. According to xAI, that effectively makes OpenAI’s chatbot the only generative AI tool with system-level access, leaving competitors like Grok at a structural disadvantage. By tying voice commands and on-device actions so closely to one service, Musk argues, Apple has set barriers that other chatbots cannot easily cross.

Alleged App Store Favoritism

The lawsuit also accuses Apple of stacking the deck in the App Store. Musk points to August 24, when neither Grok nor X made it into Apple’s “Must-Have Apps” showcase despite reportedly ranking higher in category charts. The filing suggests that Apple’s editorial choices keep its preferred partners in the spotlight while reducing visibility for competing services. Apple, however, dismissed those accusations earlier this month when Musk first threatened litigation, calling them “unfounded.”

Dispute Over Data and Updates

Another section of the complaint centers on developer access. Musk alleges Apple slows down approval times for rival updates and limits what user data third-party chatbots can access—resources Musk argues are essential for training models like Grok. The filing characterizes this as a deliberate tactic to box xAI out of meaningful growth and keep OpenAI’s system entrenched.

Relief and Early Pushback

Musk is asking the court to block Apple and OpenAI from what he calls anticompetitive collaboration and is seeking financial damages on top. Apple has not yet responded publicly to the new filing, while OpenAI has brushed it off as nothing more than harassment.

A Longstanding Rift

The case also underscores Musk’s ongoing feud with OpenAI, a company he helped co-found before departing over disagreements about its direction. That exit has fueled multiple lawsuits and sharpened Musk’s rhetoric against the now for-profit AI giant. By pulling Apple into the fight, this new lawsuit widens the battle lines and raises questions over how tightly big tech should control consumer-facing AI.

If the court takes up the case, it could become a pivotal test of how far platform owners like Apple can go in steering which AI tools users can easily access.

Would Musk’s lawsuit change how you think about Apple’s AI integrations? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

keyPoints.title: Elon Musk sues Apple and OpenAI
keyPoints.explanation: Musk's AI firm xAI and X (formerly Twitter) have filed a lawsuit accusing Apple and OpenAI of collusion to create barriers for competitors in the smartphone and AI markets.

keyPoints.title: Siri integration at the core of the dispute
keyPoints.explanation: The lawsuit highlights Apple's deep integration of ChatGPT with Siri on iPhone, which Musk claims unfairly favors OpenAI's chatbot and disadvantages other competitors.

keyPoints.title: Alleged bias in the App Store
keyPoints.explanation: Musk alleges Apple favors certain AI services by excluding rivals like Grok from prominent showcase features despite competitive rankings, suggesting biased editorial practices.

keyPoints.title: Restrictions on data and updates for competitors
keyPoints.explanation: The lawsuit claims Apple slows down approval processes and limits data access for rival chatbots, hindering their ability to improve and compete effectively.

keyPoints.title: Musk's call for court intervention and ongoing feud with openAI
keyPoints.explanation: Musk seeks legal action to prevent what he calls anticompetitive practices, while the case also reflects his long-standing disagreement and rivalry with OpenAI.

title.rendered: Apple Releases Beta 8 of iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS 26 Tahoe

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple’s Beta 8 rollout confirms nearing final stage: Apple has released Developer Beta 8 for iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe, watchOS 26, tvOS 26, visionOS 26, and HomePod Software 26.
  • Final release likely tied to iPhone 17 event: The build signals a Release Candidate before September’s iPhone 17 launch, followed by the public iOS 26 rollout about a week later.
  • Build numbers mark ongoing refinements: iOS 26 and iPadOS 26 carry build 23A5330a, while other platforms have similar updates showing Apple’s continued bug fixes and stability work.
  • Liquid Glass UI reshapes Apple’s ecosystem: This design system brings layered transparency and a glass-like aesthetic across apps and interfaces in every Apple platform update.
  • Proceed with caution on beta installs: Developer betas may include crashes or data loss risks, while public betas provide a more stable preview for enthusiasts.

Apple has rolled out developer beta 8 of its upcoming operating systems, including iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS 26 Tahoe, watchOS 26, tvOS 26, visionOS 26, and HomePod Software 26.

The latest build arrived just a week after the 7 beta, which appeared on August 18. The 8 beta of any major iOS update is usually the end of beta testing, so we expect Apple to seed the iOS 26 Release Candidate a few days before the iPhone 17 launch in September. You can expect the public release to appear a week after the launch event.

New Beta Build Numbers

  • iOS 26 beta 8: 23A5330a (replacing 23A5326a)
  • iPadOS 26 beta 8: 23A5330a (replacing 23A5326a)
  • watchOS 26 beta 8: 23R5350a (replacing 23R5346a)
  • macOS 26 Tahoe beta 8: 25A5349a (replacing 25A5346a)
  • visionOS 26 beta 8: 23M5332a (replacing 23M5328a)
  • tvOS 26 beta 8: 23J5348a (replacing 23J5346a)
  • HomePod Software 26 beta 8: 23J5348a

In addition to these, Apple also seeded RC 4 builds of macOS 15.7 (24G217) and macOS 14.8 (23J18) for testing.

What’s New in iOS 26 and Other OS Updates

The highlight feature across all Apple operating systems, be it iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, or visionOS, is the new Liquid Glass style UI. It’s a glass-based interface that adds layered transparency throughout the system UI and Apple apps.

Highlights per platform:

  • iOS 26: New battery management system, redesigned Camera app, expanded features for AirPods, and updates to ChatGPT integration.
  • iPadOS 26: Productivity upgrades with a revamped Files app, Preview support, and improved window management.
  • macOS 26 Tahoe: New Phone app, Clipboard History, and an overhauled Spotlight.
  • watchOS 26: Recently reintroduced blood oxygen measurement, plus Adaptive Power Notifications.
  • tvOS 26 & visionOS 26: Benefit from the Liquid Glass design consistency.

If you’re moving from the iOS 26 beta 7 to the 8 beta, don’t expect any visual differences, as it’s rare for beta 8 of any major iOS update to bring noticeable updates.

A Word of Caution for Testers

iGeeksBlog and Apple both advise against installing beta updates on your primary or mission-critical devices, as beta updates are known for carrying bugs and stability issues. Moreover, if you aren’t a developer or tester but are eager to preview the new features, go for the public beta updates instead.

Planning to install iOS 26 beta or waiting for the public release? Drop your thoughts in the comments section.

mainEntity.name: Can fake AirPods Pro connect to an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many fakes can connect via Bluetooth, but the pairing process is often clunky, and you won’t get Apple’s smooth animation or iOS features.

mainEntity.name: Do fake AirPods Pro support “Find My”?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. Real AirPods Pro integrates with Apple’s Find My network. If this feature is missing, it’s a strong sign of a fake.

mainEntity.name: Can I update firmware on fake AirPods Pro?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope. Fakes either don’t update at all or show fake firmware versions that don’t match Apple’s records.

mainEntity.name: Are all fake AirPods Pro terrible in quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Some high-end fakes mimic the look and sound decently, but they still lack Apple’s polish, features, and reliability.

mainEntity.name: How can I avoid buying a fake pair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Buy from trusted sources like Apple, Best Buy, or Amazon’s official store. Avoid deals that seem too good to be true, and always check the serial number.

keyPoints.title: Apple's Developer Beta 8 Releases for Multiple OSes
keyPoints.explanation: Apple has released the eighth beta of its upcoming operating systems, including iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS 26 Tahoe, watchOS 26, tvOS 26, visionOS 26, and HomePod Software 26, indicating the final stages of testing.

keyPoints.title: Expected Timeline for Final Release
keyPoints.explanation: The Beta 8 build suggests that Apple will likely release the Release Candidate for iOS 26 just before the September iPhone 17 launch, with the public version following about a week later.

keyPoints.title: Latest Build Numbers for OS Updates
keyPoints.explanation: Each OS has a new beta build number, such as 23A5330a for iOS 26 and iPadOS 26, showing ongoing improvements and refinements in this testing phase.

keyPoints.title: Major New Features Across All Platforms
keyPoints.explanation: The core highlight across all Apple OS updates is the Liquid Glass UI, which introduces layered transparency and a sleek, glass-like aesthetic system-wide.

keyPoints.title: Cautions for Beta Testers and Public Users
keyPoints.explanation: Beta updates can be unstable and buggy, so they are advised only for developers and testers, with public betas as a safer option for enthusiasts eager to try new features.

Experience

He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: How to Clear Cache on iPhone: Complete Guide & Tips

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iPhones don’t offer a universal “clear cache” button, but you can clear Safari, Chrome, and individual app caches manually when needed.
  • Clear browser cache via settings in Safari, Chrome, or Firefox, which can fix loading problems and free up storage space.
  • App cache can be cleared by offloading or reinstalling apps, or by using built-in clear data options when provided.
  • Regularly clearing cache improves speed, storage, and privacy, while also fixing glitches in apps or websites.
  • Clearing cache may log you out or reset settings, so back up important data and avoid unreliable cleaning tools.

Imagine your iPhone as your cozy digital home. Just like any home, it can get a little messy over time—things slow down, and clutter builds up. All those temporary files and cookies, collectively known as cache data, quietly accumulate behind the scenes, occupying space and sometimes making your phone feel sluggish. Cache data can accumulate and cause performance issues, such as slowdowns or app crashes.

Think of clearing your cache as a little self-care for your iPhone—and for you. It’s not just about tech stuff; it’s about keeping things running smoothly, making room for what matters, and fixing those annoying hiccups that slow you down. In this guide, I’ll walk you through simple steps to clear your iPhone’s cache so you can feel confident and in control and enjoy a smoother experience every day.

Table of Contents
  • Can You Clear Cache on an iPhone? (Understanding iOS Limitations)
  • How to Clear Browser Cache on iPhone
    • 1. Clearing Safari Cache
    • 2. Clearing Chrome Cache
    • 3. Clearing Firefox Cache
  • Quick Reference Table: Clearing Cache in Popular Browsers
  • Troubleshooting & Tips
  • How to Clear App Cache on iPhone
    • 1. Offloading Apps
    • 2. Deleting and Reinstalling Apps
    • 3. Using In-App Cache Clearing Options
  • Additional Tips to Improve iPhone Performance
  • Benefits of Clearing Cache and Cookies
  • Warning, Risks and Considerations
  • How Often Should You Clear Your Cache?
  • What You Need to Know
  • What's Next?

Can You Clear Cache on an iPhone? (Understanding iOS Limitations)

Unlike some other devices, iPhones don’t have a universal “clear cache” button. Apple’s iOS manages most cached data automatically. Apple makes specific decisions about how cache is managed, which limits user control over clearing all cached files at once. However, you do have effective tools to clear cache from browsers and individual apps and optimize your device’s performance with a few intentional steps—some apps provide a built-in option to clear cache, while others do not.

The following sections will cover various methods for clearing the cache and improving the performance of your device.

How to Clear Browser Cache on iPhone

Clearing your browser cache can fix loading issues and enhance browsing speed—here’s how to do it on different browsers.

1. Clearing Safari Cache

Safari is the default browser for most iPhone users. Clearing its cache can help resolve browsing issues, free up storage space, and improve performance. Here’s how to clear its cache:

  1. Open the Settings app > Apps.
  2. Scroll down and tap Safari.
  3. Tap Clear History and Website Data.
  4. Confirm by tapping Clear History and Data.

When you clear Safari’s cache, you’re wiping away old browsing history, cookies, and clutter—giving your web pages a fresh start and freeing up space on your iPhone. Plus, if you use iCloud, this refresh happens across all your Apple devices, so everything stays in sync and up to date.

2. Clearing Chrome Cache

If you use Google Chrome:

  1. Open the Chrome app.
  2. Tap the three dots at the bottom right and select Settings.
  3. Tap History, then Clear Browsing Data.
  4. Ensure Cookies, Site Data, and Cached Images and Files are selected.
  5. Tap Clear Browsing Data and confirm.

3. Clearing Firefox Cache

For Firefox users:

  1. Open the Firefox app.
  2. Tap the menu icon at the bottom and choose Settings.
  3. Under Privacy, select Data Management.
  4. Toggle on Cache.
  5. Tap Clear Private Data to confirm.

Quick Reference Table: Clearing Cache in Popular Browsers

Troubleshooting & Tips

  1. If you don’t see the exact menu options described, check that your browser app is updated to the latest version.
  2. Menu names and locations may change slightly with updates or if accessibility features are enabled.
  3. For browsers not listed here (like Microsoft Edge or DuckDuckGo), look for similar options in their settings or consult their help documentation.

How to Clear App Cache on iPhone

Free up space and improve performance by managing app cache using these effective methods.

1. Offloading Apps

Offloading an app is like putting it in storage—you free up space on your iPhone, but all your info, settings, and files stay safe and sound. If you ever bring the app back, everything will be right where you left it, ready for you to pick up without missing a beat.

This process can be beneficial for freeing up space on your device without permanently deleting your important information:

  1. Go to Settings > General > iPhone Storage.
  2. Select the app you want to offload.
  3. Tap Offload App.

2. Deleting and Reinstalling Apps

For a more thorough cache removal, delete and reinstall the app: This process ensures that all temporary files and cached data associated with the app are entirely removed from your device. After uninstalling, reinstall the app from your device’s app store to start fresh, which can help resolve persistent issues caused by corrupted or outdated cache.

  1. Touch and hold the app icon on your home screen.
  2. Tap Remove App > Delete App.
  3. Reinstall the app from the App Store.

3. Using In-App Cache Clearing Options

Some apps, such as Messages, Facebook, Instagram and Spotify, include built-in features that let you clear their cache directly from the app settings. These options help you remove temporary files, free up storage space, and enhance the app’s performance without requiring you to delete and reinstall the entire app.

  1. Open the app and go to its Settings or Privacy section.
  2. Look for a Clear Cache or Storage option.
  3. Follow the prompts to remove cached data.

Tip: Not all apps offer this feature, so check the app’s settings or support documentation.

Additional Tips to Improve iPhone Performance

Even after clearing the cache, these extra steps can help improve your iPhone’s performance and keep your iPhone running at its best:

  1. Restart or Force Restart Your iPhone: A simple reboot can clear temporary files, refresh your device’s memory, and resolve minor software glitches that may be causing issues.
    • To restart your iPhone, power it off and turn it back on. For a force restart, quickly press and release the volume up button, then the volume down button, and finally, press and hold the side button until you see the Apple logo.

      Alternatively, you can hold the power button and slide to power off. On devices with a home button, holding the home button after powering off can help clear RAM and further improve performance.
  2. Update to the latest iOS version: Regular iOS updates can resolve bugs and performance issues.
  3. Reset Network Settings: If you experience connectivity issues or slow internet, go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings to clear network-related problems.


  4. Turn Off Background App Refresh: Go to Settings > General > Background App Refresh. Here, you will see a list of all your installed apps. Review this list and toggle off any apps that do not need to update content or refresh in the background. Disabling Background App Refresh for unnecessary apps can help save battery life and reduce data usage.

  5. Disable Automatic Downloads and Updates: Go to Settings > App Store, then switch off automatic downloads and updates. This prevents your device from installing new apps or app updates without your permission, helping you save data and maintain more control over what gets installed on your device.

  6. Reduce Motion and Animations: Go to Settings > Accessibility > Motion and turn on Reduce Motion. With this setting, your iPhone dials back all the extra motion and fancy transitions, making it gentler on your eyes and easier to use—especially if you’re sensitive to movement. It can help cut down on distractions and even prevent that queasy feeling some people get while navigating their devices.

  7. Review iPhone Storage Recommendations: In Settings > General > iPhone Storage, check Apple’s suggestions for freeing up space. These recommendations may include deleting unused apps, offloading large attachments, optimizing photo storage, or removing cached data. Following these tips can help you manage your device’s storage efficiently.

  8. Manage resources: Regularly review your device’s storage and memory usage to ensure optimal performance.
  9. If your iPhone is running slow, consider clearing the cache, deleting unused apps, and restarting your device.
  10. Delete heavy videos and duplicate photos: Big videos and duplicate photos can quickly eat up your storage. Open the Photos app or try a cleaner app to spot and delete those photos and extra files, giving your iPhone more breathing room.

Benefits of Clearing Cache and Cookies

Clearing cache and cookies is more than a quick fix—it’s a strategic way to maintain your iPhone’s health and your peace of mind. By regularly removing this stored data, you can ensure your device runs efficiently and stays secure. Here’s how it helps:

  1. Faster Performance and Smoother Browsing: Removing old cached files helps your device and apps respond more quickly, much like tidying a cluttered room. With less unnecessary data to sift through, your iPhone can load web pages and applications faster, making everyday tasks more enjoyable.
  2. More Available Storage Space: Free up space for the things that matter—photos, videos, and essential apps—by clearing out unnecessary temporary files. Over time, cache and cookies can accumulate and take up valuable storage, so clearing them regularly ensures you have room for new memories and essential apps.
  3. Improved Privacy: Wiping cookies and cache removes stored data that websites use to track your activity, helping protect your sensitive information. This reduces the risk of targeted ads and unauthorized tracking, giving you greater control over your online privacy.
  4. Troubleshooting App and Website Issues: If an app or website is acting up, a quick cache clear can often resolve the issue. Removing old, stored data helps resolve glitches and loading issues—no complicated fixes are required.

Real-Life Scenarios:

  1. Make room for spontaneous photos at special events.
  2. Speed up your device before a critical work call or online meeting.
  3. Fix glitches in shopping or banking apps during important transactions.

Warning, Risks and Considerations

While clearing cache and cookies is generally safe and can improve your device’s performance, keep these important points in mind:

  1. You may be logged out of websites and apps: After clearing cache and cookies, you’ll likely need to log in again to your favorite sites and applications, so make sure you remember your usernames and passwords.
  2. Some settings or preferences may be reset: Certain customizations, such as saved themes, language choices, or other preferences, may return to their default state. You might need to reconfigure these settings according to your preferences.
  3. Third-party cleaner apps may present privacy risks: Not all cleaning apps are trustworthy. Only download apps from reputable sources, and always review the permissions they request to protect your data and privacy.
  4. Back Up Your Data: Before deleting or reinstalling apps, ensure important information is backed up. This includes contacts, photos, documents, and any app-specific data that you don’t want to lose. Consider using cloud services or an external storage device for added security.
  5. Don’t Expect Miracles: Clearing cache helps, but it won’t solve every performance issue—incorporate it as one part of your broader device care. For optimal results, combine cache clearing with other maintenance steps, such as updating your operating system, uninstalling unused apps, and regularly restarting your device.

How Often Should You Clear Your Cache?

  1. Regular Maintenance: Make cache clearing part of a monthly digital refresh routine for optimal performance. Regularly clearing your cache helps your devices run faster, prevents storage from filling up with outdated files, and ensures you consistently access the most recent versions of websites and apps.
  2. When Troubleshooting: If an app or website isn’t working properly, clearing the cache can resolve the issue. Cached data can sometimes become corrupted or outdated, leading to loading errors or display problems, so removing it can help restore normal function.
  3. Before Sensitive Transactions: Before typing in personal or financial details online, clear your browser cache for extra peace of mind. This simple step keeps your sensitive info from being stored on your device and helps protect your privacy from unwanted access.

What You Need to Know

Cache clearing is a small, intentional act of digital self-care that keeps your iPhone running smoothly, protects your privacy, and ensures you always have space for what matters most. By making cache clearing part of your regular device maintenance routine, you’ll enjoy faster performance, fewer headaches, and a more organized digital life—no technical expertise required.

What’s Next?

Stay proactive: periodically check for browser and app updates, review your privacy settings, and make digital hygiene a regular habit. Your iPhone—and your peace of mind—will thank you.

If you’d like this guide tailored for a specific audience or want more advanced tips, let me know!

FAQs

Will clearing cache delete my photos or contacts?

No, clearing cache only removes temporary files and does not affect your photos, contacts, or other personal data.

Can I clear cache for all apps at once?

No, iOS does not allow clearing cache for all apps simultaneously. You need to manage each app individually.

Is it safe to use third-party cleaning apps?

Use caution and only download apps from reputable developers. Always review permissions before installing.

blockGraphs.question: Will clearing cache delete my photos or contacts?
blockGraphs.answer: No, clearing cache only removes temporary files and does not affect your photos, contacts, or other personal data.

blockGraphs.question: Can I clear cache for all apps at once?
blockGraphs.answer: No, iOS does not allow clearing cache for all apps simultaneously. You need to manage each app individually.

blockGraphs.question: Is it safe to use third-party cleaning apps?
blockGraphs.answer: Use caution and only download apps from reputable developers. Always review permissions before installing.

keyPoints.title: iPhone Cache Management Limitations
keyPoints.explanation: Unlike some devices, iPhones don't have a universal cache clear button; iOS manages cache automatically, but users can clear cache from individual apps and browsers.

keyPoints.title: Clearing Browser Cache on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Users can free up space and resolve loading issues by clearing cache in Safari, Chrome, or Firefox through their respective settings menus.

keyPoints.title: Clearing App Cache on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: To clear app cache, you can offload or delete and reinstall apps, or use in-app options if available, to remove temporary data without losing important information.

keyPoints.title: Benefits of Clearing Cache and Cookies
keyPoints.explanation: Regularly clearing cache and cookies improves performance, increases storage space, enhances privacy, and fixes app or website glitches.

keyPoints.title: Precautions When Clearing Cache
keyPoints.explanation: Clearing cache may log you out of accounts and reset preferences; always back up important data and use reputable tools to avoid privacy risks.

title.rendered: How to Use Center Stage on iPad and Mac to Stay Perfectly Framed on Camera

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Center Stage is Apple’s AI-powered camera feature that auto-pans and zooms to keep you centered during video calls on iPad, Mac, or iPhone via Continuity Camera.
  • It’s supported on iPads from the 9th gen onward, as well as Macs paired with Studio Display or using iPhone 11 or later as a webcam.
  • On iPad, toggle Center Stage on in call controls or Control Center, available in apps like FaceTime, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams.
  • On Mac, enable Center Stage via FaceTime settings or Continuity Camera, where it adjusts framing automatically while you move around.
  • It shines in work calls, teaching, or fitness sessions, but can be turned off in Settings or call menus if it misbehaves or isn’t needed.

Do you often find yourself scooting closer to your camera or constantly repositioning your device during FaceTime, Zoom, or Teams calls? If yes, Apple’s Center Stage feature on iPad and Mac is exactly what you need.

Powered by Apple’s AI-driven camera tracking technology, Center Stage keeps you perfectly centered in the frame—even if you move around. Whether you’re presenting, pacing, or just shifting in your seat, the camera automatically adjusts to follow your movement smoothly and naturally. Keep reading to discover how Center Stage works and how to use it effectively on supported iPads and Macs.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Center Stage?
  • Which iPads and Macs Support Center Stage?
  • How to Enable and Use Center Stage on iPad
  • How to Use Center Stage on a Mac
    • 1. If Your Mac Has a Built-In Center Stage Camera
    • 2. With Continuity Camera (iPhone as a webcam)
    • 3. Using Studio Display
  • How to Turn Off Center Stage
    • On iPad:
    • On Mac:
  • Best Use Cases for Center Stage
  • Center Stage Not Working? Try These Fixes
  • Video: Understanding Center Stage on iPad
  • Let the Camera Follow You

What Is Center Stage?

Center Stage is Apple’s AI-powered camera framing feature designed to keep you in the center of the frame during video calls. It uses the device’s ultra-wide front-facing camera to pan and zoom automatically, ensuring you’re always visible—even if you shift around.

Which iPads and Macs Support Center Stage?

Not every Apple device supports this smart feature. Here’s the full list:

Supported iPads:

  • iPad Pro 11‑inch (3rd generation and later)
  • iPad Pro 12.9‑inch (5th generation and later)
  • iPad Air (5th generation)
  • iPad (9th generation and later)
  • iPad mini (6th generation)

Supported Macs:

  • Any Mac paired with a Studio Display
  • Any Mac paired with an iPhone 11 or newer (iOS 16+) via Continuity Camera
  • MacBook Pro and iMac (2024 or later)
  • MacBook Air (2025 or later)
Note Center Stage is not currently available on iPhones.

How to Enable and Use Center Stage on iPad

With iPadOS 15.5 and later, enabling Center Stage is seamless. It activates automatically during video calls and can be toggled on/off via Control Center.

Steps:

  1. Start a FaceTime or Zoom call.
  2. Swipe down from the top right corner to open Control Center.
  3. Tap the FaceTime controls tile.
  4. Tap the Center Stage button.

Alternatively, during a FaceTime call, tap your video thumbnail and select the Center Stage icon.

How to Use Center Stage on a Mac

There are three ways to use Center Stage on your Mac, and each method depends on the macOS version and the model of your MacBook or iMac.

1. If Your Mac Has a Built-In Center Stage Camera

  1. Open the FaceTime app on your Mac.
  2. Click the Camcorder (Video) icon in the top menu bar.
  3. Select the Center Stage option.

2. With Continuity Camera (iPhone as a webcam)

Thanks to the Continuity Camera feature, you can turn your iPhone into a webcam for your Mac and use the Center Stage feature on your Mac if you own an iPhone 11 running on iOS 16 or later and a Mac running on macOS Ventura or later.

  1. Mount your iPhone on your Mac using a MagSafe compatible stand, or place it on a tripod next to your Mac with the rear camera facing you.
  2. Open FaceTime on your Mac.
  3. In the top menu, select Video → Your iPhone.

  4. Click the Video icon again and toggle Center Stage on.
  5. Choose between “Main” or “Ultra Wide” camera if needed.

3. Using Studio Display

The Studio Display includes a 12MP ultra-wide camera with Center Stage built-in.

  1. Connect your Mac to the Studio Display using the provided cable and adjust the display as needed.
  2. Now, open the FaceTime app on your Mac.
  3. Click the Camcorder (Video) icon in the top menu bar.
  4. Select the Center Stage option.

How to Turn Off Center Stage

While Center Stage is a handy tool during a video meeting, it isn’t something you would need all the time. Thus, it’s helpful to know how to turn off Center Stage to avoid awkward instances during a meeting. Here’s how you can:

On iPad:

  1. Swipe down from the top right corner of your iPad’s screen to pull down the Control Center.
  2. Tap the FaceTime controls tile, then tap Center Stage in the additional options to turn it off.

On Mac:

  1. Click the Camcorder (Video) icon in the top menu bar.
  2. Click the Center Stage button in the drop-down menu to turn it off.

Best Use Cases for Center Stage

Although you might think of Center Stage as another novelty feature, it’s a practical, hands-free solution for many situations:

  • Remote Work: Stay in frame during active meetings.
  • Online Teaching: Move freely around a whiteboard or setup.
  • Fitness/Yoga: Perfect for movement-heavy sessions.
  • DIY or Cooking Demos: Camera tracks you hands-free.
  • Group Call: Automatically keeps multiple people in view.

Center Stage Not Working? Try These Fixes

While enabling Center Stage on your Mac or iPad is generally straightforward, there are times when the feature doesn’t work as expected or is unavailable altogether. Whatever may be the reason, try these troubleshooting tips:

  • First and foremost, ensure your Mac or iPad supports Center Stage. While you may think yours does, the reality could be otherwise.
  • Sometimes, a software bug can cause issues with functionality. To fix this, check whether a software update is available; if yes, download and install it immediately.
  • If you’re using your iPhone as your Mac’s webcam, ensure that you’ve selected the correct camera source.
  • If you are using a third-party video calling app on your Mac, verify that it has permission to access your camera. To do so, go to Settings → Privacy & Security → Camera.
  • Sometimes, a minor software bug or glitch might be the reason behind the error. Try force-quitting and reopening the app. If the issue persists, try restarting your device.

Video: Understanding Center Stage on iPad

Let the Camera Follow You

Whether you’re cooking, teaching, or just having fun with loved ones, Center Stage ensures you’re always in the spotlight—effortlessly. No more awkward camera repositioning or worrying about being off-center.

Feel free to reach out to us via comments if you need further help.

FAQs

Can I use Center Stage with Zoom or Teams?

Yes, it works system-wide and supports most video call platforms.

Does Center Stage affect video quality?

Slightly. It uses digital zoom, which may reduce sharpness, but it’s generally well-optimized.

Can Center Stage frame multiple people?

Yes, it adjusts to include everyone in view.

Is Center Stage available in QuickTime?

Yes, when using Continuity Camera or Studio Display.

@graph.name: How to Enable and Use Center Stage on iPad
@graph.description: Easily activate Center Stage on your iPad to keep yourself centered during FaceTime or Zoom calls.

step.name: Start a video call
step.text: Begin a FaceTime or Zoom call on your iPad.

itemListElement.text: Start a FaceTime or Zoom call.

step.name: Open Control Center
step.text: Swipe down from the top-right corner of the screen to access Control Center.

itemListElement.text: Swipe down from the top right corner to open Control Center.

step.name: Access FaceTime controls
step.text: Tap the FaceTime controls tile to access additional video settings.

itemListElement.text: Tap the FaceTime controls tile.

step.name: Enable Center Stage
step.text: Tap the Center Stage button to turn it on during your call.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Center Stage button.

@graph.name: How to Use Center Stage on Mac using Built-In Center Stage Camera
@graph.description: Quickly enable Center Stage on your Mac during FaceTime calls to stay centered automatically.

step.name: Launch FaceTime
step.text: Open the FaceTime app on your Mac.

itemListElement.text: Open the FaceTime app on your Mac.

step.name: Open video settings
step.text: Click the Camcorder icon in the top menu bar during a call.

itemListElement.text: Click the Camcorder (Video) icon in the top menu bar.

step.name: Enable Center Stage
step.text: From the dropdown menu, select the Center Stage option to activate it.

itemListElement.text: Select the Center Stage option.

@graph.name: How to Use Center Stage on a Mac using iPhone as webcam
@graph.description: Use your iPhone as a webcam on your Mac and enable Center Stage for auto-framing during video calls.

step.name: Position your iPhone
step.text: Mount your iPhone on a MagSafe stand above your Mac or place it on a tripod nearby with the rear camera facing you.

step.name: Open FaceTime on Mac
step.text: Launch the FaceTime app on your Mac to start setting up the video call.

itemListElement.text: Open FaceTime on your Mac.

step.name: Select your iPhone as camera
step.text: From the top menu, go to Video and select your iPhone as the camera source.

itemListElement.text: In the top menu, select Video → Your iPhone.

step.name: Enable Center Stage
step.text: Click the Video icon again and toggle Center Stage to turn it on.

itemListElement.text: Click the Video icon again and toggle Center Stage on.

step.name: Choose preferred camera
step.text: If available, select either the Main or Ultra Wide camera for your video.

keyPoints.title: What Is Center Stage?
keyPoints.explanation: Center Stage is Apple's AI-powered camera feature that automatically pans and zooms to keep you centered in the frame during video calls.

keyPoints.title: Supported Devices for Center Stage
keyPoints.explanation: Center Stage works on select iPad models from the 9th generation and newer, and on Macs paired with Studio Display or using Continuity Camera with iPhone 11 or later.

keyPoints.title: Enabling Center Stage on iPad
keyPoints.explanation: You can activate Center Stage during FaceTime or Zoom calls by toggling it on via Control Center or within the call controls.

keyPoints.title: Using Center Stage on a Mac
keyPoints.explanation: On Mac, you can enable Center Stage through the FaceTime app by selecting it in the camcorder options or using Continuity Camera with an iPhone.

keyPoints.title: Best Use Cases & Troubleshooting
keyPoints.explanation: Center Stage is useful for remote work, online teaching, fitness, and group calls, and can be turned off in settings if it doesn't work properly or isn't needed.

title.rendered: How to Loop YouTube Videos and Playlists on Any Device

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Right-click a YouTube video on desktop and select Loop, which enables endless playback without requiring extensions or a Google account.
  • You can create a looping link manually by extracting the video ID and placing it into a custom URL format that auto-repeats the video.
  • Playlists include a built-in Loop icon, letting you repeat the full playlist or lock playback to a single video inside it.
  • On iOS and Android, tap the gear icon on a video, then enable Loop for continuous playback of a single clip or playlist.
  • For looping specific video sections, use extensions like Looper, which add custom start and end points for partial repeats.

Want a YouTube video to play on repeat without tapping replay every time? Whether it’s your favorite song during a long drive, relaxing rain sounds, or your child’s go-to cartoon, YouTube makes it easy to loop videos or playlists. Here’s how you can loop content on YouTube on desktop, mobile, or TV.

Table of Contents
  • How to Loop a YouTube Video on Desktop
    • Using YouTube's Built-In Loop Feature
    • Using a URL Trick to Loop Any YouTube Video
    • How to Loop a YouTube Playlist on Desktop
  • How to Loop YouTube Videos and Playlists on Mobile (iOS & Android)
    • Looping a Single Video
    • Looping a Playlist
  • How to Loop a Specific Part of a YouTube Video Using Extensions
  • Best Use Cases for Looping YouTube Videos and Playlists
  • Troubleshooting: Why Can't I Loop Videos?
  • Just Hit Play and Let It Roll

How to Loop a YouTube Video on Desktop

Looping videos on your computer is simple and can be achieved in multiple ways, depending on your browser.

Using YouTube’s Built-In Loop Feature

This is the easiest way to repeat a video without any sign-in or extensions.

  1. Play any YouTube video in your browser.
  2. Right-click anywhere on the video player (or Control-click on Mac).
  3. Select Loop from the menu.

The video will now keep playing until you stop it.

Using a URL Trick to Loop Any YouTube Video

If the loop option doesn’t appear, you can create a one-video playlist that loops automatically:

  1. Open the YouTube video you want to loop.
  2. Copy the video ID from the URL. Example: For https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fsfR06sIK2Y, the video ID is fsfR06sIK2Y.
  3. Paste the video ID at the end of this link structure: https://www.youtube.com/watch_videos?video_ids=.  The link should look like this: https://www.youtube.com/watch_videos?video_ids=fsfR06sIK2Y
  4. Open the new URL in your browser.

Done! You now have an auto-looping playlist.

How to Loop a YouTube Playlist on Desktop

Looping an entire playlist—or even a single video in a playlist—is built into YouTube’s playlist player. Here’s how to use it.

  1. Go to YouTube and open the playlist you want to loop.
  2. It will start playing all the videos in the playlist.
  3. Beside the video player, find the Loop icon (two arrows forming a circle).

  4. Click once to loop the playlist, and again to loop only the current video.

How to Loop YouTube Videos and Playlists on Mobile (iOS & Android)

YouTube’s mobile app has a loop feature—but it’s not as obvious. Whether you’re looping a video for music, tutorials, or kids’ content, here’s how to do it properly on iOS and Android.

Looping a Single Video

This feature works within the YouTube app, but the setting is somewhat hidden.

  1. Open the YouTube app and play the video.
  2. Tap the gear (Settings) icon in the top-right corner of the video player.
  3. Tap Additional Settings.
  4. Toggle Loop video ON.

The video will now play continuously from start to end, repeating until you stop it or play something else.

Looping a Playlist

  1. Open any playlist and tap Play All.
  2. Tap the Loop icon above the video player.

  3. Tap again to loop just one video.

Tip: If your playlist only contains one video, this will loop it automatically.

How to Loop a Specific Part of a YouTube Video Using Extensions

Want to repeat just a part of a video (like a chorus or workout segment)? Use Chrome or Firefox extensions:

  1. Install a YouTube looping extension like Looper for YouTube or Enhancer for YouTube from the Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons.
  2. After installing, refresh your browser or YouTube.
  3. Play the video you want to loop.
  4. Look for new looping controls added below the video player (usually a ‘Loop’ or ‘A-B’ icon).
  5. Set the Start and End times for the section you want to loop.

  6. Choose how many times to repeat that section (or set it to an infinite loop).
  7. Press Play. The selected portion will now loop as per your settings.

You can also adjust playback speed or assign keyboard shortcuts depending on the extension.

Best Use Cases for Looping YouTube Videos and Playlists

Looping isn’t just about laziness—it actually makes life a little easier in a bunch of everyday situations. Here’s how people use it:

  • Music: Perfect for long drives or productivity playlists.
  • Studying: Loop ambient sounds or white noise to boost focus.
  • Kids: Replay favorite cartoons or rhymes automatically.
  • Workouts: Repeat fitness moves or yoga sets.
  • Meditation/Sleep: Loop calming sounds or guided meditations.
  • Training: Great for language learners, dancers, or musicians.

It’s not just a trick—it’s a productivity and comfort feature when used right.

Troubleshooting: Why Can’t I Loop Videos?

If the loop option isn’t working:

  1. Make sure you’re signed in.
  2. Try double-tapping the Loop icon—once for playlist, again for single video.
  3. Use Chrome browser—it supports Loop better than others.
  4. On mobile browser, switch to Desktop site view to get the Loop option.
  5. On Smart TV, press down on remote and look for Repeat under Settings.

Just Hit Play and Let It Roll

Looping on YouTube saves time, reduces effort, and makes content more enjoyable. Whether it’s music, sleep sounds, or a child’s favorite clip, now you know how to play it non-stop across all your devices.

FAQs

Can I loop YouTube Shorts?

No manual loop, but Shorts auto-loop by default.

Is looping allowed on YouTube?

Yes, YouTube officially supports video and playlist looping.

Can I loop videos on a Smart TV?

Yes. Use the remote to select Repeat under Settings.

Can I loop without a playlist?

Absolutely! Right-click or use app settings to loop individual videos.

Any good Android apps to loop YouTube videos?

Yes, try MusicCup—it lets you loop parts, create playlists, and stream.

Related articles worth reading:

  • How to play YouTube in the background on your iPhone
  • Transfer your Apple Music playlists to YouTube Music
  • How to enable and use YouTube Picture-in-Picture on iPhone
  • How to Turn Off Autoplay on YouTube

mainEntity.name: Can fake AirPods Pro connect to an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many fakes can connect via Bluetooth, but the pairing process is often clunky, and you won’t get Apple’s smooth animation or iOS features.

mainEntity.name: Do fake AirPods Pro support “Find My”?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. Real AirPods Pro integrates with Apple’s Find My network. If this feature is missing, it’s a strong sign of a fake.

mainEntity.name: Can I update firmware on fake AirPods Pro?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope. Fakes either don’t update at all or show fake firmware versions that don’t match Apple’s records.

mainEntity.name: Are all fake AirPods Pro terrible in quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Some high-end fakes mimic the look and sound decently, but they still lack Apple’s polish, features, and reliability.

mainEntity.name: How can I avoid buying a fake pair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Buy from trusted sources like Apple, Best Buy, or Amazon’s official store. Avoid deals that seem too good to be true, and always check the serial number.

@graph.name: How to Loop YouTube Video on Desktop Using YouTube’s Built-In Loop Feature
@graph.description: Quickly loop any YouTube video on your desktop browser without extensions by using YouTube’s built-in right-click menu.

step.name: Open YouTube and play a video
step.text: Launch your browser, go to YouTube, and play the video you want to loop.

itemListElement.text: Play any YouTube video in your browser.

step.name: Access the loop option
step.text: Right-click on the video player or Control-click on Mac to open the menu.

itemListElement.text: Right-click anywhere on the video player or Control-click on Mac.

step.name: Enable loop
step.text: Click the Loop option from the menu to make the video play on repeat.

itemListElement.text: Select Loop from the menu.

@graph.name: How to Loop a YouTube Playlist on Desktop
@graph.description: Easily loop an entire YouTube playlist or a single video within the playlist on your desktop browser.

step.name: Open the playlist on YouTube
step.text: Go to YouTube in your browser and open the playlist you want to loop.

itemListElement.text: Go to YouTube and open the playlist you want to loop.

step.name: Start playing the playlist
step.text: YouTube will automatically begin playing all videos in the playlist.

itemListElement.text: It will start playing all the videos in the playlist.

step.name: Locate the Loop icon
step.text: Find the Loop icon beside the video player that looks like two arrows forming a circle.

itemListElement.text: Beside the video player, find the Loop icon (two arrows forming a circle).

step.name: Loop the playlist or single video
step.text: Click once to loop the playlist, and again if you want to loop only the current video.

itemListElement.text: Click once to loop the playlist, and again to loop only the current video.

@graph.name: How to Loop Single YouTube Video on iPhone
@graph.description: Enable the loop feature in the YouTube app on your iPhone to repeat a single video endlessly without third-party tools.

step.name: Open and play a YouTube video
step.text: Launch the YouTube app and start playing the video you want to loop.

itemListElement.text: Open the YouTube app and play the video.

step.name: Access video settings
step.text: Tap the gear icon at the top-right corner of the video player to open settings.

itemListElement.text: Tap the gear (Settings) icon in the top-right corner of the video player.

step.name: Find Additional Settings
step.text: Tap Additional Settings from the menu that appears.

itemListElement.text: Tap Additional Settings.

step.name: Enable video loop
step.text: Toggle the Loop video option to ON to start looping the video.

itemListElement.text: Toggle Loop video ON.

@graph.name: How to Loop YouTube Playlist on iPhone
@graph.description: Quickly loop an entire YouTube playlist or a single video within the playlist using the YouTube app on your iPhone.

step.name: Play the playlist
step.text: Open the playlist on YouTube and tap Play All to begin playback.

itemListElement.text: Open any playlist and tap Play All.

step.name: Activate loop
step.text: Tap the Loop icon above the video player to loop the playlist.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Loop icon above the video player.

step.name: Switch to loop single video
step.text: Tap the Loop icon again if you want to loop just the current video.

itemListElement.text: Tap again to loop just one video.

keyPoints.explanation: Use YouTube's built-in right-click menu to select 'Loop', enabling continuous playback without sign-in or extensions.

keyPoints.title: Looping on Mobile Devices

title.rendered: How to stop iPhone apps from tracking you

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Locking a Facebook profile restricts outsiders to minimal info, showing only a profile badge while posts, photos, and details stay visible to friends.
  • Profile Lock goes beyond default privacy settings, hiding detailed information, restricting post visibility, and enabling timeline review for tighter control.
  • The feature is only available in select regions, including India and Saudi Arabia—missing options may be tied to location, app version, or Professional Mode.
  • You can lock your profile in Settings & Privacy on the Facebook app or desktop, with simple step-by-step instructions for iPhone, Android, and web.
  • Unlocking restores previous visibility settings, and if Lock isn’t available, you can still strengthen privacy manually by limiting post audiences and hiding past posts.

Your iPhone apps track your usage patterns to show targeted ads based on your recent online activity. While app tracking improves user experience in most cases, it does have its privacy risks, as you don’t know to which third-party advertisers the app is sharing your data.

Fortunately, Apple allows you to choose whether or not you want to allow a particular app to track your activity. This guide details how app tracking on an iPhone works and how to stop it.

Table of Contents
  • How apps track you on iPhone and iPad
  • How to stop apps from tracking you on iPhone or iPad
    • Disable tracking for specific apps
    • Stop all iOS apps from tracking you altogether

How apps track you on iPhone and iPad

Many iPhone apps collect data about your activities across other apps and websites to serve targeted ads or share information with data brokers. This data can include your location, browsing history, email address, app usage patterns, and other details that identify you or your device.

Understanding which apps track your activity and how they do it is essential for maintaining your privacy. Here are some common types of apps that may collect your data:

  • Social Media Apps: Track interactions, search history, and behavior to personalize ads and content.
  • Shopping & eCommerce Apps: Collect browsing, purchase history, and payment data for targeted product ads.
  • Streaming Apps: Monitor what you watch and listen to for recommendations and advertisements.
  • Navigation & Travel Apps: Use location tracking for services but may also share location data.
  • Health & Fitness Apps: Sometimes share activity and health-related data with third parties.
  • Browsers & Ad-Supported Apps: Record usage, search history, and preferences for ad targeting.

To maintain your privacy, it’s important to review and manage app permissions, disable tracking where possible, and use Apple’s built-in privacy features.

To stop user data exploitation, Apple introduced App Tracking Transparency, a feature that requires third-party apps to ask for permission to track users’ activity on the iPhone. This puts you in control over which apps on your iPhone can access your activity information.

Once you deny an app to track your activity or location on your iPhone, Apple revokes its access from your advertising identifier (IDFA) data which links your usage pattern on the app with you or your device. So, the app can no longer share your data with third parties, such as advertisers, for targeted advertising.

According to Apple’s App Tracking Transparency (ATT) framework descriptions, you will see a prompt asking for your permission to track when you open a app. Unless you grant the permission, it can’t see your device’s advertising identifier value. You may also change it later in settings.

How to stop apps from tracking you on iPhone or iPad

Take control of your privacy by limiting app tracking on your iPhone or iPad with these simple steps.

Disable tracking for specific apps

You can choose your tracking preferences when you install an app and use it for the first time on your iPhone. Simply, open the app and start setting it up or using it. After a few seconds, you will see a prompt stating “Allow [app name] to track your activity across other companies’ apps and websites?”

The prompt will also mention why the app wants to track your activity. To deny the permission, tap Ask App Not to Track. Apple will remember your choice and inform the developer about it. Even if you delete and re-install the app, your choice will be saved.

If you have accidentally given tracking access to an app, worry not! You can turn off app tracking for already downloaded apps on your iPhone. Let’s see how!

Stop all iOS apps from tracking you altogether

Apple provides a simple way to opt out of app tracking on your iPhone. Follow these steps:

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Select Privacy & Security and tap on Tracking.
  3. Here, toggle off the switch next to the apps you want to stop from tracking your activity.

If you want to stop getting app tracking prompts, toggle off Allow Apps to Request to Track. Then select Ask Apps to Stop Tracking. It will prevent all the apps you install in future from asking you to track permission. They will also be notified that you have chosen not to be tracked. Moreover, Apple will remove access from the apps you’ve already granted permission.

Now that you have stopped app tracking, you will get less intrusive targeted ads. Notably, this does not imply that advertisements will vanish. You will only see generic advertisements across apps and websites.

That being said, it’s important to remember that even if you deny the tracking permissions to an app, the app developer can still find different ways to track your usage pattern and activity. As such, you should be aware of the apps you install on your iPhone, the permissions you give them, and what you do on them.

Signing off

Protecting your privacy on iPhone is easier than ever with Apple’s tracking controls. You can also save your identity from advertisers when browsing by removing tracking parameters from URLs. Remember to regularly review your App Privacy Report to stay in control of which apps have access to your information.

Do you allow apps to track your activity on your iPhone, or do you prefer not to? Do tell us in the comments.

FAQ

What does it mean if I don’t allow an app to track?

If you don’t allow an app to track you, it won’t be able to follow your activity across other apps and websites and share your data with third-party advertisers. So, you will see fewer personalized ads. However, some app features that rely on tracking might not work properly. But the app can still collect data for its own use, like tracking your activity within the app itself (unless you adjust its specific permissions in settings).

mainEntity.name: Can fake AirPods Pro connect to an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many fakes can connect via Bluetooth, but the pairing process is often clunky, and you won’t get Apple’s smooth animation or iOS features.

mainEntity.name: Do fake AirPods Pro support “Find My”?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. Real AirPods Pro integrates with Apple’s Find My network. If this feature is missing, it’s a strong sign of a fake.

mainEntity.name: Can I update firmware on fake AirPods Pro?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope. Fakes either don’t update at all or show fake firmware versions that don’t match Apple’s records.

mainEntity.name: Are all fake AirPods Pro terrible in quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Some high-end fakes mimic the look and sound decently, but they still lack Apple’s polish, features, and reliability.

mainEntity.name: How can I avoid buying a fake pair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Buy from trusted sources like Apple, Best Buy, or Amazon’s official store. Avoid deals that seem too good to be true, and always check the serial number.

mainEntity.name: What does it mean if I don’t allow an app to track?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you don’t allow an app to track you, it won’t be able to follow your activity across other apps and websites and share your data with third-party advertisers. So, you will see fewer personalized ads. However, some app features that rely on tracking might not work properly. But the app can still collect data for its own use, like tracking your activity within the app itself (unless you adjust its specific permissions in settings).

step.text: Open Settings on your iPhone or iPad, then tap Privacy & Security to access tracking controls.

step.text: Tap on Tracking and toggle off permissions for apps you want to stop from tracking you.

keyPoints.title: App Tracking and Privacy Risks
keyPoints.explanation: Many iPhone apps track your activity for targeted advertising, but you can restrict this to protect your privacy.

keyPoints.title: How Apps Track You on iPhone and iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Apps collect data like location, browsing history, and app usage patterns to serve personalized ads or share information with third parties.

keyPoints.title: App Tracking Transparency Framework
keyPoints.explanation: Apple's ATT feature requires apps to ask for permission before tracking, giving you control over which apps can access your activity data.

keyPoints.title: Managing Tracking Permissions
keyPoints.explanation: You can manually disable tracking permissions for individual apps or stop all apps from tracking by adjusting settings in Privacy & Security.

keyPoints.title: Effectiveness and Limitations of Tracking Controls
keyPoints.explanation: Denying tracking limits data sharing with advertisers, but apps may still find alternative ways to track activity; stay vigilant about app permissions.

title.rendered: Download the New Apple Hebbal Store Wallpaper for iPhone, iPad, and Mac

content.rendered:
Bringing the heat this fall, Apple is ready to open its third store in India. Located at Phoenix Mall of Asia in Bengaluru, the Apple Hebbal Store will go live on September 2, 2025.

To start things off, Apple has dropped a beautiful, limited-edition wallpaper, celebrating India’s national bird in true Apple style. Here’s the latest Apple Hebbal store wallpaper for your iPhone, iPad, and Mac, available to download in 4K quality for free.

Apple’s Expansion in India: Third Store in Bengaluru

Apple’s love for India is growing fast with iPhone 17 production! After launching Apple BKC in Mumbai and Apple Saket in Delhi back in 2023, Bengaluru’s getting its turn with Apple Hebbal, the first Apple Store in South India.

Why Bengaluru? Well, it’s the Silicon Valley of India. Apple’s doubling down there, recently leasing a massive 2.7 lakh sq ft office space nearby for over Rs 1,000 crore over 10 years. And they’re not stopping! Rumors say Pune and Noida are next.

The store is at F-39-F-43, Phoenix Mall of Asia, Bellary Road, Byatarayanapura, Bengaluru near the iconic Hebbal Lake. That’s why the tech giant has chosen the name Apple Hebbal Store. You will be able to try out and buy the latest iPhones, iPads, Macs, and accessories, resolve issues at the Genius Bar, and attend Today at Apple sessions there.

Download the Apple Hebbal Store Wallpapers (Free 4K)

After you download the wallpaper, setting it up on your device is super easy. Here’s the step-by-step:

On iPhone or iPad:

  3. Select the downloaded image.
  4. Adjust positioning if needed, then tap Set.
  5. Choose whether you want it on your Lock Screen, Home Screen, or both.

On Mac:

  2. Go to Apple menu > System Settings > Wallpaper.
