title.rendered: How to Send WhatsApp Messages Without Saving Numbers (iPhone, Android & Web)

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Skip saving one-time contacts in WhatsApp: Adding numbers for quick chats clutters your phonebook and can expose private details unnecessarily.
  • Start new chats directly in WhatsApp: On iPhone and Android, you can enter a number in WhatsApp if it’s registered, no phonebook entry required.
  • Use WhatsApp’s official Click to Chat link: Typing wa.me/number in a browser instantly opens a secure WhatsApp chat window for that contact.
  • Send unsaved messages on iPhone and Android: Safari, Shortcuts, Chrome, or apps like Click to Chat make it easy to message without saving numbers.
  • Rely on WhatsApp Web for quick messages: Paste a wa.me link in your browser to start unsaved chats, useful for work or infrequent contacts.

Ever wished you could quickly send a WhatsApp message to a delivery driver, customer support agent, or stranger without cluttering your phonebook? By default, WhatsApp pushes you to save numbers before starting a chat, which feels unnecessary for one-time conversations.

The good news is that you don’t actually need to save every number. There are several official and safe tricks to send WhatsApp messages without saving contacts on iPhone, Android, and even WhatsApp Web.

Why You Might Not Want to Save Every Contact 

Saving every number you message on WhatsApp isn’t always the best. 

  • Privacy and security: It’s safer not to store someone’s number as they could show up on your other apps or services. 
  • Avoid clutter: It fills your phone’s contact list, making important contacts more difficult to locate. 
  • One-time chats: Storing numbers for single-use convos doesn’t make sense. 
  • Syncing concerns: Saved contacts tend to sync with cloud storage such as iCloud or Google Contacts, which can auto-fill and overwhelm other devices. 

By using methods to message without saving, you maintain control over your contact list and keep things organized. 

Method 1: Start a New Chat with a Number (iPhone & Android)

One of the simplest ways to message an unsaved number is by starting a new chat directly in WhatsApp.  

  1. Open the WhatsApp app and tap the plus icon at the top right corner to start a new chat. 
  2. Tap the search bar at the top and enter the phone number you want to ping. On Android, you can use the keypad by tapping the dialer icon at the search bar.  
  3. If the number is available on WhatsApp, you will see a Chat button next to it. Otherwise, you can invite them to WhatsApp.

This feature, available on both iPhone and Android, is quick and uses WhatsApp’s native interface. However, you’ll need to ensure the number is registered with WhatsApp, or the chat won’t start. 

Method 2: Use WhatsApp’s Official Click-to-Chat

WhatsApp’s Click-to-Chat feature is a reliable and official way to message unsaved numbers. Here’s how it works: 

  1. Open a browser on your device. 
  2. Enter the URL https://wa.me/[phonenumber] In the address bar, replace [phonenumber] with the full number, including the country code (e.g., https://wa.me/+12025550123 for a U.S. number).  
  3. Press Enter, and a WhatsApp chat window will open for that number. 
  4. Tap Open on the prompt and start typing your message. 
Note Always provide the country code without spaces, dashes, or parentheses (e.g., +12025550123, and not +1-202-555-0123). 

Pros

  • Official, secure, and easy.  
  • Functional on mobile and desktop.

Cons

  • You have to manually type the URL, which can be cumbersome for heavy usage. 

Method 3: Send a WhatsApp Message to an Unsaved Number on iPhone

iPhone users have two effective methods to message unsaved numbers: 

Using Safari + wa.me Link:

  1. Open Safari and type https://wa.me/phonenumber.
  2. Tap Go, and WhatsApp will open with a chat window for the number.
  3. Send your message.

Using Shortcuts App: 

  1. Download and add this WhatsApp Unsaved Number shortcut.
  2. Go to Shortcuts App.
  3. Tap on the WhatsApp Unsaved Number shortcut.
  4. Enter the country code and contact number. You don’t have to include the symbol of the country code.
  5. Now, you will be taken to the chat without saving the number.

Pros

  • Lightning-fast after setup.
  • No contact clutter and supports repeat task automation.

Cons

  • Minor setup work required.
  • Works only in the iOS environment.

Want to take your iPhone automation skills further? Check out our guide on how to edit Shortcuts on iPhone to customize, organize, and personalize them to your liking.

Method 4: Send a WhatsApp Message to an Unsaved Number on Android

Android users can also use the wa.me link or third-party apps:

Using Chrome + wa.me Link: 

  1. Open Chrome and enter https://wa.me/phonenumber. 
  2. Hit Enter, and WhatsApp will launch with the chat window. 
  3. Send your message.

Using Third-Party Apps (with Caution) 

There are apps, like Click to Chat, Easy Message, etc., that provide a front-end for generating wa.me links without manual typing. 

Here’s how to use the Click to Chat app:

  1. Download the app from the Google Play Store and open it.  
  2. Enter the country code in the Prefix section and then the number. 
  3. Tap Open to launch the chat. 

That’s all! You can quickly send a WhatsApp message without saving the number with a tap. 

Pros

  • Handy UIs to avoid typing full wa.me links each time. 
  • Can save your frequently used numbers (without adding to your contacts). 

Cons & Safety Tips

  • Only get apps from reliable stores such as Google Play. 
  • Check reviews and permissions. Avoid such apps that ask for access to all your contacts or messages. 

However, I recommend using WhatsApp’s official steps for security. 

Method 5: Use WhatsApp Business App 

The WhatsApp Business app is appropriate for those who send numerous messages to unknown numbers. It also comes with other settings like Quick Replies and Labels to organize conversations. To utilize it: 

  1. Download WhatsApp Business from the App Store or Google Play. 
  2. Press the plus button and enter a number manually. 
  3. Now, send the message you want. 

Method 6: Use Third-Party Tools (Extra Options)

There are some third-party apps on iOS, Android, and the web that facilitate easy messaging of unsaved numbers.

On iPhone and iPad, you can use Direct Message: Click to Chat, Direct Message for WhatsApp, etc., apps. They provide a simple interface to input a number and initiate a WhatsApp conversation without saving it. 

Also, the popular caller ID application Truecaller has a WhatsApp integration. If you search for a number, you will see their Caller ID. If the number has been registered on WhatsApp, you’ll have an option. Tap Open in WhatsApp to start a conversation.  

Pros

  • Don’t need to type URLs and offer shortcuts for frequent uses.

Cons

  • Some apps may request excessive permissions, posing privacy or security threats. Avoid them. 

Bonus Tip: Send WhatsApp Messages Without Saving Contact on WhatsApp Web

For WhatsApp Web or Desktop users, the Click-to-Chat feature is equally effective: 

  1. Open your browser and go to https://web.whatsapp.com. 
  2. In a new tab, enter https://wa.me/phonenumber in the address bar. 
  3. The chat will open in WhatsApp Web after you scan the QR code. 

This method is perfect for work-related messaging and keeps the phone’s contact list untouched. 

Things to Keep in Mind 

Messaging any number on WhatsApp is easy. However, you must take note of a few things for a seamless experience: 

  • Always double-check the number format. It must include the country code and no spaces or special characters. 
  • Be cautious with third-party apps. Check permissions, user reviews, and whether the app is well-maintained. 
  • Avoid spamming random numbers. Use these methods only for legitimate one-time or infrequent communications. 

WhatsApp Like a Pro! 

It’s simpler than ever to send WhatsApp messages without adding contacts, with in-app functionalities and platform-specific shortcuts. The Click-to-Chat method (wa.me) is convenient, secure, and platform-independent, and it’s the most popular option among users. On iPhone, Android, or WhatsApp Web, there’s a solution that suits your requirements.

Give it a try with whatever approach works best for your phone and enjoy streamlined messaging without clogging your contact list!

title.rendered: How to Back Up WhatsApp Messages on iPhone and Android

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • WhatsApp backup options on iPhone: You can back up chats manually or automatically using iCloud, while individual chats can also be exported locally.
  • Manual backup using iCloud: Go to Settings > Chats > Chat Backup and tap Back Up Now to instantly save WhatsApp data to iCloud.
  • Backing up without iCloud: If storage runs out, you can export selected WhatsApp conversations as Zip files and keep them directly on your iPhone.
  • Automatic WhatsApp backup setup: Turn on auto-backup in WhatsApp settings to ensure chats are regularly saved to iCloud as long as space is available.
  • Restoring chats on a new iPhone: Reinstall WhatsApp, verify your number, then select Restore Chat History to recover messages from your latest iCloud backup.

We all understand how valuable our WhatsApp conversations are. But what if you lose your phone, upgrade to a new one, or mistakenly remove the app? Poof, your conversations may be gone! That’s why it’s essential to back up your WhatsApp messages, so you can restore them anytime.

In this guide, I’ll show you how to back up WhatsApp chats on both iPhone (with iCloud) and Android (with Google Drive), plus alternatives if you don’t want to use cloud storage. It’s easier than you think!

What Does a WhatsApp Backup Include?

A WhatsApp backup usually saves:

  • Messages: Your complete chat history.
  • Photos and videos: Depending on your settings (you can exclude videos to save space).
  • Documents and voice notes: All shared files.
  • Channels and community updates.

It does not include:

  • Your WhatsApp account settings.
  • Call history. 

On iPhone, WhatsApp backs up to iCloud. On Android, it usually saves to Google Drive.

Note iPhone users should avoid doing both iCloud device backups and in-app WhatsApp backups, as this creates duplicate files and eats up storage. Choose one method.

Prepare Your Device Before Backing Up

Before backing up WhatsApp, ensure your device is ready:

  • Check storage space:
    • iPhone: You need at least 2.05× the backup size available on both iCloud and your device. (Example: a 1GB backup needs ~2.05GB free.)
    • Android: Ensure you have enough Google Drive and device storage.
  • Use stable Wi-Fi: Backups can be large; avoid mobile data charges.
  • Update WhatsApp: Install the latest version from the App Store or Google Play.
  • Sign in: iCloud for iPhone (Settings > [your name] > iCloud). Google Account for Android.
  • Enable iCloud sync (iPhone only): Settings > [your name] > iCloud > Saved to iCloud > toggle on WhatsApp.

Taking these steps ensures a smooth backup process without interruptions. 

How to Back Up Your WhatsApp on iPhone and Android

WhatsApp makes it easy to back up your chats, either manually or on a schedule. Here’s how to do it on both platforms. 

1. Set Automatic Backups

Automatic backups save your chats daily, weekly, or monthly, so you don’t have to remember to do it manually. 

On iPhone:

  1. Open WhatsApp and tap Settings from the bottom toolbar. 
  2. Go to Chats > Chat Backup.
  3. Tap Auto Backup and choose Daily, Weekly, or Monthly. 
  4. Tap < at the top and toggle on Include Videos if you want to back up videos (this increases backup size).
  5. Ensure you’re signed into iCloud and have enough storage. The backup will run automatically at the chosen frequency.

On Android:

  1. Open WhatsApp and tap the three-dot menu at the top-right corner. 
  2. Go to Settings > Chats > Chat Backup. 
  3. Tap Automatic backups and select Daily, Weekly, or Monthly. 
  4. If you see that your Google storage is full, you can change your account. Tap Google Account and choose one. 
  5. Toggle Include Videos if desired. Backups will save to Google Drive as scheduled. 

2. Take a Manual Backup

If you need to do instant backups, you can take one manually.

On iPhone:

  1. Open WhatsApp and access Settings > Chats > Chat Backup.
  2. Tap Back Up Now. Wait for the process to finish, which will vary based on your chat size and internet connectivity.
  3. Verify the backup status under Last Backup to ensure it’s complete.

On Android:

  1. Open WhatsApp > three-dot menu > Settings > Chats > Chat Backup. 
  2. Tap Back Up. Make sure the correct Google account is selected.
  3. Wait for the backup to complete. You’ll see the last backup time and size at the top.

Manual backups are perfect before switching phones or updating software.

Optional: iPhone Device-Level Backup

As I stated before, aside from the in-app backup, you can also back up your whole iPhone to iCloud, including WhatsApp data. Yet this process copies all apps and settings, not only WhatsApp, and restoring it replaces your phone’s existing data.

  1. Go to Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > iCloud Backup.
  2. Turn on Back Up This iPhone.
  3. Tap Back Up Now to start a manual backup or enable automatic backups when your phone is charging, locked, and connected to Wi-Fi.
Note If you want to exclude WhatsApp from your iPhone backup to save space, go to iCloud settings > iCloud Backup > [your device name] > toggle off WhatsApp and select Turn Off. Ensure you take regular WhatsApp in-app backups to prevent losing your chat history.

How to Enable End-to-End Encrypted Backups

For extra privacy, WhatsApp lets you encrypt backups.

On iPhone or Android:

  1. Launch WhatsApp and navigate to Settings > Chats > Chat Backup. 
  2. Tap End-to-End Encrypted Backup. 
  3. Tap Turn On and select to create a password (min. 6 characters) or a 64-digit encryption key. 
  4. Follow instructions and tap Create to activate encryption. Your next backup will be encrypted.

Keep the key safe; if you lose it, you can’t restore your backup.

Save WhatsApp Chats Without Cloud

Don’t want to use iCloud or Google Drive? Export chats instead:

On iPhone:

  1. Open WhatsApp and select the chat (individual or group) you want to export. 
  2. Tap the contact or group name at the top. 
  3. Scroll down and tap Export chat. 
  4. Choose Without media (text only) or Attach media (includes photos/videos, but file size limits may apply). 
  5. Select an app like Mail, Messages, or Notes to send the zip file or tap Save to Files. 

On Android:

  1. Open the chat you want to export in WhatsApp.
  2. Tap the three-dot icon at the top right corner.
  3. Select More > Export Chat.
  4. Choose Include Media or Without Media.
  5. Finally, share or save the zip file.

This is perfect for archiving vital chats or sharing them with someone else. You can also manually save WhatsApp photos to the iPhone Camera Roll.

How to Restore WhatsApp Chats

You can only restore WhatsApp chats if you have a backup. In addition, messages received or sent after the most recent backup won’t be restored.

On iPhone: 

  1. Make sure you’re logged into the same iCloud account that’s used for backing up.
  2. Delete and reinstall WhatsApp from the App Store.
  3. Launch WhatsApp, enter your phone number (which must match the backup number).
  4. If prompted, tap Restore Chat History and authenticate.
  5. Wait for the process to complete. Your chats and media will reappear in WhatsApp.

On Android: 

  1. Sign in to the same Google account used for the backup.
  2. Reinstall WhatsApp from the Google Play Store.
  3. Verify your phone number.
  4. Tap Restore when prompted to recover chats from Google Drive.
  5. Wait for the restoration to finish.

For encrypted backups, you’ll need your password/key.

Best Practices for WhatsApp Backup

To have your WhatsApp data secure and convenient:

  • Back Up Frequently: Create auto-backups daily or weekly to minimize data loss. 
  • Check Storage: Check iCloud (iPhone) or Google Drive (Android) storage space to make sure there is ample space. Upgrade storage if necessary. 
  • Secure Encrypted Backups: Keep your encryption password or key in a secure location, such as a password manager. 
  • Stable Connection: Backup and restore using Wi-Fi to minimize interruptions. 
  • Verify Backups: Check the Last Backup time under WhatsApp settings after a backup to confirm completion. 
  • Avoid Repetition: On iPhones, turn off WhatsApp in iCloud settings when using in-app backups to conserve space. 

Troubleshooting WhatsApp Backup Issues

WhatsApp backup or restore problems? Try these fixes: 

Still stuck? Try WhatsApp Support via Settings > Help > Contact Us, or use trusted third-party tools like MobileTrans or Dr.Fone for PC backups.

Keep Your WhatsApp Chats Safe

Backing up WhatsApp messages only takes a few minutes but can save years of conversations. Whether you use iCloud, Google Drive, or encrypted backups, keeping your chats safe ensures peace of mind when switching phones or recovering from mishaps.

Set up your backup today, it’s a small step for a big sense of security.

@graph.name: How to backup WhatsApp messages with iCloud
@graph.description: Manually back up your WhatsApp messages to iCloud directly from the app's settings on your iPhone.

step.name: Access WhatsApp settings
step.text: Open WhatsApp on your iPhone and tap the Settings icon at the bottom right of the screen.

itemListElement.text: Launch the WhatsApp app on your iPhone.
Tap the Settings icon located in the bottom-right corner.

step.name: Navigate to Chat Backup
step.text: Tap on Chats in the settings menu, then choose Chat Backup from the list of options.

itemListElement.text: In the Settings menu, tap Chats.
Select Chat Backup from the next screen.

step.name: Start the backup
step.text: Tap Back Up Now to manually back up your WhatsApp messages to iCloud.

itemListElement.text: Tap Back Up Now to begin the backup immediately.
Wait for the backup to complete—stay connected to Wi-Fi.

@graph.name: How to backup WhatsApp messages on iPhone without iCloud
@graph.description: Export specific WhatsApp chats manually from your iPhone and save them using any app without needing iCloud.

step.name: Go to Export Chats
step.text: Open WhatsApp, go to Settings, tap on Chats, and select Export Chats.

itemListElement.text: Launch WhatsApp and tap on Settings at the bottom right.
Tap Chats and then tap Export Chats.

step.name: Select and export chats
step.text: Choose the chats you want to export, select whether to include media, then share the exported file through your preferred app.

itemListElement.text: Select the chat you want to export.
Choose whether to Attach Media or export without it.
Wait for the chat to be archived.
Pick the app you want to use to save or share the exported chat file.

@graph.name: How to turn on automatic WhatsApp chat history on iPhone
@graph.description: Enable auto backup for WhatsApp chats on your iPhone and choose a schedule to keep your messages backed up regularly.

supply.name: iPhone with WhatsApp and iCloud enabled

step.name: Navigate to Auto Backup
step.text: Open WhatsApp settings, go to Chats, then tap Chat Backup and select Auto Backup.

itemListElement.text: Launch WhatsApp and tap Settings.
Go to Chats > Chat Backup.
Tap Auto Backup to configure the schedule.

step.name: Select backup frequency
step.text: Choose how often you want WhatsApp to automatically back up your chats: daily, weekly, or monthly.

itemListElement.text: Select Daily to back up chats every day.
Or choose Weekly or Monthly based on your preference.

@graph.name: How to restore WhatsApp messages on iPhone
@graph.description: Restore your WhatsApp chats from an iCloud backup when setting up WhatsApp on a new or reset iPhone.

step.name: Install WhatsApp
step.text: Download WhatsApp from the App Store and install it on your iPhone.

itemListElement.text: Open the App Store on your iPhone.
Search for WhatsApp and download the app.
Install and open WhatsApp.

step.name: Sign in and restore backup
step.text: Sign in with your phone number, and if a backup is found on iCloud, tap Restore Chat History to begin the recovery.

itemListElement.text: Enter your phone number and verify it.
Wait for WhatsApp to check for available iCloud backups.
If prompted, tap Restore Chat History.
Wait for the restore process to finish.
Once complete, all your previous chats will appear in the app.

keyPoints.title: WhatsApp Backup Options on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: WhatsApp on iPhone provides manual and automatic backup options using iCloud or local storage to prevent data loss and restore chat history.

keyPoints.title: Manual WhatsApp Backup via iCloud
keyPoints.explanation: To manually back up WhatsApp, access Settings > Chats > Chat Backup in the app and tap 'Back Up Now' to save chats to iCloud.

keyPoints.title: Backing Up WhatsApp Without iCloud
keyPoints.explanation: If iCloud storage is full, you can export individual chats as Zip files and store them locally on your iPhone.

keyPoints.title: Enabling Automatic WhatsApp Backup on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Activate automatic backups in WhatsApp settings to keep your chat history regularly synced with iCloud, provided you have enough storage.

keyPoints.title: Restoring WhatsApp Chats on a New iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Reinstall WhatsApp, verify your number, and choose 'Restore Chat History' during setup to recover chats from your iCloud backup.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
"The founder of iGeeksBlog, Dhvanesh, is an Apple aficionado, who cannot stand even a slight innuendo about Apple products. He dons the cap of editor-in-chief to make sure that articles match the quality standard before they are published."

About Dhvanesh

Ever since teenage years, gadgets and technology have held a special place in Dhvanesh's heart. This fascination with gadgets and their inner workings fueled a lifelong passion for exploration and troubleshooting. Disassembled electronic items scattered around the house became a familiar sight during his younger years, a testament to this insatiable curiosity.

From SEO Expert to Apple Evangelist

After completing his IT engineering diploma, Dhvanesh's professional journey began with a 4.5-year stint as an SEO executive, honing valuable digital marketing skills. However, the desire to share tech knowledge and connect with a like-minded community proved stronger. In 2012, Dhvanesh embarked on a new adventure, founding iGeeksBlog. This blog became a haven for Apple enthusiasts and tech aficionados seeking insightful and in-depth information about everything Apple.

A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge

In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. As the founder, he has steered the blog’s vision, ensuring it remains a trusted resource for Apple users worldwide. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development.

Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach

Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience.

Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem

Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. Currently, he also manages the iGeeksBlog+ weekly newsletter, delivering curated Apple news, gadgets, apps, tips and tricks straight to subscribers' inboxes. This unwavering commitment to Apple technology and a genuine desire to empower fellow users make him a valuable asset to the iGeeksBlog team.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 Air Could Revive Apple’s Bumper Case

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple may bring back bumper cases: The iPhone 17 Air could get a modern bumper case, reviving the edge-protecting design first introduced with the iPhone 4.
  • Slim profile needs new protection: Traditional cases may feel too bulky on the ultra-thin iPhone 17 Air, making bumpers a practical way to keep the sleek profile intact.
  • Nod to Antennagate history: The bumper’s return recalls the iPhone 4’s Antennagate era, where it doubled as a fix for signal issues and became a defining accessory.
  • Battery case could also return: Apple is exploring a battery case for iPhone 17 Air to offset smaller battery capacity and extend daily use for heavier users.
  • Accessory strategy matters: Reviving bumpers and battery cases signals Apple’s intent to balance design goals with practical protection, while avoiding compromises in slimness or usability.

Apple may bring back an accessory it hasn’t sold in over a decade. According to Mark Gurman, the company has internally discussed introducing a bumper case for the upcoming iPhone 17 Air. The design would echo the iPhone 4’s case from 2010, wrapping around the edges while leaving the back fully exposed.

Why Apple Might Revisit the Bumper

The iPhone 17 Air is expected to stand out for its ultra-thin build, a trait that could make traditional cases feel counterintuitive. A bumper case would strike a middle ground, giving owners some level of protection against drops and scratches while preserving the slim profile Apple is reportedly prioritizing. That balance could appeal to buyers wary of hiding the device’s key selling point under bulky protection.

A Callback to “Antennagate”

The original bumper case wasn’t born out of design ambition but controversy. After iPhone 4 users reported reception issues when gripping the phone in certain ways, Apple began handing out free bumpers to mitigate the problem. While the iPhone 17 Air doesn’t appear to face a similar technical flaw, the rumored return of the bumper style may resonate with longtime users who remember that era.

Battery Case Could Return Too

Separate reporting from The Information’s Wayne Ma suggests Apple is also developing a battery case for the iPhone 17 Air. Apple hasn’t offered one since the iPhone 11, shifting instead to the MagSafe Battery Pack, which it discontinued in 2023. Given the thinner build and likely smaller battery capacity of the Air model, a battery case could provide a practical option for heavy users who need more longevity.

What It Could Signal

If Apple follows through, reintroducing the bumper case would give customers a way to safeguard their phone without undermining its design focus. Pairing that with a battery case hints at a dual strategy: catering both to style-conscious buyers and to those prioritizing endurance. Whether Apple actually commits to selling these accessories, however, remains to be seen.

Would a slim bumper be enough protection for your phone, or would you stick with a full case? Share your thoughts below.

keyPoints.title: Apple Might Reintroduce Bumper Cases
keyPoints.explanation: Apple is considering bringing back the bumper case style for the iPhone 17 Air, echoing the design of the 2010 iPhone 4 case that protected the edges while leaving the back exposed.

keyPoints.title: Slim Profile with Protective Bumper
keyPoints.explanation: The ultra-thin design of the iPhone 17 Air could make traditional cases feel bulky, so a bumper case would offer protection while maintaining the phone's slim and sleek profile.

keyPoints.title: Historical Connection to 'Antennagate'
keyPoints.explanation: The return of the bumper case style harks back to the 'Antennagate' controversy with the iPhone 4, where bumpers helped mitigate reception issues, appealing to longstanding Apple users.

keyPoints.title: Potential Battery Case Revival
keyPoints.explanation: Apple might also reintroduce a battery case for the iPhone 17 Air to compensate for smaller battery capacities, catering to heavy users needing extended longevity.

keyPoints.title: Strategic Significance of Accessories
keyPoints.explanation: Reintroducing bumpers and battery cases would allow Apple to offer protective options that align with the device's design goals and user needs, balancing style and functionality.

title.rendered: Foldable iPhone Reportedly Planned for 2026 With Four Cameras

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Launch Timeline for Foldable iPhone: Apple is aiming for a fall 2026 release with a book-style design, making it the company’s first foldable iPhone.
  • Four-Camera Folding Phone: Expected setup includes an outer display camera, inside front sensor, and dual rear lenses for both folded and unfolded photography.
  • Return of Touch ID: Touch ID may return in the side button, replacing Face ID due to limited space in the foldable design.
  • Connectivity and Display Innovations: Apple could use a C2 modem, eSIM-only setup, and new display tech designed to minimize crease issues.
  • Part of a Larger Apple Roadmap: The foldable iPhone fits into plans for an iPhone Air in 2025 and a 20th anniversary redesign in 2027.

Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone may finally have a launch window. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman and multiple analyst reports, the company is targeting a fall 2026 debut for the device. Early details point to a book-style foldable with four cameras, a return of Touch ID, and Apple’s own cellular modem.

A Foldable With Four Cameras

Leaks suggest the foldable iPhone will feature a total of four cameras: one on the outer display, a front-facing sensor on the inside for use when unfolded, and two rear cameras.

Industry analysts believe the back module will pair a high-resolution main sensor with either an ultra-wide or a telephoto lens. The arrangement would allow the foldable to function much like a traditional iPhone in both folded and unfolded modes, without sacrificing photography features.

Touch ID Instead of Face ID

Apple appears to be bringing back Touch ID for authentication. Reports indicate a fingerprint reader will likely be built into the side button, replacing Face ID. The reasoning comes down to space constraints: the foldable’s slim profile cannot accommodate the large TrueDepth system that Face ID requires.

Supporting Face ID would mean installing two separate setups for folded and unfolded use, something Apple reportedly ruled out. Gurman and analyst Ming-Chi Kuo expect the device to measure between 9 and 9.5mm thick when folded, and under 5mm when open, potentially making it the thinnest iPhone to date.

Connectivity and Design Choices

On the connectivity front, the foldable will reportedly use Apple’s second-generation C2 modem and ship as an eSIM-only device, eliminating a physical SIM slot entirely. Early leaks also suggest a limited color lineup at launch, with only black and white options available.

Display technology is another focus. Apple has reportedly shifted from on-cell to in-cell panels during testing, which could help reduce the crease that plagues most foldables today. Kuo has gone further, suggesting a new laser-drilled display plate may deliver what he calls a “crease-free” viewing experience.

Release Window and Pricing

Supply chain chatter points to production ramping up in early 2026, setting the stage for a fall release. Pricing, however, remains uncertain. With premium Android foldables already landing between $1,800 and $2,000, analysts caution that Apple’s entry into the category will likely come at a similar or higher cost.

Part of Apple’s Larger Roadmap

The foldable iPhone is said to be just one piece of Apple’s upcoming product roadmap. In 2025, reports suggest Apple plans to introduce an “iPhone Air,” a slimmer model expected to replace the current Plus line.

Then, in 2027, the iPhone’s 20th anniversary, the company is rumored to be preparing a major design overhaul, including curved glass edges and a departure from the flat-sided aesthetic it has used since the iPhone 12.

If accurate, the 2026 foldable would mark Apple’s first major shift in iPhone form factor since the iPhone X. Whether it proves to be a turning point for the lineup may come down to how Apple balances durability, thinness, and price against rivals who already have years of foldable experience.

Would a foldable iPhone matter to you, or has Apple missed the moment? Let us know below.

keyPoints.title: Launch Timeline for Foldable iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Apple is targeting a fall 2026 release for its long-rumored foldable iPhone, with early details suggesting a book-style design and key features.

keyPoints.title: Four-Camera Folding Phone
keyPoints.explanation: The foldable iPhone is expected to have four cameras: one on the outer display, a front sensor inside, and two rear cameras for high-quality photography in both folded and unfolded modes.

keyPoints.title: Return of Touch ID
keyPoints.explanation: Apple seems to be bringing back Touch ID, likely integrated into the side button, to save space and replace Face ID due to design constraints.

keyPoints.title: Connectivity and Display Innovations
keyPoints.explanation: The device may use Apple's second-generation C2 modem, be eSIM-only, and feature new in-cell or laser-drilled displays to reduce the crease in foldables.

keyPoints.title: Part of a Larger Apple Roadmap**
keyPoints.explanation: The foldable iPhone is part of a broader plan including an iPhone Air in 2025 and a major design overhaul for the 20th anniversary in 2027, signaling significant shifts in iPhone design.

title.rendered: Apple Health+ Tipped to Bring AI Coaching Next Year

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple Health+ subscription in development: Apple is working on a premium health service for iPhone and iPad, extending the Health app with new personalized features.
  • AI-driven health coach at the center: Health+ will use artificial intelligence to create custom nutrition guidance and wellness plans based on personal data collected through Apple devices.
  • Launch delayed beyond original timeline: Initially expected with iOS 26, Apple Health+ is now slated for iOS 27 or later due to refinement or regulatory review.
  • Pricing still unannounced by Apple: While not confirmed, Health+ will likely follow Apple’s existing subscription tiers, similar to Apple Music and Fitness+.
  • Precautions about wellness versus medical advice: Apple’s move could reshape digital wellness, but it also blurs lines between lifestyle coaching and medical guidance that typically requires professional oversight.

Apple could soon be extending its subscription lineup with a new health and wellness service. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the company is preparing to introduce Apple Health+ as early as next year, positioning it as a premium tier built on top of the existing Health app for iPhone and iPad.

AI-Powered Health Coach

The centerpiece of Health+ is said to be an AI-driven coach. The service would generate personalized nutrition plans and health suggestions by analyzing user data already collected by the Health app.

Gurman previously expected Apple to debut this platform alongside iOS 19.4, which Apple later renamed iOS 26. That timeline has reportedly slipped, and the service is now pegged for iOS 27 or beyond. Delays like this suggest Apple is either refining the technology or weighing the regulatory and privacy implications before launch.

Pricing Still Unclear

Apple has not set pricing details yet. If the service does ship, it would join Apple’s expanding roster of paid offerings that already includes Music, TV+, Fitness+, News+, and iCloud+. Given that mix, Health+ would likely fall into a similar monthly range rather than an outlier subscription.

More Than Just Another Subscription?

Apple has been threading artificial intelligence deeper into its ecosystem, and Health+ could be another sign of that shift. A subscription built around health data might set a new precedent for digital wellness platforms if handled carefully.

The bigger question is whether Apple can walk the line between offering lifestyle guidance and veering into territory that normally requires medical oversight. A misstep there could open Apple up to criticism from both regulators and health professionals.

If the execution proves thoughtful, however, Health+ could place the iPhone in more direct competition with wellness apps such as Noom and MyFitnessPal, while also reinforcing Apple’s broader pitch that its devices can play a central role in personal healthcare.

Would you put your trust in an AI-driven health coach for nutrition and wellness guidance? Let us know what you think in the comments.

excerpt.rendered: Apple Health+ may arrive in 2026 with AI-powered health coaching, personalized nutrition plans, and wellness tips, potentially rivaling top fitness apps.

keyPoints.title: Apple's New Health+ Service in Development
keyPoints.explanation: Apple is preparing to launch a premium health and wellness subscription called Apple Health+ that will extend the capabilities of the existing Health app on iPhone and iPad, possibly as early as next year.

keyPoints.title: AI-Powered Personal Health Coach
keyPoints.explanation: At the core of Health+ will be an AI-driven coach that creates personalized nutrition plans and health suggestions based on user data, marking a significant step in digital wellness.

keyPoints.title: Delayed Launch Compared to Initial Expectations
keyPoints.explanation: Originally anticipated alongside iOS 19.4 (later iOS 26), the launch of Health+ has been pushed back to iOS 27 or later, indicating ongoing technology refinement or regulatory review.

keyPoints.title: Unclear Pricing and Market Positioning
keyPoints.explanation: While pricing details are not yet announced, Health+ is expected to follow Apple’s existing subscription models, likely costing similar to other services like Apple Music or Fitness+.

keyPoints.title: Potential Impact on Digital Wellness and Healthcare Ecosystem
keyPoints.explanation: Health+ signals Apple's deeper integration of AI into health management, which could challenge existing wellness apps and raise questions about the balance between lifestyle advice and medical oversight.

title.rendered: 13 Essential things you should do before selling an old iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Create a backup of your data: Use iCloud, Finder, or iTunes to back up your iPhone before selling it so nothing important gets lost.
  • Transfer and secure contacts: Move contacts to iCloud or export them as a vCard file to ensure you keep access when switching to a new device.
  • Unpair and disconnect accessories: Unpair Bluetooth devices and Apple Watch so they can pair smoothly with your next iPhone or another owner’s device.
  • Cancel AppleCare and remove personal data: End any AppleCare coverage, delete personal files and apps, and sign out of iCloud and Apple ID for privacy protection.
  • Erase and finalize for sale: Factory reset your iPhone, remove it from trusted devices, and confirm it’s completely wiped before handing it over.

Let me guess… after years of use, your iPhone is starting to look a little dull. So, you’ve decided to sell it and upgrade to the newer model. But before selling your old iPhone, it’s wise to carry out a few simple procedures like backing up your data to a secure location and wiping out all existing settings and content.

This is done to ensure nothing is left on your device, and all of your personal data is secure. Follow along as I walk you through the 12 most important things you must do before selling your old iPhone.

Table of Contents
  • What things to do before selling your old iPhone?
    • 1. Create an iCloud or local backup
    • 2. Transfer contacts to iCloud or export them
    • 3. Unpair iPhone from other devices
    • 4. Cancel your AppleCare plan
    • 5. Delete photos
    • 6. Sign out of apps and remove accounts
    • 7. Delete apps
    • 8. Remove your SIM card or eSlM
    • 9. Turn off Find My and Sign out of Apple ID
    • 10. Erase all content and settings on iPhone
    • 11. Remove iPhone from list of trusted devices
    • 12. Clean the iPhone and inspect it for damage
    • 13. Find the original accessories and box

What things to do before selling your old iPhone?

1. Create an iCloud or local backup

The first thing you must do before selling your old iPhone is create a backup of your data. And the quickest way you can do this is through iCloud.

However, if you’re running low on iCloud storage or not connected to the internet, you can create a local backup using Finder on macOS or iTunes on Windows.

If you want to create an iCloud backup of your iPhone, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap the Apple ID banner with your name → Select iCloud.


    ‍ ‍ 
  3. Select iCloud Backup → Toggle on Back Up This iPhone.
    On 5G–supported models, you can also turn on Backup Over Cellular.
  4. Then, tap Back Up Now to create a iCloud backup.

If you want to create a local backup of your iPhone, follow these steps:

  1. Connect your iPhone to Mac or Windows computer with a USB cable.
  2. Open Finder on your Mac or iTunes on your Windows computer.
  3. Click the iPhone icon located on the left pane inside Finder.
    The same option can be found in the top-left corner in iTunes.
  4. Then, click Back Up Now to create a local backup.

2. Transfer contacts to iCloud or export them

Next up, you would want to ensure that all your contacts are stored safely. To do this, you can choose to either transfer all your contacts to iCloud or export them as a vCard file that can be stored on your Mac or Windows PC.

 If you want to transfer your contacts to iCloud, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap the Apple ID banner with your name → Select iCloud.

  3. Tap Show All under Apps using iCloud → Toggle on Contacts.

Further, if you wish to export contacts, you can follow our guide on how to export contacts as vCard.

3. Unpair iPhone from other devices

If you have paired your iPhone with several Bluetooth devices like AirPods, speakers, headphones, or your car’s infotainment system, you might want to unpair them from your iPhone. This ensures that your Bluetooth devices can easily connect with another device without searching for your iPhone.

  1. Go to Settings → Bluetooth.
  2. Tap the blue info button next to a paired device.
  3. Then, select Forget This Device to unpair it from your iPhone.

Apart from other Bluetooth devices, if you have an Apple Watch paired to your iPhone, you’ll have to unpair it via the Watch app. If you need help with the same, you should check out this guide on how to unpair Apple Watch.

4. Cancel your AppleCare plan

If you have an active AppleCare plan for your old iPhone, it’s important to terminate it to avoid unnecessary charges. You can easily cancel monthly or annual plans directly on your iPhone by navigating to Settings → Apple ID Banner → Subscriptions.

But, If you are unable to locate your plan or if you paid for the plan upfront, you will need to reach out to Apple Support.

5. Delete photos

Since you have already taken a backup of your Photos to iCloud, you can delete them from your iPhone storage.

Now, a general reset will clear all your photos, but it’s always safer to delete them individually. That way, you are clearing out traces (making it better than what a general reset will do).

Clearing out photos includes clearing out albums. Unfortunately, since the iPhone/iOS doesn’t come with an option to delete multiple photos at once, you’ll have to resort to a little trick to delete them in bulk.

In your album, pinch the screen to zoom out. Now tap Select in the top right (if you don’t see Select, you’ve zoomed out too far and need to zoom back in). Drag your finger across the rows or columns of photos you want to delete.

Tap the trash can icon and watch your photos disappear. Well, to the ‘Recently Deleted’ album.

6. Sign out of apps and remove accounts

As a precautionary measure, it’s recommended that you sign/log out of all third-party banking and conferencing apps on your iPhone that have access to your sensitive data.

Furthermore, you should disconnect any synchronized email or calendar accounts from Apple Mail, Calendar, and Contacts.

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Select either Mail, Contacts, or Calendar → Tap Account.

  3. Select an account you want to remove → Tap Delete Account.

7. Delete apps

Once you’re done deleting photos (which is some of the most personal stuff you’d have on your old iPhone), you can start clearing out the apps.

Why delete apps when a reset clears them out? Just an extra precaution. Deleting apps will delete most caches associated with these apps. It’ll also delete any traces of login/personal information that the apps might’ve stored on your iPhone. (I’m thinking of Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, etc.)

8. Remove your SIM card or eSlM

Next up, if your iPhone has a physical SIM card slot, you’ll have to remove the SIM card from your iPhone. On the other hand, if you have a dual SIM iPhone or iPhone without a SIM card slot, you’ll have to delete the eSIM.

  1. Use the SIM ejector tool to remove a SIM card from your iPhone.
  2. If you need to delete an eSIM, go to Settings → Cellular.
  3. Select the eSIM you want to delete → Tap Delete eSIM.
  4. Tap Delete eSIM again to confirm your action.

9. Turn off Find My and Sign out of Apple ID

Once you complete the previous steps, you’ll have to turn off Fing My on your iPhone to disable the Activation Lock and Sign out of your Apple ID. Even though you can always turn off Find My manually, Signing out of your Apple ID will automatically do this for you.

Here are the steps for the same:

  1. Launch the Settings app → Tap the Apple ID banner.
  2. Scroll down and tap Sign Out.
  3. Enter your Apple ID’s password → Tap Turn off.

  4. Select the content you want to store offline. Then, tap Sign out (twice).

10. Erase all content and settings on iPhone

Now that you’ve created a backup of your crucial data, disabled iMessage and FaceTime, removed any connected accounts, and signed out of your Apple ID, you can finally Erase all content and settings on your iPhone.

  1. Go to Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  2. Choose Erase All Content and Settings.


    ‍ 
  3. Tap Continue → type the iPhone Passcode. Then you may follow the on-screen instructions once the automatic iCloud backup completes.

11. Remove iPhone from list of trusted devices

Once your iPhone is ready to be sold, one last thing you should ensure is that it still doesn’t show up in your list of trusted devices. If you happen to have another iPhone, iPad, or Mac, you can remove a device from your Apple account from the Settings app. Alternatively, you can follow these steps:

  1. Go to appleid.apple.com → Enter your credentials → Hit Enter/Return.

  2. Select Devices from the list of options available on the left.
  3. Select iPhone from the list of trusted devices.

  4. Scroll down and click Remove from Account.

12. Clean the iPhone and inspect it for damage

Once you complete the steps that I’ve mentioned above, you may want to clean your iPhone with a soft, damp cloth and inspect it for damage. This will ensure that you can get the maximum value out of your old iPhone.

If your iPhone is somehow damaged beyond cosmetic blemishes in a way that affects its function, you might want to get it fixed by a professional. Even though you can always sell your old iPhone without fixing anything, I won’t recommend this as it might significantly reduce the resale value.

13. Find the original accessories and box

Apart from cleaning your iPhone and inspecting it for damage, you must also ensure that you gather all the original accessories and packaging before selling it to the new owner. iPhones with original accessories and undamaged boxes sell at a much higher value than the ones without them.

Wrapping up…

So, these are some of the essential things you must do before giving away your device to anyone (or selling it). Of course, it’s a little time-consuming. However, it’s better to go through the grind in order to keep your precious data as safe as possible.

So, which device are you planning to switch to?

mainEntity.name: Can fake AirPods Pro connect to an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many fakes can connect via Bluetooth, but the pairing process is often clunky, and you won’t get Apple’s smooth animation or iOS features.

mainEntity.name: Do fake AirPods Pro support “Find My”?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. Real AirPods Pro integrates with Apple’s Find My network. If this feature is missing, it’s a strong sign of a fake.

mainEntity.name: Can I update firmware on fake AirPods Pro?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope. Fakes either don’t update at all or show fake firmware versions that don’t match Apple’s records.

mainEntity.name: Are all fake AirPods Pro terrible in quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Some high-end fakes mimic the look and sound decently, but they still lack Apple’s polish, features, and reliability.

mainEntity.name: How can I avoid buying a fake pair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Buy from trusted sources like Apple, Best Buy, or Amazon’s official store. Avoid deals that seem too good to be true, and always check the serial number.

acceptedAnswer.text: No, your tweets, followers, and account data stay intact. Only temporary files are removed.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Clearing cache removes temporary files, while deleting data resets the app and logs you out.

mainEntity.name: What does it mean if I don’t allow an app to track?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you don’t allow an app to track you, it won’t be able to follow your activity across other apps and websites and share your data with third-party advertisers. So, you will see fewer personalized ads. However, some app features that rely on tracking might not work properly. But the app can still collect data for its own use, like tracking your activity within the app itself (unless you adjust its specific permissions in settings).

keyPoints.title: Create a Backup of Your Data
keyPoints.explanation: Before selling your old iPhone, ensure you back up all your data via iCloud or locally using Finder or iTunes to prevent data loss.

keyPoints.title: Transfer Contacts and Export Them
keyPoints.explanation: Safeguard your contacts by transferring them to iCloud or exporting as a vCard file to your computer.

keyPoints.title: Unpair and Disconnect Devices
keyPoints.explanation: Unpair Bluetooth accessories and Apple Watch from your iPhone to ensure they can connect to other devices without issues.

keyPoints.title: Cancel AppleCare and Remove Personal Data
keyPoints.explanation: Terminate any active AppleCare plans, delete photos and apps, and sign out of all accounts to protect your privacy.

keyPoints.title: Erase and Prepare for Sale
keyPoints.explanation: Complete a factory reset by erasing all content and settings, then remove the device from trusted devices and verify it's ready for sale.

title.rendered: How to check trade in value of iPhone, Apple Watch, and Mac

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Understanding trade-in value: Apple trade-ins give you credit toward a new device, with final pricing confirmed after inspection of your current hardware.
  • Timing your trade-in for maximum benefit: Values drop right after new model launches, so trading in before an Apple event usually secures a better payout.
  • Checking iPhone trade-in value: Apple’s trade-in page or Best Buy estimates provide a ballpark, but the actual offer depends on your iPhone’s condition.
  • Trading in Apple Watch and iPad: Both require a reset and condition check, with values available online or in-store through Apple and authorized retailers.
  • MacBook and other Apple product trade-ins: Apple usually offers the highest MacBook trade-in values, though direct selling often beats retail estimates for older devices.

Scouting for a mouth-watering deal on Apple products? Consider trading in your current device when buying your next device. But what exactly is a trade-in, and how do you check the trade-in value of iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and MacBook?

Well, this article explains it all! Besides, there are many ways to trade-in your old Apple device. Let’s start with the basics!

Table of Contents
  • What is trade-in value?
  • Which is the best time to trade in your iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and Mac?
  • How to check iPhone trade-in value
    • 1. Trade-in iPhone with Apple
    • 2. Trade-in iPhone with Bestbuy
  • Check the Apple Watch trade-in value
    • 1. Trade-in Apple Watch for Apple Store credit
    • 2. Check Apple Watch trade-in value on BestBuy
  • How to check iPad trade-in value
    • 1. Check iPad trade-in value on Apple
    • 2. How to check iPad trade-in value on Bestbuy
  • How to check MacBook trade-in value
    • 1. Trade-in MacBook with Apple
    • 2. Check MacBook Trade-in value on BestBuy

What is trade-in value?

Trade-in value is the money you get for your Apple device. Typically, vendors adjust the value of your current device against new purchases. For instance, you can trade-in your old iPhone and get a credit to buy a new one.

However, it is essential to check your device’s (iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and MacBook) trade-in value before upgrading. I suggest spending some time across multiple websites to get the best quote. But when is the right time for trade-in? Read on.

Note: The majority of trade-in programs mandate purchasing a new device. In other words, you get store credits instead of cash.

Which is the best time to trade in your iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and Mac?

Trade-in value depends on many factors, including your device’s condition and the product’s life cycle. Hence, obviously, newer iPhones, Apple Watches, and MacBooks will fetch a better price than older ones.

The best time to trade-in your device is before new ones are launched. Values of current devices plunge after Apple launches newer models. It is especially true for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch. Besides, the price drop is as steep as 30%.

How to check iPhone trade-in value

iPhone is arguably the most popular smartphone. It is easy for companies to refurbish used iPhones and make a profit. The websites quote depending on self-assessment. Furthermore, the trade-in will be approved only after a visual inspection.

1. Trade-in iPhone with Apple

  1. Go to Apple’s trade-in section.
  2. Check the estimated trade-in value for your iPhone.
  3. Scroll down and select your device for an accurate quote.
  4. Select Smartphone.
  5. Choose the model (iPhone 12 mini in my case.)
  6. Answer the questionnaire.

That’s it! Now, your iPhone’s trade-in value will be displayed. You also get an option to trade-in iPhone for a gift card.

2. Trade-in iPhone with Bestbuy

Use this option only if you are buying on BestBuy.

  1. Scroll down to Estimate your trade-in value on BestBuy.
  2. Select iPhone and choose the model.
  3. Choose your current teleservices provider.
  4. Specify other details like storage and color.
  5. Detail your iPhone’s condition.
    If your device has screen damage or dents, it is time to mention it.

BestBuy will give you an estimated trade-in value. However, if you prefer cash over store credit, it’s better to sell your iPhone.

Check the Apple Watch trade-in value

Planning to buy a fancy new Apple Watch? Trade-in your smartwatch and save some money. Apple Watch has a relatively low trade-in value, primarily because of high battery replacement costs and high out-of-warranty fees. Before selling, ensure you have reset it to the default factory settings to protect your data from falling into the wrong hands.

Below are some of the best ways to trade-in the Apple Watch.

1. Trade-in Apple Watch for Apple Store credit

  1. Visit Apple’s trade-in webpage.
  2. Scroll down and select Apple Watch.
  3. Enter the Serial number.
    Go to Settings→ General → About on Apple Watch.
  4. Apple displays the trade-in value after verifying the serial number.

However, you can trade-in your Apple Watch against store credits.

2. Check Apple Watch trade-in value on BestBuy

  1. Go to BestBuy trade-in and select Apple Watch Series.
  2. Choose body type and size.
    BestBuy displays a list of Apple Watch variants with color.
  3. Select the right combination.
  4. Specify the condition of the watch.

Now, trade-in Apple Watch for a BestBuy gift card. Use it for your next purchase.

How to check iPad trade-in value

Apple recently took the wraps from the M1-powered iPad Air. The latest iPad offers unparalleled performance while the mini-LED Liquid Retina takes care of display needs. Now is the right time to switch to the new iPad. Trade-in your current iPad and use the credits to buy a shiny new iPad.

 1. Check iPad trade-in value on Apple

  1. Open Apple’s trade-in webpage.
  2. Select Tablet.
  3. Enter the serial number and verify.

2. How to check iPad trade-in value on Bestbuy

  1. Go to the BestBuy trade-in section.
  2. Select iPad.
  3. Specify the exact model.
    E.g., iPad Pro 11.
  4. Enter other details like storage capacity and color.
  5. Specify product condition.
    Ensure the information is accurate as it is used to determine trade-in value.

BestBuy will now show the trade-in value. After a successful trade-in, you will receive a gift card!

How to check MacBook trade-in value

The new M1, M1 Max, and M1 Ultra MacBooks are here. Now is the time to exchange your old and sluggish Intel Mac for a newer one. Before trading, ensure that your Mac is backed up. Battery health, physical condition, and other factors decide the final trade-in value. Keep MacBook serial number in handy.

1. Trade-in MacBook with Apple

  1. Select MacBook on the Apple trade-in site.
  2. Enter the serial number. (Open the Apple menu and select About This Mac.)
  3. Specify screen and other physical conditions.
  4. Trade-in MacBook against Apple store credits.

2. Check MacBook Trade-in value on BestBuy

  1. Open the BestBuy trade-in webpage.
  2. Select Apple Notebooks.
  3. Specify MacBook series, year of manufacturing, screen size, storage option, and color.
  4. State the item’s condition.
    Include battery health and chargers’ physical condition.
  5. BestBuy asks to log out of iTunes, iCloud, and Apple ID. Once done, you need to factory reset MacBook.

That’s it!

Interestingly, Apple offers the best trade-in value for MacBook. Perhaps this is to incentivize new MacBook purchases. DeClutter offered the least price for my MacBook Air. However, the case is the opposite for other Apple products! You get more value for iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch on selling.

Typically, you will get more money selling directly. However, selling directly is not easy. You will have to waste hours replying to prospective customers, meeting them up, and waiting for the deal to close. Trade-in offers cash/store credit upfront.

In other words, you are trading peace of mind for a little less money. When upgrading, also check for deals on refurbished iPhones, Apple Watch, and MacBook.

Moreover, sometimes Apple offers bonus trade-in value for select Android flagships. The offer is aimed at persuading Android users to jump ship. Share your experience trading in an Apple device in the comments below.

  • What to do before selling your old iPhone
  • How to reset your old Mac before you plan to sell it

keyPoints.title: Understanding Trade-in Value
keyPoints.explanation: Trade-in value is the amount of money you receive for your Apple device, which is typically used as a credit toward purchasing a new device.

keyPoints.title: Timing Your Trade-in for Maximum Benefit
keyPoints.explanation: The best time to trade in your Apple device is before new models are launched, as trade-in values tend to drop significantly after the release.

keyPoints.title: Checking iPhone Trade-in Value
keyPoints.explanation: You can check your iPhone's trade-in value via Apple's official trade-in webpage or Best Buy, with the final offer confirmed after a visual inspection.

keyPoints.title: Trading in Apple Watch and iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Apple Watch and iPad trade-in values are available through official websites and retail stores, often requiring the device to be reset and its condition accurately assessed.

keyPoints.title: Trading in MacBook and Other Apple Products
keyPoints.explanation: MacBook trade-in values are highest when checked directly through Apple; other stores like Best Buy offer estimates based on device condition, but direct selling may yield more money.

title.rendered: 11 Things to do before selling your Mac (Complete guide)

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Quick reset for Apple Silicon and T2 Macs: The “Erase All Content and Settings” option securely wipes your Mac without reinstalling macOS, but back up first.
  • Pre-reset data protection steps: Always save important files using Time Machine, iCloud, or external storage, and cancel AppleCare+ before wiping your Mac.
  • Transfer data to a new Mac: Migration Assistant moves your apps, settings, and documents smoothly, making setup on a new Mac far easier.
  • Deauthorize Apple services and sign out: Remove access from Apple Music, TV, Podcasts, and iCloud to avoid unauthorized use and free account slots.
  • Erase, reinstall, and finalize reset: Use Recovery Mode to erase and reinstall macOS, then reset NVRAM on Intel Macs to fully prepare for resale or handoff.

If you are planning to sell, give, or trade your old Mac, the first thing you’d want to do is factory reset it. However, if you’ve used your Mac for a while, you surely have all sorts of data, including sensitive ones, stored in it. And you definitely don’t want to lose your precious data or, worse, pass it on to someone else

So before I teach you how to reset your MacBook, here’s a list of 11 things to do to protect your data and ensure a nice transition for its new owner.

Quicker reset for Macs

If you own a Mac with Apple silicon or a T2 security chip, you don’t have to go through the laborious process outlined below before selling your MacBook.

You can easily use the Erase All Content and Settings feature. It allows you to securely and quickly erase all your data while retaining the current OS so that you don’t need to reinstall it.

However, before you erase everything, save and back up all your important data, which you can restore on your new device. Also, remember to cancel your AppleCare+ plan for that Mac. If you have a new Mac, you may transfer the plan.

We’ve already written how to factory reset a Mac. Basically, you just need to click the Apple logo → System Settings → General → Transfer or Reset → Erase All Content and Settings, then follow the onscreen prompts.

Older models do not have a quick function like macOS Monterey. However, while there’s a lot to do, they’re pretty straightforward.

Let’s jump to the list!

  1. Backup your files
  2. Migrate files to a new Mac
  3. Deauthorize your Mac from Apple Music, Apple TV, and Podcasts
  4. Sign out of iCloud and Apple ID
  5. Sign out of all your accounts and apps
  6. Unpair all your accessories
  7. Sign out of iMessage and FaceTime
  8. Disable File Vault
  9. Erase your Mac and reinstall macOS
  10. Reset NVRAM/PRAM
  11. Remove Mac as a Trusted Device

1. Backup your files

It is crucial to back up your data to avoid the risk of losing them while resetting your device. It also allows you to readily restore all your data with a few clicks once you have your new device. Here are different ways to back up your Mac:

Time Machine

Time Machine is a built-in backup feature that automatically backs up all of your personal data on your Mac. However, you’d need an external storage device, like a USB, FireWire, or Thunderbolt port.

Store files in your iCloud and iCloud Drive

iCloud is Apple’s own cloud storage and computing service that allows you to store and sync all your photos, files, music, notes, contacts, and more across all your Apple devices.

This service works across the Apple ecosystem so that if you have an iPhone or an iPad, you can also back up your data from your iPhone or iPad on your iCloud. Note that each Apple ID only has 5GB of free iCloud space. You would need to upgrade your iCloud account for higher storage space.

External storage

While iCloud seems to be the best option for an Apple user, you can also use other cloud-based storage devices to store your data online.

However, like iCloud, backups done through external cloud storage are pretty limited compared to Time Machine backups that allow you to store all your Mac’s data.

2. Migrate files to a new Mac

If you upgraded to a new Mac, you could use the Migration Assistant to migrate data from your old Mac to your new MacBook. This includes all your settings, apps, user accounts, and documents.

The process varies depending on the OS the Macs are running. But generally, you’ll need to plug both devices into a power source and connect them to the same WIFI network or cable. 

3. Deauthorize your Mac from Apple Music, Apple TV, and Podcasts

An authorized device has access to all your Apple Music content. Apple allows you to authorize up to five devices under an Apple ID. Forgetting to deauthorize means you lose one slot from the five devices for your account. More importantly, you’d risk giving the new Mac owner access to your Apple Music content.

To deauthorize your Mac:

  1. Open the Music app.
  2. Click Account from the menu bar.
  3. Click Authorizations → Deauthorize This Computer.

Similarly, you should also deauthorize your old Mac from your Apple TV account. Just open the app, and head to Account → Authorizations → Deauthorize This Computer. For Podcasts, just open the app, click Account, then select Sign Out.

4. Sign out of iCloud and Apple ID

As mentioned earlier, iCloud syncs everything across your Apple devices. So, if you’re using it, you must log out of your account. This ensures that your old Mac can no longer access all your files and the new owner’s data is not syncing to your cloud.

Signing out of iCloud automatically signs you out of the App Store, iMessage, and FaceTime. 

Note: Turn off Find My Mac before signing out. Go to your Apple ID → iCloud → Show More Apps → Find My Mac → Click Turn Off.

  1. Click the Apple logo → System Settings.
  2. Select Apple ID in the sidebar.
  3. Click Sign Out below the window.

On Mac running macOS Mojave or earlier:

  1. Click the Apple logo → System Preferences.
  2. Choose iCloud, then select Sign Out.

You’ll be asked if you want to keep a copy of your Calendars, Keychain, and Contacts before signing out. Unselect them because you don’t want to leave any data from your old Mac that you intend to give away or sell.

Don’t worry—all of your iCloud data will remain in iCloud and on your other Apple devices signed in on iCloud with your Apple ID.

5. Sign out of all your accounts and apps

Aside from the Apple services, be sure to log out of all the other apps that you own before you even uninstall them. This is especially true for software licensed to you. Not doing this can lead to complications if the new Mac owner ever decides to download and install the same apps or software.

Make sure to sign out of all your other internet accounts, especially if your emails and calendars are synced to your Mac. Go to System Settings → Internet Accounts, select an account in the sidebar, and click Delete Account at the bottom to remove it.

6. Unpair all your accessories

If you’re using Bluetooth devices with your Mac, it’s ideal to unpair all of them, especially if the one you’re selling your old Mac to is a peer or family member you often spend time with. You don’t want your devices to connect to your old device accidentally. 

Go to System Settings → Bluetooth. You should see a list of paired devices. Click the info button beside the device and click Forget This Device to unpair it. A prompt will appear; select Forget Device.

7. Sign out of iMessage and FaceTime

Suppose you use your Mac to send and receive texts and calls through iMessage or call peers and family through FaceTime. In that case, you should sign out of both services to prevent the new owner from accidentally gaining access to your private conversations.

To turn off iMessage on Mac:

  1. Open the Messages app.
  2. On the menu bar, select Messages → Settings, then click the iMessage tab.
  3. Click Sign Out. Select Sign Out again from a pop-up that will appear.

To turn off FaceTime:

  1. Open FaceTime and click Facetime → Settings in the menu bar.
  2. Click Sign Out in the General tab.

8. Disable File Vault   

File Vault is a feature that encrypts all the information on your Mac. This prevents hackers from stealing or hacking your data or gaining access to your device.

If you previously encrypted your file contents, you need to turn this off to decrypt your disk. If you don’t do this, your old Mac will ask for your password, leaving the new owner unable to set up their new Mac. 

To do this:

  1. Head to System Settings → Network.
  2. Select the FileVault tab, then toggle off FileVault.

9. Erase your Mac and reinstall macOS

Now that you’ve wiped your old Mac clean of any remaining personal and sensitive data, it’s time to erase your hard drive. 

The exact steps to reset a Mac depend on the model and the OS it is running on. For a more comprehensive dive, read our article on how to reset a MacBook or any Mac.

Simply go to the Apple menu → Shut Down. Now start Mac in Recovery mode and select Disk Utility. Choose your hard disk and hit Erase. Follow the instructions to reset your Mac. Once done, exit Disk Utility and select Reinstall macOS from the Recovery page.

10. Reset NVRAM/PRAM 

The NVRAM, short for non-volatile random-access memory, stores OS-related settings, startup disk selection, and other configurations. Apple suggests resetting your NVRAM before selling your MacBook. 

Note: This step only applies to Intel Macs.

Resetting NVRAM can restore security features that may have been changed or if the Mac is running weirdly. Resetting this also clears user settings, ensuring that your Mac is ready for its new owner. 

11. Remove Mac as a Trusted Device

If you have set your Mac as a Trusted Device for your other devices, check your other devices and remove your old Mac from your list. This prevents your devices from accidentally sending verification code requests to your old Mac.

On your iPhone or iPad:

  1. Head to Settings, then tap your name.
  2. Tap your old Mac. You’ll know that it is a trusted device if you see the statement This device is trusted and can receive Apple ID verification codes.
  3. Tap Remove from the account.

Wrapping up

Whether you plan to sell, give away, or trade-in your Mac to upgrade to a newer model, protecting your personal data is crucial. This also makes your old Mac ready for its new users and ensures that they won’t encounter problems while setting it up.

Related Reads:

  • How to Restore your Mac from a Backup
  • Useful macOS Terminal Commands That Every Mac User Should Try
  • Mac Recovery Mode not working issue? 14 Tips to fix it
  • Screenshot not working on Mac? 8 Quick fixes

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. Real AirPods Pro integrates with Apple’s Find My network. If this feature is missing, it’s a strong sign of a fake.

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope. Fakes either don’t update at all or show fake firmware versions that don’t match Apple’s records.

mainEntity.name: Are all fake AirPods Pro terrible in quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Some high-end fakes mimic the look and sound decently, but they still lack Apple’s polish, features, and reliability.

mainEntity.name: How can I avoid buying a fake pair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Buy from trusted sources like Apple, Best Buy, or Amazon’s official store. Avoid deals that seem too good to be true, and always check the serial number.

keyPoints.title: Quick Reset for Macs with Apple Silicon or T2 Chip
keyPoints.explanation: Use the 'Erase All Content and Settings' feature for a fast and secure way to reset your Mac without reinstalling macOS, but ensure you back up your data first.

keyPoints.title: Pre-Reset Data Protection Steps
keyPoints.explanation: Before resetting your Mac, back up all important files using Time Machine, iCloud, or external storage, and cancel any active AppleCare+ plans.

keyPoints.title: Transferring Data to a New Mac
keyPoints.explanation: Use Migration Assistant to seamlessly transfer all your settings, apps, and documents from your old Mac to a new one.

keyPoints.title: Deauthorize and Sign Out from Apple Services
keyPoints.explanation: Deauthorize your Mac from Apple Music, TV, Podcasts, and sign out of iCloud, Apple ID, and all account apps to prevent unauthorized access and free up device slots.

keyPoints.title: Erase and Reinstall macOS, and Final Reset Steps
keyPoints.explanation: Erase your Mac via Recovery Mode, reinstall macOS, and reset NVRAM (for Intel Macs) and other settings to prepare your device for its new owner.
