title.rendered: How to Accept Shared Album Invite on iPhone or iPad

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Enable Shared Albums in Settings > Photos to receive invites—this feature must be on before you can view or join any shared albums.
  • Accept Shared Album invites from Notification Center by long-pressing the alert and tapping ‘Accept’—great for quick access when you get notified.
  • You can also accept from the Photos app under the ‘For You’ tab—tap Shared Albums to view pending invitations and join from there.
  • To leave a Shared Album, tap the three-dot menu in the album view and select ‘Unsubscribe’—you’ll lose access to all shared media.
  • iCloud Photos must be turned on for Shared Albums, and you’ll need enough iCloud space to view or add shared content across your Apple devices.

We all love to create and document memories with our loved ones through photos and videos on our iPhones. But what’s the use of making memories with loved ones when they’re confined to your iPhone?

This is exactly where the iCloud Shared Albums feature comes in handy. A Shared Album allows you to share photos and videos and collaborate with participants in real time.

While creating a shared album is easy, accepting the invite to join has countless iPhone users confused. Keep reading to learn how to accept a Shared Album invite on an iPhone and iPad.

Table of Contents
  • How to accept a Shared Album invitation on your iPhone or iPad
    • How to accept a Shared Album invite via Notification Center
    • How to accept an invite to a Shared Album via the Photos app
  • How to leave a shared photo album on an iPhone

How to accept a Shared Album invitation on your iPhone or iPad

To use Shared Albums on your iPhone, you must ensure it’s turned on, as you won’t receive the invite if it isn’t.

While the feature is turned on by default, it’s possible that you may have turned it off at some point. Here’s how to verify if Shared Albums is turned on and enable it if it isn’t:

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Scroll down and select Apps.
  3. Here, locate and tap on Photos.
  4. Finally, toggle on Shared Albums if it isn’t already.

If you’ve toggled on the Shared Album feature just now, ask your friend to share the invitation to join it again. Once you receive the invitation, you can accept it and start collaborating on it, as shown below.

How to accept a Shared Album invite via Notification Center

  1. Swipe down from the top-left of the iPhone screen to access the Notification Center.
  2. Locate the Shared Album Invite notification and long-press on it.
  3. Next, tap the Accept button to accept the invitation.
  4. Alternatively, tap the Decline button if you’re unaware of the person who sent you the invite.

How to accept an invite to a Shared Album via the Photos app

  1. Open the Photos app and go to the For You tab.
  2. Scroll down to the Shared Albums section and tap on it to see the Shared Album invite you’ve received.
  3. Tap the Accept button on the invite to accept the invitation and start collaborating.
Note
  • You won’t be able to use Shared Albums if the iCloud Photos is turned off on your iPhone, and you can’t turn on iCloud Photos if there isn’t enough space available in your iCloud storage.

How to leave a shared photo album on an iPhone

iCloud Shared Albums is a great way to engage and collaborate with your loved ones. However, there may come an instance when you may no longer want to be part of a Shared Album. In that case, you can leave the shared photo album like this:

  1. Open the Photos app and go to the For You tab.
  2. Scroll down to the Shared Albums section and tap on it.
  3. Here, select the Shared Album you want to leave.
  4. Tap the three-dot icon button in the top-right corner and select Unsubscribe from the available options.
  5. Next, tap Unsubscribe again when the confirmation prompt appears to confirm removing yourself from the Shared Album.
Note
    Before leaving a Shared Album, be sure to save the photos and videos you need to your iPhone. Once you unsubscribe, you’ll lose access to all the photos and videos in the Shared Album.

Enjoy shared memories…

Now that you know how to accept Shared Album invites on an iPhone, you can see the Shared Album’s contents and leave your comments under photos and videos for everyone to see. In addition, you can also collaborate on the Shared Album by sharing your own photos and videos.

Shared Albums doesn’t just help you collaborate easily with others, but it also ensures you enjoy increased privacy and high-quality images without relying on any third-party apps.

If you still have some questions, feel free to comment below.

FAQs

What should you do if you don’t see a Shared Album invite?

If you’re unable to use Shared Albums on your iPhone, make sure you’ve turned on the iCloud Photos feature in the Photos app settings.

Can you accept a Shared Album invite on multiple devices?

You don’t need to accept a Shared Album invite on multiple Apple devices signed in with the same Apple ID. If you’ve turned on iCloud Photos, you’ll see the Shared Album on all your devices.

What happens if you accidentally decline a Shared Album invite?

You’ll need to ask the sender to resend the Shared Album invite.

Can you share a Shared Album with people who don’t use Apple devices?

Yes, you can. All you need to do is head to the Shared Album in the Photos app > People tab and turn on Public Website. This will publish the content in the Shared Album to a public website that anyone with the website link can access.

mainEntity.name: Why is my iCloud syncing paused even with enough storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Other issues, such as network problems, Low Power/Low Data Mode, Apple server outages, or VPN/firewall restrictions, can also pause syncing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if syncing is paused?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your latest data (photos, messages, contacts) won't appear on other devices until syncing resumes, but it remains safe on your current device.

mainEntity.name: Will resetting network settings erase my photos or messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, but you'll lose saved Wi-Fi passwords, VPN, and Bluetooth settings.

mainEntity.name: How often should I update my iOS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check for updates monthly or whenever you experience issues—updates often fix bugs affecting iCloud.

mainEntity.name: Where can I find saved markup images?

acceptedAnswer.text: Saved markup edits are automatically saved within the app you used them in. This includes Photos, Files, etc. However, if you used the Markup tool on a document at the time of attaching it, such as in Messages or Mail, the edited file will only be sent as an attachment, and there will not be a downloaded/saved copy of the same.

mainEntity.name: Is Apple Pencil necessary to use the Markup tool on an iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, an Apple Pencil isn't necessary to use the Markup tool on an iPad. You can easily use your finger for editing with the Markup tool. That said, the Apple Pencil, or any other stylus for that matter, does offer a more precise markup experience.

mainEntity.name: What to do if the Markup tool isn't working on iPhone and iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the Markup tool isn't working, try restarting your iPhone or iPad, ensuring iOS or iPadOS is up to date, and checking that the app you're using supports Markup.

mainEntity.name: Is Markup available for third-party apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, no; Markup is currently limited to Apple's built-in apps. However, some third-party apps may offer their own built-in editing tools. For instance, both WhatsApp and Telegram offer native editing tools for their users.

mainEntity.name: What should you do if you don't see a Shared Album invite?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you're unable to use Shared Albums on your iPhone, make sure you've turned on the iCloud Photos feature in the Photos app settings.

mainEntity.name: Can you accept a Shared Album invite on multiple devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: You don't need to accept a Shared Album invite on multiple Apple devices signed in with the same Apple ID. If you've turned on iCloud Photos, you'll see the Shared Album on all your devices.

mainEntity.name: What happens if you accidentally decline a Shared Album invite?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll need to ask the sender to resend the Shared Album invite.

mainEntity.name: Can you share a Shared Album with people who don't use Apple devices?

@graph.name: How to accept Shared Album invitation on iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Enable Shared Albums in your iPhone or iPad settings to ensure you can accept and view shared album invites from others.

step.name: Enable Shared Albums
step.text: Open your device settings, go to Photos under the Apps section, and make sure the Shared Albums toggle is turned on.

itemListElement.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
Scroll down and tap on Photos from the app list.
Toggle on Shared Albums if it’s currently off.

@graph.name: How to accept Shared Album invite via Notification Center
@graph.description: Quickly respond to Shared Album invitations directly from the Notification Center on your iPhone.

step.name: Access Notification Center
step.text: Swipe down from the top-left of the screen to open Notification Center.

itemListElement.text: Unlock your iPhone and swipe down from the top-left corner.
Look for the Shared Album invite notification.

step.name: Respond to the invitation
step.text: Long-press the Shared Album invite notification and tap Accept to join or Decline if you don’t recognize the sender.

itemListElement.text: Long-press the Shared Album invite notification.
Tap Accept to join the album.
Tap Decline if the invite is unexpected.

@graph.name: How to accept invite to Shared Album via Photos app
@graph.description: Accept Shared Album invitations directly from the Photos app on your iPhone or iPad by visiting the For You tab.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad with Photos app

step.name: Open the Photos app and find the invitation
step.text: Launch the Photos app and go to the For You tab. Scroll down to see Shared Album invites.

itemListElement.text: Open the Photos app on your iPhone or iPad.
Tap the For You tab at the bottom.
Scroll to the Shared Albums section to locate your invite.

step.name: Accept the invitation
step.text: Tap Accept to join the Shared Album and start viewing or adding photos.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Accept button on the invitation.
You’ll now have access to the Shared Album.

@graph.name: How to leave shared photo album on iPhone
@graph.description: Remove yourself from a Shared Album on iPhone using the Photos app to stop receiving shared media updates.

step.name: Open Shared Albums in the Photos app
step.text: Go to the For You tab in the Photos app and scroll to find the Shared Albums section.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Photos app on your iPhone.
Tap the For You tab at the bottom.
Scroll to the Shared Albums section and tap to open it.

step.name: Leave the Shared Album
step.text: Choose the album you want to leave, tap the three-dot icon, and select Unsubscribe. Confirm to complete the process.

itemListElement.text: Select the Shared Album you wish to leave.
Tap the three-dot menu in the top-right corner.
Choose Unsubscribe from the options.
Tap Unsubscribe again to confirm removal.

keyPoints.title: Enabling Shared Albums on iPhone or iPad
keyPoints.explanation: To accept Shared Album invites, ensure that the Shared Albums feature is turned on in Settings > Photos, which might have been disabled previously.

keyPoints.title: Accepting Invitations via Notification Center
keyPoints.explanation: Swipe down from the top-left to access Notification Center, long-press the Shared Album invite, then tap 'Accept' to join the album.

keyPoints.title: Accepting Shared Album Invitations in the Photos app
keyPoints.explanation: Open the Photos app, go to the 'For You' tab, and tap the Shared Albums section to find and accept the invitation.

keyPoints.title: Leaving a Shared Album When No Longer Needed
keyPoints.explanation: In the Photos app, under Shared Albums, select the album, tap the three-dot menu, and choose 'Unsubscribe' to leave the album.

keyPoints.title: Important Tips for Shared Albums and Troubleshooting
keyPoints.explanation: You must have iCloud Photos enabled and enough storage to use Shared Albums; also, you can access shared content across all your devices signed in with the same Apple ID.

title.rendered: 18 Trendy Drippy Wallpapers For Your iPhone

content.rendered:
If you’ve been scrolling through TikTok or Instagram lately, you’ve probably noticed drippy wallpapers have become a big trend. Their abstract, liquid-like designs and bold, colorful melt effects go well with the iOS 26’s Liquid Glass aesthetic.  

Here, we have curated some of the best drippy wallpapers to give your iPhone a fun and artistic makeover. Each wallpaper is in 4K quality and available to download for free. So, let’s get started!

Table of Contents
  • Why Choose Drippy Wallpapers for Your iPhone?
  • Best 4K Drippy Wallpapers to Make Your iPhone Trendy
    • Drippy Baseball Wallpaper
    • Drippy Bear on Black Background
    • Car on a Rainy Day
    • Drippy Cross Wallpaper
    • Get Elmo on Your iPhone
    • Drippy Football Wallpaper
    • Halloween in a Drippy Style
    • Supreme Drippy Wallpaper
    • Sneaker Wallpaper for iPhone
    • Drippy Naruto Wallpaper
    • Cool Drippy iOS Wallpaper
    • Drippy Smiley Face Wallpaper
    • Drippy Background
    • The Simpsons Wallpaper
    • Cool Apple Logo Wallpaper
    • iPhone Wallpaper for Spongbob Fans
    • Flaunt Black & White Classic
    • Landscape Wallpaper For iPhone
  • How to Set Drippy Wallpapers on iPhone
  • Tips to Make Your Wallpaper Pop
  • Show Off Your Style!

Why Choose Drippy Wallpapers for Your iPhone? 

Drippy wallpapers are more than just pretty pictures, they’re a vibe! Here’s why iPhone users can’t get enough of them: 

  • They’re eye-catching and make your home screen stand out from the usual minimal or nature themes. 
  • With several options available, you can find one that matches your personality. 
  • These wallpapers look amazing on iPhone’s Retina OLED displays, especially in high-resolution 4K. 
  • Drippy designs give your phone a cool, Gen-Z aesthetic that’s all over social media.

Best 4K Drippy Wallpapers to Make Your iPhone Trendy

Ready to upgrade your iPhone’s look? Here are some awesome drippy wallpapers for you:

Drippy Baseball Wallpaper

If you are a sports fan, this wallpaper shows your love in style. The baseball mid-air with cool splashes around it gives a fun, energetic feel. 

Download

Drippy Bear on Black Background

How about black wallpaper with Gothic vibes? The design has a cute teddy bear with Broken Culture written in a drippy style behind it.

Download

Car on a Rainy Day 

This drippy wallpaper shows a car driving through a rainy night. The mix of rain, lights, and dark nature vibes gives it a super cool, almost cinematic feel.

Download

Drippy Cross Wallpaper

Here’s another artistic wallpaper showing a bold black cross made with a paintbrush style. The drips and splatters give it a cool edgy vibe.

Download

Get Elmo on Your iPhone

This artwork puts a fun twist on our favorite Elmo. With bold red background, big drippy eyes, and a wide smile, it’s playful and eye-catching.

Download

Drippy Football Wallpaper

Football fans assemble! Bold splashes of red and orange with paint-like effects make this wallpaper super intense.

Download

Halloween in a Drippy Style

This Halloween set the spooky mood with this drippy wallpaper. It looks like you’re walking into a creepy haunted forest every time you unlock your phone.

Download

Supreme Drippy Wallpaper

This wallpaper puts a cool twist on the classic logo with melting paint-like edges. The scratched-up background adds that extra grunge touch.

Download

Sneaker Wallpaper for iPhone

Are you also a sneakerhead? And looking to add the same swag to your iPhone as well? We’ve got you covered! It shines as it is but looks pretty dope in monochrome.

Download

Drippy Naruto Wallpaper

Any weebs in here? I know anime fans are gonna love this one! We got tons of love from y’all when we released our Boruto collection. Hoping the same for this one as well.

Download

Cool Drippy iOS Wallpaper

Here’s another one for the Sneaker-gang! If you didn’t fall for the earlier one, this wallpaper is the way to go. It’s pretty minimal and goes hand-in-hand with all ambiance.

Download

Drippy Smiley Face Wallpaper

Looking for some positive vibes? Here’s what we’ve for you. This will go really light on both your home screen and lock screen. It will keep reminding you to be gentle while also maintaining the swag.

Download

Drippy Background

This one rolls in a simple background with purple vibes. If you’re a fan of simple clean backgrounds, you’d like our minimalist wallpaper collection.

Download

The Simpsons Wallpaper

This one hold really punchy colors with mischievous vibes. Bart Simpson never fails to entertain and holds on to his A-game, no matter what.

Download

Cool Apple Logo Wallpaper

Apple fans, this one is for you. This wallpaper features a Apple logo with colors blooming out of it.

Download

Want more Apple logo wallpapers? You know where to click, right?

iPhone Wallpaper for Spongbob Fans

This wallpaper is such a vibe. Swaying a yellow aesthetic all along! SquarePants fans, I know you love the new squared-off iPhone design language.

Download

Flaunt Black & White Classic

If you would want to rock the classic black & white vibes, here’s to you! Hope you’ll enjoy it. 

Download

Landscape Wallpaper For iPhone

Fond of natural sceneries? I’m sure you’ll love this one.

Download

How to Set Drippy Wallpapers on iPhone 

Setting up your new drippy wallpaper is super easy. Just follow these steps: 

  1. Explore our collection and tap the Download button below the wallpaper you want to download. 
  2. It will open the image in Drive. Select the download icon at the top. 
  3. Go to Files app > Recents tab and tap and hold the wallpaper. 
  4. Now, select Share > More > Save Image to your photo library.  
  5. Launch Photos, open the wallpaper, and tap the Share icon. 
  6. Select Use as Wallpaper.   
  7. Pinch to zoom or move the image to fit your screen perfectly. Customize the Lock Screen with appropriate clock style and widgets.  
  8. Then, choose if you want it for your Home Screen, Lock Screen, or both. 
  9. Tap Add and voilà! Your iPhone is dripping with style. 

Pro tip: You can use them to create Live wallpapers and provide an animation effect. 

Tips to Make Your Wallpaper Pop 

Want your drippy wallpaper to be even better? Here are the tricks to do that: 

  • Match Your Icons: Set a custom app icon pack that matches your wallpaper’s color for uniformity
  • Keep It Clean: Avoid cluttering your Home Screen with too many apps so the drippy design can shine. 
  • Use Dark Mode: If your wallpaper has bright colors, Dark Mode can make them pop even more. 
  • Play With Widgets: Add simple widgets that blend with the drippy aesthetic. Apps like Widgetsmith can help. 
  • Switch It Up: Change your wallpaper every few weeks to keep your phone feeling fresh and exciting. 

Show Off Your Style! 

Drippy wallpapers are great for giving your iPhone a bold, creative personality. We have tried to curate a style for everyone. In 4K, they look stunning on any iPhone screen. 

So go ahead, pick your favorite drippy design, set it as your wallpaper, and enjoy the fresh new look every time you unlock your phone. 

Fear of missing out?

  • Stranger Things wallpapers for iPhone
  • 10 mind-warping Doctor Strange wallpapers for iPhone
  • 10 Best Foggy Forest Wallpapers for iPhone

title.rendered: Meta Poaches Sixth Apple AI Researcher in 7 Weeks

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Meta quietly bypasses its hiring freeze for AI experts: Despite an official freeze, Meta recruits senior talent like Apple’s Frank Chu to strengthen its Superintelligence Labs division.
  • Selective exceptions highlight AI’s strategic weight at Meta: Meta’s freeze doesn’t apply to top-tier candidates, showing how aggressively it prioritizes AI over other business areas.
  • Meta spends heavily to lure away elite researchers: Compensation packages are reportedly up to 50 times higher than rivals, targeting experts from Apple, Google, and OpenAI.
  • Apple struggles to retain senior AI leadership: Multiple defections to Meta raise concerns about Apple’s long-term AI strategy and its ability to compete in core research.
  • Frequent restructuring creates risk for Meta’s AI push: Ongoing internal clashes could undermine cohesion and slow the integration of new hires, despite record-breaking offers.

Meta’s appetite for AI talent isn’t slowing down, even as reports suggest the company has imposed a hiring freeze. According to Bloomberg, Meta has poached Frank Chu, a senior AI leader from Apple, marking the sixth high-profile defection from Cupertino to Menlo Park in under two months. The move adds fuel to an intensifying talent war in Silicon Valley and raises deeper questions about Apple’s ability to retain top researchers in a fiercely competitive market.

Meta’s So-Called Hiring Freeze Has Loopholes

Officially, Meta is supposed to be on pause when it comes to bringing in new AI hires. Just this week, internal reports indicated a stop to recruitment across AI divisions and restrictions on internal transfers between teams. But Frank Chu’s arrival suggests the freeze comes with caveats—especially when the candidate is seen as too valuable to pass up.

Chu previously led Apple’s AI work on cloud infrastructure, training systems, and search technologies. He’s now joined Meta’s newly formed Superintelligence Labs, the division reportedly spearheading the company’s next big AI push.

His hiring follows that of Ruoming Pang, formerly head of Apple’s foundation models team, who was reportedly lured to Meta with a package north of $200 million. Pang’s exit appears to have triggered a wave of departures, with Chu’s move now seen as the most significant since Pang left.

High Salaries, Higher Stakes

Meta’s approach isn’t about broad expansion—it’s about acquiring top-tier names at staggering cost. Mark Zuckerberg’s company is offering massive compensation packages, in some cases up to 50 times what competitors are willing to pay, in order to secure elite researchers.

Since July, Meta has pulled in more than 50 AI staffers from Apple, Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic. The strategy has sparked optimism around Meta’s AI capabilities, but also concern about ballooning stock-based compensation and whether those high-priced hires can deliver meaningful results.

Zuckerberg appears committed to consolidating AI talent under Superintelligence Labs, betting that critical mass will translate into leadership in the next phase of machine learning development. But the pressure to justify these costs is mounting.

Also Read: Tim Cook Says Apple Is Now ‘Open to’ Big AI Acquisitions

Apple Struggles to Retain Its AI Bench

Apple is facing a growing perception problem. With six senior AI figures defecting to Meta in just seven weeks, doubts are deepening about Apple’s standing in the AI race. CEO Tim Cook fielded questions about Apple’s strategy during its Q3 earnings call and later held an internal meeting to emphasize that the company is investing heavily in the space.

But public statements and private briefings may not be enough. Apple’s AI efforts, often seen as incremental and cautious, have struggled to match the momentum of rivals. Siri’s underperformance is still viewed as emblematic of a broader lag, and losing key engineers like Pang and Chu only reinforces that narrative.

Meta’s Internal Friction Adds Complexity

Despite the recruitment streak, Meta’s internal AI structure remains in flux. The company has restructured its AI organization four times in just six months. Reports describe ongoing friction between teams and cultural mismatches that make it difficult to unify direction.

Even so, Meta continues to make exceptions to its hiring freeze to bring in top-tier talent. That underscores how vital these individuals are to the company’s long-term AI ambitions, even if integrating them poses operational challenges.

Concentrating elite researchers in a single division may accelerate Meta’s development timeline. But it could also create blind spots, reduce diversity in thought, and lead to culture clashes if teams aren’t aligned. For Apple, the more pressing issue is whether it can find a way to stop the bleeding before its AI credibility takes another hit.

Will Apple Stop the Slide?

Meta’s targeted hires and Apple’s inability to plug the talent drain highlight just how intense the AI talent war has become. For Meta, the question is whether the payoff justifies the cost. For Apple, it’s whether a reactive stance can evolve into a competitive strategy.

Does Meta’s aggressive recruitment strategy change your view on Apple’s AI future? Sound off in the comments.

keyPoints.title: Meta’s Aggressive Talent Acquisition Despite Hiring Freeze
keyPoints.explanation: Meta continues to poach top AI talent, such as Apple’s Frank Chu, contradicting its official hiring freeze, highlighting the importance of top-tier researchers for its AI ambitions.

keyPoints.title: Loopholes in Meta’s Hiring Freeze
keyPoints.explanation: Although Meta claims to have halted AI recruitment, exceptions are made for highly valuable candidates like Chu, especially for strategic divisions like Superintelligence Labs.

keyPoints.title: High Costs of Securing AI Talent at Meta
keyPoints.explanation: Meta is offering extremely lucrative packages, up to 50 times higher than competitors, to attract elite researchers from rivals including Apple, Google, and OpenAI.

keyPoints.title: Challenges at Apple in Retaining AI Talent
keyPoints.explanation: Apple is facing difficulties in keeping senior AI researchers, with multiple defections to Meta, questioning its position and strategy in the competitive AI landscape.

keyPoints.title: Internal Friction and Strategic Risks at Meta
keyPoints.explanation: Meta’s frequent restructuring and cultural clashes within its AI teams pose risks to the integration of top talent and could impact its long-term AI leadership.

title.rendered: How to Check Your Weekly Activity Summary on Apple Watch and iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Weekly Activity Summary explained: Apple Watch creates a 7-day report tracking Move, Exercise, and Stand goals, giving you clear insights into progress and habits.
  • Check the Weekly Summary on Apple Watch: Open the Fitness app, tap the graph icon, and see activity details, with quick options to adjust goals as needed.
  • See long-term Weekly Summary on iPhone: The Health app shows daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly activity trends if your Apple Watch and iPhone are properly synced.
  • Apple Watch vs iPhone summary views: The Watch offers quick daily motivation, while iPhone delivers graphs and long-term activity analysis for deeper insights.
  • Share your Weekly Summary with friends: The Fitness app lets you share progress or start challenges with friends to stay accountable and motivated.

Both the Apple Watch and iPhone come with built-in fitness tracking features that use advanced sensors to monitor your activity and help you stay on top of your health goals. The best part? They don’t just log your movement; they give you a clear picture of your progress with the Weekly Activity Summary.

This summary shows whether you’ve been consistent with your Move, Exercise, and Stand goals over the past week, helping you spot trends and stay motivated.

In this guide, I’ll walk you through what the Weekly Activity Summary is, how to view it on Apple Watch and iPhone, and tips to make the most of it.

Table of Contents
  • What is the Weekly Activity Summary?
  • How to View Weekly Activity Summary on Apple Watch
  • How to View Weekly Activity Summary on iPhone
  • Difference Between Weekly Summary on Apple Watch vs iPhone
  • How to Share Weekly Activity Summary with Friends
  • Tips to Make the Most of Weekly Activity Summary
  • Troubleshooting if Weekly Summary Doesn't Show
  • Stay Consistent with Your Goals

What is the Weekly Activity Summary?

The Weekly Activity Summary is a detailed 7-day report that highlights your fitness activity and goals. Think of it as your progress report for the week; it tells you if you’re smashing your goals or if you need to adjust your daily routine.

It includes:

  • Move Goal progress: Calories burned through activity.
  • Exercise Goal progress: Total minutes spent exercising.
  • Stand Goal progress: Hours you stood and moved around.
  • Daily averages: A snapshot of average activity per day.
  • Trends & achievements: Insights on where you’re improving or falling behind.

How to View Weekly Activity Summary on Apple Watch

One thing to note: your Apple Watch doesn’t permanently store old summaries. After Monday, the current week replaces the previous one. So, if you want to check last week’s data, you need to view it before the new week begins.

Here’s how to see your weekly activity on Apple Watch:

  1. Open the Fitness app, and your Activity Rings for today will appear.
  2. To view your weekly activity summary, tap the Graph icon at the top left corner.
  3. Here, you can review your Move, Exercise, and Stand averages for the past week and whether you managed to beat your week’s daily goal.

Moreover, if you feel your goals are too easy or too hard, you can adjust your Move, Exercise, and Stand goals to better match your lifestyle.

Here’s how:

  1. Scroll down to the bottom of your weekly activity summary.
  2. Tap Change Goal.
  3. Set your Move, Exercise, and Stand goals.

How to View Weekly Activity Summary on iPhone

Your iPhone goes beyond weekly insights; it stores long-term summaries in the Health app. That means you can review your activity for weeks, months, or even years.

Here’s how:

  1. Open the Health app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap on Activity on the Summary tab.
  3. If the Activity tile isn’t available on the Summary tab, tap the Browse tab (iOS 18) or Magnifying Glass icon (iOS 26), then select Activity under Health Categories.
  4. By default, the Health app will show you the activity summary for the present day. You can tap the Week, Month, 6 Months, or Year tab to view and analyze the corresponding activity summary graph.

Tip: Make sure your Apple Watch and iPhone are synced for accurate results.

Difference Between Weekly Summary on Apple Watch vs iPhone

How to Share Weekly Activity Summary with Friends

Apple makes it fun to stay accountable. You can share your summary with friends and even compete in challenges. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Fitness app on the iPhone.
  2. Tap the Sharing tab at the bottom > Tap the Invite Friends button.
  3. Tap Invite a Friend.
  4. Enter your friend’s Apple ID or phone number, then tap Send.

Once they accept, they’ll see your activity and can challenge you to stay consistent.

Tips to Make the Most of Weekly Activity Summary

Here are a few simple ways to maximize your Weekly Activity Summary for better results:

  • Adjust goals regularly: As your fitness improves, increase your Move, Exercise, or Stand goals.
  • Track Trends: Use the Trends section in the Fitness app to spot long-term progress.
  • Pair with Apple Fitness+: Access guided workouts that integrate with your activity rings.
  • Stay positive: Treat weekly summaries as motivation, not pressure. Small improvements count.

Troubleshooting if Weekly Summary Doesn’t Show

Stay Consistent with Your Goals

That’s everything you need to know about checking your Weekly Activity Summary on Apple Watch and iPhone. By regularly reviewing your stats, adjusting goals, and sharing progress with friends, you’ll stay motivated and on track with your health journey.

acceptedAnswer.text: No, an Apple Pencil isn't necessary to use the Markup tool on an iPad. You can easily use your finger for editing with the Markup tool. That said, the Apple Pencil, or any other stylus for that matter, does offer a more precise markup experience.

mainEntity.name: What to do if the Markup tool isn't working on iPhone and iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the Markup tool isn't working, try restarting your iPhone or iPad, ensuring iOS or iPadOS is up to date, and checking that the app you're using supports Markup.

mainEntity.name: Is Markup available for third-party apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, no; Markup is currently limited to Apple's built-in apps. However, some third-party apps may offer their own built-in editing tools. For instance, both WhatsApp and Telegram offer native editing tools for their users.

mainEntity.name: What should you do if you don't see a Shared Album invite?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you're unable to use Shared Albums on your iPhone, make sure you've turned on the iCloud Photos feature in the Photos app settings.

mainEntity.name: Can you accept a Shared Album invite on multiple devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: You don't need to accept a Shared Album invite on multiple Apple devices signed in with the same Apple ID. If you've turned on iCloud Photos, you'll see the Shared Album on all your devices.

mainEntity.name: What happens if you accidentally decline a Shared Album invite?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll need to ask the sender to resend the Shared Album invite.

mainEntity.name: Can you share a Shared Album with people who don't use Apple devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can. All you need to do is head to the Shared Album in the Photos app > People tab and turn on Public Website. This will publish the content in the Shared Album to a public website that anyone with the website link can access.

keyPoints.title: What is the Weekly Activity Summary?
keyPoints.explanation: It is a detailed 7-day report that shows your progress on Move, Exercise, and Stand goals, helping you track weekly fitness trends and achievements.

keyPoints.title: Viewing the Weekly Activity Summary on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Access the summary by opening the Fitness app, tapping the Graph icon, and reviewing your weekly data, with options to adjust goals for better alignment to your lifestyle.

keyPoints.title: Viewing the Weekly Activity Summary on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Use the Health app to see long-term summaries, with options to view daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly activity data and ensure your devices are synced for accuracy.

keyPoints.title: Difference Between Weekly Summary on Apple Watch and iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Apple Watch offers quick, real-time glanceable data perfect for daily motivation, while iPhone provides detailed graphs and long-term history for in-depth analysis.

keyPoints.title: Sharing Your Weekly Activity Summary with Friends
keyPoints.explanation: You can share your activity data via the Fitness app and invite friends to view or compete, helping you stay accountable and motivated.

title.rendered: How To Rotate The Screen on an iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Turn off Portrait Lock in Control Center by swiping from the corner and tapping the circular arrow—this enables automatic screen rotation across supported apps.
  • AssistiveTouch gives quick rotation access, letting you assign custom gestures to toggle screen orientation under Settings > Accessibility > Touch.
  • Not all apps support landscape mode—Safari, YouTube, and games do, but apps like Twitter, Settings, and the Home Screen stay portrait-only.
  • If rotation isn’t working, restart your iPhone or force-quit the app—hardware issues or locked sensors may require Apple Support.
  • Rotation enhances videos and games, and both Control Center and AssistiveTouch make it easy to toggle on the fly.

It’s convenient to hold your iPhone vertically, i.e., in portrait mode, for activities like calling, chatting on WhatsApp, and scrolling through a webpage. However, when watching videos on YouTube or Netflix, viewing PDFs, and gaming, rotating the screen to landscape mode offers a better experience.

Thankfully, the screen on your iPhone can rotate as you want—to landscape and back to portrait. In this guide, we’ll show you how to rotate the screen on your iPhone and other important details that may be helpful to you.

Table of Contents
  • How to rotate the screen on an iPhone
    • Enable screen rotation from the Control Center
    • Turn on iPhone screen rotation using Assistive Touch
  • What to do if screen rotation isn't working on my iPhone
    • 1. Force Quit the app
    • 2. Restart your iPhone
    • 3. Contact Apple Support

How to rotate the screen on an iPhone

It’s easy to rotate the screen on your iPhone. All you need to do is tilt the phone to rotate the screen to your desired orientation.

However, if this doesn’t work, you should disable the Portrait Orientation Lock. Below, we explain two ways to enable screen rotation on an iPhone.

Enable screen rotation from the Control Center

The Control Center allows you to enable screen rotation on your iPhone. This is done by disabling the Portrait Orientation Lock. Here’s how:

  1. Swipe down from the top-right of the screen to bring up the Control Center. On iPhones with a Home button, you’ll have to swipe up from the bottom of the Home Screen.
  2. Find the icon with a circular arrow inscribed with a lock. If the icon is highlighted, it means Portrait Orientation Lock is enabled.
  3. Tap the icon, and you should see a message that reads, “Portrait Orientation Lock: Off.”

After this, your screen will auto-rotate wherever you change your iPhone’s orientation on supported apps.

If you want to disable auto-rotation at any point, simply tap the Portrait Orientation Lock again.

Turn on iPhone screen rotation using Assistive Touch

Another way to enable screen rotation on your iPhone is using Assistive Touch. Here’s what you need to do:

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Scroll down and select Accessibility.
  3. Select Touch, then tap AssistiveTouch.
  4. Next, toggle on AssistiveTouch.
  5. Select Double-Tap or any unused custom action you prefer under Custom Actions.
  6. On the resulting menu, select Lock Rotation, and you’re good to go.
Note
  • During my testing, I discovered that most iPhone apps like Safari, YouTube, Notes, and LinkedIn allowed landscape rotation.

Now, anytime you want to turn on your iPhone screen rotation, double tap the AssistiveTouch circle. If you’ve used another custom action, do the respective touch to enable/disable screen rotation.

Keep in mind that certain apps, such as Settings and Twitter, don’t support landscape mode, so you’ll have to use them in portrait mode itself. This also applies to the Home Screen for iPhones with Face ID.

What to do if screen rotation isn’t working on my iPhone

Although rare, it’s possible that screen rotation may sometimes not work on your iPhone, even on apps that support landscape orientation. This could be due to a glitch on your iPhone or the app you’re trying to rotate.

Here are some fixes you can try to fix it.

1. Force Quit the app

If you’re trying to rotate the screen in an app and it isn’t responding, the app itself might be glitchy. An easy way to fix this is to Force Quit the app. Then, relaunch it and try rotating the screen again.

You should ensure the app supports screen rotation and that you’ve disabled the Portrait Orientation Lock.

2. Restart your iPhone

Another fix I recommend if screen rotation isn’t working is to restart your iPhone. This gives your device a fresh start and helps resolve any glitches.

3. Contact Apple Support

Lastly, if none of the solutions work, you can contact Apple Support for further assistance.

Signing off…

You can easily rotate your iPhone screen as you want when you disable the Orientation Lock. While you can do this in two ways, the Control Center method is the most straightforward. The AssistiveTouch method is also easy once you’ve set it up.

Which method do you prefer? Let us know in the comment section below.

Read more:

  • How to reduce photo file size on your iPhone and iPad
  • Best hidden iPhone secret codes
  • How to view and manage notifications on an iPhone or iPad

@graph.name: How to Enable screen rotation from the Control Center
@graph.description: Easily enable screen rotation on your iPhone by turning off Portrait Orientation Lock from the Control Center.

step.name: Open the Control Center
step.text: Swipe down from the top-right of the screen on Face ID iPhones or swipe up from the bottom on Home button models.

itemListElement.text: If you have a Face ID iPhone, swipe down from the top-right corner.
On iPhones with a Home button, swipe up from the bottom edge of the screen.

step.name: Disable Portrait Orientation Lock
step.text: Look for the icon with a lock inside a circular arrow. If it's highlighted, tap it to turn off Portrait Orientation Lock.

itemListElement.text: Find the circular arrow icon with a lock inside it.
If the icon is highlighted, that means Portrait Orientation Lock is enabled.
Tap the icon to turn it off—you’ll see 'Portrait Orientation Lock: Off'.

@graph.name: How to Turn on iPhone screen rotation using Assistive Touch
@graph.description: Enable screen rotation on your iPhone using AssistiveTouch by customizing a gesture to toggle rotation lock.

step.name: Enable AssistiveTouch
step.text: Go to Accessibility settings on your iPhone, tap Touch, then AssistiveTouch, and toggle it on.

itemListElement.text: Open the Settings app.
Scroll down and select Accessibility.
Tap Touch, then tap AssistiveTouch.
Toggle on the AssistiveTouch switch.

step.name: Assign Lock Rotation to a gesture
step.text: Customize an AssistiveTouch gesture like Double-Tap to toggle screen rotation using Lock Rotation.

itemListElement.text: Under Custom Actions, tap Double-Tap or any unused action you prefer.
From the menu, choose Lock Rotation.
Now you can double-tap the AssistiveTouch button to toggle screen rotation.

keyPoints.title: How to Rotate Screen Using Control Center
keyPoints.explanation: Swipe down from the top right or up from the bottom on older iPhones, then tap the circular arrow icon to disable Portrait Orientation Lock and enable auto-rotation.

keyPoints.title: Enable Screen Rotation with AssistiveTouch
keyPoints.explanation: Activate AssistiveTouch through Settings > Accessibility > Touch, then customize a double-tap or other gesture to lock or unlock screen rotation for easy access.

keyPoints.title: Supported Apps and Limitations
keyPoints.explanation: Most apps like Safari and YouTube support landscape rotation, but some, like Settings and Twitter, only work in portrait mode, including the Home Screen.

keyPoints.title: Troubleshooting Screen Rotation Issues
keyPoints.explanation: If your screen isn't rotating, try force quitting the app, restarting your iPhone, or contacting Apple Support for assistance.

keyPoints.title: Additional Tips for Better Usage Experience
keyPoints.explanation: Disabling Orientation Lock gives you flexible screen rotation, which enhances activities like gaming and watching videos, while the Control Center and AssistiveTouch are quick fixes.

title.rendered: How to download Facebook videos on iPhone, iPad, and desktop

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Facebook doesn’t let you download videos directly on iPhone, but you can save them in-app for later viewing within the Facebook app only.
  • The iOS Shortcuts app supports video downloads, using tools like the Facebook Video Downloader shortcut to save public videos safely to your Photos.
  • Apps like FaceSave allow Facebook video downloads, but may include ads or raise privacy concerns—use with caution and check app permissions.
  • Only download videos you have rights to, and avoid sketchy sources or unauthorized sharing to stay clear of copyright or security issues.
  • Downloading on desktop is easier with browser tweaks—just switch the video URL to the mobile site and save directly through your browser.

Downloading Facebook videos on your iPhone for offline viewing can be tricky due to the social media platform’s built-in limitations. Facebook allows you to save a video to watch later, but there is no official way to download it to your device. However, I’ve found some solutions for you. In this guide, I’ll show you how to download Facebook videos to your iPhone, iPad, or desktop.

Table of Contents
  • Factors to consider before you download a Facebook video
  • How to download Facebook videos to your iPhone or iPad
    • 1. Download a Facebook video on an iPhone using an iOS shortcut
    • 2. Save a Facebook video on an iPhone using a third-party app
  • How to download Facebook videos on your Mac or desktop
  • How to save a video on Facebook to watch later
    • 1. Using the Facebook iOS app
    • 2. Using the Facebook website
  • Video: How to download Facebook videos on iPhone and Desktop

Factors to consider before you download a Facebook video

Before I explain how to download videos from Facebook to your iPhone camera roll, let me point out some important things you should keep in mind.

  1. Keep things legal: Before downloading a video, make sure that you have the necessary rights or permissions to download and use it. Remember that copyright infringement is unlawful, so exercise caution.
  2. Get permission: Before downloading Instagram Reels or Facebook video content, it’s a good idea to get permission from the video creators to avoid any copyright issues.
  3. Stay safe: Download videos only from trusted sources. Many online tools or apps that claim to help you download Facebook videos may contain malware or compromise your privacy.
  4. Check video quality: Remember that high-quality videos often have large file sizes, so it may take longer to download and consume more storage space on your device.
  5. Check video format: Some video formats might not work on your device. So check if the downloaded video format is compatible with your device.

How to download Facebook videos to your iPhone or iPad

Below are some handy ways to download videos from Facebook on your iPhone or iPad. However, as discussed above, remember to always respect the privacy and intellectual property rights of others when downloading and sharing videos.

1. Download a Facebook video on an iPhone using an iOS shortcut

One of the simplest and safest ways to download Facebook videos to your iPhone or iPad is by using the iOS Shortcuts app. There’s a shortcut called Facebook Video Downloader that makes this process a breeze. I prefer this method because you don’t need to install any third-party apps.

First, set up the shortcut on your iPhone or iPad using the following steps:

  1. Go to the Facebook Video Downloader shortcut page.
  2. Tap Get Shortcut, and it’ll redirect you to the Shortcuts app.
  3. Select the Add Shortcut button.
  4. Next, go to the App Store and search for the a-Shell mini app.
  5. Tap the Get button to download the app.

Once you’ve installed the shortcut and the required app, you can download a Facebook video using the shortcut like this:

  1. Access the Facebook video and tap the Share button under the post.
  2. Select Copy Link.

  3. Now, go to the Shortcuts app and tap the Facebook Video Downloader shortcut.
  4. Hit Allow to proceed.
  5. Next, select Always Allow.

  6. The shortcut will run and redirect you to the a-Shell mini app. Wait while the video is processed and finished downloading.

  7. Once done, you’ll get a popup asking for permission to save the item to the Photos app. Select Always Allow.
  8. Finally, you’ll see the Video Saved to Photos App message, indicating that the video has been downloaded. Tap OK to close it.

Note
  • I faced a-Shell errors when running the shortcut for the first time. If you face an error, too, open the a-Shell mini app and type pip install yt-dlp –upgrade. Then, once the command has completed running, type pip install –upgrade pip. Finally, force close the app and run the shortcut again.

2. Save a Facebook video on an iPhone using a third-party app

If you’re having trouble using the Shortcuts method explained above, using a third-party app can make things easier. Whether you want to download a video from X or Facebook, many third-party apps on the iPhone or iPad can help. I used the FaceSave app, as explained below.

  1. Install the FaceSave app from the App Store and launch it.
  2. Select Ask App Not to Track on the popup.
  3. Tap Login and enter your Facebook credentials to log in.

  4. Now, select the Paste button and hit Allow Paste on the prompt.
  5. Tap Find to fetch the video.

  6. It’ll now ask for Photos app permission. Tap Allow to grant it access.
  7. When the Share Sheet opens, scroll down and tap Save Video.

Your selected Facebook video should now be downloaded to your iPhone Photos app.

This method is really easy but on the downside, the app displays ads, which can be annoying. Also, be cautious of using third-party apps like these as they can misuse your Facebook account information.

The Shortcut method is, therefore, the safer option. Alternatively, as shown below, you can download Facebook videos to your computer.

How to download Facebook videos on your Mac or desktop

Downloading Facebook videos is much simpler on a Mac or other desktop computer than on your iPhone. Just follow the steps below.

  1. Open a browser such as Safari or Chrome and go to the Facebook video you want to download.
  2. Click the three-dots icon in the top-right corner of the post.
  3. Choose the Copy Link option from the popup menu.

  4. Now, click the + icon in the Safari menu bar to open a new tab.
  5. Paste the link in the address bar and hit Return/Enter.

  6. You’ll now see the video in the browser. Click the address bar and replace www with mbasic.
    If you don’t see www, click the address bar and put the cursor at the end of the URL before pressing Return/Enter.
  7. Again, press Return/Enter, and it’ll redirect you to the mobile version of Facebook.

  8. Now, if you’re using Safari, right-click on the video thumbnail and select Download Linked File. If you’re using another browser such as Chrome, first click the play button and when the video starts playing, right-click on it and select Save Video As.

That’s all! The Facebook video will be downloaded to your computer.

How to save a video on Facebook to watch later

Facebook lets you save videos to watch later like the bookmark function of a web browser. Using this feature is more convenient than downloading a video. Plus, this approach has the following benefits, too:

  • Saved videos are kept within the Facebook app. So, it doesn’t take up space on your device.
  • Saving videos to watch later does not infringe on any copyright laws and Facebook’s terms of service.
  • You can access your saved videos from any device by logging into your Facebook account. On the other hand, downloaded videos stay on the device you used to save them.

That said, you need to have an active internet connection to watch your saved videos on the Facebook app or website. Let’s see how to do this:

1. Using the Facebook iOS app

  1. Open the Facebook app and access the video you want to save.
  2. Tap the three-dots icon on the post.
  3. Select Save Video from the menu that appears.
  4. You may also create Collections to organize the saved videos better.

2. Using the Facebook website

  1. Visit the Facebook website using any browser.
  2. Navigate to the video you wish to save.
  3. Click the three-dots icon and select Save Video.
  4. Choose a Collection and click Done.

Video: How to download Facebook videos on iPhone and Desktop

Signing off

I hope this has helped you download Facebook videos to your iPhone, iPad, or computer. If you run into any problems, let me know in the comments below. I think the best option is always just to save the video to watch later using the default option provided by Facebook. It’s super easy and convenient!

FAQs

Are there risks associated with downloading Facebook videos using third-party services?

Yes, using third-party services can pose risks, such as malware or violating copyright laws. Always ensure you use reputable services and respect content ownership.

Can I download live Facebook videos to my iPhone?

Downloading live videos is more complex, as they’re not stored on Facebook after the live stream ends. However, if you have access to the video link while it’s live, you can save it as watch later. I attempted to download live videos using the third-party Facebook video downloaded app or websites. The video was downloaded in MPD format and didn’t open.

How to save Facebook videos to a gallery without any app on an iPhone?

The easiest way to download a Facebook video to your iPhone is using a Shortcut. Alternatively, you can use a third-party app like FaceSave.

  • How to find recently viewed ads on Facebook and Instagram

keyPoints.title: No Official Download Option for Facebook Videos on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Facebook allows you to save videos within the app for later viewing but does not provide an official way to download videos directly to your iPhone.

keyPoints.title: Using iOS Shortcuts to Download Facebook Videos
keyPoints.explanation: You can use the Facebook Video Downloader shortcut in the iOS Shortcuts app to download videos onto your iPhone or iPad, offering a safe and efficient method.

keyPoints.title: Third-Party Apps for Downloading Facebook Videos
keyPoints.explanation: Apps like FaceSave enable you to download Facebook videos directly to your device, but be cautious of privacy concerns and ads that may appear in these apps.

keyPoints.title: Legal and Safety Considerations
keyPoints.explanation: Always ensure you have permission to download videos, respect copyright laws, and download from trusted sources to avoid malware or privacy risks.

keyPoints.title: Downloading Facebook Videos on Desktop is Simpler
keyPoints.explanation: On a Mac or PC, you can copy the video link, modify the URL to the mobile version, and then download it directly through your browser.

Key Takeaways:

  • Apple planning TechWoven cases for iPhone 17: Apple is rumored to debut fabric-style TechWoven accessories with the iPhone 17, replacing its discontinued FineWoven cases.
  • Why TechWoven replaces FineWoven: Leaker Majin Bu claims FineWoven’s durability issues like scratches and stains pushed Apple to try TechWoven as a stronger, longer-lasting material.
  • Added hardware-friendly features: Rumored TechWoven cases may include aluminum buttons, MagSafe support, a lanyard slot, and a cutout for the iPhone 17’s new Camera Control button.
  • Design matches iPhone 17 lineup: Leaks suggest TechWoven will mirror iPhone 17 Pro’s wider horizontal camera layout and ship across all models in the iPhone 17 range.
  • Unverified leaks raise caution: Since the source remains uncertain, it’s possible these details are inaccurate, so don’t assume TechWoven cases are confirmed until official launch.

Apple appears to be preparing a new line of fabric-style accessories to debut alongside the iPhone 17 series in September, with fresh images suggesting a “TechWoven” case could replace last year’s short-lived FineWoven material.

Leaker claims TechWoven will replace FineWoven

The claim comes from Majin Bu, a leaker with a history of mixed reliability, who shared photos of what appear to be iPhone 17 cases in a new textured fabric finish. The cases shown come in several muted colors—black, blue, green, purple, and orange—and are said to introduce Apple’s next-generation fabric accessory branding: TechWoven.

According to the leak, this new design will fully replace the FineWoven cases that shipped with the iPhone 15 lineup but were discontinued ahead of the iPhone 16. That material was heavily criticized for being prone to wear, fraying, and picking up stains, even under light use. If the leak is accurate, TechWoven could be Apple’s answer to widespread complaints about FineWoven’s durability.

Improved materials, added functionality

Beyond the updated fabric, the cases are rumored to include several refinements. These reportedly include aluminum or metal buttons for a more premium feel, support for MagSafe accessories, a cutout near the bottom edge for attaching lanyards or straps, and—most notably—a dedicated Camera Control button. That last detail aligns with ongoing rumors that this year’s Pro models will feature a new hardware shutter button.

The leaked cases appear to match the rumored design of the iPhone 17 Pro, which is expected to feature a wider, horizontal camera layout. However, Majin Bu claims TechWoven cases will be available across the entire iPhone 17 lineup, not just the Pro tier.

Skepticism remains over legitimacy

As with any leak tied to Majin Bu, these images should be viewed with some skepticism. The leaker has been accurate on some accessory details in the past, but also has a track record of sharing renders or prototypes that don’t always match final products. Given the lack of corroborating sources, it’s unclear if these images reflect actual production cases or early-stage mockups.

Still, if Apple is planning to move forward with TechWoven, it would signal a second attempt at introducing fabric-style accessories after the FineWoven experiment largely fell flat. A more resilient material paired with hardware upgrades might be enough to win over some critics, but that depends heavily on how these cases perform in everyday use.

A second shot at fabric cases

If real, TechWoven represents a quiet course correction for Apple, which has faced criticism for prioritizing aesthetics over usability with past accessory choices. While the new cases could look familiar on the surface, durability and real-world practicality may be what define their success this time.

Would a more rugged, fabric-style case change your mind about Apple’s accessory lineup? Let us know in the comments below.

title.rendered: How to fix “Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” on a Mac

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • The “No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” error means macOS can’t copy or paste—usually due to clipboard or background process issues.
  • Common triggers include full storage, buggy apps, or faulty system services, like the pboard or WindowServer process getting stuck.
  • Try restarting your Mac first, which clears RAM and temporary glitches that might be blocking clipboard functions.
  • Use Activity Monitor or Terminal to restart the pboard process, which directly manages clipboard data and often restores copy-paste.
  • You can also restart the WindowServer process, but it logs you out—save everything first to avoid losing open work.

The copy-paste functions on a Mac allow you to reproduce text, images, and other data from one source to a destination. However, several Mac users complain about getting the “Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” error when using the copy/paste function.

If you, too, are getting the “Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” error when copy-pasting items on your Mac, here are some proven fixes you can try to resolve the problem on your Mac.

Table of Contents
  • What does "Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed" mean on a Mac?
  • Why is my Mac saying "Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed?"
  • 5 ways to fix "Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed" on a Mac
    • 1. Restart your Mac
    • 2. Quit the pboard process
    • 3. Restart the WindowServer process
    • 4. Remove third-party clipboard managers
    • 5. Update macOS

What does “Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” mean on a Mac?

When you see the “Sorry, No manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” error, it simply means the copy-paste functionality has stopped working on your Mac. In all likelihood, this is because there’s something wrong with macOS clipboard.

The clipboard is essential for the copy-paste functionality to work on your Mac. It temporarily stores the data—text, images, and more—after you use the copy function until you paste it. However, the copy-paste function relies on certain processes, which can sometimes falter and throw errors like “Sorry, No manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” on your Mac.

Why is my Mac saying “Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed?”

The “Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” error is due to an issue with the process that handles the copy-paste functions. Here are the common causes of this problem:

  • Your Mac’s storage is full.
  • Issues with macOS.
  • Malfunctioning clipboard.
  • Interference from third-party software affecting copy-paste functions on your Mac.
  • Restrictions on copying data from an app or page.

5 ways to fix “Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” on a Mac

Not being able to use the copy-paste function on your Mac can be quite frustrating, but it is entirely possible to fix it. Below are some proven solutions that have helped users fix the “Sorry No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” issue on their Macs.

1. Restart your Mac

It may sound cliché, but restarting your Mac can often resolve most issues, including the broken copy-paste functionality. This solution gives your Mac a fresh start by clearing the RAM and removing temporary files that could possibly be causing the clipboard problem. Here’s how to restart your Mac:

  1. Click on the Apple logo in the upper-left corner of the screen.
  2. Select Restart from the resulting menu.
  3. Finally, click Restart again, and your Mac should commence the restart process.

2. Quit the pboard process

The Pasteboard or pboard process manages your Mac’s copy-paste functions. If an issue with pboard causes the “Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” error, you may need to restart pboard to fix it.

To do this, you should force quit the pboard process using Activity Monitor or Terminal, and let it restart automatically. Here’s how to quit the pboard process:

Force Quit pboard from Activity Monitor:

  1. Click the Launchpad button in the Dock, click the Other folder, then choose Activity Monitor.
  2. In the Activity Monitor window, type pboard in the search bar.
  3. You will now see the pboard process for each logged-in user. Double-click the pboard process under your user account and select Quit.
  4. Click Force Quit to confirm force quitting the pboard process.

Force Quit pboard from Activity Terminal:

  1. Click the Launchpad icon in the Dock, go to Other, and open Terminal.
  2. Next, type sudo killall pboard in the Terminal window and press the Return key.
  3. When asked for your Mac password, enter it, and the pboard process should end.

The process restarts automatically on its own since it’s a system process.

3. Restart the WindowServer process

The WindowServer process manages the graphical user interface on your Mac—the visual elements on your screen, open windows, and others. You should restart the process and see if it helps fix the “Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” issue, as it could be a glitch or bug with it that’s causing your clipboard not to function.

Note Restarting the WindowServer will log you out of your Mac. But your open apps and windows are restored when you log back in.

Here’s how to restart the WindowServer process on a Mac:

  1. Open Activity Monitor on your Mac.
  2. Click the search bar in the Activity Monitor window and type WindowServer.
  3. You’ll now see the WindowServer process under the Process Name tab. Double-click it and select Quit.
  4. Finally, click Force Quit, and the process will close immediately.

4. Remove third-party clipboard managers

I find this solution very handy as it has helped many users. Third-party clipboard managers often interfere with your Mac’s native clipboard functions. If you’ve installed a third-party clipboard manager, try uninstalling it temporarily to see if it resolves your clipboard issue. You can uninstall apps on your Mac in three ways, depending on your preference.

5. Update macOS

Lastly, outdated macOS versions can be buggy and might cause clipboard malfunctions. Therefore, you should update your macOS to see if it resolves the issue. Here’s how:

  1. Click the Apple icon in the top-left corner of your Mac screen.
  2. Choose System Settings (or System Preferences for older macOS versions).
  3. Click General, then Software Update. For older versions, go directly to Software Update.
  4. Click Update Now or Upgrade Now and follow the on-screen prompts to complete the update.

Signing off…

The “Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed” issue indicates a problem with your Mac’s copy-paste and clipboard functions, including the Universal Clipboard. Various factors can cause this, and as you’ve seen in this guide, there are respective solutions for each.

We hope one of our solutions helped resolve the issue on your Mac. If it did, feel free to share your experience in the comments section below.

Read more:

  • How to copy Mac screenshot to clipboard
  • How to fix copy paste not working on Mac

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many fakes can connect via Bluetooth, but the pairing process is often clunky, and you won’t get Apple’s smooth animation or iOS features.

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. Real AirPods Pro integrates with Apple’s Find My network. If this feature is missing, it’s a strong sign of a fake.

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope. Fakes either don’t update at all or show fake firmware versions that don’t match Apple’s records.

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Some high-end fakes mimic the look and sound decently, but they still lack Apple’s polish, features, and reliability.

mainEntity.name: How can I avoid buying a fake pair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Buy from trusted sources like Apple, Best Buy, or Amazon’s official store. Avoid deals that seem too good to be true, and always check the serial number.

keyPoints.title: Understanding the Error
keyPoints.explanation: The 'Sorry, No Manipulations With Clipboard Allowed' error indicates a malfunction in the macOS clipboard system, stopping copy-paste functions from working.

keyPoints.title: Common Causes of Clipboard Issues
keyPoints.explanation: Problems like full storage, macOS issues, faulty clipboard processes, third-party interference, or app restrictions can cause this clipboard error.

keyPoints.title: Restart Your Mac
keyPoints.explanation: A simple restart can resolve temporary glitches affecting the clipboard by clearing RAM and temporary files, often fixing the issue.

keyPoints.title: Restart the pboard Process
keyPoints.explanation: Terminating and restarting the pboard process, which manages the clipboard, can resolve this error; it can be done via Activity Monitor or Terminal.

keyPoints.title: Restart the WindowServer Process
keyPoints.explanation: Restarting the WindowServer, which handles the graphical interface, can fix bugs affecting the clipboard, but it logs you out, so save your work first.

title.rendered: How to connect PS5 controller to iPhone for best gaming experience

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Pairing a PS5 controller boosts mobile gaming by adding physical controls for smoother play in compatible iPhone games with Game Mode support.
  • You can connect via Bluetooth or USB-C, depending on your setup—wireless is more flexible, while wired offers zero lag during gameplay.
  • To pair over Bluetooth, hold PS and Share buttons until the light flashes, then select ‘DualSense Wireless Controller’ in iPhone Bluetooth settings.
  • Works best with iPhones running iOS 14.5 or later, and battery life averages 11–12 hours when connected wirelessly.
  • iPads with iPadOS 14.5+ also support DualSense, and you can check controller compatibility inside most App Store games under their supported accessories list.

With more and more AAA gaming titles available on iPhones, gaming is much more accessible. However, the only thing that causes the roadblock for many gamers like me is getting used to playing games directly on a screen with no physical buttons. If that’s the case, you can easily use your PS5 Controller on your iPhone instead.

Keep reading to learn how to connect your PS5 controller to your iPhone and enhance your gaming experience to the pro level.

Table of Contents
  • How to connect a PS5 controller to an iPhone or iPad

How to connect a PS5 controller to an iPhone or iPad

While many console and PC games now have an iPhone port, those games are currently limited to the iPhone 15 Pro series and the latest iPad models. Connecting your PS5 controller to your iPhone is fairly easy, as you only need to use the Type C available in your iPhone’s box.

However, if a wired connection doesn’t suit your fancy, you can easily create a wireless connection between the two using Bluetooth. Here’s how:

  1. First, make sure your PS5 controller isn’t connected to your PS5 and is turned off.
  2. Now, Press and hold the Home (PS) and the Share buttons simultaneously until the Controller’s lightbar starts flashing.
  3. The flashing of the lightbar indicates your PS5 controller is now in pairing mode.
  4. Next, switch to your iPhone and head to the Bluetooth settings.
  5. Here, turn Bluetooth on if it isn’t already.
  6. Once done, your PS5 controller will appear as a “DualSense Wireless Controller” under the Other Devices section.
  7. Tap on it to connect the controller to your iPhone.
  8. Once the controller is connected to your iPhone, the lightbar will turn Orange or Amber.
Note
  • If the controller is connected but isn’t working, press the Home (PS) button once, and the controller will start working.

You can now use Sony’s PS5 controller to control your iPhone. Combined with the newly introduced Game Mode on iPhone, the PS5 controller can significantly improve your gaming experience and make you a pro in portable gaming. But to enjoy the best gaming experience possible, set up the PS5 controller in any game you plan to play.

Game mode on….

Now that you know how to use a PS5 controller with your iPhone, you can make the best out of AAA titles like Resident Evil Village, Assassins Creed Mirage, and more.

Which is your favorite gaming title on the App Store? Do share with us in the comments.

FAQs

Can PS5 controller connect to two devices?

Unfortunately, you can only connect the PS5 controller to one device at a time. You must create a fresh connection every time you wish to switch the device.

Is PS5 DualSense compatible with iPad?

All iPads running on the iPadOS 14.5 or later are compatible with the PS5 DualSense controller.

How long does the PS5 controller last on one charge when connected to an iPhone?

The battery life of the PS5 controller depends on how intense you are gaming on your iPhone. However, in my testing, I found the battery to last roughly 11 to 12 hours on a single charge.

@graph.description: Learn how to pair your PS5 DualSense controller with an iPhone or iPad for an enhanced gaming experience on iOS.

step.name: Put your PS5 controller in pairing mode
step.text: Make sure your PS5 controller is turned off and not connected to your console. Then press and hold the PS (Home) and Share buttons until the lightbar starts flashing.

itemListElement.text: Turn off your PS5 controller if it’s connected to the console.
Press and hold the PS (Home) and Share buttons at the same time.
Wait for the lightbar to start flashing to indicate pairing mode.

step.name: Connect the controller via Bluetooth on your iPhone or iPad
step.text: Go to the Bluetooth settings on your iPhone or iPad, enable Bluetooth if needed, and select 'DualSense Wireless Controller' from the list of available devices.

itemListElement.text: Open Settings on your iPhone or iPad and tap on Bluetooth.
Make sure Bluetooth is turned on.
Wait for 'DualSense Wireless Controller' to appear under Other Devices.
Tap on the controller name to connect it to your device.
Look for the lightbar on the controller turning orange or amber to confirm the connection.
