@graph.name: How to Clear Notifications on an iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Quickly tidy your Notification Center on iPhone or iPad, clear individual alerts or wipe everything at once so you can stay focused.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad with recent iOS or iPadOS

step.name: Open Notification Center
step.text: Swipe down from the top left of the screen to open Notification Center.

itemListElement.text: Place your finger near the top left edge.
Swipe downward to reveal recent notifications.

step.name: Clear a single notification
step.text: Swipe left on a notification, then tap Clear to remove just that alert.

itemListElement.text: Find the notification you want to dismiss.
Swipe left on it and tap Clear.

step.name: Clear all notifications
step.text: Remove everything at once by tapping the X button, then choose Clear.

itemListElement.text: Tap the X in the upper corner of Notification Center.
Select Clear to delete all notifications.

@graph.name: How to Change the Default Notification Style on an iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Choose between List, Stack, or Count to customize how notifications appear on your iPhone or iPad, so you can view alerts the way that suits you best.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad running iOS or iPadOS

step.name: Open Settings
step.text: Unlock your iPhone or iPad and open the Settings app from your home screen.

itemListElement.text: Locate the gray gear-shaped Settings icon.
Tap it to open Settings.

step.name: Go to Notifications
step.text: Scroll down and tap Notifications to view all related settings.

itemListElement.text: Scroll through the Settings menu until you see Notifications.
Tap Notifications to open it.

step.name: Select Display As style
step.text: Choose how notifications appear by selecting List, Stack, or Count under the Display As section.

itemListElement.text: Tap List to see notifications in a scrollable list view.
Tap Stack to group them with the latest one on top.
Tap Count to only show the number of notifications.

@graph.name: How to Change the Notification Sound on an iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Customize the alert tone for texts, voicemail, or mail on your iPhone or iPad so new notifications sound exactly the way you want.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad signed in and unlocked

step.name: Open Sounds & Haptics
step.text: Open the Settings app, then tap Sounds & Haptics to view system alert options.

itemListElement.text: Launch Settings from the Home Screen or App Library.
Tap Sounds & Haptics.

step.name: Review available alert types
step.text: Scroll through the list to see the system wide notification sounds you can customize.

itemListElement.text: Look for options like Text Tone, New Voicemail, and New Mail.

step.name: Pick a category
step.text: Select Text Tone, New Voicemail, or New Mail to change that alert’s sound.

itemListElement.text: Tap the alert type you want to customize.

step.name: Choose and confirm your tone
step.text: Tap a sound to preview it, then leave the screen to save your choice automatically.

itemListElement.text: Tap different tones to hear previews.
Exit back to Sounds & Haptics to keep the selected tone.

@graph.name: How to Turn On or Off Notifications on an iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Quickly enable or disable app notifications on your iPhone or iPad so you only get alerts that matter.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad running iOS or iPadOS

step.name: Open Notifications settings
step.text: Open the Settings app, then tap Notifications to see your notification controls.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Settings app from your Home Screen or App Library.
Tap Notifications to open the notification menu.

step.name: Choose the app
step.text: Under the Notification Style section, select the app you want to manage.

itemListElement.text: Scroll through the list to find the app.
Tap the app name to open its notification options.

step.name: Turn notifications on or off
step.text: Use the Allow Notifications toggle to enable or disable alerts for that app.

itemListElement.text: Turn on Allow Notifications if you want to receive alerts.
Turn off Allow Notifications if you do not want any alerts from this app.

@graph.name: How to Customize a Specific App’s Notifications on an iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Fine‑tune how a single app alerts you on iPhone or iPad. Choose delivery timing, banner style, sounds, badges, Siri announcements, previews, and grouping so notifications work the way you like.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad with iOS or iPadOS

step.name: Open the app’s notification settings
step.text: Open Settings, tap Notifications, then choose the app you want to customize.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Settings app.
Tap Notifications.
Select the app under Notification Style.

step.name: Choose delivery timing
step.text: Pick whether the app’s alerts arrive right away or get included in your Scheduled Summary.

itemListElement.text: Select Immediately to deliver alerts as they happen.
Select Scheduled Summary to bundle them for later.

step.name: Enable Time Sensitive notifications
step.text: Allow critical alerts to break through Focus and stay on your Lock Screen for an hour when needed.

itemListElement.text: Toggle on Time Sensitive Notifications.
Leave it off if you prefer standard delivery rules.

step.name: Set your banner style
step.text: Pick how long banners stay visible at the top of the screen.

itemListElement.text: Tap Banner Style.
Choose Temporary or Persistent.

step.name: Choose a custom sound
step.text: Assign a unique tone so you can identify this app’s alerts by ear.

itemListElement.text: Tap Sounds.
Select your preferred alert tone.

step.name: Turn badges on or off
step.text: Decide whether a red badge appears on the app icon for new alerts.

itemListElement.text: Toggle Badges on to show unread counts.
Toggle Badges off to hide them.

step.name: Let Siri announce notifications
step.text: Have Siri read notifications through your headphones to minimize distractions.

itemListElement.text: Tap Announce Notifications.
Toggle Announce Notifications on.
Select Time Sensitive Notifications if you only want critical alerts announced.

step.name: Choose Lock Screen previews
step.text: Control when message previews appear on the Lock Screen for this app.

itemListElement.text: Tap Show Previews.
Pick Always, When Unlocked, or Never.

step.name: Set notification grouping
step.text: Organize multiple alerts from the app into a tidy stack or show them individually.

itemListElement.text: Tap Notification Grouping.
Choose Automatic, By App, or Off.

@graph.name: How to Change Notification Previews on an iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Control when notification previews appear on your iPhone or iPad, so you can keep alerts private or see them at a glance.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad with iOS or iPadOS

step.name: Open Notifications settings
step.text: Open the Settings app, then tap Notifications to access alert options.

itemListElement.text: Launch Settings from your Home Screen or App Library.
Tap Notifications to open the notification menu.

step.name: Open Show Previews
step.text: Tap Show Previews to choose when message content appears in notifications.

itemListElement.text: Find the Show Previews option near the top of the screen.
Tap Show Previews to view the available choices.

step.name: Choose your preview style
step.text: Pick when previews appear based on your privacy needs.

itemListElement.text: Select Always to show previews whether the device is locked or unlocked.
Select When Unlocked to only show previews after you unlock the device.
Select Never to hide previews entirely.

@graph.name: How to Enable or Disable Notifications While Screen Sharing on an iPhone
@graph.description: Decide whether notifications are visible to others during screen sharing on your iPhone so you can keep alerts private or let them show.

step.name: Open Notifications settings
step.text: Open the Settings app, then tap Notifications to view alert options.

itemListElement.text: Launch Settings from the Home Screen or App Library.
Tap Notifications.

step.name: Open Screen Sharing
step.text: Tap Screen Sharing to control what shows while you share your screen.

itemListElement.text: Find Screen Sharing in the list.
Tap to open Screen Sharing settings.

step.name: Allow or hide notifications
step.text: Use the Allow Sharing toggle to decide if notifications appear to others during screen sharing.

itemListElement.text: Turn on Allow Sharing to let others see your notifications.
Turn off Allow Sharing to keep notifications hidden.

@graph.name: How to Set a Scheduled Summary of Notifications on an iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Bundle less urgent alerts into a tidy summary on your iPhone or iPad, choose the delivery times, and pick which apps are included so you are not interrupted all day.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad running iOS or iPadOS

step.name: Open Settings
step.text: Unlock your device and open the Settings app to begin.

itemListElement.text: Locate the gray gear shaped Settings icon.
Tap it to open Settings.

step.name: Open Scheduled Summary
step.text: Go to Notifications, then tap Scheduled Summary to manage your summary schedule.

itemListElement.text: Tap Notifications in the main Settings list.
Tap Scheduled Summary to open its options.

step.name: Add a new summary time
step.text: Create a schedule for when your summary should arrive.

itemListElement.text: Tap Add Summary to create a new delivery time.
Adjust the hours and minutes to your preference.

step.name: Delete a summary time
step.text: Remove a schedule you no longer need in a couple of taps.

itemListElement.text: Tap the minus button next to the schedule.
Tap Delete when the option appears.

step.name: Choose which apps are included
step.text: Pick the apps whose notifications should be bundled into your summary.

itemListElement.text: Scroll to the list of apps in Scheduled Summary.
Toggle on the apps you want to include.

@graph.name: How to Silence Notifications on an iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Quickly mute incoming alerts on your iPhone or iPad using Do Not Disturb, so you can focus without interruptions.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad with iOS or iPadOS

step.name: Open Control Center
step.text: Swipe down from the top right corner of the screen to reveal Control Center.

itemListElement.text: Place your finger near the top right edge of the display.
Swipe downward to open Control Center.

step.name: Open Focus
step.text: Press and hold the Focus tile to expand its options.

itemListElement.text: Find the crescent moon Focus tile.
Long press the tile to see available Focus modes.

step.name: Turn on Do Not Disturb
step.text: Tap Do Not Disturb to silence notifications immediately.

itemListElement.text: Tap Do Not Disturb to enable it.
Look for the moon icon in the status bar to confirm it is on.

@graph.name: How to Turn Government Alerts On or Off on an iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Control emergency and test alerts on your iPhone or iPad, including whether they are read aloud in Silent mode, so you only get the warnings you want.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad with iOS or iPadOS

step.name: Open Notifications settings
step.text: Open Settings on your device, then tap Notifications and scroll to the bottom of the page.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Settings app from your Home Screen or App Library.
Tap Notifications and swipe down to the Government Alerts section.

step.name: Toggle Test Alerts
step.text: Turn Test Alerts on or off to control whether you receive periodic test messages from your government.

itemListElement.text: Use the Test Alerts switch to enable or disable test notifications.

step.name: Control spoken alerts
step.text: Choose whether these alerts are read aloud even when your iPhone is in Silent mode.

itemListElement.text: Toggle Always Read Out on to have government alerts spoken.
Toggle Always Read Out off to keep them silent.

keyPoints.title: Viewing Notifications on Your iPhone or iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Notifications arrive in real-time unless Do Not Disturb or Focus mode is active; they can be viewed in Notification Center or on the Lock Screen.

keyPoints.title: Clearing Notifications
keyPoints.explanation: Swipe up on a notification to clear it or open Notification Center to remove all notifications by tapping the X button and selecting 'Clear'.

keyPoints.title: Changing Default Notification Style
keyPoints.explanation: Customize how notifications appear—List, Stack, or Count—through Settings > Notifications to suit your preferences.

keyPoints.title: Modifying Notification Sounds
keyPoints.explanation: Go to Settings > Sounds & Haptics to select new notification sounds for texts, voicemails, or emails.

keyPoints.title: Managing Notification Settings Per App
keyPoints.explanation: In Settings > Notifications, you can turn notifications on/off for individual apps or customize their delivery, alerts, sounds, and grouping.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Everything You Need to Know About Apple Card Family

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What is Apple Card Family?: Apple Card Family, launched in 2021, lets you share one credit card account with up to five family members through the Wallet app.
  • Core Features: It provides shared credit lines, credit building, spending limits for kids, rewards pooling, and privacy controls, all managed directly in Apple Wallet.
  • Eligibility Rules: You need an Apple Card, a US-based Apple ID, and a compatible device, while co-owners must be 18 and participants at least 13.
  • Setup Process: You can add co-owners or participants in the Wallet app, send invitations, and complete credit checks before access is granted.
  • Pros and Cautions: Apple Card Family supports joint credit growth and rewards sharing, but shared debt responsibility, limited availability, and lack of travel perks remain concerns.

Managing money as a family is complicated, from tracking your spending to creating joint credit or establishing limits for children. Apple makes this simpler with Apple Card Family, a feature that enables you to share an Apple Card with the people you care about without giving up control of how it’s used.  

In this guide, we’ll break down everything you need to know about Apple Card Family from how to set it up to how to share it with a co-owner. So, you can decide if it’s the right fit for your family. 

Table of Contents
  • What is Apple Card Family?
  • Key Features of Apple Card Family
  • Eligibility Requirements
  • How to Set Up Apple Card Family
    • To Add a Co-Owner
    • Add a Participant
    • Accepting an Apple Card Family Invite
  • Advantages of Apple Card Family
  • Drawbacks & Limitations
  • Apple Card Family vs Other Shared Credit Options
  • Tips for Managing Apple Card Family Effectively
  • Manage Your Household Spending Wisely!

What is Apple Card Family? 

Apple Card Family launched in 2021 to let users share their Apple Card account with up to five other people in their Family Sharing group.  

One person is the account holder, another may be a joint holder with equal responsibility, and the remaining members are users who can spend but are not responsible for making payments. It’s all controlled from the Wallet app on your iPhone or iPad, making one credit card a household resource. 

So, what’s the Apple Card Family’s unique feature from the standard Apple Card? 

  • With an individual Apple Card, it’s just your spending, your bills, and your rewards. 
  • With Apple Card Family, you can share the credit line, set spending limits for others, and even build credit together if you’re a co-owner. Everyone earns their own Daily Cash back on purchases. 

Compared to typical authorized user setups on other cards, it emphasizes equal credit building and family controls. It works seamlessly with the Wallet app on iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, with real-time updates and notifications. 

Key Features of Apple Card Family 

Apple Card Family packs in tools to make shared credit safe and rewarding. Here’s a breakdown: 

  • Shared Credit Line: The account owner and co-owner share one credit line. Other participants in the Family Sharing group can use it. You can even merge existing Apple Cards and request to increase credit limit. 
  • Co-owner Transparency: You can also share the responsibility of making payments and check details of each other’s spending from a single monthly bill. 
  • Parental Controls & Spending Limits: Add anyone who is 13 years or older as a participant to allow them independent spending. You get their transaction insights, set optional transaction limits, lock their ability to spend, and receive notifications about their purchases.  
  • Credit Reporting for Participants Over 18: Co-owners always build credit equally, with all activity reported to credit bureaus in their names. Adult participants can opt in to be reported as authorized users, helping them build credit history even if they’re not responsible for payments. 
  • Daily Cash Rewards Shared: Everyone earns unlimited Daily Cash back on their own purchases up to 3% at Apple and select partners, 2% with Apple Pay, and 1% elsewhere. It goes directly to each person’s Apple Cash account, so rewards stay personal. 
  • Privacy and Security Features: Each person can see only their own transactions in the Wallet app, ensuring privacy. It uses Apple’s top-notch security, like device-based authentication and no card numbers on the physical titanium card. Plus, all family members get their own card (digital immediately, physical for 18+) 

These are the reasons why it is a favorite among families, with emphasis on control, rewards, and credit building. 

Eligibility Requirements 

You must satisfy some minimal requirements to become a part of Apple Card Family: 

  • The owner of the account must already have an Apple Card and be part of a Family Sharing group with other members you wish to share your card with.  
  • You need an iPhone or iPad with the latest iOS or iPadOS or a compatible Apple Watch with the latest watchOS. 
  • Everyone must have an Apple ID with region set to the US, as Apple Card is only available there. 
  • Participants must be at least 13 years old. Co-owners must be 18 or older, and participants wanting to build credit must also be 18+. 

If you’re adding a co-owner, both of you have to agree to merge your separate cards or qualify credit-wise as a new user. 

How to Set Up Apple Card Family

Setting up is easy and done directly in the Wallet app. Here’s how:  

To Add a Co-Owner

  1. On your iPhone, launch Wallet and tap your Apple Card. Tap the More button (three dots), then select Account Details.

    For iPad, go to Settings > Wallet & Apple Pay > Apple Card > Info tab.
  2. Scroll to Apple Card Family and tap Add User. (On older iOS versions, tap Share My Card under the People section)
  3. Then select Continue to proceed.
  4. Pick a participant from your Family Sharing group. If they’re not in it, tap Invite Someone to add them first. Note: only one co-owner allowed.
  5. Tap Become Co-Owners.
  6. Follow the prompts to enter details like their total annual income or Social Security number for credit checks.
  7. Tap Send Invitation and authenticate with your passcode or Face ID.

Add a Participant

  1. From the Wallet app, go to your Apple Card, tap More button, and select Account Details.
  2. Now, tap Share My Card > Continue.
  3. Select a family member and tap Add as Participant.
  4. Enter an amount to set a credit limit for them.
  5. Tap Next at the top right corner to proceed.
  6. Finally, tap Send Invitation.

Accepting an Apple Card Family Invite

  1. Once the owner successfully sets up Apple Card Family, you’ll get a notification. Tap it, or open Wallet and tap the badge in the corner. 
  2. Tap Continue, then select Accept Apple Card (for participants).

    If you’re a co-owner, enter your details and complete the application. Once Apple approves your card, tap Accept Shared Card. The owner also needs to accept the shared card to start spending.
  3. Adult participants can choose to build credit during acceptance or later in Account Details > Build Credit History. 

After you share your Apple Card with family, all can begin using the card digitally immediately. Physical titanium cards are mailed to 18+; owners can request them for participants under 18. 

Advantages of Apple Card Family 

Apple Card Family is more than just sharing a credit card: it’s about making money management simpler and smarter for everyone in your home. Here are some of the biggest perks: 

  • For couples, co-owners can merge credit lines and build credit together, sharing responsibility without separate bills. Families can set limits for teens to learn budgeting while earning Daily Cash on their buys. 
  • Everyone builds better habits: positive payments boost credit scores for co-owners and opting-in participants.  
  • Rewards add up fast, with no annual fees, and privacy keeps things fair.  

It’s all in one app, with real-time tracking, making it easier than juggling multiple cards. Plus, it’s a great way to teach financial literacy to kids starting at 13. 

Drawbacks & Limitations 

While handy, Apple Card Family isn’t perfect. Here are a few things to keep in mind before you jump in: 

  • The biggest issue is shared responsibility. Late payments or high balances hurt everyone’s credit, especially co-owners who are equally liable. Participants’ credit can suffer too if they opt in. 
  • It’s limited to the US and requires Apple devices, so Android users or international families are out.  
  • Daily Cash goes to each person’s Apple Cash account if set up, which might not suit families wanting pooled rewards.  
  • Adding a co-owner means a credit check, and you can’t easily switch back without closing the account. 
  • There’s no sign-up bonus like some cards, and if the Goldman Sachs partnership ends (rumored by 2030), changes could come.  
  • You won’t find extras like airline miles or travel points that some traditional credit cards offer. 
  • Also, under-18s can’t build credit, and maxing out limits affects scores. 

So, while Apple Card Family is great for Apple users who want simple money sharing, it might not be the best fit if you’re after more advanced rewards or if not everyone in your family uses Apple devices. 

Apple Card Family vs Other Shared Credit Options 

Apple Card Family isn’t the only way to share a credit account. Banks have been offering joint credit cards and authorized user options for years. But Apple puts its own spin on things. Let’s break it down: 

  • Vs. Traditional Authorized Users (e.g., Chase Sapphire Preferred or Amex Gold): These let you add users, but only the primary cardholder builds credit, authorized users often don’t, or it’s limited. Apple allows opting in for participants 18+, and co-owners build equally. Controls are basic on others; Apple’s app makes limits and notifications easier. 
  • Vs. Joint Accounts (e.g., Capital One Duo or Discover Cards): Joint accounts share responsibility like Apple’s co-owner, but they’re rarer and don’t offer family-style participants or kid controls. Apple integrates with your phone for better finance tracking. 
  • Vs. Other Family Cards (e.g., Amazon Prime Rewards Visa): These might share rewards but lack Apple’s privacy, credit equality, or seamless setup. Apple wins on no fees and Daily Cash, but others could have better travel perks. 

Overall, if you’re in the Apple world and want credit building for all, it’s top-notch. You don’t need to pay any annual fees, late fees, or foreign transaction fees. However, for broader rewards, look elsewhere. 

Tips for Managing Apple Card Family Effectively 

Sharing a credit card with family or friends can be super convenient but it also needs a little teamwork to keep things running smoothly. Here are some simple tips to make the most of Apple Card Family: 

  • Set Clear Limits Early: Use the Wallet app to set limits for kids or younger users. It keeps surprises off your bill and helps them learn good habits. 
  • Talk about Money Openly: Chat with others about budgets and spending to prevent misunderstandings later. 
  • Monitor Spending: Keep an eye on transactions, Daily Cash rewards, and spending summaries. The Wallet app shows all in real time. 
  • Opt In for Credit Wisely: For 18+ participants, enable credit reporting if the account is in good shape and not overly utilized. 
  • Handle Rewards Smartly: Since Daily Cash is personal, teach users to save or transfer it via Apple Cash. 
  • Pay on Time, Every Time: Since co-owners share credit responsibility, make sure payments are never late. It helps protect everyone’s credit score. 
  • Review Who’s on the Account: Every once in a while, check if everyone still needs access. If not, you can easily remove the participants. 

These keep things smooth and educational. 

Manage Your Household Spending Wisely! 

Apple Card Family makes it easier to share a credit card, manage spending, and even build credit together, all within the Apple ecosystem you already use. It’s great for families or couples who want transparency, control, and rewards without the hassle of extra fees.  

So, if you have an Apple Card, try sharing it with your family members and see how it streamlines your household spending! Along with these, try other Family Sharing features such as sharing apps and subscription purchases to save money.

FAQs

Can I remove a family member from Apple Card Family? 

Yes, account owners or co-owners can remove participants via the Wallet app: Go to Account Details, select the person, and tap Stop Sharing. Participants can self-remove too. For co-owners, you must close the entire account. After removal, they can’t spend, but you’re still responsible for any balance. 

Does Apple Card Family affect my credit score? 

Yes, it can. Positive habits like on-time payments boost scores for co-owners and opting in participants. But negatives, like late payments or high utilization, hurt everyone involved. 

Can kids under 18 join Apple Card Family? 

Yes, as participants starting at age 13. They can spend within limits and earn Daily Cash, but they can’t build credit history until 18. 

How many people can be added? 

You can add up to five people: one co-owner and four participants, for a total of six including the owner. 

Is Apple Card Family free to use? 

Yes, there’s no extra fee for Apple Card Family. It’s part of the no-annual-fee Apple Card. You just pay interest on balances like any credit card.

mainEntity.name: Can I remove a family member from Apple Card Family?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, account owners or co-owners can remove participants via the Wallet app: Go to Account Details, select the person, and tap Stop Sharing. Participants can self-remove too. For co-owners, you must close the entire account. After removal, they can't spend, but you're still responsible for any balance.

mainEntity.name: Does Apple Card Family affect my credit score?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it can. Positive habits like on-time payments boost scores for co-owners and opting in participants. But negatives, like late payments or high utilization, hurt everyone involved.

mainEntity.name: Can kids under 18 join Apple Card Family?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, as participants starting at age 13. They can spend within limits and earn Daily Cash, but they can't build credit history until 18.

mainEntity.name: How many people can be added?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can add up to five people: one co-owner and four participants, for a total of six including the owner.

mainEntity.name: Is Apple Card Family free to use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, there's no extra fee for Apple Card Family. It's part of the no-annual-fee Apple Card. You just pay interest on balances like any credit card.

keyPoints.title: What is Apple Card Family?
keyPoints.explanation: Apple Card Family, launched in 2021, allows users to share their Apple Card with up to five family members, sharing a credit line and building credit together.

keyPoints.title: Key Features of Apple Card Family
keyPoints.explanation: This service offers shared credit lines, parental controls, credit reporting, rewards sharing, and privacy features, all managed via the Wallet app.

keyPoints.title: Eligibility Requirements
keyPoints.explanation: To join, you need an existing Apple Card, a compatible Apple device, an Apple ID in the US, and participants must be at least 13 years old.

keyPoints.title: How to Set Up Apple Card Family
keyPoints.explanation: Setup involves using the Wallet app to add co-owners or participants, sending invitations, and entering necessary details for credit checks.

keyPoints.title: Advantages and Limitations
keyPoints.explanation: It simplifies family money management, boosts credit, and offers rewards with privacy, but has shared responsibility risks, limited to US users, and no additional travel perks.

title.rendered: How to Cancel Subscriptions on  iPhone, Mac or Apple Watch

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • You can only cancel App Store-linked subscriptions from your Apple ID—others like Netflix or Spotify need to be canceled on their own platforms.
  • On iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Subscriptions to view, manage, or cancel any active plans billed through Apple directly on your device.
  • Mac users can cancel in System Settings or App Store under Media & Purchases, with small UI differences depending on where you start.
  • Apple Watch also lets you cancel subscriptions—just open the App Store app, tap Account, then Subscriptions, and cancel from there.
  • To track unknown charges, search Apple invoices or bank records—then cancel via Apple or the original platform, depending on where it was billed.

Whether you want to cut down on your expenses or the subscription benefits no longer excite you, knowing how to manage or cancel an app subscription is essential. While it is hard to keep track of all your active subscriptions, Apple has made this complex task relatively straightforward on all its devices. In this article, I will show you multiple ways to cancel subscriptions on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch.

Table of Contents
  • Which subscriptions can you cancel?
  • How to cancel subscriptions on your iPhone or iPad
    • Via Settings
    • Via App Store
  • How to cancel subscriptions on your Mac
    • Via Settings
    • Via App Store
  • How to cancel subscriptions on your Apple Watch
  • How to cancel a subscription on an iPhone if you can't find it
  • How to reactivate a canceled subscription on your iPhone

Which subscriptions can you cancel?

Before you cancel or manage subscriptions on your iPhone, you’ll want to know which subscriptions you can cancel directly from your iPhone.

Simply put, you can cancel all those subscriptions directly from your iPhone that are connected to your Apple ID and were set up through the App Store. If you have subscriptions that are not connected to your Apple ID, such as a Netflix subscription, you can cancel them through the company’s app or website or by contacting customer support.

How to cancel subscriptions on your iPhone or iPad

Remembering all your active subscriptions can be a task. Thankfully, Apple offers a complete list of all the apps with active subscriptions in a single place on your iPhone, making managing and canceling them easier. Below, we check out two ways to cancel a subscription on an iPhone.

Via Settings

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap on your name and photo at the top.
  3. On your account page, tap on the Subscriptions tab. This will open a list of all the active and inactive subscriptions you have.

  4. Next, tap on an active subscription under Active that you want to cancel.
  5. Tap on Cancel Subscription on the subsequent page.
  6. Finally, tap the Confirm button on the confirmation prompt that appears to confirm canceling the subscription.

Via App Store

  1. Open the App Store on your iPhone.
  2. Tap your profile icon in the top-right corner.
  3. Here, tap on Subscriptions.

  4. Next, tap on the app subscription you want to cancel.
  5. Tap on Cancel Subscription, then tap the Confirm button on the confirmation prompt to confirm cancellation.

How to cancel subscriptions on your Mac

Like the iPhone and iPad, you can cancel an active subscription on a Mac via Settings and the App Store. However, the steps to do so differ greatly.

Via Settings

  1. Open the System Settings on your Mac.
  2. Click on your name and photo at the top in the left sidebar.
  3. On the account page, click on Media & Purchases.

  4. Next, click the Manage button next to Subscriptions.

  5. Now, click on the active subscription you want to cancel.

  6. Finally, click on Cancel Subscription, then the Confirm button to confirm your decision.

Via App Store

  1. Open the App Store on your Mac.
  2. Click on your profile icon in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click on Account Settings on the Account page and sign in with your Apple ID.

  4. Now, scroll down to the Manage section and click on Manage next to Subscriptions.

  5. Select the subscription you want to cancel.

  6. Click on Cancel Subscription, then the Confirm button to confirm canceling your subscription.

How to cancel subscriptions on your Apple Watch

Thanks to the Apple ecosystem, each subscription that can be canceled through your iPhone and Mac can also be canceled through the paired Apple Watch. Here’s how:

  1. Open the App Store on your Apple Watch.
  2. Scroll to the bottom and tap Account.
  3. Here, tap on Subscriptions, then select the subscription you want to cancel.

  4. Next, scroll to the bottom and tap the Cancel Subscription button.
  5. Tap the Confirm button to confirm your decision.

How to cancel a subscription on an iPhone if you can’t find it

There may be instances where you simply can’t find a subscription on your Apple device. It may be due to a different Apple ID being used for the subscription or because you bought it directly from the company’s website. Here’s what you can do in such cases:

  1. Open the Mail app on your iPhone.
  2. Enter the phrase receipt from Apple or invoice from Apple in the search bar at the top to find the subscription invoice emails.
  3. Open the subscription invoice and inspect which Apple ID is being used.

  4. If the Apple ID that appears differs from yours, but you have access to it, sign in with it on your iPhone and follow the steps we discussed in the previous section.
  5. If the Apple ID being used for the subscription is your friend’s or a family member’s, ask them to cancel the subscription on your behalf.
  6. If you can’t find the subscription email, you may have bought the subscription directly from the company, not through Apple. You can view your bank or credit card statement to know which company is billing you. Once done, you can cancel the subscription using the company’s app or contact customer support.

How to reactivate a canceled subscription on your iPhone

You can have many apps on your iPhone whose subscriptions are useful but only for a particular period. For example, the Splitwise app’s subscription is only useful to me when I am on a trip with my friends; after that, it is useless for the time being. That’s why I keep canceling and resubscribing to Splitwise often. Here’s how you, too, can do this:

  1. Head to the subscription list in the App Store or the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Here, tap the app under the Inactive subscription section to which you want to resubscribe.
  3. Next, tap the Renew button and confirm with your Face ID or Apple ID password.

  4. Alternatively, tap on See All Plans to subscribe to a different plan.

Signing off…

Now you know how easy it is to cancel a subscription on your iPhone. So, going forward, you can ensure you are only paying for the services you use regularly.

Please note that canceling the subscription will not immediately terminate the related services. You can still enjoy the subscription benefits until the end of the current billing period.

If you have any questions or run into any issues, comment below, and we’ll be happy to provide a resolution.

FAQs

How do I see what subscriptions I have on my iPhone?

Open the App Store and go to Account > Subscriptions, and you’ll see a list of all your iPhone subscriptions on your screen.

Why can’t I cancel a subscription on my iPhone?

Any subscription that isn’t connected to your Apple ID can not be canceled directly from the iPhone.

Why can’t I access my Apple subscriptions?

If you can’t access your Apple subscriptions, ensure you are signed in with the same Apple ID you used to buy the subscription and try again.

Read more:

  • How to stop “Verification Required” when installing app apps
  • How to change App Store country or region on iPhone, iPad, or Mac

excerpt.rendered: Only subscriptions billed through your Apple Account can be cancelled in Settings. Here is how to do that on every device, plus what to do about services like Netflix billed directly.

mainEntity.name: Can I remove a family member from Apple Card Family?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, account owners or co-owners can remove participants via the Wallet app: Go to Account Details, select the person, and tap Stop Sharing. Participants can self-remove too. For co-owners, you must close the entire account. After removal, they can't spend, but you're still responsible for any balance.

mainEntity.name: Does Apple Card Family affect my credit score?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it can. Positive habits like on-time payments boost scores for co-owners and opting in participants. But negatives, like late payments or high utilization, hurt everyone involved.

mainEntity.name: Can kids under 18 join Apple Card Family?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, as participants starting at age 13. They can spend within limits and earn Daily Cash, but they can't build credit history until 18.

mainEntity.name: How many people can be added?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can add up to five people: one co-owner and four participants, for a total of six including the owner.

mainEntity.name: Is Apple Card Family free to use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, there's no extra fee for Apple Card Family. It's part of the no-annual-fee Apple Card. You just pay interest on balances like any credit card.

@graph.name: How to cancel subscriptions on iPhone or iPad Via Settings
@graph.description: Quickly cancel an active App Store subscription from the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad so you stop future renewals.

supply.name: Apple ID signed in on the device

step.name: Open Settings
step.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone to manage your Apple ID subscriptions.

itemListElement.text: Unlock your iPhone or iPad.
Tap the Settings icon to open it.

step.name: Open your Apple ID
step.text: Tap your name and photo at the top of Settings to access account options.

itemListElement.text: Find your Apple ID banner at the top.
Tap it to open your account page.

step.name: Go to Subscriptions
step.text: Tap the Subscriptions tab to view all Active and Inactive subscriptions.

itemListElement.text: Tap Subscriptions on the Apple ID page.
Review the list under Active and Inactive headings.

step.name: Select the subscription to cancel
step.text: Under Active, tap the subscription you want to cancel to open its details.

itemListElement.text: Scroll if needed to find the service you want to cancel.
Tap the subscription to view its options.

step.name: Cancel the subscription
step.text: Tap Cancel Subscription on the subscription details page.

itemListElement.text: Locate the Cancel Subscription option.
Tap it to begin cancellation.

step.name: Confirm cancellation
step.text: Tap Confirm on the prompt to finalize canceling the subscription.

itemListElement.text: Read the confirmation message.
Tap Confirm to stop future renewals.

@graph.name: How to cancel subscriptions on your iPhone or iPad Via App Store
@graph.description: Cancel an active App Store subscription directly from the App Store app on your iPhone or iPad so future renewals stop.

supply.name: Apple ID signed in on the device

tool.name: iPhone or iPad with App Store app

step.name: Open your account in the App Store
step.text: Open the App Store, then tap your profile picture in the top right to access account options.

itemListElement.text: Launch the App Store on your iPhone or iPad.
Tap your profile icon in the top right corner.

step.name: Open Subscriptions
step.text: Tap Subscriptions to view your Active and Inactive subscriptions.

itemListElement.text: Tap Subscriptions from the account sheet.
Wait for the list to load.

step.name: Choose the subscription to cancel
step.text: Tap the app subscription you want to cancel to open its details page.

itemListElement.text: Scroll through the Active section to find the service.
Tap the subscription name to view options.

step.name: Cancel and confirm
step.text: Tap Cancel Subscription, then confirm the cancellation when prompted.

itemListElement.text: Tap Cancel Subscription on the details page.
Tap Confirm on the pop up to finalize the cancellation.

@graph.name: How to Cancel Subscriptions on Mac via Settings
@graph.description: Learn how to easily cancel active subscriptions on your Mac through the System Settings app, so you can stop recurring charges whenever you want.

supply.name: Active subscription linked to your Apple ID

tool.name: Mac computer with macOS System Settings

step.name: Open System Settings
step.text: Open the System Settings app on your Mac.

itemListElement.text: Click on the Apple menu and select System Settings.

step.name: Go to Media & Purchases
step.text: Click on your name and photo in the left sidebar, then select Media & Purchases on the account page.

itemListElement.text: Click on your Apple ID name at the top of the sidebar.
Select Media & Purchases from the options.

step.name: Manage Subscriptions
step.text: Click the Manage button next to Subscriptions to view your active plans.

itemListElement.text: Locate the Subscriptions section.
Click Manage to see your subscriptions.

step.name: Choose Subscription to Cancel
step.text: Click on the subscription you want to cancel from the list of active plans.

itemListElement.text: Select the active subscription you want to cancel.

step.name: Cancel Subscription
step.text: Click on Cancel Subscription, then confirm your choice to stop the service.

itemListElement.text: Click Cancel Subscription.
Confirm the cancellation when prompted.

@graph.name: How to Cancel Subscriptions on Mac via App Store
@graph.description: Cancel any active Mac App Store subscription using your Apple ID in a few quick clicks so you can stop recurring charges on your terms.

supply.name: Active subscription tied to your Apple ID

tool.name: Mac with the App Store app

step.name: Open the App Store
step.text: Launch the App Store on your Mac from the Dock or Applications folder.

itemListElement.text: Click the App Store icon to open it.

step.name: Go to your profile
step.text: Click your profile icon in the bottom left to open your account page.

itemListElement.text: Select the circular profile icon.

step.name: Open Account Settings and sign in
step.text: Click Account Settings on the account page, then sign in with your Apple ID if asked.

itemListElement.text: Click Account Settings.
Enter your Apple ID password if prompted.

step.name: Open Subscriptions manager
step.text: Scroll to the Manage section and click Manage next to Subscriptions.

itemListElement.text: Find the Subscriptions row.
Click Manage to view your plans.

step.name: Select the plan to cancel
step.text: Choose the active subscription you want to cancel to open its details.

itemListElement.text: Click the subscription you want to manage.

step.name: Cancel and confirm
step.text: Click Cancel Subscription, then click Confirm to finish the cancellation.

itemListElement.text: Click Cancel Subscription.
Confirm when the dialog appears.

@graph.name: How to Cancel Subscriptions on Your Apple Watch
@graph.description: Quickly cancel unwanted subscriptions directly from your Apple Watch through the App Store, so you can manage your payments without needing your iPhone or Mac.

supply.name: Active subscription linked to your Apple ID

tool.name: Apple Watch with the App Store app

step.name: Open the App Store
step.text: Press the Digital Crown, find the App Store app, and open it on your Apple Watch.

itemListElement.text: Tap the App Store icon from your watch's home screen.

step.name: Go to Account
step.text: Scroll down to the bottom of the App Store and tap Account to access your Apple ID settings.

itemListElement.text: Swipe down until you see Account.
Tap Account to open it.

step.name: Open Subscriptions
step.text: Tap on Subscriptions, then choose the plan you want to cancel.

itemListElement.text: Select Subscriptions from the list.
Tap the subscription you want to manage.

step.name: Cancel Subscription
step.text: Scroll to the bottom and tap Cancel Subscription, then confirm your choice to finish.

itemListElement.text: Scroll down and tap Cancel Subscription.
Tap Confirm to finalize the cancellation.

keyPoints.title: Which subscriptions can be canceled?
keyPoints.explanation: You can cancel subscriptions connected to your Apple ID and set up through the App Store, while others like Netflix require cancellation through their platform.

keyPoints.title: How to cancel subscriptions on iPhone or iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Use Settings or the App Store to view a list of active subscriptions and cancel directly from your device.

keyPoints.title: How to cancel subscriptions on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: Cancel subscriptions via System Settings under Media & Purchases or through the App Store, with slightly different steps for each method.

keyPoints.title: Cancel subscriptions on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Open the App Store on your Apple Watch, go to Account > Subscriptions, select the subscription, and tap Cancel.

keyPoints.title: How to find and cancel unknown subscriptions
keyPoints.explanation: Check your email for invoices from Apple to identify the Apple ID used, or review your bank statements for non-Apple subscriptions and cancel through the respective platform.

title.rendered: How to Change WhatsApp Background Wallpaper on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Change WhatsApp wallpaper from Settings or chats by choosing a preset, solid color, or photo—making conversations feel more personal or fun.
  • Set a wallpaper for all chats by going to WhatsApp Settings > Chats > Chat Wallpaper and picking a background from WhatsApp’s gallery or your photos.
  • To customize one chat only, open the chat, tap the name at the top, choose Wallpaper, then pick an image or color just for that thread.
  • Reset to the original wallpaper anytime from Settings > Chats > Chat Wallpaper > Reset if you want to go back to the default look.
  • Update the app if wallpaper options are missing and note that WhatsApp Web only supports solid colors for chat backgrounds.

Are your WhatsApp chats looking a little drab lately? You can spice things up and add some personality with fresh new wallpaper!

WhatsApp makes it super easy to customize your chat backgrounds on an iPhone by offering a range of wallpapers on different themes. It also allows you to set your images as custom chat wallpaper.

In this article, we will explore how to change WhatsApp chat wallpaper on an iPhone.

Table of Contents
  • How to change your chat wallpaper on WhatsApp for iPhone
    • Change WhatsApp wallpaper for all chats
    • Change WhatsApp wallpaper for a specific chat
  • How to reset your WhatsApp wallpaper on an iPhone

How to change your chat wallpaper on WhatsApp for iPhone

Changing your WhatsApp chat wallpaper on an iPhone is a quick and easy process. You can either choose from the pre-designed wallpapers provided by WhatsApp or use your own images.

Change WhatsApp wallpaper for all chats

If you want to change the background wallpaper for all your WhatsApp chats on an iPhone, follow these steps:

  1. Open WhatsApp on your iPhone.
  2. Tap on Settings at the bottom.
  3. Select Chats.
  4. Select Chat Wallpaper, then hit Choose a New Wallpaper on the following screen.
  5. Here you can see WhatsApp’s wallpaper libraries. Choose one based on your preference:
    • Bright: Vibrant wallpapers of beautiful landscapes and themes.
    • Dark: If you love black wallpaper, you will love this library.
    • Solid Colors: For minimalists, WhatsApp provides solid color wallpapers.
    • Photos: You may choose images from your camera roll to set as wallpaper.
  6. Browse through the available options and select the one you like.
  7. Adjust the image as needed and tap Set to apply it.

While setting the wallpaper, you will see a label at the bottom stating Wallpaper Motion: On. This means WhatsApp has added a parallax effect to the chat wallpaper, meaning it moves the wallpaper in response to the movements you are making on your phone. For instance, if you tilt the phone left, the wallpaper will appear to move to the left.

If you don’t want to have the motion effect, tap the motion button (with a phone icon) in the middle, and it will turn it off. You can then proceed to set the wallpaper.

Similarly, the solid color wallpapers have the default WhatsApp doodle. If you want to have a cleaner look, tap the effect button in the middle before applying the wallpaper.

Change WhatsApp wallpaper for a specific chat

You may change the chat background on WhatsApp for one person for more personalization. Here’s how:

  1. Open WhatsApp.
  2. Go to the chat you want to customize.
  3. Tap the contact’s name at the top of the screen to view their Contact Info page.
  4. Select Wallpaper.
  5. Then tap Choose a New Wallpaper.
  6. Pick a wallpaper from the wallpaper library, Photos, or use a solid color.
  7. Once you’ve selected and adjusted the image, tap Set to apply it to that specific chat.

How to reset your WhatsApp wallpaper on an iPhone

Want to get the classic WhatsApp vibes? You can easily revert to the default WhatsApp wallpaper. To reset the background of WhatsApp:

  1. Open WhatsApp and go to Chats settings as shown in the screenshot below.
  2. Select Chat Wallpaper.
  3. Tap Reset in the top-right corner of the screen.
  4. Confirm the action by tapping Reset.

Signing off…

Changing your WhatsApp wallpaper on an iPhone is a simple yet effective way to personalize your chatting experience. Whether you want a uniform look across all chats or unique backgrounds for specific conversations, WhatsApp gives you the flexibility to customize your app to your liking.

FAQs

Can you change your WhatsApp Web background?

You can change the wallpaper on WhatsApp Web but there’s a catch. WhatsApp only provides solid color wallpaper options on the web version. You may remove the doodle on them. But you can’t set custom images as chat background on WhatsApp Web.

Why can’t I change my WhatsApp wallpaper?

If you are having trouble changing your WhatsApp wallpaper, ensure that you have the latest version of WhatsApp installed. Sometimes, issues can arise from using outdated versions of the app. If the issue persists, try clearing the app’s cache, reinstalling WhatsApp, or contact WhatsApp for more help.

  • How to send photos as documents in WhatsApp on iPhone
  • How to remove Meta AI from WhatsApp, Instagram, and Facebook
  • How to use WhatsApp chat themes to customize your conversations

mainEntity.name: Can you change your WhatsApp Web background?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can change the wallpaper on WhatsApp Web but there's a catch. WhatsApp only provides solid color wallpaper options on the web version. You may remove the doodle on them. But you can't set custom images as chat background on WhatsApp Web.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I change my WhatsApp wallpaper?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you are having trouble changing your WhatsApp wallpaper, ensure that you have the latest version of WhatsApp installed. Sometimes, issues can arise from using outdated versions of the app. If the issue persists, try clearing the app's cache, reinstalling WhatsApp, or contact WhatsApp for more help.

@graph.name: How to change WhatsApp wallpaper for all chats
@graph.description: Customize the look of your WhatsApp chats by changing the wallpaper for all conversations on your iPhone. Choose from built-in wallpaper libraries or your own photos.

step.name: Open WhatsApp settings
step.text: Open WhatsApp on your iPhone and tap Settings at the bottom of the screen.

itemListElement.text: Launch WhatsApp.
Tap Settings in the bottom navigation bar.

step.name: Go to Chat Wallpaper
step.text: Select Chats from the Settings menu, then tap Chat Wallpaper on the next screen.

itemListElement.text: Tap Chats in the Settings menu.
Select Chat Wallpaper.

step.name: Choose a wallpaper
step.text: Tap Choose a New Wallpaper and browse through the available libraries or your photos.

itemListElement.text: Tap Choose a New Wallpaper.
Browse options under Bright, Dark, Solid Colors, or Photos.

step.name: Set the wallpaper
step.text: Browse through the available wallpapers, adjust the image as needed, and tap Set to apply it to all chats.

itemListElement.text: Select the wallpaper you like.
Drag or zoom to adjust the image if needed.
Tap Set to finalize your wallpaper.

@graph.name: How to change WhatsApp wallpaper for a specific chat
@graph.description: Set a unique wallpaper for one WhatsApp conversation on your iPhone, so that chat stands out from the rest.

step.name: Open the chat you want to customize
step.text: Open WhatsApp, then go to the conversation for which you want a custom wallpaper.

itemListElement.text: Launch WhatsApp on your iPhone.
Tap the chat you want to personalize.

step.name: Open Contact Info
step.text: Tap the contact’s name at the top of the screen to open the Contact Info page.

itemListElement.text: Tap the name banner at the top of the chat.
Wait for the Contact Info screen to appear.

step.name: Choose Wallpaper
step.text: Select Wallpaper, then tap Choose a New Wallpaper to browse options for this chat only.

itemListElement.text: Tap Wallpaper on the Contact Info page.
Tap Choose a New Wallpaper to continue.

step.name: Pick a wallpaper source
step.text: Pick from WhatsApp’s wallpaper libraries, your Photos, or a solid color, then preview how it looks in the chat.

itemListElement.text: Browse Bright, Dark, Solid Colors, or open Photos to select an image.
Use the preview to make sure the text is readable.

step.name: Set the custom wallpaper
step.text: Adjust the image if needed by dragging or zooming, then tap Set to apply it to this specific chat.

itemListElement.text: Adjust positioning until it looks right.
Tap Set to save the wallpaper for this chat only.

@graph.name: How to reset your WhatsApp wallpaper on an iPhone
@graph.description: Restore the default WhatsApp chat wallpaper on your iPhone from the Chats settings in just a few taps.

step.name: Open Chats settings in WhatsApp
step.text: Open WhatsApp and go to the Chats settings as shown in the screenshot.

itemListElement.text: Launch WhatsApp on your iPhone.
Tap Settings at the bottom, then tap Chats.

step.name: Open Chat Wallpaper
step.text: Select Chat Wallpaper to view your wallpaper options.

itemListElement.text: Tap Chat Wallpaper from the Chats settings screen.

step.name: Tap Reset
step.text: Tap Reset in the top right corner to revert to the default wallpaper.

itemListElement.text: Locate the Reset option at the top right of the screen.
Tap Reset to begin reverting the wallpaper.

step.name: Confirm the reset
step.text: Confirm the action by tapping Reset again to apply the default wallpaper to all chats.

itemListElement.text: Read the confirmation prompt carefully.
Tap Reset to finalize the change.

keyPoints.title: Easy Steps to Change WhatsApp Wallpaper on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: You can personalize your WhatsApp chat backgrounds on an iPhone either by selecting from preset wallpapers or by using your own images, making chats more fun and engaging.

keyPoints.title: How to Set a Wallpaper for All WhatsApp Chats
keyPoints.explanation: Navigate through WhatsApp settings to the 'Chats' section, then tap on 'Chat Wallpaper' and choose from WhatsApp's library or your photos to customize the background for all chats.

keyPoints.title: Personalize a Specific Chat with a Unique Wallpaper
keyPoints.explanation: Open the desired chat, tap the contact's name, select 'Wallpaper,' and pick a background from options like libraries, photos, or solid colors for individual chat customization.

keyPoints.title: Resetting WhatsApp Wallpaper to Default on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: If you wish to revert to the default wallpaper, go to 'Chats' > 'Chat Wallpaper' and tap 'Reset' to restore the original WhatsApp chat background.

keyPoints.title: Additional Tips and Troubleshooting
keyPoints.explanation: Ensure you have the latest app version to avoid issues in changing wallpapers, and remember that WhatsApp Web offers limited wallpaper customization with only solid colors available.

title.rendered: Adaptive Power vs Low Power Mode on iPhone: Which is Better

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Low Power Mode explained: This iPhone feature reduces background activity and visual effects to extend battery life, most helpful when your charge dips below 20 percent.
  • Adaptive Power in iOS 26: Apple’s new background system automatically adjusts performance during heavy tasks, conserving energy with little to no noticeable slowdown.
  • Main differences to note: Low Power Mode requires manual toggling and slows your phone more aggressively, while Adaptive Power works quietly in the background.
  • When to use each mode: Rely on Adaptive Power for everyday efficiency on newer iPhones, but switch on Low Power Mode when you’re running critically low.
  • Extra battery-saving habits: Lower screen brightness, limit background refresh, disable unnecessary location tracking, use Airplane Mode in weak-signal areas, and enable optimized charging.

An iPhone excels in almost everything it offers, except when it comes to battery capacity compared to its competition. For years, Low Power Mode has been the go-to feature for users wanting to squeeze extra hours out of their iPhones. Now, with iOS 26, Apple has introduced a new feature called Adaptive Power, joining the lineup alongside the long-standing Low Power Mode.

While both aim to extend your iPhone’s battery life, they work in very different ways.

So, if you’re wondering which one to use, Adaptive Power or Low Power Mode, you’re in the right place. This guide explains how each works, their differences, and the best situations to use them.

Table of Contents
  • What is Low Power Mode?
  • What is Adaptive Power in iOS 26?
  • Key Differences Between Adaptive Power and Low Power Mode
  • Which One Should You Use?
    • Use Adaptive Power Mode if:
    • Use Low Power Mode if:
  • How to Turn On or Off Adaptive Power and Low Power Mode
  • Tips to Maximize iPhone Battery Life Beyond Power Modes
  • Final Verdict

What is Low Power Mode?

Low Power Mode has been around since iOS 9 and is available on all modern iPhones. Once enabled, it immediately reduces system activity and pauses power-hungry background tasks to extend battery life.

The mode reduces overall iPhone power usage by:

  • Throttling CPU and GPU performance
  • Disabling background app refresh
  • Reducing display brightness
  • Stopping automatic downloads and mail fetch
  • Limiting visual effects and animations

You can enable or disable Low Power Mode manually at any time. iOS also prompts you to turn it on when your battery dips below 20%. Once your iPhone charges to 80% or higher, it turns off automatically.

When active, the battery icon turns yellow in the status bar instead of white.

Although you can use Low Power Mode even when your iPhone is fully charged, Apple designed it as an emergency power-saving feature, making it best when your iPhone is running low and you can’t plug it in right away.

What is Adaptive Power in iOS 26?

Adaptive Power made its debut in iOS 26 (currently in beta) as Apple’s newest smart battery optimization tool. Unlike Low Power Mode, which aggressively reduces power usage until turned off, Adaptive Power runs quietly in the background and activates only during high-demand moments.

Think of it as a smart efficiency assistant, fine-tuning your iPhone’s power usage in real time without making the phone feel sluggish.

Example:

If you’re editing a batch of RAW photos, recording 4K video, or gaming on a graphics-intensive app, Adaptive Power may dim the display slightly, limit background activity, or temporarily adjust performance to save energy, all while remaining almost unnoticeable.

Since Adaptive Power is part of the Apple Intelligence suite, it’s exclusive to iPhone 15 Pro and newer models.

Key Differences Between Adaptive Power and Low Power Mode

Here’s a quick comparison:

Which One Should You Use?

The answer depends on your iPhone model:

  • If you own an iPhone 15 or older, you only get Low Power Mode.
  • If you have an iPhone 15 Pro or newer, you can use both.

Use Adaptive Power Mode if:

  • You want hands-free, smart battery management.
  • You own a latest-gen iPhone with Apple Intelligence.
  • You regularly perform heavy tasks but don’t want big performance drops.

Use Low Power Mode if:

  • Your battery is critically low.
  • You want manual control over when to save power.
  • You’re traveling or going hours without charging.
  • Your battery health has dropped below 80%, and you want to stretch it without replacing it.

How to Turn On or Off Adaptive Power and Low Power Mode

The steps are nearly identical.

Low Power Mode:

  1. Open Settings → Battery → Toggle on Low Power Mode.
  2. Alternatively, pull down the Control Center and tap the Low Power Mode button to turn it on.

You can also ask Siri to enable it.

Adaptive Power:

  1. Open Settings → Battery → Power Mode.
  2. Toggle on Adaptive Power.

Tips to Maximize iPhone Battery Life Beyond Power Modes

Besides relying on these two features, here are everyday habits that can boost battery life:

  • Lower screen brightness or enable Auto-Brightness.
  • Limit Background App Refresh for unnecessary apps.
  • Enable Optimized Battery Charging for long-term health.
  • Turn off Location Services for apps that don’t need it.
  • Use Airplane Mode in low-signal areas to reduce drain.

Final Verdict

Both Adaptive Power Mode and Low Power Mode are valuable, but they serve different purposes.

  • Adaptive Power is your smart, everyday companion that optimizes in the background.
  • Low Power Mode is your emergency savior when every percent counts.

The best strategy is to use both. Let Adaptive Power handle daily efficiency, and switch to Low Power Mode when your iPhone’s battery gets critically low.

Which one do you prefer, the subtle efficiency of Adaptive Power or the aggressive savings of Low Power Mode? Share your thoughts in the comments.

focus.keyphrase: Adaptive Power vs Low Power Mode

keyPoints.title: What is Low Power Mode?
keyPoints.explanation: Low Power Mode is an available feature on all modern iPhones that reduces system activity and pauses background tasks to extend battery life, especially useful when the battery is low.

keyPoints.title: What is Adaptive Power in iOS 26?
keyPoints.explanation: Adaptive Power is Apple's new smart battery optimization tool introduced in iOS 26, which runs quietly in the background and activates during high-demand tasks to conserve energy without noticeable performance drops.

keyPoints.title: Key differences between Adaptive Power and Low Power Mode
keyPoints.explanation: Adaptive Power automatically activates during demanding tasks on newer iPhones and makes minimal adjustments, while Low Power Mode is manually toggled and causes noticeable slowdown to maximize battery savings.

keyPoints.title: Which one should you use?
keyPoints.explanation: Use Adaptive Power if you want automatic, intelligent management of power on compatible iPhone models, and Low Power Mode if you need manual control or are experiencing critically low battery.

keyPoints.title: Tips to maximize iPhone battery life beyond power modes
keyPoints.explanation: Improve battery life through habits like lowering screen brightness, limiting background app refresh, enabling optimized charging, turning off unnecessary location services, and using airplane mode in low-signal areas.

title.rendered: What is Optimized Battery Charging on iPhone and How to Use it?

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What It Is: This feature learns your daily charging routine to slow battery aging by waiting at 80% and finishing the charge right before you normally use your phone.
  • The New 80% Limit: On newer iPhones (15 and up) with iOS 18+, you can set a hard 80% charge limit to further protect your battery’s long-term health.
  • How to Enable: You can enable these features by going to Settings > Battery > Battery Health & Charging and choosing between Optimized Charging or a hard 80% limit.
  • The Main Benefit: The primary benefit is reducing battery wear by minimizing the time your iPhone sits at a full 100% charge, which is stressful for lithium-ion batteries.
  • How It Learns: For the feature to work effectively, your iPhone needs to learn a consistent charging routine, such as charging overnight in the same location on a regular basis.

No matter how advanced your iPhone’s processor or camera may be, all those cutting-edge features are only as good as your battery. You’re not alone if you’ve ever reached for a charger sooner than you’d like. Every lithium-ion battery gradually loses capacity, which means less time between charges as the months go by. The good news? Apple has your back with Optimized Battery Charging. This clever iOS feature is built to help slow down battery aging so you can enjoy your iPhone for longer without worrying about constant battery replacements.

In this guide, I’ll explain everything you need to know about Optimized Battery Charging: what it is, how it works, the pros and cons, and how you can set it up to fit your daily routine. Whether you’re a longtime iPhone user or just curious about getting the most out of your device, you’ll find practical tips to help your battery stay healthier and longer.

What is Optimized Battery Charging?

Think of Optimized Battery Charging as your iPhone’s way of looking out for you—and itself. This innovative feature is designed to help your battery last longer by cutting down on your phone’s time sitting at a full 100% charge. Once you turn it on, your iPhone learns your charging habits and determines the best time to finish charging so your battery isn’t under unnecessary stress. After all, letting a lithium-ion battery linger at 100% for too long can speed up its aging process, but with this feature, your device does the heavy lifting to help keep your battery healthy for the long haul.

Note: While this feature is currently designed for iPhones, similar battery optimization features are available on some Android devices and laptops. And if you use an Apple Watch, you can learn how to manage its optimized charging settings in our dedicated Apple Watch guide.

Optimized Battery Charging vs. Standard Charging

Figuring out the difference between traditional charging and Optimized Battery Charging can help you make the smartest choice for your daily routine and your iPhone’s long-term health.

Aspect Standard Charging Optimized Battery Charging Charging Process Charges rapidly to 100% and maintains full charge Charges quickly to 80%, then pauses and completes based on your routine Convenience always provides a full charge as soon as possible may delay the final 20% to align with your usage patterns User Experience Predictable; device always reaches 100% when plugged in Works best with regular routines; may not be fully charged if your schedule changes unexpectedly Battery Health Can accelerate battery aging due to prolonged time at 100% Designed to minimize battery wear and extend overall lifespan.

If you’re the type who always needs your phone to hit 100% as fast as possible—no matter what time it is—standard charging is probably your best bet. It’s quick and predictable, but keep in mind that always rushing to full charge can wear out your battery faster over time. On the other hand, Optimized Battery Charging takes a more thoughtful approach. It might hold off on that last bit of charging sometimes, but it’s doing so to help your battery last longer, so you can keep your phone running strong day after day.

How Does Optimized Battery Charging Work?

Here’s how the feature operates:

  1. Learns Your Routine: Your iPhone uses on-device machine learning to understand when you typically charge and unplug your device.
  2. Charges Normally Up to 80%: The battery charges at regular speed until it reaches 80%.
  3. Pauses Charging: Once at 80%, charging is paused to avoid prolonged time at full charge.
  4. Completes Charge Before You Need It: Based on your routine, your iPhone finishes charging to 100% just before you usually unplug it.

Example: If you typically plug in your iPhone at 10 PM and unplug it at 7 AM, the device will charge to 80% quickly, then wait. Around 6:30 AM, it will resume charging so you have a full battery when you wake up.

New Charging Limit Options (iOS 18+, iPhone 15/16)

If you’re using iOS 18 on an iPhone 15 or 16, there’s a handy new feature just for you: now, you can set a maximum charging limit for your device. Want your phone to stop at 80%, 85%, 90%, or 95%? Pick your preferred limit in the battery settings, and your iPhone will pause charging once it hits that number. For instance, if you choose 85%, your phone will hold steady at that level until you tell it otherwise—no need to worry about overcharging.

Apple introduced this feature to give you even more control over your battery’s health and long-term performance. It’s a great way to slow down battery aging even further. Remember, though, that if you pick a lower charging limit, your iPhone might not last quite as long between charges as it would if you let it reach 100%. It’s all about finding the best balance for your daily routine!

Impact on Device Performance and Battery Health

1. Slowing Battery Aging and Preserving Capacity

When you let Optimized Battery Charging do its thing, your iPhone spends less time sitting at 100%—and that’s a big win for your iPhone battery’s health. This simple tweak helps slow down the chemical aging process, so you’re less likely to need a battery replacement anytime soon and can enjoy smoother performance from your device for longer.

The numbers can vary, but studies and real-world user experiences show that constantly keeping your battery at 100% can speed up capacity loss—sometimes by as much as 20% over two years! Optimized Battery Charging gives your phone a better shot at holding onto its original capacity so that you can get more life out of every charge.

2. Maintaining Peak Performance

A healthy battery helps your iPhone maintain peak performance. When battery health declines, iOS may activate performance management features (sometimes called “throttling”) to prevent unexpected shutdowns. Optimized Battery Charging can help your device avoid slowdowns and deliver a more consistent user experience by maintaining battery health.

Users who consistently use this feature often report higher battery health percentages (as seen in Settings > Battery > Battery Health) even after a year or more, compared to those who disable the feature.

3. Compatibility with Fast Charging

Optimized Battery Charging works seamlessly with fast charging technologies. Your iPhone will still fast-charge up to 80%, then pause as needed to protect battery health. This means you get the convenience of rapid charging without sacrificing long-term performance.

4. Benefits Across Device Generations

The effectiveness of Optimized Battery Charging may be even greater on newer iPhones (15/16 series) thanks to more advanced battery chemistry and the added option to set custom charging limits. However, even older iPhones benefit from reduced wear and more stable performance over time.

5. Impact on Resale and Trade-In Value

Maintaining higher battery health can directly impact your iPhone’s resale or trade-in value. Devices with a battery health above 85% are more desirable and may fetch higher prices on the secondhand market.

Benefits of Optimized Battery Charging

  1. Reduces Battery Wear: By minimizing the time your iPhone spends at 100%, you slow down the chemical aging process of the battery.
  2. Preserves Battery Capacity: Helps maintain your iPhone’s battery health and performance for a longer period.
  3. Delays Battery Replacement: With less wear, you’re less likely to need a battery replacement as soon.
  4. Convenient and Automatic: Once enabled, the feature works in the background without requiring any extra effort from you.

Why does this matter?

Lithium-ion batteries degrade faster when kept at full charge, especially in warm conditions. Reducing time at 100% helps preserve your battery’s ability to hold a charge.

How to Enable, Customize, or Disable Optimized Battery Charging on iPhone

For iPhone 15 and 16 Series (iOS 18 and later):

  1. Open Settings → Battery.
  2. Tap Charging.
  3. Select Optimized Battery Charging.
  4. Choose a charging limit between 80% and 95%, or allow the phone to manage charging automatically.

For iPhone 14 and Earlier:

  1. Open Settings → Battery.
  2. Tap Battery Health & Charging.
  3. Toggle Optimized Battery Charging on or off.

Temporary Override:

If you need a full charge sooner than usual, you can temporarily disable Optimized Battery Charging from the charging notification that appears on your lock screen while charging. Simply touch and hold the notification and select “Charge Now” to resume charging to 100% immediately.

Default Setting:

Optimized Battery Charging is enabled by default on most iPhones running iOS 13 or later.

When Should You Disable Optimized Battery Charging?

In most cases, leaving Optimized Battery Charging enabled is best. However, you might want to disable it if:

  1. You have irregular charging schedules (charging at different times each day).
  2. You need your phone fully charged earlier than usual (for example, before early travel).
  3. You have an emergency and need a quick full charge.
Tip: If you’re leaving for the airport at 4 AM instead of your usual 7 AM, consider turning off Optimized Battery Charging the night before to ensure a full charge.

General Tips for Battery Health

  1. Avoid Extreme Temperatures: Charging in very hot or cold environments can accelerate battery aging.
  2. Use Approved Chargers: Stick to Apple-certified or high-quality chargers for safe, efficient charging.
  3. Don’t Let Your Battery Drain Completely: Try to recharge before your battery drops to 0% for optimal longevity.

Example: Avoid charging your iPhone in direct sunlight or leaving it plugged in inside a hot car.

Let Your iPhone Charge the Smart Way

Optimized Battery Charging is a powerful tool for extending your iPhone’s battery lifespan and maintaining long-term performance. By learning your routine and managing the charging process, it helps you get the most out of your device with minimal effort. For most users, leaving the feature enabled is the best way to keep your iPhone running smoothly for years to come. If your needs change, Apple makes it easy to customize or disable the feature as needed.

FAQs

Does Optimized Battery Charging slow down charging?

No. Your iPhone charges at normal speed up to 80%. The last 20% is intentionally delayed to protect battery health, but you can override this if needed.

Does it work with fast charging?

Yes. Fast charging is supported up to 80%. The optimization only affects the timing of the final portion of the charge.

Is it safe to leave on all the time?

Absolutely. For most users, keeping the feature enabled is the best way to preserve battery health. If your needs change, you can always disable it.

What if my routine is unpredictable?

The feature works best with consistent charging habits. If your schedule varies, you may not see the full benefits—but it won’t harm your device.

  • How to turn off Optimized Battery Charging on Apple Watch
  • How to check iPhone charge cycle count
  • How to fix iPhone battery draining faster

mainEntity.name: Does Optimized Battery Charging slow down charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your iPhone charges at normal speed up to 80%. The last 20% is intentionally delayed to protect battery health, but you can override this if needed.

mainEntity.name: Does it work with fast charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Fast charging is supported up to 80%. The optimization only affects the timing of the final portion of the charge.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to leave on all the time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. For most users, keeping the feature enabled is the best way to preserve battery health. If your needs change, you can always disable it.

mainEntity.name: What if my routine is unpredictable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The feature works best with consistent charging habits. If your schedule varies, you may not see the full benefits—but it won't harm your device.
