mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.

keyPoints.title: iOS 26 Beta 6 Focuses on Refinements
keyPoints.explanation: Apple's beta 6 for iOS 26 emphasizes polishing the Liquid Glass interface, enhancing animation speed, and reversing a controversial Camera app swipe change, indicating they're close to final release.

keyPoints.title: Seven New Ringtones and a Fresh Sound
keyPoints.explanation: Beta 6 introduces seven new ringtones, including variations of 'Reflection' and a new original tone called 'Little Bird,' potentially encouraging users to toggle silent mode.

keyPoints.title: Enhanced Liquid Glass Design Details
keyPoints.explanation: The new transparent and somewhat playful Liquid Glass style features a floating clock, shimmering toggles, and dynamic background transparency, balancing aesthetics with usability.

keyPoints.title: Restoration of Camera Swipe Default Behavior
keyPoints.explanation: Apple reverted to the original swipe direction for camera modes, removing the toggle setting introduced in beta 5, restoring user muscle memory.

keyPoints.title: Performance Boosts and Guided Onboarding
keyPoints.explanation: Animation speed has been increased for a more responsive feel, complemented by an onboarding video guiding users through the new Liquid Glass interface and features.

From iPhones and MacBooks to Android phones and AI tools, I’ve always enjoyed turning complicated features into simple, jargon-free guides. Recently, I switched sides and joined the Apple camp. Whether you want to try out new features, catch up on the latest news, or tweak your Apple devices, I’m here to help you get the most out of your tech.

Whether you’re customizing your iPhone, troubleshooting your Android, or tweaking Chrome OS settings, my goal is to help you get more out of your tech.

title.rendered: iOS 26 Beta 5: All the New Features and UI Changes So Far

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iOS 26 Beta 5 focuses on UI polish with smoother animations, better button layouts, and refined transitions that improve visual clarity across the system.
  • Camera app adds Classic Mode swipe option that restores the older scrolling direction between photo modes for a more familiar feel.
  • AirDrop gets a new icon design in the iOS 26 Share Sheet, better matching the system’s updated visual style.
  • Lock Screen animations feel more fluid with smoother transitions for passcode entry and Now Playing indicators.
  • Control Center adds security insights with better Wi-Fi transition effects and clearer network encryption icons on long-press.

Just a few days after releasing the first public beta of iOS 26, Apple has now seeded the fifth developer beta of iOS 26. While major feature additions in recent betas have slowed down ahead of the expected September release, this update still brings several small but noteworthy changes.

This update primarily focuses on enhancing the user experience by refining button placements, improving animations, and polishing the visual design across the system.

Here’s a complete breakdown of everything new in iOS 26 beta 5, so you know exactly what to expect.

Camera: Classic Mode for Easier Swiping

Apple has introduced a new feature in the Camera app called Classic Mode, which reverses the scroll direction when switching between shooting modes. This brings a more intuitive feel for users accustomed to the older swipe pattern.

AirDrop: Refreshed Icon Design

Before iOS 26 beta 5, the AirDrop icon looked nearly identical to its iOS 18 version. Now, a redesigned AirDrop icon appears in the Share Sheet, bringing it in line with iOS 26’s updated visual language.

Lock Screen: New Passcode and Music Animations

Apple has significantly improved animations across the UI with iOS 26 beta 5:

  • Passcode animation: When entering your passcode, the numbers now bounce into place with a smooth, fluid motion.
  • Music lock animation: Locking your iPhone while music is playing now triggers a subtle new animation.

Control Center: Smoother Page Transitions

Similar to the Lock Screen, iOS 26 beta 5 brings a bouncier animation to the Control Center. Switching between pages now features a more natural and visually appealing transition.

Wi-Fi Details: More Transparent Security Info

Long-pressing the Wi-Fi tile in the Control Center now reveals whether a network is secured or public. A small lock icon will appear next to private networks for better clarity.

Siri: Smarter Travel Recommendations

Siri is getting more proactive. In beta 5, it can detect when you’re about to travel and offer cellular connectivity suggestions outside your home country. However, this feature may not be useful for everyone.

Wallet: Clearer Preauthorized Payments Label

In the Wallet app, Apple has updated the UI by replacing the ambiguous “Payments” button for Apple Card with a clearer “Preauthorized Payments” label, making its function more obvious.

Dynamic Island: Low Battery Warning

The Dynamic Island now expands to display a low battery warning when your iPhone’s charge dips to 20%, offering a more visible cue without interrupting your experience. This cute new low battery animation adds a touch of personality while ensuring you’re aware of your battery status at a glance.

Dock: Expanded Liquid Glass Effect

The Liquid Glass effect on the Home Screen dock has been slightly expanded. Although subtle, the change gives the dock a richer, more refined look that fits iOS 26’s updated aesthetic.

Splash Screens: Feature Highlights in More Apps

Apple has added new splash screens in several apps to showcase recently added features. These pop-ups help users better understand what’s new after updating.

Fitness+: Updated App Icon

The Fitness app now sports a new icon for Fitness+, aligning with Apple’s ongoing design evolution in iOS 26.

iOS 26: Stable Release Timeline

With the iPhone 17 series launch event rumored for September 9, 2025, Apple is expected to roll out the stable iOS 26 update between September 14 and 16, right before iPhone 17 deliveries begin.

Right now, Apple seems to be shifting from feature rollouts to fine-tuning the overall experience. These subtle refinements in beta 5 suggest that the final release is just around the corner.

What do you think of these updates in iOS 26 beta 5? Which feature are you most excited to try out? Let us know in the comments!

mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.

keyPoints.title: Refined User Experience in iOS 26 Beta 5
keyPoints.explanation: Apple emphasizes polishing visual design, button placements, and animations, focusing on a smoother and more intuitive system visual experience.

keyPoints.title: Introduction of Classic Mode in Camera App
keyPoints.explanation: A new Classic Mode reverses the scroll direction between shooting modes, making switching more intuitive for users familiar with older swipe patterns.

keyPoints.title: Updated AirDrop Icon Design
keyPoints.explanation: The AirDrop icon in the Share Sheet has been redesigned to align with iOS 26’s visual language, providing a fresh look.

keyPoints.title: Enhanced Lock Screen Animations
keyPoints.explanation: Animations around passcode entry and music locking are now smoother and more fluid, improving overall visual feedback.

keyPoints.title: Smoother Control Center Transitions and Security Info
keyPoints.explanation: Page transitions in the Control Center are more natural, and long-pressing Wi-Fi reveals network security status with clearer icons.

title.rendered: WhatsApp to Introduce Instagram Profile Link Verification

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • WhatsApp to verify linked Instagram profiles: A new iOS feature will add verified badges to linked Instagram accounts to reduce impersonation risks.
  • Current Instagram link setup lacks safeguards: At present, WhatsApp only allows pasting Instagram links in profiles without any ownership checks, which can be misused.
  • Verification will confirm account ownership: Instead of entering just a username, users will complete a verification process before the linked Instagram shows a verified badge.
  • Boosts trust for public-facing accounts: Verified cross-links will help public figures, influencers, and businesses confirm authenticity and make impersonation more difficult.
  • Still in early iOS beta with no launch date: The code is live in beta builds but not publicly available, hinting at Meta’s push for integrated identity checks.

WhatsApp is preparing a feature for iOS that would let users link their Instagram profiles with a verified badge, reducing the risk of fake accounts. The change was first spotted by WABetaInfo in the latest TestFlight beta build.

What Is Changing

Currently, WhatsApp lets you paste an Instagram profile link into your account info, but there’s no check to confirm it actually belongs to you. That gap has often been exploited for impersonation or misleading links.

The upcoming version changes the process. Instead of typing in a username, users would go through an ownership verification step. Once approved, the Instagram link would display with a “verified” label, signaling that it’s genuinely tied to the WhatsApp account holder.

Why It Matters

Meta is framing this as a way to help people quickly identify legitimate accounts. Public figures, influencers, and small businesses could see the most benefit, since verified cross-links make it harder for copycats to pose as them. It could also build user trust in conversations where identity matters.

Still in Development

Although the code is present in the iOS beta, testers can’t use the feature yet. WhatsApp hasn’t shared a release window, so it may be weeks or months before it appears in a public update.

Part of Meta’s broader app strategy

If rolled out, this would mark another step in Meta’s slow push toward deeper integration between its platforms. Verified Instagram links on WhatsApp could be a small but telling move toward a more unified online identity across its apps.

Would you trust a WhatsApp account more if its Instagram link was verified? Drop your thoughts below.

mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.

title.rendered: How to Add Music to Your Snapchat Story

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • The “Sounds” Feature: Snapchat’s “Sounds” feature allows you to legally add popular licensed songs or create your own custom audio clips to make your snaps and stories more engaging.
  • Adding Licensed Music: After taking a snap, tap the music note icon, search for a licensed song, and then trim the clip to select the exact part you want to play.
  • Using Your Own Sound: To use your own audio, tap the music note icon and select “Create Sound” to either record a new clip or upload audio from your camera roll.
  • Editing or Removing Music: You can easily change your song choice by tapping the music icon again, or remove the sound completely by dragging the song’s sticker to the trash can.
  • The Benefit: Adding the right music or sound to your snaps helps to set a mood, add humor, or make your content more memorable and likely to be shared.

Adding music to your Snapchat stories makes them look more lively regardless of whether you use a featured sound or one of your own. A perfect soundtrack adds depth to your stories, and people are more likely to watch and enjoy your Snapchat stories if they include an interesting soundtrack.

The post details how to add music to your Snapchat stories on your iPhone.

Table of Contents
  • What is Snapchat's Music feature?
  • How to add music to your Snapchat story on iPhone
  • How to add your own sound to a Snapchat story
  • How to remove or change the music in a Snapchat story

What is Snapchat’s Music feature?

Starting in October 2020, Snapchat struck a licensing deal with various music labels and publishers, which led to the introduction of the Sounds feature on the social media platform. This feature provides access to a large library of licensed songs, sound effects, and even your own recorded sounds, allowing you to add music to your snaps.

Once added, the music plays in the background while your Snap video or photo is displayed.

How to add music to your Snapchat story on iPhone

Adding a music track to your Snapchat story isn’t some nuclear science that even a person with little to no technical competence can do. Here’s how you can:

  1. Open the Snapchat app.
  2. Now, tap the Capture button to take a photo snap or tap and hold the Capture button to record a video snap.
  3. Once done, tap the Music Note button on the right toolbar.

  4. Next, browse through the available music or use the search bar to find a specific track.
  5. Tap the Play button next to the selected track to preview it.
  6. Once you’ve selected a song, a sound wave bar will appear at the bottom of the screen.
  7. You can use the adjustment sliders on either side of the sound wave bar to choose which part of the song you want to add to your Snapchat Story.
  8. Once done, tap the Checkmark (✅) icon, and the song will be added to your story.

Once the song is added to your snap, the song’s name and artist will appear as a sticker, which you can drag, resize, or reposition anywhere on the screen. You can now post this snap as your Snapchat story, as you usually do.

How to add your own sound to a Snapchat story

If no music track in Snapchat’s music library entices you or suits your Snapchat story, you can record or upload your custom sound and use it on your Snapchat story. Here’s how:

  1. Open Snapchat and capture a snap.
  2. Tap the Music Note icon in the right toolbar.
  3. Here, locate and tap the + Create Sound button.

  4. Now, Choose whether to upload a sound from the camera roll or record it. 
  5. If you choose Upload From Camera Roll, select a video from your library whose audio you want to use in your snap.
  6. Next, give your sound a name, choose whether to make the sound public, use the adjustment sliders on either side of the sound wave bar to adjust it, and then tap Save Sound.

  7. Alternatively, if you choose to Record Sound, tap & hold the Microphone button to record the sound, give your sound a name, and tap the Save Sound button.

  8. Now, tap on My Favourites in the sounds menu, followed by the My Sounds button.

     
  9. Select the sound you added to Snapchat in the previous steps to add it to your snap.
  10. Adjust the sound per your requirement, tap the Checkmark (✅) icon and the sound will be added to your story.

Once done, post the snap as a Snapchat story as usual.

How to remove or change the music in a Snapchat story

If, for some reason, you no longer want to use the added music in your Snapchat story, you can easily remove it and add a new soundtrack altogether. Below, I’ve detailed how you can:

  1. To remove the added song, simply drag the song’s sticker to the Bin icon that appears at the bottom center.
  2. Alternatively, you can tap on X in the music tile at the top center.

  3. To change the music, tap the Music Note icon again and choose a different soundtrack.

Final thoughts…

With music in your Snapchat stories, you can enhance the overall experience and make them more fun and engaging. Good music has the power to transform an ordinary Snap into something memorable and expressive.

Will you use music in your Snapchat story often? Let us know your thoughts in the comments!

mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.

step.text: Use the sliders on the sound wave bar to choose the part of the song you want.

step.name: Add the music to your story
step.text: Tap the Checkmark icon to add the song to your Snapchat Story.

@graph.name: How to Add Your Own Sound to Snapchat Story
@graph.description: Step-by-step guide on how to upload or record your own sound and add it to your Snapchat story.

supply.name: iPhone or Android device with Snapchat installed

step.name: Capture your snap
step.text: Open Snapchat and take a photo or record a video by tapping or holding the Capture button.

step.name: Tap the Music Note icon
step.text: In the right toolbar, tap the Music Note icon and then tap the + Create Sound button.

step.name: Choose upload or record
step.text: Choose whether to upload a sound from your Camera Roll or record it directly.

step.name: Upload a sound
step.text: If uploading, select a video from your library, name your sound, set privacy, adjust the sound wave sliders, and tap Save Sound.

step.name: Record a sound
step.text: If recording, tap and hold the Microphone button, name your sound, and tap Save Sound.

step.name: Add your saved sound to your snap
step.text: Go to My Favourites in the sounds menu, tap My Sounds, select your sound, adjust it, and tap the Checkmark icon to add it to your story.

keyPoints.title: Snapchat's Music Feature 'Sounds'
keyPoints.explanation: Introduced in October 2020 after a licensing deal with music labels, the Sounds feature allows users to add licensed songs, sound effects, or recorded sounds to their snaps, enhancing their stories.

keyPoints.title: Adding Music to Snapchat Stories on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Users can easily add music to their Snapchat stories by capturing a snap, selecting the Music Note icon, browsing or searching for a track, previewing, and adjusting the part of the song to be played.

keyPoints.title: Adding Your Own Sounds to Snapchat Stories
keyPoints.explanation: If Snapchat's library doesn't suit your story, you can record or upload your own sounds, giving you full customization by creating new audio clips from your camera roll or microphone.

keyPoints.title: Removing or Changing Music in Stories
keyPoints.explanation: You can remove or change the soundtrack in your Snapchat story by dragging the music sticker to the bin icon, tapping the 'X' on the music tile, or selecting a new track through the Music Note icon.

keyPoints.title: Enhancing Stories with Music
keyPoints.explanation: Using music in your Snapchat stories makes them more lively, engaging, and memorable, transforming simple snaps into expressive content that captures viewers' interest.

title.rendered: How to set and manage alarms on your Apple Watch

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why It’s Effective: The Apple Watch is a great alarm because its haptic vibrations on your wrist provide a silent but effective alert that is less likely to be missed.
  • The Easiest Method: Siri: The quickest way to set an alarm is with your voice. Simply activate Siri and say a command like, “Set an alarm for 6:30 AM.”
  • The Manual Method: Alarms App: You can also set alarms manually by opening the Alarms app on your watch, tapping the plus icon, and using the Digital Crown to set the time.
  • Managing Your Alarms: From the Alarms app, you can easily manage your alarms by tapping on one to change its time, toggle it on or off, or delete it.
  • Customization Options: For more customization, you can disable the snooze function for any alarm or turn on Silent Mode on your watch to get a vibration-only alarm.

While you can use your iPhone for alarms, there is a chance you might miss certain alarms, maybe because sometimes your iPhone might be too far away, on Silent Mode, or out of charge. However, an Apple Watch is pretty much always on your wrist, which makes it a great alarm clock.

Keep reading, and I will show you two ways to set an alarm on your Apple Watch and manage it when needed.

Table of Contents
  • 2 ways to set an alarm on Apple Watch
    • Using Siri on Apple Watch
    • Using the Alarms App on Apple Watch
  • How to manage and edit alarms on Apple Watch
    • Change alarm time on Apple Watch
    • Turn off snooze in an alarm
    • Delete Apple Watch alarms
    • Skip a wake-up alarm
  • Sync alarms on iPhone and Apple Watch
  • Set the Apple Watch as a bedside clock with alarm
  • How to add an alarm to watch face
  • How to set vibrate-only alarms on Apple Watch

2 ways to set an alarm on Apple Watch

There are two ways to set alarms on an Apple Watch in 2 ways. You can either ask Siri to do it or take matters into your own hands and set one up using the Alarms app on your Apple Watch.

Using Siri on Apple Watch

The best and most straightforward way to set an alarm on your Apple Watch is using Siri. Here’s what you need to do:

  1. Activate Siri on your Apple Watch by saying “Hey Siri” or holding the Digital Crown.
  2. Then, say, “Set an Alarm for X: XX AM (or PM).”

That’s all. Siri will now set the alarm for you. You can head to the Alarms app on your Apple Watch to verify it.

Using the Alarms App on Apple Watch

If you don’t prefer using Siri, you can use the Alarms app on your Apple Watch to set an alarm. Here’s how you do it:

  1. Open the Alarms app on your Apple Watch.
  2. Tap the + icon and set the time of your alarm. Rotate the Digital Crown to change the hours and minutes. Remember to choose AM and PM correctly if the watch is set to a 12-hour format.
  3. Once done, tap the green checkmark icon in the bottom-right corner to set the alarm.

Repeat the steps above to add multiple alarms.

How to manage and edit alarms on Apple Watch

After you have set an alarm on your Apple Watch, you can edit it or make other changes to it if required. Let’s show you how.

Change alarm time on Apple Watch

To change the alarm time for a set alarm, open the Alarms app and follow these steps:

  1. Tap the set alarm.
  2. Tap on Change Time.
  3. Now, reset the new time for the alarm. When done, hit the green checkmark in the bottom-right corner to save the alarm.

Turn off snooze in an alarm

By default, your alarms have the Snooze option turned on. This means you get the ability to temporarily postpone your alarm when it goes off. However, if you do not prefer this, you can turn off the Snooze option for an alarm like this:

  1. In the Alarms app, tap the already set alarm.
  2. Scroll down and flip the Snooze toggle off.

Delete Apple Watch alarms

For times when you no longer need an alarm, you can simply delete it to avoid clutter. Here’s how:

  1. In the Alarms app, tap the already set alarm.
  2. Scroll down and tap the Delete button.

Skip a wake-up alarm

When you set up your sleep schedule and an alarm in the Apple Watch’s Sleep app, it will also appear in the Alarms app. You can skip this wake-up alarm by doing the following:

  1. Head to the Alarms app.
  2. Tap the Wake Up alarm.
  3. Tap the Skip for Tonight button.

  4. If you change your mind, you can reverse the skip by following the same steps and tapping the Don’t Skip button.

Sync alarms on iPhone and Apple Watch

You can also make your Apple Watch alert you to the alarms set up on your iPhone. Follow these steps to do this:

  1. Open the Watch app on your iPhone and go to the My Watch tab.
  2. Find and tap the Clock app.
  3. Toggle on the Push Alerts from iPhone option on the following screen.

Now, your Apple Watch will also alert you for the alarms set on your iPhone.

Set the Apple Watch as a bedside clock with alarm

Since you can use an Apple Watch as your bedside clock, setting an alarm on your Apple Watch will also show it in the Nightstand Mode. To know how to turn on the Nightstand Mode and learn more about it, check out our guide on how to use Nightstand Mode on an Apple Watch.

How to add an alarm to watch face

If you want convenient access to your upcoming alarms, you can add alarms to your watch face on your Apple Watch. These are the steps you need to follow:

  1. Tap and hold the watch face and tap Edit.
  2. Swipe right until you reach the Complications settings.
  3. Here, tap any of the four corners where you want your alarm to be displayed.
  4. Now select Alarms and tap the screen again to set.

Alternatively, you can also use the Watch app on your iPhone to do this. Follow the steps.

  1. Tap the watch face.
  2. Under Complications, select one of the four corners.
  3. Then, select Alarm.

Your alarms will now be seen directly on the watch face.

How to set vibrate-only alarms on Apple Watch

At times, you may want your Apple Watch alarms to just vibrate instead of making a sound. You can easily set up a vibrate-only alarm for such instances using the following steps:

  1. Access the Control Center on your Apple Watch by pressing the Side button.
  2. Tap the Silent Mode button (with a bell icon) to put your watch into Silent Mode.

Now, your Apple Watch will only vibrate to alert you of your alarm.

Signing off…

If you own an Apple Watch, you must make the most of its capabilities. Setting up alarms on it is one way to do it, especially if you use your Apple Watch to track your sleep. So go ahead and set it up and eliminate the risks of missing your next alarm and oversleeping.

FAQs

Can I use my Apple Watch to set multiple alarms?

Yes, you can set multiple alarms on your Apple Watch.

Why is my Apple Watch alarm not working?

There may be multiple reasons for this. As a quick fix, try restarting your Apple Watch and ensure you are on the latest watchOS version. If the issue persists, contact Apple support.

You might also like:

  • How to change Apple Watch ringtone in watchOS 11
  • How to set an alarm on Mac
  • How to change or customize alarm sound on iPhone

mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.

@graph.name: How to Set an Alarm Using Siri on Apple Watch
@graph.description: A quick guide to setting an alarm on your Apple Watch using Siri voice commands.

step.name: Activate Siri
step.text: Activate Siri on your Apple Watch by saying 'Hey Siri' or holding the Digital Crown.

step.name: Set the alarm
step.text: Say, 'Set an alarm for X:XX AM (or PM).' Siri will confirm the alarm time.

@graph.name: How to Set an Alarm Using the Alarms App on Apple Watch
@graph.description: Step-by-step guide to setting an alarm directly from the Alarms app on your Apple Watch.

step.name: Open the Alarms app
step.text: On your Apple Watch, open the Alarms app.

step.name: Tap the plus icon
step.text: Tap the + icon to create a new alarm.

step.name: Set the alarm time
step.text: Rotate the Digital Crown to adjust the hours and minutes. Ensure AM or PM is correct if using 12-hour format.

step.name: Confirm the alarm
step.text: Tap the green checkmark icon in the bottom-right corner to set the alarm.

keyPoints.title: Apple Watch as an Effective Alarm Clock
keyPoints.explanation: Since it's always on your wrist and vibrates, the Apple Watch is a reliable alternative to the iPhone for alarms, less likely to be missed.

keyPoints.title: Ways to Set an Alarm on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: You can set alarms on your Apple Watch either by using Siri voice commands or manually through the Alarms app.

keyPoints.title: Using Siri to Set Alarms
keyPoints.explanation: Activate Siri by saying 'Hey Siri' or holding the Digital Crown, then instruct it to set an alarm for your desired time.

keyPoints.title: Using the Alarms App
keyPoints.explanation: Open the Alarms app on your watch, tap the plus sign, set the time with the Digital Crown, and confirm to create a new alarm.

keyPoints.title: Managing and Customizing Alarms
keyPoints.explanation: You can change alarm times, turn off snooze, delete alarms, skip wake-up alarms, or set alarms to vibrate-only to suit your preferences.

title.rendered: How to Easily Delete Photo Albums on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Photos Are Safe: The most important thing to know is that deleting an album does not delete the photos inside it; they remain safely stored in your main photo library.
  • How to Delete: To delete an album you created, go to the Albums tab, tap “See All,” then “Edit,” and tap the red minus icon to remove it.
  • System Albums: You cannot delete the default albums that iOS creates automatically, such as “Recents,” “Screenshots,” “Favorites,” or the “People & Places” albums.
  • Shared Albums: For shared albums, only the original creator can delete the entire album. As a participant, you can only choose to “Unsubscribe” from it.
  • Synced Albums: Albums synced from a Mac or PC using Finder cannot be deleted on your iPhone; you must manage them on the computer where they originated.

The Photos app on iPhone makes it easy to organize pictures into albums, but over time, you may find yourself with too many albums. So, you may find it difficult to find the photos you need. Deleting unnecessary albums can help declutter your Photos app.

In this blog, I’ll share how to remove a photo album from your iPhone. However, before you start, it’s important to know that not all albums can be deleted. Let’s learn in detail!

Table of Contents
  • Things to know before deleting photo albums on iPhone
  • How to delete a photo album on your iPhone
    • Delete shared album from your iPhone
  • What happens when you delete an album?
  • Why can't I delete photo albums on my iPhone?

Things to know before deleting photo albums on iPhone

With iOS 18, the Photos app is completely redesigned and offers different sections. So, now you can’t see the system-generated albums such as Favorites, Live Photos, Recently Deleted, etc. These are available as Utilities.

Under the Albums section, you will see different app albums such as Instagram, WhatsApp, Snapchat, etc. Whichever app has access to save media on your iPhone creates an album automatically. And yes, you can delete them using the same method described below.

If you delete a shared album, it is removed across the devices of every participant as they are stored in iCloud. However, if any subscriber has downloaded a photo or video from the shared album that will remain on their photo library.

How to delete a photo album on your iPhone

If you’ve created an album manually and no longer need it, follow these steps to delete it:

  1. Open the Photos app on your iPhone.
  2. Scroll down and tap on Albums.
  3. Now, under the Personal tab, tap and hold the album you wish to remove.

  4. Select Delete Album and confirm your choice by tapping Delete Album.

That’s all! You can repeat the steps to remove the photo albums individually from your iPhone.

Tip If you only want to remove photos from the album and keep it as it is, open the album, tap and hold the image, and select Remove from Album.

Delete shared album from your iPhone

In the case of shared albums, only the creators can delete them. The process is similar:

  1. Open the Photos app and tap on Shared Albums. If you can’t see it, go to Albums and move to the Shared tab.
  2. Tap and hold the shared album and select Delete Album.
  3. Confirm by selecting Delete.

Do you not own the shared album but want to delete it from your iPhone? To remove yourself from a shared album, you need to unsubscribe it:

  1. Go to the Shared Albums section and open the album you wish to leave.
  2. Now, tap the three-dot icon at the top right corner.
  3. Tap Unsubscribe.

This removes the album from your device, but the owner and other members will still have access.

What happens when you delete an album?

  • The album disappears from your Photos app, but the pictures remain in the library and other albums they belong to. Only the album structure is removed.
  • Since deleting an album doesn’t remove the photos, it does not free up storage space. If you want to free up space on your iPhone, you need to manually delete the photos themselves.
  • If you use iCloud Photos, deleting an album on one Apple device (iPhone, iPad, or Mac) will delete it from all other devices linked to the same Apple ID.
  • If you delete a shared album that you created, it is removed from your iPhone and from everyone else’s devices who had access to it. The photos in the shared album will also be deleted unless someone has saved them to their own library.
  • If you were added to a shared album and you remove yourself, the album disappears from your iPhone, but the owner and other members will still have access to it.

Why can’t I delete photo albums on my iPhone?

Though removing an album from your iPhone is quite simple, you may run into some problems. Here are possible reasons:

  • If you previously synced albums from a Mac or PC, they cannot be deleted directly from your iPhone. To remove them, first, connect your iPhone to your computer. Now, open Finder (on macOS) or iTunes (on Windows) and deselect the albums you want to remove under the Photos sync settings. Finally, click Apply to update the changes.
  • You can’t delete a shared album that you didn’t create. If someone else created the shared album, you can only leave the album (see steps above). Sometimes, an album may not delete instantly if iCloud Photos is actively syncing. Wait for the sync to complete, then try again.

Signing off

Deleting photo albums on an iPhone is a great way to keep your photo library organized. By following these methods, you can easily access important memories while getting rid of clutter. Happy organizing!

You may find these helpful:

  • How to find and delete duplicate photos on iPhone
  • How to edit photos on iPhone
  • How to use extensions in the Photos app on iPhone and iPad
  • How the Shared Albums iCloud storage trick worked

mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.

@graph.name: How to Delete a Photo Album on Your iPhone
@graph.description: Step-by-step guide to deleting a photo album from the Photos app on your iPhone.

step.name: Open the Photos app
step.text: Open the Photos app on your iPhone.

step.name: Go to Albums
step.text: Scroll down and tap on Albums.

step.name: Select album to delete
step.text: Under the Personal tab, tap and hold the album you wish to remove.

step.name: Delete the album
step.text: Select Delete Album and confirm your choice by tapping Delete Album again.

@graph.name: How to Delete a Shared Album from Your iPhone
@graph.description: Step-by-step guide to deleting a shared album from the Photos app on your iPhone.

step.name: Open the Photos app
step.text: Open the Photos app and tap on Shared Albums. If you can’t see it, go to Albums and move to the Shared tab.

step.name: Select album to delete
step.text: Tap and hold the shared album and select Delete Album.

step.name: Confirm deletion
step.text: Confirm by selecting Delete.

keyPoints.title: Photos App Albums Management
keyPoints.explanation: The Photos app allows organizing pictures into albums, and deleting unnecessary ones can help keep your library decluttered, although some system-generated albums cannot be deleted.

keyPoints.title: Prerequisites Before Deleting Albums
keyPoints.explanation: Not all albums can be deleted directly from iPhone, especially those synced from a computer or created by other users in shared albums; understanding these limitations is essential.

keyPoints.title: How to Delete a Personal Album
keyPoints.explanation: To delete a manually created album, open the Photos app, navigate to Albums, select the album, and choose Delete Album to remove it from your device.

keyPoints.title: Managing Shared Albums
keyPoints.explanation: Shared albums can be deleted only by their creators, or you can unsubscribe if you're a participant, which removes the album from your device but doesn't affect access for others.

keyPoints.title: Impact of Deleting Albums and Troubleshooting
keyPoints.explanation: Deleting an album removes only its structure, not the photos, which stay in the library; issues with deletion often stem from prior sync settings or shared album permissions.

title.rendered: Apple’s Rumored $599 MacBook Could Launch in Late 2025

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple developing $599–$699 budget MacBook: Aimed at competing with Chromebooks, this marks Apple’s first affordable laptop push in more than ten years.
  • Possible A18 Pro chip instead of M-series: Using the iPhone 16 Pro’s processor could cut costs, but may limit performance compared to current MacBook chips.
  • Rumored 12.9-inch lightweight design: Expected to ship in Silver, Blue, Pink, and Yellow, offering a more colorful, portable option for budget-conscious buyers.
  • Production starting late 2025 or early 2026: Could boost MacBook sales by up to 40% and bring in first-time or cost-sensitive customers.
  • Lower price may mean trade-offs: Expect reduced pro-level features compared to M-series MacBooks, making it better suited for everyday rather than heavy creative work.

Apple is reportedly developing a new entry-level MacBook priced as low as $599, with a possible debut before the end of next year. The move would mark the company’s first major push into the budget laptop segment in over a decade.

What We Know So Far

Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo first hinted at Apple’s work on a more affordable MacBook, describing it as a 13-inch-class device aimed squarely at competing with Chromebooks and revitalizing Mac sales. While Kuo did not speculate on cost, DigiTimes now suggests a price range between $599 and $699, cheaper than the base iPhone 16.

For comparison, Apple’s least expensive 13-inch MacBook Air currently starts at $999 in the U.S., or $899 with the education discount. A price cut of that scale would be a clear shift in Apple’s laptop strategy.

Powered by the A18 Pro Chip

If DigiTimes’ pricing claim is accurate, the new MacBook is unlikely to carry Apple’s M-series processors. Instead, reports point to the A18 Pro as having the same chip inside the iPhone 16 Pro, making its first appearance in a Mac.

This would lower costs but also mean trade-offs. Compared to the M-series, the A18 Pro offers fewer CPU and GPU cores, supports less memory, and lacks Thunderbolt connectivity. Buyers should expect standard USB-C ports instead of the high-speed connections found on other Macs.

Design and Display

Rumors indicate the laptop will feature a 12.9-inch display, slightly smaller than the MacBook Air’s 13.6-inch screen. Kuo also predicts an ultra-thin, lightweight chassis, with finishes in Silver, Blue, Pink, and Yellow — reportedly echoing the color palette of the upcoming iPhone 17 Air.

Production and Release Timeline

DigiTimes reports that most components are expected to hit mass production in the third quarter of 2025, with final assembly taking place at Quanta’s facilities in the fourth quarter. This schedule could put the launch in late 2025 or early 2026, aligning with Kuo’s earlier forecasts.

Market Impact

At the rumored price, shipments could hit 5 to 7 million units annually, which would push Apple’s total MacBook sales up by as much as 40% from the current 17 to 18 million. A more aggressive entry-level offering could also lure budget-conscious buyers away from Chromebooks, especially in education markets.

The Big Question

A MacBook under $600 would be Apple’s most affordable laptop in years, lowering the barrier for students, first-time buyers, and those switching from Windows or ChromeOS. The lack of Thunderbolt might be a dealbreaker for professional workflows, but for basic computing, the trade-off could be acceptable.

Would Apple’s cheapest MacBook in years tempt you, or would the compromises be too steep? Drop your thoughts in the comments.

mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.

title.rendered: How to Free Up Storage Space on Your Apple Watch

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • The Storage Limit: The Apple Watch has fixed, non-expandable storage (e.g., 32GB or 64GB), which makes actively managing your available space essential for optimal performance.
  • How to Check: To see what’s using your space, either go to Settings > General > Storage on the watch itself or use the Watch app on your paired iPhone.
  • Managing Apps: The quickest way to free up significant space is to delete any third-party apps you no longer use, either directly from the watch or via the iPhone.
  • Managing Media: Reduce the biggest storage hogs by deleting downloaded music, podcasts, and audiobooks, and by limiting the number of photos synced from your iPhone.
  • Other Data: To clear out cached data, try restarting your Apple Watch. You can also delete old workout data from the Health app to reclaim additional storage.

Unlike on iPhones, you don’t get multiple storage options for Apple Watches. While the premium Apple Watch Ultra models come with 64GB storage capacity, the latest regular models still have a 32GB capacity.

If you are a power user, this limited storage space can quickly fill up, leaving you wanting more. Although you can’t expand your Apple Watch’s limited storage, there are ways to free it up. This guide details multiple ways to free up space on your Apple Watch.

Table of Contents
  • Check the storage space on an Apple Watch
  • 7 ways to free up storage space on an Apple Watch
    • 1. Delete unused apps
    • 2. Delete unnecessary photos
    • 3. Remove downloaded music and podcasts
    • 4. Clear cached data and system files
    • 5. Remove old messages and call history
    • 6. Delete old workout data if no longer needed
    • 7. Disable automatic app installation

Check the storage space on an Apple Watch

Before we look at what you can remove from your Apple Watch to reclaim the lost storage space, it is crucial to identify what’s consuming the most space. Once you do this, you will know what exactly you need to delete. Here’s how you to check your Apple Watch’s storage space.

Directly on your Apple Watch:

  • Go to Settings → General → Storage. Here, you will see a breakdown of storage usage, including apps, media, and system files.

Using the Watch app:

  • Open the Watch app and go to General → Storage. Check how much storage space is free and what’s consuming the most space.

7 ways to free up storage space on an Apple Watch

Now that you know what’s consuming the most space, it’s time to act. Here’s what you can do.

1. Delete unused apps

There is no point in having apps you no longer need or use installed on your Apple Watch. Not only will these apps make finding other apps harder, but they will also consume precious storage space. Here’s how you can remove them:

Directly on your Apple Watch:

  • In Grid View, tap and hold the app you want to remove and tap the X button that appears in the top-left corner of the app icon.

  • In List View, swipe left on the app you want to remove and tap the trash icon.

Via the Watch app:

  • Open the Watch app, scroll down, and select the app you want to delete. Then, toggle off Show App on Apple Watch.

2. Delete unnecessary photos

Your Apple Watch, by default, syncs a limited number of photos from the paired iPhone to it. While having access to photos on your wrist can be useful at times, viewing those photos on such a tiny screen isn’t always practical.

As such, if you never use this functionality, you can disable photo sync completely. Alternatively, you can limit it to a maximum of 25 photos to retain access to the ones you need regularly.

Using the Watch App:

  1. Open the Watch app, scroll down, and tap on Photos.
  2. Here, toggle off Photo Syncing.

  3. Alternatively, you can tap on Photos Limit and select 25 Photos on the subsequent menu.

3. Remove downloaded music and podcasts

If you previously added music or podcasts to your Apple Watch, but you don’t access them as regularly as you anticipated, it’s wise to remove them and reclaim the space.

Remove music directly on your Apple Watch:

  • Open the Music app and head to Library → Downloaded. Swipe left on the song you wish to remove and tap Delete.

Remove music via the Watch app:

  1. Open the Watch app, scroll down, and tap on Music.
  2. Here, toggle off Recent Music under Automatically Add.
  3. Next, tap on Edit in the top right corner.
  4. Now, tap the – (minus) sign before the music you want to remove.

Remove podcasts via the Watch app

  • On the Watch app, select Podcasts. Select the podcast you wish to remove under Shows and tap Remove Show.

4. Clear cached data and system files

Like the iPhone, the Apple Watch also stores temporary files, system logs, and cache data that may take up space. While Apple offers no direct way to manually clear the cache on the Apple Watch, restarting or unpairing your Apple Watch can help.

Here’s how you can restart your Apple Watch:

  • Press and hold the Side button and tap the power icon in the top-right corner. Drag the Slide to Power Off slider to the right and give the watch a few seconds to turn off. Then, press and hold the Side button to turn it on again.

If restarting your Apple Watch does not help, you can unpair it and pair it again, as it can help clear the junk. Here’s how:

  • Open the Watch app and go to All Watches. Tap the i button and tap Unpair Apple Watch.

Once the unpairing is complete, you can pair your Apple Watch again as new.

5. Remove old messages and call history

Due to the same Apple Account, text messages and call logs stored on your iPhone are also stored on your Apple Watch, which can take up unnecessary space over time. So, deleting old messages and call history can be wise as it can free up storage. Also, any text messages and call logs you delete from your Apple Watch will not be removed from your iPhone, making it a safe choice. Here’s how you can do this.

To delete messages:

  • Open the Messages app. Swipe left on the conversation you wish to delete and tap the trash icon.

To delete your recent calls:

  • Open the Phone app and go to Recents. Swipe left on the call you wish to delete and tap the X button.

6. Delete old workout data if no longer needed

Over time, all your workout and activity data, including steps, calories, heart rate, and workout history, are stored on your Apple Watch. While the data helps you track your fitness progress, it can consume considerable storage, especially if you have a long history of workouts.

While there is no direct way of deleting this data from the Apple Watch, you can remove old workout and activity data through the Health app on the paired iPhone. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Health app on your iPhone and tap the profile icon in the top-right corner.
  2. tap on Devices under Privacy.

  3. Now, locate and select your Apple Watch from the list of devices.
  4. Scroll down and tap Delete All Data from [your name Apple Watch].

7. Disable automatic app installation

When automatic app installation is enabled, any app you install on the paired iPhone is automatically downloaded and installed on the Apple Watch, granted the watch supports it. So, it would be better to disable automatic app installation because not all your apps need to be on your Apple Watch.

Directly on your Apple Watch:

  • Go to Settings → App Store and toggle off Automatic Downloads.

Via the Watch app:

  • Open the Watch app and go to App Store. Toggle off Automatic Downloads.

Once done, you can manually install apps on your Apple Watch.

Wrapping up…

Regularly managing and keeping your Apple Watch storage organized allows for smoother performance and lets you install new apps, download new music and podcasts, and more without storage issues. So go ahead, check what’s occupying your Apple Watch’s storage, and get rid of the stuff you don’t need.

You can comment below if you still have some doubts, and we will be happy to help you.

  • How to empty trash on iPhone to free up space

mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.

aioseo_meta_data.description: Is your Apple Watch running low on storage? Here are seven effective ways to free up storage space on an Apple Watch.

keyPoints.title: Limited Storage Options on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Unlike iPhones, Apple Watch models only come with fixed storage capacities—64GB for Ultra and 32GB for regular models—making storage management crucial for power users.

keyPoints.title: How to Check Storage Usage on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: You can directly check your storage on the watch under Settings > General > Storage or via the Watch app on your iPhone to identify what’s consuming space.

keyPoints.title: Delete Unused Apps to Free Up Space
keyPoints.explanation: Removing apps you no longer need, either directly from the watch or through the Watch app, can reclaim significant storage and improve performance.

keyPoints.title: Manage Photos, Music, and Podcasts
keyPoints.explanation: Disabling photo sync, deleting downloaded music and podcasts, and limiting stored photos can dramatically reduce storage use on your Apple Watch.

keyPoints.title: Clear Cached Data and Manage Workout Data
keyPoints.explanation: Restarting or unpairing your watch can clear cache and system files, while removing old workout data through the Health app helps free additional space.

title.rendered: Will the iPhone 17 Lineup See a Price Hike?

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Potential price hike for iPhone 17: Analysts expect $50 to $100 higher prices, likely from new U.S. tariffs despite Apple’s cost-cutting moves.
  • Tariffs and trade policies driving costs: Import duties on China-made parts could push Apple to raise prices, though India assembly offsets some of the impact.
  • Storage tweaks may hide increases: Apple could follow the iPhone 15 Pro Max approach by starting at higher storage tiers to justify a higher base price.
  • Long streak of stable Pro pricing: Apple hasn’t raised the base iPhone Pro price in nearly 10 years, signaling caution in changing consumer price perception.
  • Trade policy uncertainty adds risk: Sudden tariff changes or expired exemptions could spike costs, forcing mid-cycle pricing changes despite supply chain optimizations.

iPhone 17 Could Break Apple’s Seven-Year Price Freeze

Apple has kept the starting price of its flagship Pro iPhone steady at $999 since the iPhone X in 2017, weathering inflation, chip shortages, and years of analyst warnings. That streak might end with the iPhone 17 lineup, as several industry watchers now believe a price hike is more likely than not.

Why 2025 Might Be Different

Jeff Pu of GF Securities says U.S. buyers should expect higher prices for iPhone 17 models, citing ongoing tariff risks. At present, Apple pays a 20% tariff on iPhones imported from China but avoids those fees on devices assembled in India. The company has shifted most U.S.-bound production to India, a move Tim Cook has confirmed publicly, but shifting trade policy could erode that advantage quickly.

Apple sidestepped price increases last year through expanded Indian assembly and temporary tariff exemptions. That buffer is not guaranteed to hold. Earlier this year, Chinese electronics faced a proposed 145% tariff before smartphones were excluded — an exemption that remains temporary. If it lapses, even a small portion of U.S.-made iPhones made in China could push costs higher.

What Analysts Are Predicting

Some Wall Street projections point to a $50 to $100 jump over current iPhone 16 prices. One rumor outlines a $50 increase for the iPhone 17 Air, Pro, and Pro Max, leaving the base iPhone 17 unchanged at $799.

That would set the lineup at:

  • iPhone 17: $799
  • iPhone 17 Air: $949
  • iPhone 17 Pro: $1,049
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max: $1,249

Apple could also mask a price change by altering storage configurations. This happened with the iPhone 15 Pro Max, which dropped the 128GB tier and began at 256GB for $1,199. A similar shift for the iPhone 17 Pro would allow Apple to raise the base price while claiming added value.

Reasons Prices Might Hold

Despite multiple opportunities, Apple has resisted raising the U.S. price of the base Pro model for nearly a decade, suggesting a deliberate effort to maintain key price points. Moving the Pro from $999 to $1,049 risks crossing a psychological threshold that could complicate the debut of the new Air model, especially if buyers already struggle to place it in the lineup.

While tariffs cost Apple an estimated billion dollars per quarter, much of that is absorbed rather than passed to customers. Indian assembly now covers most U.S. demand, cushioning the impact of China-specific tariffs. But if exemptions expire or new sector tariffs target electronics, that buffer could disappear quickly, forcing Apple’s hand.

For now, the most realistic read is that the iPhone 17 may cost more, but Apple has shown discipline in shielding customers from every added expense. Whether they hold that line in 2025 will depend less on product strategy and more on the unpredictability of U.S. trade policy.

Would a $50 jump on the iPhone 17 Pro make you rethink upgrading? Share your thoughts in the comments.

mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.

title.rendered: How to Change Featured Photos on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • New in iOS 18: The new iOS 18 update gives you significantly more control over your Featured Photos widget, allowing you to manually add, remove, or hide specific photos.
  • How Photos Are Chosen: Your iPhone automatically selects photos to feature based on an algorithm that recognizes important people, pets, special events, and your recent activity in the Photos app.
  • Manual Curation: You can manually remove any unwanted image from the widget by selecting the “Remove from Featured Photos” option. Favoriting photos can also influence their appearance.
  • Hiding People & Memories: For broader control, you can prevent a specific person from ever appearing in the widget or turn off certain types of Memories, like holiday events.
  • Best Practices: To improve the automatic selections, regularly organize your library by favoriting your best shots, deleting duplicates, and hiding photos you don’t want to see featured.

We all love seeing our favorite memories on the iPhone Home Screen thanks to the Photos widget. But what if you want to remove certain featured photos? Well, in iOS 18, Apple allows you to set, modify, or edit featured photos in a new way, giving users more control over what appears.

In this guide, I’ll show you how to change or remove certain featured photos on your iPhone in detail. So, let’s get started!

Table of Contents
  • How does the iPhone choose featured photos?
  • How to edit Featured Photos on your iPhone
    • Add Featured Photos
    • Remove images from Featured Photos
  • How to stop people, places, or Memories from showing in Featured Photos
    • Hide certain people
    • Turn off holiday Memories from appearing in Featured Photos
  • Tips for managing Featured Photos widget efficiently
  • Stop your iPhone from showing Featured Photos

How does the iPhone choose featured photos?

Apple’s Photos app automatically selects featured photos randomly. The system scans your photo library to curate images that it believes are visually appealing, meaningful, or recent. These images appear in the Photos widget and Memories or other recommended sections.

Here’s how your iPhone determines which photos to feature:

  • People and pets: If you frequently take pictures of certain individuals or pets, the system assumes they are important and highlights them. Additionally, marking a person as a favorite in the People album increases the chances of their photos being featured.
  • Memories and events: Apple prioritizes significant events like holidays, vacations, birthdays, and anniversaries. Suppose you have clicked multiple photos at a specific location or date. iOS may feature them as a Memory.
  • Recent additions to your library: Newly added or recently edited photos have a higher chance of being featured. If you frequently interact with an image (e.g., sharing, favoriting, or editing), iOS considers it more relevant.
  • Smart suggestions based on activity: Apple shows you photos in line with what you recently did. For instance, if you tend to take photos of the scenery while walking in the morning, similar images may be included. Or photos of places you frequently visit (such as your favorite coffee shop) could end up in recommendations.
  • Album and category preferences: If you often swipe through an album, like Pets, Travel or Family, iOS may feature photos from those collections. As I interact more with portrait shots, landscapes, or food photography, my iPhone adjusts the selections accordingly.

While Apple does a great job of picking the best shots for your Photos widget, sometimes it may not appeal to your preferences. But don’t worry! You can quickly change the featured photos and add the desired ones. Let’s look at how to do that next.

How to edit Featured Photos on your iPhone

Customizing images on your Photos widget is simple in iOS 18. First, I’ll show you steps to manually add featured photos.

Add Featured Photos

  1. Launch the Photos app and open the image you want to feature.
  2. Tap the heart icon to mark the photo as a favorite. The image will now appear in the Featured Photos widget and Memories.

Remove images from Featured Photos

  1. Open the Photos app and scroll down to the Featured Photos section.
  2. Tap the > icon next to it to view all the featured images.
  3. Scroll down and find the images you want to remove. Press and hold it and select Remove from Featured Photos. The photo will no longer be suggested as a featured image.

How to stop people, places, or Memories from showing in Featured Photos

Sometimes, your iPhone may feature photos of people or places that you’d rather not see. Fortunately, you can hide them specifically or entire memories from being selected.

Here’s how to customize and remove unwanted content from Featured Photos.

Hide certain people

  1. Go to the Photos app and open the image of the person you want to hide.
  2. Tap the three-dot icon at the top right corner.
  3. Select Feature This Person Less.
  4. You’ll be given the option to:
    • Feature This Person Less: This option removes their individual photos and videos from the Memories and Photos widget. However, their group images may still remain in featured suggestions.
    • Never Feature This Person: This completely removes the person from all featured sections.
  5. Tap Confirm to save your choice.

Turn off holiday Memories from appearing in Featured Photos

Apple’s Photos app automatically creates Memories based on your past travels and vacations. If you don’t want to see particular memories of your region on the Photos widget, follow these steps:

  1. Go to Settings on your iPhone and tap Apps at the bottom.
  2. Here, scroll down and select Photos.
  3. Toggle off Show Holiday Events.

It will turn off all memories that feature holiday events in your home country or region.

Tip If you want to undo your Feature Less choices, tap Reset People & Pets Suggestions and select Reset from here. Your iPhone will rescan your photo library and show you new suggestions including all people and pets.

Tips for managing Featured Photos widget efficiently

If you’d like to have more control over which images appear in your Featured Photos widget, here are some tips to help you organize and curate your picks:

  • Favorite important photos: Mark your best photos as Favorites in the Photos app. This ensures that meaningful or aesthetically pleasing images appear more frequently.
  • Regularly remove unwanted featured photos: As your photo library grows, your iPhone will show newer featured images. This prevents unnecessary images from being shown on your Home Screen.
  • Hide photos you don’t want featured: If you never want a photo to highlight, open the image, tap the three-dot icon and select Hide → Hide Photo. The image will move to the Hidden album and won’t appear in Featured Photos or Memories.
  • Keep your photo library organized: Regularly delete duplicates, blurry images, and screenshots to prevent unwanted selections.

By following these tips, you can fine-tune which images show up in your Featured Photos widget and Memories. This also makes your iPhone’s photo experience more personalized and enjoyable.

Stop your iPhone from showing Featured Photos

If you prefer not to have the featured photos section at all, you can turn it off:

  1. Go to Settings → Apps and select Photos.
  2. Scroll down to the Featured Content section and toggle off Show Featured Content.

This will stop all featured photos and Memories from automatically appearing on your iPhone.

Signing off…

Controlling which images show up in the Featured Photos widget is easier than ever in iOS 18. Regardless of what method you choose, make sure the home screen shows the moments that are most relevant to you. What are your thoughts on this new feature? Let me know in the comments below!

mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.
