mainEntity.name: Can I change the download location for each file in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On Mac, Yes! You can set Safari to ask where to save each file. Just go to Safari > Settings > General, then choose Ask for each download for the file download location. On iPhone or iPad, No. Safari doesn’t let you choose a folder for each file. You can only set one default download location.

mainEntity.name: Will changing the download location affect iCloud syncing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it can. If you choose a folder inside iCloud Drive, your downloads will sync across your Apple devices. If you pick a folder that’s not in iCloud Drive (like "On My iPhone" or a local folder on Mac), the files will stay only on that device and won’t sync with others.

mainEntity.name: Does this change affect other browsers like Chrome or Firefox?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Changing Safari’s download location only affects Safari. Other browsers like Chrome, Firefox, or Edge have their own separate settings for where to save downloads—you’ll need to adjust those separately in each browser’s settings.

@graph.name: How to Connect Bluetooth Mouse to iPad
@graph.description: Pair a Bluetooth mouse with your iPad through the Bluetooth settings for easier navigation and control.

step.name: Open Bluetooth settings
step.text: On your iPad, go to Settings and tap Bluetooth.

itemListElement.text: Open the Settings app.
Select Bluetooth.

step.name: Turn on Bluetooth
step.text: Enable Bluetooth and allow your iPad to scan for nearby devices.

itemListElement.text: Toggle the Bluetooth switch on.
Wait for your mouse to appear under Other Devices.

step.name: Pair the mouse
step.text: Tap the mouse name when it appears under Other Devices to connect.

itemListElement.text: Select your mouse from the list.

step.name: Confirm connection
step.text: Once paired, your mouse will appear in the My Devices section.

itemListElement.text: Look under My Devices to confirm the connection.

@graph.name: How to Enable AssistiveTouch on iPad
@graph.description: Turn on AssistiveTouch on your iPad to enable touch-based navigation and accessibility features, including a virtual trackpad and click sounds.

step.name: Open Accessibility settings
step.text: Go to Settings on your iPad, then select Accessibility from the list.

itemListElement.text: Open the Settings app.
Tap Accessibility.

step.name: Turn on AssistiveTouch
step.text: Find AssistiveTouch and toggle it on to enable accessibility gestures and features.

itemListElement.text: Locate AssistiveTouch.
Turn the toggle on.

step.name: Enable Virtual Trackpad (optional)
step.text: Scroll down, tap Virtual Trackpad, and turn it on for easier navigation if your mouse wheel is broken.

itemListElement.text: Tap Virtual Trackpad.
Turn it on.

step.name: Enable Sound on Click
step.text: Go back to AssistiveTouch settings, find Sound on Click, and toggle it on to hear a sound when clicking the mouse button.

itemListElement.text: Locate Sound on Click.
Turn it on.

@graph.name: How to Customize Pointer Options on iPad
@graph.description: Adjust pointer settings on your iPad to change its appearance, behavior, and scrolling speed for a personalized navigation experience.

step.name: Open Accessibility settings
step.text: Go to the Settings app on your iPad and tap Accessibility.

itemListElement.text: Open Settings.
Select Accessibility.

step.name: Access Pointer Control
step.text: Scroll down and tap Pointer Control to view customization options.

itemListElement.text: Scroll down.
Tap Pointer Control.

step.name: Customize pointer settings
step.text: Modify settings like Increase Contrast, Automatically Hide Pointer, Pointer Animations, Scrolling Speed, and more according to your preference.

itemListElement.text: Adjust visual appearance options.
Change pointer behavior and speed.

@graph.name: How to Assign Custom Actions to Mouse Buttons on iPad
@graph.description: Customize mouse button functions on your iPad through AssistiveTouch settings to perform quick actions with a single click.

step.name: Access Touch settings
step.text: Open Settings on your iPad, go to Accessibility, and tap Touch.

itemListElement.text: Open Settings.
Go to Accessibility → Touch.

step.name: Go to connected devices
step.text: Navigate to AssistiveTouch, then tap Devices under the Connected Devices section.

itemListElement.text: Tap AssistiveTouch.
Select Devices.

step.name: Open customization menu
step.text: Select your connected mouse and tap Customize Additional Buttons.

itemListElement.text: Tap your mouse name.
Select Customize Additional Buttons.

step.name: Click the mouse button
step.text: When prompted, press the mouse button you want to customize.

itemListElement.text: Click the desired mouse button.

step.name: Assign an action
step.text: Choose your preferred action from the menu to assign it to the selected button. Repeat for other buttons if needed.

itemListElement.text: Select an action from the menu.
Repeat for additional buttons.

keyPoints.title: Requirements for Using a Mouse with iPad
keyPoints.explanation: To connect a mouse to an iPad, it must be running iPadOS 13.4 or later, and you need a compatible mouse, either wired or Bluetooth.

keyPoints.title: Connecting a Bluetooth Mouse to iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Enable Bluetooth on your iPad, put your mouse in pairing mode, and tap on its name in the Bluetooth settings to connect.

keyPoints.title: Connecting a Wired Mouse to iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Use a matching port and possibly a dongle (USB-C or Lightning to USB Adapter) to connect a wired mouse if the ports do not match.

keyPoints.title: Configuring Mouse Settings on iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Adjust mouse settings by enabling AssistiveTouch, customizing pointer options, and assigning actions to mouse buttons through the Accessibility menu.

keyPoints.title: Benefits of Using a Mouse on iPad
keyPoints.explanation: A mouse enhances editing, navigation, copy-pasting, and multitasking capabilities on an iPad, making it more versatile for work and entertainment.

title.rendered: How to Clear Cache on Chrome: Desktop, iPhone, and Android

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Chrome cache speeds up loading but can break pages when outdated files conflict with newer site content or designs.
  • Cache vs cookies vs history: Cache stores assets, cookies remember preferences, and history tracks sites; clearing cache won’t erase passwords or bookmarks.
  • Clear cache in Chrome desktop via Settings or shortcut: Use Ctrl+Shift+Del, pick time range, uncheck extras, then delete to refresh stored site data.
  • Fix a single site using Developer Tools: Right-click the refresh icon and select ‘Empty Cache and Hard Reload’ to troubleshoot specific loading problems.
  • Avoid frequent clearing to maintain speed: Clear cache when needed but don’t overdo it, as emptying too often slows initial page loads unnecessarily.

We’ve all been there. A webpage just won’t load right. Images look broken, buttons don’t work, or a website feels stuck in the past, even after updates. Often, the culprit behind such issues is cache. Clearing it can fix these glitches and make Chrome feel fresh again. Here’s what browser cache is and how you can remove it from Chrome.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Cache in Google Chrome?
  • How to Clear Cache on Chrome for Desktop (Windows and Mac)
    • Clear Cache on Only One Site
  • How to Clear Cache on Chrome for iPhone and iPad
  • How to Clear Cache on Chrome for Android
  • How Often Should You Clear Chrome Cache?

What Is Cache in Google Chrome?

Chrome’s cache acts like quick memory for websites. It saves parts of pages so they load faster the next time you visit. But if these saved files become outdated or corrupted, websites can start behaving unexpectedly.

In case you’re wondering, cache is different from other browser data.

Cache vs Cookies vs History:

  • Cache stores parts of websites like images, scripts, and layouts to help them load faster. However, outdated cache can make sites appear broken.
  • Cookies remember user-specific details like logins, preferences, and shopping cart items. Clearing them may sign you out of websites.
  • Browsing history is simply a list of websites you’ve visited. Deleting it removes the record but does not affect logins or saved data.

When you clear Chrome’s cache, only temporary files are removed. Your bookmarks and passwords remain safe, though you might need to log in again on some websites.

How to Clear Cache on Chrome for Desktop (Windows and Mac)

Chrome on desktop gives you more control over what and how much you want to clear. You can remove all cached files or limit the removal to a specific time range.

Steps:

  1. Open Chrome on your Windows PC or Mac.
  2. Click the three-dot menu (top-right corner).
  3. Go to Delete Browsing Data
  4. Choose the Time range (Last hour, Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 4 weeks, or even All Time).
  5. Uncheck everything except Cached images and files. (Optionally, check Cookies if you want to log out of sites.)
  6. Finally, click Delete data.

Pro Tip: Use a shortcut to open the clear cache window faster:

  • On Windows: Ctrl + Shift + Delete
  • On Mac: Command (⌘) + Shift + Delete

Related: How to Clear Safari Cache on Mac

Clear Cache on Only One Site

Sometimes, only one website causes problems. Here’s how to clear the cache for that specific site:

  1. Open Chrome and visit the site.
  2. Click on three-dot menu > More tools > Developer Tools (Alternatively, press F12 on Windows or Option + Command (⌘) + I on Mac).
  3. Right‑click the refresh button.
  4. Select Empty Cache and Hard Reload to clear only that site’s cache. 

How to Clear Cache on Chrome for iPhone and iPad

Clearing cache on Chrome for iOS is slightly different but just as easy.

Steps:

  1. Open the Chrome app.
  2. Tap the three-dot menu (bottom-right).
  3. Select Delete browsing data. (If it’s not available, you can go to Settings > Privacy and security)
  4. Choose the Time range (Last 15 minutes, Last hour, Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 4 weeks, or even All Time).
  5. Now tap on Browsing data. 
  6. Uncheck everything except Cached Images and Files (and Cookies if needed). 
  7. Once done, tap on Confirm and then Delete data.

Related: How to Clear Safari Cache on iPhone and iPad

How to Clear Cache on Chrome for Android

The process on Android is similar to iOS, with a few added steps for system-level cache clearing.

From the Chrome app:

  1. Open Chrome.
  2. Tap the three-dot menu (top-right).
  3. Select Delete browsing data 
  4. Select More options.
  5. Choose the Time range (Last 15 minutes, Last hour, Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 4 weeks, or even All Time). 
  6. Uncheck everything except Cached Images and Files (and Cookies if needed). 
  7. Tap Delete data.
  8. Confirm by tapping Delete again in the pop-up.

From device settings (for deeper cleaning):

  1. Go to Settings > Apps > Chrome.
  2. Tap Storage & cache.
  3. Choose Clear cache.

How Often Should You Clear Chrome Cache?

You don’t need to clear cache daily. Do it when:

  • Webpages load incorrectly or appear broken.
  • A site doesn’t reflect recent updates.
  • Chrome starts feeling slow or laggy.
  • You want to free up storage space.
Note Over-clearing cache means Chrome will need to re-download everything, making the first visit to websites slower.

FAQs

Is there a way to auto-clear cache in Chrome?

Yes, you can use Chrome extensions or browse in Incognito Mode, which doesn’t save cache or cookies.

Does clearing cache log me out?

No, unless you also clear cookies. Cache alone won’t log you out.

Does clearing cache delete passwords?

No. Passwords remain safe unless you manually select the “Passwords” option while clearing data.

Related articles worth reading:

  • Safari vs. Chrome: Which browser is better for iPhone, iPad, and Mac
  • How to Turn Off Google AI Overviews on Desktop and Mobile
  • Chrome for iOS Adds Secure Work and Personal Account Switch
  • How to Remove Search Marquis from Mac? (Complete Guide)

mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take for the Explore page to learn my interests again?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no set timeframe. Instagram’s algorithm typically takes a few days to a week to adjust, depending on how actively you engage with new content. Consistently liking, commenting, and following accounts aligned with your interests speeds up the process. If you’re still seeing old content, keep marking it as Not Interested to refine the feed faster.

mainEntity.name: Why does my Explore page show things I don’t like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Instagram’s Explore page is based on your past activity, likes, saves, searches, and posts you interact with. If you engage with something by mistake or your interests change, the algorithm might still show related content.

mainEntity.name: What is the fastest way to clear my Instagram Explore page?

acceptedAnswer.text: Using the built-in Reset suggested content settings is the best way to go. This will wipe your current suggestions so Instagram can build your feed from scratch.

mainEntity.name: Does clearing my cache reset my Explore page on iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing your cache will not directly reset your Instagram Explore page. However, it removes the old temporary files which may give you a fresh start.

mainEntity.name: What happens when I click "Not Interested" on Instagram?

acceptedAnswer.text: Instagram hides that post and reduces similar content in your Explore page over time.

mainEntity.name: Can I undo a reset of my suggested posts?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Once you reset, your old suggestions are gone, and Instagram starts learning your interest like the first time.

mainEntity.name: Will resetting my Explore page affect my main feed?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your main feed stays the same because it’s based on accounts you follow, not Explore suggestions. Both follows different algorithms to curate content.

mainEntity.name: Can I change the download location for each file in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On Mac, Yes! You can set Safari to ask where to save each file. Just go to Safari > Settings > General, then choose Ask for each download for the file download location. On iPhone or iPad, No. Safari doesn’t let you choose a folder for each file. You can only set one default download location.

mainEntity.name: Will changing the download location affect iCloud syncing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it can. If you choose a folder inside iCloud Drive, your downloads will sync across your Apple devices. If you pick a folder that’s not in iCloud Drive (like "On My iPhone" or a local folder on Mac), the files will stay only on that device and won’t sync with others.

mainEntity.name: Does this change affect other browsers like Chrome or Firefox?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Changing Safari’s download location only affects Safari. Other browsers like Chrome, Firefox, or Edge have their own separate settings for where to save downloads—you’ll need to adjust those separately in each browser’s settings.

blockGraphs.question: Is there a way to auto-clear cache in Chrome?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes, you can use Chrome extensions or browse in Incognito Mode, which doesn't save cache or cookies.

blockGraphs.question: Does clearing cache log me out?
blockGraphs.answer: No, unless you also clear cookies. Cache alone won't log you out.

blockGraphs.question: Does clearing cache delete passwords?
blockGraphs.answer: No. Passwords remain safe unless you manually select the “Passwords” option while clearing data.

keyPoints.title: Understanding Browser Cache in Chrome
keyPoints.explanation: Chrome's cache stores website components like images and scripts to enable faster loading on revisits, but outdated cache can cause display issues.

keyPoints.title: Difference Between Cache, Cookies, and History
keyPoints.explanation: Cache saves parts of web pages for speed, cookies store user preferences and logins, while history is a record of visited sites; clearing cache does not remove passwords or bookmarks.

keyPoints.title: How to Clear Cache on Chrome Desktop
keyPoints.explanation: Access Chrome's 'Delete Browsing Data' menu, select the desired time range, uncheck unnecessary options, and click 'Delete data' to clear cache, with shortcuts for speed.

keyPoints.title: Clearing Cache for a Single Website
keyPoints.explanation: Use Chrome Developer Tools to right-click the refresh button and select 'Empty Cache and Hard Reload' for fixing issues with specific sites.

keyPoints.title: Regular Cache Maintenance and Safety Tips
keyPoints.explanation: Clear cache when sites malfunction or appear outdated, but avoid over-clearing to prevent slow initial load times; cache clearing won't log you out or delete passwords.

title.rendered: How to import passwords from other apps into new Apple Passwords

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple Passwords now supports CSV imports on macOS Sequoia so you can switch from third-party managers like Chrome or 1Password with secure syncing via iCloud.
  • You’ll need macOS Sequoia and iCloud Keychain to import passwords, and your old manager must support CSV export to start the migration.
  • Exporting passwords from browsers like Chrome is manual—you’ll save them as a CSV file and store it locally for the import step.
  • Import directly in the new Passwords app for Mac by verifying your identity and selecting the CSV file, which gets securely stored in iCloud Keychain.
  • Delete the CSV file after import to avoid leaks since it’s unencrypted and could expose all saved credentials if left on your Mac.

Previously, third-party password managers were best to securely save your passwords. However, with iOS 18, Apple has launched a dedicated Passwords app to offer a seamless and secure experience across all your devices. If you have used third-party password managers, here’s how to import your old passwords to the Apple Passwords app.

Requirements to migrate passwords to Apple Passwords app

Before you begin moving your passwords to the Apple Passwords app, make sure you have everything you need.

  • At the time of writing, Apple only allows users to import passwords into the Passwords app on a Mac running macOS Sequoia or later. If you don’t have a Mac, you won’t be able to migrate passwords directly, but you can still import them to Safari on your iPhone or iPad (explained later in this guide).
  • Apple Passwords works best when you enable iCloud Keychain, which allows your saved passwords to sync across all your Apple devices, including iPhones, iPads, and even Windows computers (via the iCloud Passwords app).
  • Export your passwords from your current password manager into a CSV (Comma-Separated Values) file format. This file stores your saved usernames and passwords in a simple format that can be transferred to another service.

If you don’t know how to export passwords from your current password manager, don’t worry! The next section of this guide will show you how to do it step by step.

How to export passwords from third-party password managers

Exporting your passwords is a straightforward process. Here’s how to do it using Google Chrome as an example:

  1. Launch the Google Chrome browser on your computer.
  2. Click on the three dots located in the upper right corner of the browser window.
  3. Navigate to Settings → Autofill and passwords → Google Passwords Manager.

  4. It will open a new tab. Go to the Settings section.
  5. Next to Export passwords, select Download file.

  6. Confirm the action by authenticating Touch ID when prompted.
  7. Choose a secure location on your computer to save the exported CSV file containing your passwords and click Save.

Note The steps may vary slightly depending on the password manager you are using. Always ensure that the exported CSV file is stored securely, as it contains sensitive information.

Import your old passwords into Apple Passwords app

Now that you have the CSV file, follow the steps below to import your passwords. As mentioned above, currently, the import feature is exclusive to Mac.

  1. Launch the Passwords app and verify your Touch ID.
  2. In the menu bar, select File → Import Passwords from File.

  3. Click on Choose File and locate the CSV file you exported earlier.

  4. Click the Import button.

After importing, all your saved passwords will appear on Apple Passwords app. You can now autofill the credentials and share them with your friends and family.

What to do after importing passwords to Apple Passwords app

Once you have successfully imported your passwords into Apple’s Passwords app, there are a few important steps you should take to ensure your passwords are secure and accessible across all your devices.

Immediately delete the CSV file

A CSV file physically contains all of your usernames and passwords in plain text, meaning anyone who has access to it can read your credentials. Because Apple Passwords encrypts your data at rest, you can delete the CSV file after import.

So, find the CSV file from the Finder on your Mac. Next, select it by right-clicking on it and choose Move to Trash. Finally, remember to empty the Trash so the file is permanently deleted.

For added protection, if you shared the CSV file using a cloud service (like Google Drive or Dropbox) delete it from both the cloud storage and any device where it was downloaded.

Sync passwords across your devices

Make sure iCloud Keychain is enabled to find your saved passwords on iPhone, iPad, and other Apple devices.

For Mac:

  1. Open System Settings.
  2. Click Apple ID (your name at the top).
  3. Go to iCloud → Passwords & Keychain.
  4. Toggle on Sync this Mac and hit Done.

For iPhone or iPad:

  1. Open Settings and tap your name at the top.
  2. Select iCloud and tap on Passwords.
  3. Turn on Sync this iPhone/iPad.

Once iCloud Keychain is enabled, all your saved passwords will be available in the Passwords app on all your Apple devices.

Access passwords on Windows using iCloud Passwords

If you use a Windows PC, you can still access your Apple Passwords by installing the iCloud for Windows app. This lets you use your saved credentials in Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge via the iCloud Passwords extension.

  1. Download and install the iCloud for Windows app from the Microsoft Store.
  2. Open the app and sign in with your Apple ID.
  3. Enable Passwords in the iCloud settings.
  4. Install the iCloud Passwords Chrome extension if you want autofill support in Chrome or Edge.

Once set up, you can access and use your Apple Passwords on your Windows computer.

Check and organize your imported passwords

After importing, it’s a good idea to review your saved passwords to ensure they were imported correctly.

  • Check for duplicates: If you notice multiple entries for the same login, you can manually delete extra entries.
  • Update outdated passwords: If you find old or weak passwords, update them using Apple’s built-in strong password generator feature.

How to transfer your old passwords to Safari on iPhone

If you don’t have a Mac and want to use Apple’s native password manager, you can do so. With the release of iOS 18.2, Apple has introduced the ability to import passwords directly into Safari using your iPhone. Here’s how:

Follow the steps outlined earlier to export your passwords into a CSV file on your iPhone.

  1. Open Settings on your iPhone.
  2. Scroll down and tap on Apps → Safari.

  3. Tap on Import located below History and Website Data.
  4. Select the Choose File option and locate the CSV file and follow the prompts to complete the import.

Now, you can autofill your passwords on websites via Safari directly from your iPhone.

Getting password importing errors? How to fix

Sometimes, you can encounter errors during the import process. Your Mac may show a conflict dialogue box with the number and list of passwords it failed to import.

Here, I will go through a few simpler solutions to make sure your passwords get migrated to the Passwords app:

  • Verify CSV format: Ensure that the CSV file is correctly formatted. The file should have headers like name, URL, username, and password.
  • Check for duplicates: Duplicate entries can cause issues. Review the CSV file and remove any duplicates before attempting the import again.
  • Update your software: Ensure that your Mac is running the latest version of macOS. Outdated software can lead to compatibility issues during the import process.
  • Manually add the password: If any certain passwords are not imported, you can add them manually on your Passwords app.

If problems persist, consider reaching out to Apple Support for further assistance.

Signing off

Importing your passwords into Apple’s Passwords app pushes your security even further while giving a good experience across all your Apple devices. I hope you have successfully moved your passwords with these steps. If you have any more issues, let me know in the comments below!

  • How to see your Wi-Fi passwords on iPhone or iPad
  • Export passwords from iCloud Keychain on Mac, iPhone, or iPad

mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take for the Explore page to learn my interests again?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no set timeframe. Instagram’s algorithm typically takes a few days to a week to adjust, depending on how actively you engage with new content. Consistently liking, commenting, and following accounts aligned with your interests speeds up the process. If you’re still seeing old content, keep marking it as Not Interested to refine the feed faster.

mainEntity.name: Why does my Explore page show things I don’t like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Instagram’s Explore page is based on your past activity, likes, saves, searches, and posts you interact with. If you engage with something by mistake or your interests change, the algorithm might still show related content.

mainEntity.name: What is the fastest way to clear my Instagram Explore page?

acceptedAnswer.text: Using the built-in Reset suggested content settings is the best way to go. This will wipe your current suggestions so Instagram can build your feed from scratch.

mainEntity.name: Does clearing my cache reset my Explore page on iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing your cache will not directly reset your Instagram Explore page. However, it removes the old temporary files which may give you a fresh start.

mainEntity.name: What happens when I click "Not Interested" on Instagram?

acceptedAnswer.text: Instagram hides that post and reduces similar content in your Explore page over time.

mainEntity.name: Can I undo a reset of my suggested posts?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Once you reset, your old suggestions are gone, and Instagram starts learning your interest like the first time.

mainEntity.name: Will resetting my Explore page affect my main feed?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your main feed stays the same because it’s based on accounts you follow, not Explore suggestions. Both follows different algorithms to curate content.

mainEntity.name: Can I change the download location for each file in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On Mac, Yes! You can set Safari to ask where to save each file. Just go to Safari > Settings > General, then choose Ask for each download for the file download location. On iPhone or iPad, No. Safari doesn’t let you choose a folder for each file. You can only set one default download location.

mainEntity.name: Will changing the download location affect iCloud syncing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it can. If you choose a folder inside iCloud Drive, your downloads will sync across your Apple devices. If you pick a folder that’s not in iCloud Drive (like "On My iPhone" or a local folder on Mac), the files will stay only on that device and won’t sync with others.

mainEntity.name: Does this change affect other browsers like Chrome or Firefox?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Changing Safari’s download location only affects Safari. Other browsers like Chrome, Firefox, or Edge have their own separate settings for where to save downloads—you’ll need to adjust those separately in each browser’s settings.

@graph.name: How to export passwords from third-party password managers
@graph.description: Learn how to securely export your saved passwords from third-party password managers using Google Chrome in just a few steps.

step.name: Open Chrome settings
step.text: Launch the Google Chrome browser on your computer and click the three dots in the top right corner.

itemListElement.text: Open Google Chrome on your computer.
Click on the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of the browser window.
Navigate to Settings, then select Autofill and passwords, and click on Google Password Manager.

step.name: Export passwords to a file
step.text: In the new tab, go to the Settings section, click Download file next to Export passwords, and authenticate using Touch ID when prompted.

itemListElement.text: Go to the Settings section in the Password Manager tab.
Click on Download file next to Export passwords.
Authenticate with Touch ID or your device password when prompted.

step.name: Save the exported password file
step.text: Choose a secure location on your computer to store the CSV file and click Save.

itemListElement.text: Select a safe and private location on your computer to save the file.
Click Save to download your passwords in a CSV format.

@graph.name: How to Import your old passwords into Apple Passwords app

step.name: Open the Passwords app
step.text: Launch the Passwords app on your Mac and confirm your identity using Touch ID or device password.

itemListElement.text: Open the Passwords app on your Mac.
Authenticate with Touch ID or enter your Mac password when prompted.
In the menu bar, click File and then select Import Passwords from File.

step.name: Choose the CSV file
step.text: Click on Choose File, find the exported CSV file from your computer, and select it.

itemListElement.text: Click the Choose File button.
Locate the exported CSV file on your computer and select it.

step.name: Import the passwords
step.text: Click the Import button to add your old passwords into the Apple Passwords app.

itemListElement.text: Click on the Import button to complete the import process.

keyPoints.title: Enhanced Security and Integration with Apple Passwords
keyPoints.explanation: Switching from third-party password managers to Apple Passwords improves security and offers seamless synchronization across all Apple devices.

keyPoints.title: Requirements for Migrating Passwords to Apple Passwords
keyPoints.explanation: Migration requires a Mac running macOS Sequoia or later and the export of passwords in CSV format from your current manager, with iCloud Keychain enabled for syncing.

keyPoints.title: How to Export Passwords from Third-Party Managers
keyPoints.explanation: Passwords can be exported as CSV files by accessing the passwords manager in browsers like Google Chrome and securely saving the file on your device.

keyPoints.title: Importing Passwords into Apple Passwords App on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: Users can import passwords by opening the Passwords app, verifying their identity, and selecting the CSV file to upload, after which passwords are securely stored.

keyPoints.title: Post-Import Security and Sync Measures
keyPoints.explanation: After importing, delete the CSV file to protect sensitive data, and enable iCloud Keychain to ensure your passwords are synchronized and accessible across all Apple devices.

title.rendered: Forgot Screen Time Passcode? How to Reset It Without Data Loss

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple ID reset works on iOS 13.4 or later by tapping “Forgot Passcode” and entering your Apple ID to create a new Screen Time code.
  • Restoring from old backups may remove passcode if the backup was made before Screen Time was enabled, but this erases recent data.
  • Apple Support can unlock Screen Time if needed but you’ll need proof of purchase or ownership for them to help.
  • Avoid future lockouts with simple safeguards like enabling Apple ID recovery and not using the same PIN as your device unlock code.
  • Third-party unlock tools usually wipe your data, and Apple’s built-in methods are safer if you want to preserve settings and content.

We’ve all been there. You set a Screen Time passcode months ago to keep yourself (or your kids) off certain apps, and now it’s long forgotten. Every attempt to guess feels like playing a dangerous game because too many wrong tries lock you out for longer.

The good news? You don’t need to wipe your iPhone clean. Apple has built-in methods to reset your Screen Time passcode without losing any data. Let’s go step by step.

Table of Contents
  • What Is the Screen Time Passcode and Why It's Important
  • Things to Know Before You Begin
  • Method 1: Reset Screen Time Passcode Using Apple ID
    • Change Screen Time Passcode on a Child's Device
  • Method 2: Restore from a Backup (Advanced Users)
  • Method 3: Contact Apple Support for Assistance
  • Tips to Avoid Screen Time Passcode Issues in the Future

What Is the Screen Time Passcode and Why It’s Important

Screen Time is a feature on iPhones and iPads that tracks your device usage. It shows app activity, pickups, and allows you to set limits using tools like App Limits and Downtime.

To secure these settings, Apple uses a separate Screen Time passcode. This passcode prevents anyone from disabling limits or modifying restrictions without authorization. Parents commonly use it to prevent kids from bypassing content and app limits.

You can change or remove it anytime in Settings > Screen Time > Change Screen Time Passcode. But since it’s different from your primary unlock code, it’s easy to forget, especially if it was set a long time ago or on another device.

Important Avoid guessing repeatedly. Too many incorrect attempts will increase the lockout duration. That’s why Apple’s recovery methods are the safest way to reset the passcode.

Also Read: 15 Ways to Fix Screen Time on iPhone When It’s Not Working

Things to Know Before You Begin

Before attempting to reset the passcode, keep the following in mind:

  • Apple ID and password: You’ll need the same Apple ID that was used when Screen Time was initially set up.
  • Latest iOS version: Update your iPhone or iPad to the latest iOS version for compatibility.
  • Backup your device: While these steps typically don’t erase data, backing up is always a smart precaution.

Method 1: Reset Screen Time Passcode Using Apple ID

This is the easiest and most reliable option if your device runs iOS 13.4 or later.

  1. Open Settings > Screen Time.
  2. Tap Change Screen Time Passcode → Tap again to confirm.
  3. Select Forgot Passcode?.
  4. Enter your Apple ID and password used to set up Screen Time. (This is different from your device Apple ID)
  5. Create a new Screen Time passcode and confirm it.

If Share Across Devices is enabled, the new passcode will automatically sync across all your Apple devices.

Change Screen Time Passcode on a Child’s Device

If you’re using Family Sharing and manage your child’s Screen Time:

  1. On the family organiser’s device, open Settings > Screen Time.
  2. Scroll to the child’s name under Family.
  3. Tap Change Screen Time Passcode and then confirm.
  4. Authenticate with Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode.
  5. Enter and confirm the new Screen Time passcode.

Method 2: Restore from a Backup (Advanced Users)

If you can’t use your Apple ID, your only option is to restore from a backup.

Important If the backup includes the Screen Time passcode, restoring it will bring the passcode back. Use a backup created before setting the passcode, if available.

Here’s how:

  1. Connect your iPhone to a Mac or PC and open Finder (macOS Catalina or later) or iTunes (macOS Mojave or Windows).
  2. Make an Encrypted Backup to keep your app data, Wi-Fi settings, and health data safe.
  3. Once the backup is complete, choose Restore iPhone in Finder or iTunes to erase the device and remove the passcode.
  4. When the device restarts, follow the setup steps and choose Restore from Backup.
  5. Select a backup made before the Screen Time passcode was set. Restoring a backup created afterward will keep the passcode in place.

Once restored, your device will reboot with all your data. You can now create a new Screen Time passcode or leave it off entirely.

Method 3: Contact Apple Support for Assistance

If neither method works, perhaps you don’t have access to the Apple ID, or all backups include the passcode. Apple Support is your next best option.

Be prepared to provide proof of ownership or purchase.

They will guide you through the official recovery process step-by-step.

Alternatively, you can choose to factory reset your iPhone and start fresh. Just remember: this will erase all data, so back up important files to another device first.

Tips to Avoid Screen Time Passcode Issues in the Future

Once you’ve reset the passcode, here are a few tips to avoid forgetting it again:

  • Enable Apple ID Recovery so you can reset the passcode easily in the future.
  • Save it in a secure password manager like iCloud Keychain.
  • Avoid reusing your device PIN as your Screen Time passcode; it’s less secure and more predictable.

Forgetting your Screen Time passcode is frustrating, but you don’t have to lose everything. In most cases, your Apple ID can help you reset it with ease. And if that doesn’t work, Finder/iTunes or Apple Support will help you recover access, without any data loss.

FAQs

Can third-party apps help reset Screen Time?

Yes, apps like Stellar Toolkit and iMyFone LockWiper can remove it, but they often erase data. Apple’s built-in methods are safer and more reliable.

Is the Screen Time passcode the same as my iPhone unlock PIN?

No. The Screen Time passcode only protects Screen Time settings, not device unlocking.

Can I remove Screen Time without an Apple ID?

No. Without the Apple ID or a backup that predates the passcode, you’ll need to contact Apple Support for help.

  • How to setup and use Screen Distance on iPhone and iPad
  • How to use Screen Time on Mac: A detailed guide
  • How to reset your iPhone passcode if your forgot it

mainEntity.name: How do I leave Family Sharing on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you’re 13 years and older, you can leave the group from Settings > Family > [your name] > Stop Using Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data if I leave my family group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your personal data stays safe, but you lose access to shared content like calendars, photo albums, and reminders, subscriptions, and services.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I see the “Leave Family” option?

acceptedAnswer.text: You might be under 13, have Screen Time on, or not be signed in to your Appe Account correctly.

mainEntity.name: Can a child under 13 leave Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the organizer must remove or transfer the child’s account.

mainEntity.name: Will my Apple Music subscription be canceled if I leave?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it was family-shared; you'll need to buy your own plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I rejoin Family Sharing after leaving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the organizer invites you again or you start/join a new group. Note that you can only switch Family Sharing groups once a year.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove a child from Family Sharing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As organizer, you need to ask other guardians to invite the child account to a different family group in-person and approve the request from your iPhone. Once done, you can remove them from Settings > Family > [child name] > Remove from Family Sharing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to the shared payment method?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will no longer apply to your purchases; you must add your own payment method.

mainEntity.name: If I leave family sharing will they be notified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, family members get a notification when someone leaves or is removed from the group.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take for the Explore page to learn my interests again?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no set timeframe. Instagram’s algorithm typically takes a few days to a week to adjust, depending on how actively you engage with new content. Consistently liking, commenting, and following accounts aligned with your interests speeds up the process. If you’re still seeing old content, keep marking it as Not Interested to refine the feed faster.

mainEntity.name: Why does my Explore page show things I don’t like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Instagram’s Explore page is based on your past activity, likes, saves, searches, and posts you interact with. If you engage with something by mistake or your interests change, the algorithm might still show related content.

mainEntity.name: What is the fastest way to clear my Instagram Explore page?

acceptedAnswer.text: Using the built-in Reset suggested content settings is the best way to go. This will wipe your current suggestions so Instagram can build your feed from scratch.

mainEntity.name: Does clearing my cache reset my Explore page on iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing your cache will not directly reset your Instagram Explore page. However, it removes the old temporary files which may give you a fresh start.

mainEntity.name: What happens when I click "Not Interested" on Instagram?

acceptedAnswer.text: Instagram hides that post and reduces similar content in your Explore page over time.

mainEntity.name: Can I undo a reset of my suggested posts?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Once you reset, your old suggestions are gone, and Instagram starts learning your interest like the first time.

mainEntity.name: Will resetting my Explore page affect my main feed?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your main feed stays the same because it’s based on accounts you follow, not Explore suggestions. Both follows different algorithms to curate content.

mainEntity.name: Can I change the download location for each file in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: On Mac, Yes! You can set Safari to ask where to save each file. Just go to Safari > Settings > General, then choose Ask for each download for the file download location. On iPhone or iPad, No. Safari doesn’t let you choose a folder for each file. You can only set one default download location.

mainEntity.name: Will changing the download location affect iCloud syncing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it can. If you choose a folder inside iCloud Drive, your downloads will sync across your Apple devices. If you pick a folder that’s not in iCloud Drive (like "On My iPhone" or a local folder on Mac), the files will stay only on that device and won’t sync with others.

mainEntity.name: Does this change affect other browsers like Chrome or Firefox?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Changing Safari’s download location only affects Safari. Other browsers like Chrome, Firefox, or Edge have their own separate settings for where to save downloads—you’ll need to adjust those separately in each browser’s settings.

keyPoints.title: Forgot Screen Time Passcode? Use Apple ID for Easy Reset
keyPoints.explanation: If your device runs iOS 13.4 or later, you can reset your Screen Time passcode by selecting 'Forgot Passcode' and entering your Apple ID credentials to create a new one.

keyPoints.title: Backup and Restore for Advanced Users
keyPoints.explanation: Restoring from a backup made before the passcode was set can remove the Screen Time passcode, but ensure the backup predates the passcode to avoid restoring it.

keyPoints.title: Contact Apple Support When All Else Fails
keyPoints.explanation: If you cannot reset the passcode via Apple ID or restore from a suitable backup, contacting Apple Support is the next step, with proof of purchase or ownership.

keyPoints.title: Preparing for Future Passcode Issues
keyPoints.explanation: Enable Apple ID Recovery, store your passcode securely, and avoid reusing device PINs as your Screen Time passcode to prevent future lockouts.

keyPoints.title: Third-Party Apps Are Not the Safer Choice
keyPoints.explanation: Although some third-party apps claim to remove Screen Time passcodes, they often erase data, and Apple's built-in methods are safer and more reliable.

title.rendered: How to turn off iPhone notifications on your Mac

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • How It Works: With iPhone Mirroring, your iPhone’s notifications will appear on your Mac as long as the phone is nearby, even when the mirroring app is closed.
  • Why Disable Them: Disabling these mirrored notifications helps to reduce distractions during focused work, protect your privacy in shared spaces, and can help conserve your Mac’s battery life.
  • Disabling from Your Mac: The easiest way to stop all alerts is on your Mac: go to System Settings and turn off the main “Allow Notifications from iPhone” toggle.
  • Disabling from Your iPhone: For more granular control, you can go into each app’s notification settings on your iPhone and individually toggle off the “Show on Mac” option.
  • Customizing Your Experience: By using these settings, you can create a custom notification experience, allowing only essential iPhone alerts to appear on your Mac while blocking the rest.

With macOS Sequoia and iOS 18, Apple has elevated its ecosystem experience with the new iPhone Mirroring app for Macs. With iPhone Mirroring, you can easily use and control your iPhone wirelessly, right from your Mac.

While useful, the functionality can turn annoying and distracting since it mirrors the iPhone notification on your Mac, even when you terminate iPhone Mirroring. Fortunately, Apple allows you to turn off iPhone notifications on a Mac. Let’s jump in to learn how.

Table of Contents
  • How iPhone notifications work on Mac?
  • Why turn off iPhone notifications on Mac?
  • How to disable iPhone notifications on Mac
    • On Mac
    • On iPhone

How iPhone notifications work on Mac?

Before we proceed, it’s important to know how iPhone notifications work on a Mac. Here’s a quick breakdown to make things easier to understand:

  • When you use iPhone Mirroring on your Mac for the first time, everything on your iPhone starts appearing on the Mac, including the notifications. However, unlike other iPhone stuff, your Mac automatically receives and showcases iPhone notifications even when you quit the iPhone Mirroring app. All it needs is for your iPhone to be near your Mac and not turned off.
  • Any notifications you receive on your iPhone appear automatically alongside Mac notifications in the top-right corner of the screen.
  • Interacting with the iPhone notifications on your Mac opens the corresponding app in the iPhone Mirroring app window, allowing you to continue the task as you would on your iPhone.
  • Clearing the notifications on your iPhone also clears them from your Mac.
  • If you use iPhone Mirroring on multiple Macs, they all receive notifications from your iPhone.

Why turn off iPhone notifications on Mac?

While having your iPhone notifications appear on your Mac ensures you don’t miss out on anything important when you are not using your iPhone, it can sometimes become overwhelming. Here are some of the most common scenarios where disabling iPhone notifications on Mac might help:

  • Prevent workflow disruption: When you’re focused on a task on your Mac, the last thing you need is a constant stream of notifications breaking your concentration, especially the ones from your iPhone. Turning off your iPhone notifications on your Mac can help you focus better on the task and avoid social media distractions.
  • Privacy concern: Having your iPhone notifications pop-up on your Mac out of nowhere can be problematic if you’re using your Mac in a public space, meeting, or sharing your screen. By disabling iPhone notifications, you can protect your privacy and ensure sensitive information stays private.
  • Tailored notifications experience: Not all notifications are as important as others. For example, you might want to see calendar alerts but avoid social media updates on your Mac. Turning off notifications on Mac from specific iPhone apps can customize your notifications experience, and you will only see what matters most.
  • Battery performance and optimization: Although Macs are known for their superb battery performance and efficiency, having unnecessary iPhone notifications pop-up on your Mac can still use system resources. Turning off such notifications can help you slightly extend your Mac’s battery life.

How to disable iPhone notifications on Mac

Luckily, turning off iPhone notifications on a Mac requires little to no technical competence. You can completely disable them or control which notifications your Mac receives. While it can be done on both your Mac and iPhone, a total shutdown is only possible via Mac.

On Mac

Restricting iPhone alerts, either all or from individual apps, from appearing on your Mac is super easy and can be done in a few simple steps. Let me show you how you can do it:

  1. Open the System Settings app and click on Notifications in the left sidebar.
  2. Locate and click on Allow Notifications from iPhone on the right.

  3. Next, toggle off Allow Notifications from iPhone.

  4. Alternatively, you can toggle off notifications from individual iPhone apps instead of completely shutting off iPhone notifications on Mac.
Note If an app setting has an “Installed on Mac” label beneath it, you will only see notifications from the Mac app—and not the iPhone app.

On iPhone

While Apple does not allow you to directly turn off all the iPhone notifications from appearing on Mac via your iPhone, it does let you to turn off alerts from individual apps you have on your iPhone from appearing on your Mac. Here’s how it’s done:

  1. Open Settings and head to Notifications.
  2. Scroll down and select the app from which you don’t want your Mac to receive alerts.
  3. Next, toggle off Show on Mac.

Focus mode on…

Managing iPhone notifications on your Mac gives you better control over your workflow and privacy. While you can turn off iPhone notifications altogether, my advice would be to toggle them off only for the apps that are less important to you. This way, you won’t miss out on important notifications. If the need arises, you can enable iPhone notifications again anytime.

Feel free to reach out to us via comments if you want more tips to enhance your Apple ecosystem experience.

You might also like:

  • How to silence notifications on your iPhone
  • How to turn off notifications on Mac
  • How to use automatic window tiling in macOS Sequoia

@graph.name: How to Disable iPhone Notifications on Mac
@graph.description: Turn off iPhone notifications on your Mac through System Settings, either completely or for individual apps, to reduce distractions.

step.name: Open Notifications settings
step.text: Open the System Settings app on your Mac and click Notifications in the left sidebar.

itemListElement.text: Open System Settings.
Click Notifications in the sidebar.

step.name: Disable iPhone notifications
step.text: Locate Allow Notifications from iPhone on the right, then toggle it off to stop receiving all iPhone notifications on your Mac.

itemListElement.text: Find Allow Notifications from iPhone.
Toggle it off.

step.name: Optionally disable specific app notifications
step.text: If you prefer, toggle off notifications only for individual iPhone apps instead of completely disabling iPhone notifications on your Mac.

itemListElement.text: Scroll to the desired app.
Toggle notifications off for that app.

@graph.name: How to Disable iPhone Notifications on Mac via iPhone
@graph.description: Stop specific iPhone app notifications from appearing on your Mac directly from the iPhone's Notifications settings.

step.name: Open Notifications settings
step.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone and tap Notifications.

itemListElement.text: Tap Settings on your home screen.
Go to Notifications.

step.name: Select the app
step.text: Scroll down and select the app from which you don’t want your Mac to receive alerts.

itemListElement.text: Scroll to find the app in the list.
Tap the app to open its notification settings.

step.name: Turn off Mac alerts
step.text: Toggle off Show on Mac to stop receiving that app’s notifications on your Mac.

itemListElement.text: Find the Show on Mac toggle.
Switch it off.

keyPoints.title: iPhone Notifications on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: When using iPhone Mirroring on your Mac, notifications from your iPhone appear automatically on your Mac, even after quitting the Mirroring app, as long as the iPhone is nearby and powered on.

keyPoints.title: Reasons to Turn Off iPhone Notifications on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: Disabling notifications can prevent workflow disruptions, protect privacy in public spaces, allow for tailored notification experiences, and help conserve system resources and battery life.

keyPoints.title: Disabling iPhone Notifications on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: You can restrict notifications through System Settings by disabling 'Allow Notifications from iPhone' or selectively turning off notifications from specific iPhone apps.

keyPoints.title: Managing Notifications on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: While you cannot turn off all notifications for Mac from your iPhone, you can disable alerts from individual apps by toggling off 'Show on Mac' in the iPhone's notification settings.

keyPoints.title: Benefits of Managing Notifications
keyPoints.explanation: Controlling your notifications enhances workflow, upholds privacy, allows customization of alerts, and can contribute to longer battery performance on your Mac.

title.rendered: Apple’s New Brain-Controlled iPad Revealed in a Video

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iOS 26 adds support for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), making Apple devices natively compatible with assistive tech like Synchron’s thought-controlled implants.
  • First real-world BCI demo shows an ALS patient using an iPad, highlighting how users can browse and type using only brain signals.
  • Synchron’s system sends brain signals wirelessly to iPad using the new BCI HID protocol, with a stent-like implant near the motor cortex.
  • Enables hands-free access for users with paralysis, allowing basic tasks like texting and reading, which helps reclaim independence.
  • Less invasive than Neuralink’s surgical method, Synchron’s approach avoids open-brain procedures, making it more viable for accessibility right now.

Earlier this year, Apple confirmed that iOS 26 and iPadOS 26 would support brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) for accessibility. Now, we have our first public look at the technology in action. A new video from Synchron shows Mark Jackson, a participant in the company’s COMMAND clinical trial and a person living with ALS, controlling an iPad using only his thoughts.

In the clip, Mark navigates the home screen, opens apps, and even composes messages without touching the screen, speaking, or moving his eyes. It’s powered by Synchron’s Stentrode implant and Apple’s new BCI Human Interface Device (HID) protocol.

Watch the demo here:

In the demo, Mark says:

“When I lost the use of my hands, I thought I had lost my independence. Now, with my iPad, I can message my loved ones, read the news, and stay connected with the world, just by thinking. It’s given me part of my life back.” Synchron’s team added that Mark is the first person in the world to control an iPad entirely through thought using the new BCI HID, calling it a massive milestone for accessibility and BCI technology.

Apple first tested its BCI HID system with Vision Pro in 2024 before expanding to iPhones and iPads. While it didn’t make a big marketing push, the technology is now baked into iOS 26 and is actively being used in FDA-approved trials. Synchron has implanted its Stentrode in 10 participants so far, across the United States and Australia.

How Apple’s Brain Control Tech Works

If you want to take a closer look, here’s how this brain control technology works in simple terms:

The Stentrode is placed in a blood vessel near the brain’s motor cortex using a simple procedure through the jugular vein. It picks up brain signals related to movement. These signals travel wirelessly to a small decoder that connects directly to iPadOS using Apple’s BCI HID protocol.

Apple’s system works with its Switch Control accessibility feature, so the iPad reads brain signals just like it would touch or voice input. The iPad also shares on-screen context back to the BCI, helping improve accuracy and navigation.

Unlike Neuralink’s N1 chip, which requires open-brain surgery, Synchron’s approach is far less invasive. That makes it more practical for medical and accessibility use right now.

This is still an early preview, and Apple hasn’t officially showcased it yet. How Apple chooses to present it and how widely it’s adopted by people with accessibility needs remains to be seen.

title.rendered: iOS 26 Beta Leak Teases Larger Apple Watch Ultra 3 Display

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple Watch Ultra 3 may gain a 422×514 display by shrinking bezels, offering more screen space without changing the device’s external size.
  • Upgrades could include satellite emergency alerts plus a brighter, smoother screen, faster chip, and early support for blood pressure tracking.
  • Launch likely during Apple’s fall keynote alongside iPhone 17 and Apple Watch Series 11, two years after the Ultra 2 arrived.
  • Design sticks with rugged exterior but boosts usability with a more expansive view and potentially improved battery efficiency.
  • No confirmed features yet, so manage expectations as leaks may change and not all rumored health tools or chips may debut this cycle.

Apple has just released iOS 26 beta 5, and it includes a major clue about the next-generation Apple Watch Ultra, expected to debut this fall alongside the iPhone 17 lineup.

MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris posted on X, uncovering an image that reveals a screen resolution different from any existing Apple Watch. This strongly suggests that Apple is working on a new model, most likely the Apple Watch Ultra 3, featuring a larger display than current versions.

A Larger Display Without a Bigger Casing

The leaked image points to a 422 x 514 resolution, which is a noticeable upgrade from the 410 x 502 resolution found on the current Apple Watch Ultra 2. However, it’s highly unlikely that Apple will increase the casing size on the Ultra 3. Instead, the company may be reducing the bezel size to offer more screen real estate while keeping the watch’s rugged build and familiar dimensions.

Rumored Features Coming to Apple Watch Ultra 3

If current reports and leaks are accurate, the Apple Watch Ultra 3 could bring some exciting upgrades, including:

  • Satellite connectivity for emergency off-grid communication.
  • A brighter display with an improved refresh rate.
  • A next-gen chip for enhanced performance and battery efficiency.
  • Potential new health tools, such as blood pressure monitoring.

Expected Launch Timeline

Apple is expected to unveil the Apple Watch Ultra 3 just over a month from now, two years after the launch of the Ultra 2. It will likely be revealed alongside the iPhone 17 lineup and the Apple Watch Series 11 during Apple’s annual fall keynote event.

What feature are you most excited to see in the Apple Watch Ultra 3? Share your thoughts with fellow readers in the comments below.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: iOS 26 Beta 5 Tweaks Low Battery Look, Passcode Animations & More Ahead of Final Release

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • New low battery animation in iOS 26 Beta 5 flashes a red radar-style pulse at 20% and smoothly enters Low Power Mode if it’s enabled.
  • Passcode screen now animates each digit with a bounce effect, making the iPhone lock screen feel more fluid and tactile.
  • App splash screens highlight recent changes for built-in apps like Apple Music and Reminders when launched for the first time after updating.
  • Control Center swipes feel smoother and faster, with snappier transitions and a bouncier touch as Apple refines overall polish.
  • This iOS 26 build focuses on subtle UX tuning, with no major features added as Apple gears up for the iPhone 17 release window.

Apple has been teasing Liquid Glass as the crown jewel of iOS 26 visuals. However, iOS 26 Beta 5, released today, includes a few smaller tweaks beyond what Liquid Glass initially promised. One of the most interesting changes is a new low battery icon and animation.

Instead of simply making the icon glass‑like and keeping it static, the iPhone now flashes a radar‑style red pulse when it drops to 20 percent. Then it transitions into Low Power Mode smoothly (if enabled).

Here’s what it looks like, including its transition to Low Power Mode.

These types of micro‑interactions, something Apple is known for, have been missing from the Liquid Glass design style so far. With this beta, Apple appears to be bringing them back.

And It’s Not the Only Non-Liquid Glass Change in iOS 26 Beta 5

The passcode screen now has an updated animation where each number bounces into place as you enter it, giving the lock screen a more dynamic feel.

Apple has also added new splash screens that appear the first time you open apps like Apple Music or Reminders, highlighting what’s new in each.

Control Center has been refined too, with smoother, more responsive swiping between pages and a slightly bouncier transition that makes navigation feel faster and cleaner.

These aren’t major changes, but they make iOS 26 feel tighter and more consistent. At this stage, Apple is no longer adding features. It is tuning the software for its final release.

The public version of iOS 26 is expected in September, likely following the iPhone 17 launch, which is rumored for September 9. Beta 5 is a clear sign that Apple is in the final phase of preparation.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 Event Likely Set for September 9, Leak Suggests

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple’s 2025 event likely set for September 9 with iPhone 17 pre-orders soon after and in-store availability expected by September 19 in key markets.
  • iPhone 17 lineup includes a new ‘Air’ model, replacing the Plus variant, alongside iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max.
  • Apple Watch Series 11 and SE 3 likely to debut, with Watch Ultra 3 and AirPods Pro 3 also rumored but not yet confirmed.
  • Press invites expected around September 2, continuing Apple’s usual one-week lead time before its annual September keynote.
  • iPhone 17 Air signals a potential shift in naming and positioning strategy, hinting at broader updates across Apple’s product ecosystem.

With fall around the corner, Apple appears to be locking in plans for its iPhone 17 launch. While the company hasn’t made anything official yet, new details from German mobile carriers point to Tuesday, September 9, 2025, as the likely date for Apple’s annual September keynote. The claim surfaced via iphone-ticker.de, citing internal sources tied to regional telecoms.

The reported date also lines up with Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, who recently predicted Apple would schedule its next product unveiling during the week of September 8, narrowing it down to either the 9th or 10th.

Apple’s iPhone 17 Launch Timeline Taking Shape

If Apple sticks to its usual cadence, pre-orders for the iPhone 17 lineup would likely begin on Friday, September 12. That sets the stage for first shipments and in-store availability to follow on Friday, September 19. Launch day typically spans major markets including the United States, China, Europe, and Japan.

What to Expect from the iPhone 17 Event

The headline announcement will, of course, be the iPhone 17 series. According to ongoing leaks and naming rumors, Apple is expected to debut four models:

  • iPhone 17
  • iPhone 17 Air (replacing the current Plus)
  • iPhone 17 Pro
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max

Beyond the iPhone refresh, the event should also bring updates to Apple’s wearables lineup. The Apple Watch Series 11, a new Watch SE 3, and a possible Apple Watch Ultra 3 are all reportedly in the pipeline. There’s also a chance Apple will use the stage to debut AirPods Pro 3, though that remains less certain.

Press invites typically land about a week ahead of the event, so Apple could make things official by Tuesday, September 2.

Our Take

Apple has stuck to a fairly rigid September launch rhythm over the years, and all signs point to more of the same this fall. That said, this year’s event could bring a more significant shakeup than usual. The rumored introduction of an “iPhone 17 Air” model replacing the Plus line could signal a shift in how Apple packages its mid-tier iPhones. For users frustrated with the oversized Plus models or indifferent to the Pro price tags, this new variant might fill a long-standing gap.

Combined with updates across the Apple Watch and possibly AirPods categories, this could shape up to be one of Apple’s busiest hardware events in recent memory.

What part of the September launch are you watching most closely? Drop your thoughts in the comments below.

  • Apple September Event 2025: Date, Time, and Everything We Expect to See

title.rendered: How to turn off location on iPhone photos and videos

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What Geotagging Is: Your iPhone automatically embeds GPS coordinates and other metadata, known as a “geotag,” into every photo and video you take with the Camera app.
  • The Privacy Risk: Sharing photos with location data intact can unintentionally reveal your home, workplace, or daily routine, posing a significant risk to your personal privacy and safety.
  • Prevent Future Geotagging: To stop geotagging all future photos, go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services, find the Camera app, and set its access to “Never.”
  • Remove from Existing Photos: For photos already in your library, you can remove location data by opening a photo, tapping “Adjust Location,” and selecting “No Location.”
  • Share Without Location: When sharing a photo, tap “Options” at the top of the Share Sheet and turn off the “Location” toggle to send it without geotag data.

Your iPhone automatically adds location data to photos and videos you capture. While this can help organize memories, it can also pose a privacy and safety risk, especially when shared publicly or in real time.

In this guide, I’ll show you how to disable geotagging on iPhone photos and videos, and how to remove location metadata from existing media—so you stay in control of what you’re sharing.

What is location data in iPhone photos and videos?

Ever heard of geotagging? It’s a feature that embeds GPS location data into your media files using EXIF metadata (Exchangeable Image File Format). This data includes your iPhone camera settings, the date and time, and the exact location where the image or video was captured.

By default, the iPhone Camera app automatically saves this information. While this is handy for sorting and memories, the risks outweigh the benefits for many. Disabling location tagging will prevent new photos and videos from including location data, while older ones can be edited anytime (I’ll show you how later).

Why you should turn off location data on iPhone photos

Sharing geotagged media—especially in real-time—can unintentionally reveal your whereabouts. Here’s why you might want to turn off location services for your photos:

  • Protect your privacy: Publishing images with embedded location data could reveal sensitive locations like your home, workplace, or favorite hangouts—info you probably didn’t intend to share.
  • Stay safe: Sharing real-time media can disclose where you are right now—potentially making you a target for theft or stalking, especially while traveling.
  • Avoid oversharing: Most users don’t realize their photos contain hidden geolocation data. Disabling this ensures you’re not sharing more than you intend.
  • You have full control: Apple makes it easy to disable or remove location data—either automatically or before sharing specific photos.

How to disable location for photos and videos on iPhone

To stop your iPhone from tagging new photos with location data, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Scroll down and tap Privacy & Security.
  3. Tap Location Services.

  4. Scroll down and select Camera.
  5. Choose Never to deny location access to the Camera app.

After this, your iPhone Camera won’t save GPS data to any new photos or videos.

How to remove location data from existing iPhone photos and videos

Already have photos with geotags? No worries—your iPhone lets you delete that info easily.

For a single photo or video

  1. Launch the Photos app and find that image or video.
  2. Tap the Info (i) button or swipe up.
  3. Tap Adjust next to the location field.
  4. Tap No Location to remove it.

That’s all! Your location information is wiped out instantly.

For multiple photos or videos

Need to wipe geolocation from a bunch of pics?

  1. Open the Photos app, go to an album or the Recents tab.
  2. Tap Select, then choose multiple photos.

  3. Tap the three-dot icon at the bottom.
  4. Select Adjust Location and tap No Location.

And just like that, all selected items are cleared of their GPS tags.

How to remove location when sharing iPhone photo or video

Don’t want to permanently delete the info, but still want to keep it private when sharing? You can disable it per share:

  1. Open the Photos app and choose the image.
  2. Tap that share icon.
  3. Tap Options at the top of the share sheet.
  4. Under the Include section, turn off Location.
  5. Tap Done and share away—location-free!

This is perfect for sending photos via Messages, AirDrop, or social media without revealing your GPS data.

Keep your iPhone photos private

There you go—you now know how to take full control of location settings on iPhone photos and videos. Whether you turn off Camera location access, remove metadata from old images, or disable it just before sharing, your privacy stays protected.

So snap those beautiful shots, and share them with confidence—minus the creepy location tags.

Check out next:

  • How to edit photos on iPhone
  • How to recover deleted photos from iPhone or iPad

@graph.name: How to Disable Location for Photos and Videos on iPhone
@graph.description: Turn off location services for the Camera app on your iPhone to prevent GPS data from being saved in your photos and videos.

step.name: Open Privacy & Security settings
step.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone, scroll down, and tap Privacy & Security.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Settings app.
Scroll down and select Privacy & Security.

step.name: Open Camera location settings
step.text: Tap Location Services, scroll down, and select Camera from the list of apps.

itemListElement.text: Tap Location Services.
Scroll to find Camera and select it.

step.name: Disable location access
step.text: Choose Never to prevent the Camera app from saving location data in your photos and videos.

itemListElement.text: Tap Never to turn off Camera location access.

@graph.name: How to Remove Location Data for a Single Photo or Video on iPhone
@graph.description: Remove location metadata from an individual photo or video on your iPhone using the Photos app to protect your privacy before sharing.

step.name: Open the photo or video
step.text: Launch the Photos app on your iPhone and find the image or video you want to edit.

itemListElement.text: Tap Photos on your home screen.
Select the photo or video you want to edit.

step.name: Access location info
step.text: Tap the Info (i) button or swipe up on the photo or video to view its location details.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Info button.
Or swipe up to reveal location data.

step.name: Remove location data
step.text: Tap Adjust next to the location field, then select No Location to delete the location metadata from the file.

itemListElement.text: Tap Adjust beside the location.
Tap No Location.

@graph.name: How to Remove Location Data for Multiple Photos or Videos on iPhone
@graph.description: Remove location metadata from multiple photos or videos at once on your iPhone using the Photos app for enhanced privacy.

step.name: Select multiple photos or videos
step.text: Open the Photos app, navigate to an album or the Recents tab, tap Select, then choose multiple photos or videos you want to edit.

itemListElement.text: Open Photos app and go to an album or Recents.
Tap Select and choose multiple photos or videos.

step.name: Open location adjustment menu
step.text: Tap the three-dot icon at the bottom of the screen to open more options.

itemListElement.text: Tap the three-dot icon.

step.name: Remove location data
step.text: Select Adjust Location, then tap No Location to remove GPS data from all selected items.

itemListElement.text: Select Adjust Location.
Tap No Location.

@graph.name: How to Remove Location When Sharing iPhone Photo or Video
@graph.description: Easily remove location metadata from an iPhone photo or video before sharing it, using the Options menu in the Photos app share sheet.

step.name: Open photo or video
step.text: Open the Photos app on your iPhone and select the photo or video you want to share without location data.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Photos app icon.
Select the desired photo or video.

step.name: Open share options
step.text: Tap the share icon, then tap Options at the top of the share sheet.

itemListElement.text: Tap the share icon.
Tap Options in the share sheet.

step.name: Disable location sharing
step.text: Under the Include section, toggle off Location, then tap Done to save your settings.

itemListElement.text: Turn off the Location toggle.
Tap Done.

step.name: Share the file
step.text: Choose your preferred sharing method and send the file without any location data.

itemListElement.text: Select an app or contact to share with.
Send the file.
