keyPoints.title: What is location data in iPhone photos and videos
keyPoints.explanation: Location data, embedded via geotagging using EXIF metadata, includes GPS coordinates, camera settings, date, and time, automatically added by the iPhone Camera app.

keyPoints.title: Risks of sharing geotagged media
keyPoints.explanation: Sharing photos or videos with embedded location data can reveal your private locations, potentially compromising privacy and safety, especially in real-time sharing scenarios.

keyPoints.title: How to disable location tagging on new photos and videos
keyPoints.explanation: You can stop your iPhone from adding location data by disabling camera access to location services in the Privacy & Security settings under Location Services.

keyPoints.title: Removing location data from existing media
keyPoints.explanation: Existing photos and videos can have their geolocation information removed through the Photos app by adjusting the info and selecting 'No Location' for individual or multiple files.

keyPoints.title: Disabling location sharing when sharing media
keyPoints.explanation: You can choose to hide location data temporarily when sharing a photo or video by turning off the 'Include Location' option in the share options, maintaining privacy without deleting metadata.

title.rendered: How to make group FaceTime calls on iPhone, iPad, and Mac

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • The Requirements: To use Group FaceTime, all participants with Apple devices must have a supported OS version, a stable internet connection, and be signed into FaceTime.
  • How to Start a Call: Start a Group FaceTime call from the FaceTime app by adding multiple contacts, or by tapping the FaceTime button inside an existing group iMessage chat.
  • In-Call Management: During a call, you can add more people, mute your microphone, switch cameras, use video effects, or leave the call using the on-screen controls.
  • Including Non-Apple Users: You can invite Android and Windows users to join a Group FaceTime call by creating and sharing a web link for them to use in their browser.
  • Troubleshooting: If you have issues, ensure all devices are on a stable internet connection, are running updated software, and are properly signed into their Apple ID.

People have different ways of staying connected; some send memes on Instagram, while others prefer talking over calls. Similarly, some love catching up over group video calls.

If you have friends or family members who, too, prefer video calls over other ways, you’re in luck, as Apple lets you make group FaceTime calls with up to 32 people on your Apple devices. Keep reading, and I’ll show you how to start and manage group FaceTime calls on your iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Requirements for making group FaceTime calls

Make sure your Apple devices and software version meet the following requirements to be able to make group FaceTime calls:

  • Your Apple devices should be running iOS 12.1.4 or later, iPadOS 13 or later, or macOS Mojave 10.14.3 or later for this feature to work.
  • You must be signed in with your Apple Account and should have FaceTime enabled.
  • A strong Wi-Fi or cellular data connection is necessary for smooth FaceTime video calls.

How to start a group FaceTime call on iPhone and Mac

You can start a group FaceTime call from all your Apple devices, but the way you initiate it differs from device to device. Let’s look at how to do it on different Apple devices.

Starting a group FaceTime call on iPhone and iPad

You can start group Facetime calls on your iPhone and iPad using either the FaceTime or the Messages app.

Using the FaceTime app:

  1. Open the FaceTime app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Tap the New FaceTime button.
  3. Enter the names, phone numbers, or email IDs in the search field or tap the + icon and choose a contact from the list.
  4. Tap the FaceTime button to start a group call with the selected contacts.

Going forward, you don’t have to create a call group again to speak to the same people. You can start a call with them by simply tapping the call group you just created.

Using the Messages app:

  1. Open the Messages app.
  2. Open an existing group conversation or tap the + icon and add people to create a new group chat.
  3. Tap the video camera icon in the top-right corner and select FaceTime Video to start a group video call with everyone in the chat.

You can now chat with your friends and family over the video call.

Starting a group FaceTime call on Mac

Similar to iPhones, you can initiate a group FaceTime call on your Mac using the Messages app as well as the FaceTime app. Here’s how.

Using the FaceTime app:

  1. Open the FaceTime app on your Mac.
  2. Click the New FaceTime button.

  3. Type the name of the contacts you wish to go on a group FaceTime call with. Or, click the + icon and choose the people from the contacts list.
  4. Click the FaceTime icon to initiate the call.

Click the group call you just created the next time you want to speak to the same people again.

Using the Messages app:

  1. Open the Messages app on your Mac. 
  2. Open an existing group conversation or click the new message icon and add people to create a new group chat.

  3. Click the video camera icon in the top-right corner and select FaceTime Video to start a group video call with everyone in the chat.

How to manage a group FaceTime call

Once you’re on a group FaceTime call, you get a bunch of options to manage the call. Let’s see how to use them and what they let you do.

Add people during an ongoing FaceTime call

If you’re already on a FaceTime call, you can easily add more people by tapping on the names above, then tap the + Add People button, and typing their contact details or choosing from the list by tapping the + button.

Switch between front and rear cameras

At any point, if you want to give people on the call a better view of your surroundings or show them some object at your desk, you can switch the camera. Simply tap the camera flip icon in the lower-right corner, and FaceTime will automatically switch to the other camera.

Mute, turn off video, or leave the call

FaceTime gives you controls in a row at the top of the screen to quickly mute audio, turn off video, or leave the call.

  • Tap the mute icon to silence your microphone.
  • Tap the video camera icon to turn off your video feed.
  • Tap the red X button to end the call when you’re done.

Group FaceTime isn’t working? Try these fixes

If you’re having trouble making a FaceTime call, these fixes can save your day:

  • Make sure you’re signed in with your Apple Account and FaceTime is activated.
  • Verify your internet connection is stable.
  • Restart your device to clear any glitches.
  • Update to the latest iOS, iPadOS, or macOS version.

If none of these methods work, contact Apple Support for help.

Signing Off

Whether it’s a virtual hangout, a family catch-up, or a spontaneous online get-together with friends, group FaceTime calls make it easy to connect with multiple people at once, no matter what part of the world they are in. Now that you know how to start and manage group FaceTime calls on your iPhone, iPad, and Mac, you’re all set for seamless video chats. Go ahead, gather your crew, and enjoy real-time conversations.

FAQs

Can Android or Windows users join a group FaceTime call?

Yes. With iOS 15 and later, you can create a FaceTime link that Android and Windows users can use to join the call via a web browser. Follow our guide on how to use FaceTime on your Android or PC to know how.

Can I use effects like Memoji or filters during Group FaceTime?

Absolutely! You can use Memoji, filters, and other effects to make your calls more fun. Check out our guide on how to use FaceTime effects for more details.

Can I schedule a group FaceTime call in advance?

While you can’t schedule a group FaceTime call directly in the FaceTime app, you can create a FaceTime link, share it with participants and ask them to join at a specific time.

Other helpful FaceTime posts:

  • How to make a FaceTime call on Apple Watch
  • How to fix FaceTime hand gestures not working on iPhone
  • How to record FaceTime with audio

mainEntity.name: Can Android or Windows users join a group FaceTime call?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. With iOS 15 and later, you can create a FaceTime link that Android and Windows users can use to join the call via a web browser. Follow our guide on how to use FaceTime on your Android or PC to know how.

mainEntity.name: Can I use effects like Memoji or filters during Group FaceTime?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely! You can use Memoji, filters, and other effects to make your calls more fun. Check out our guide on how to use FaceTime effects for more details.

mainEntity.name: Can I schedule a group FaceTime call in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can't schedule a group FaceTime call directly in the FaceTime app, you can create a FaceTime link, share it with participants and ask them to join at a specific time.

keyPoints.title: Device and Software Requirements for Group FaceTime
keyPoints.explanation: To make group FaceTime calls, your Apple device must run specific iOS, iPadOS, or macOS versions and be signed in with FaceTime enabled, with a stable internet connection.

keyPoints.title: Starting a Group FaceTime on iPhone and iPad
keyPoints.explanation: You can initiate a group FaceTime call via the FaceTime app by creating a new call or through a group message in the Messages app, where you add contacts and select FaceTime Video.

keyPoints.title: Starting a Group FaceTime on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: On Mac, group FaceTime calls can be started using the FaceTime or Messages app by selecting contacts and clicking the FaceTime icon or creating a group chat and launching a video call.

keyPoints.title: Managing an Ongoing Group FaceTime Call
keyPoints.explanation: During a call, users can add more participants, switch between front and rear cameras, mute microphones, turn off videos, or leave the call using on-screen controls.

keyPoints.title: Troubleshooting Group FaceTime Issues and FAQs
keyPoints.explanation: Common problems can be resolved by checking account sign-in status, internet connection, device updates, or contacting Apple Support; FAQs address joining calls from Android/Windows and using effects or scheduling.

With the increasing number of internet-based activities in recent years, online privacy and security have become major concerns for iPhone users around the globe. So, to avoid the risk of data breaches or cyberattacks, using a Virtual Private Network (VPN) on your iPhone or iPad is essential. Additionally, VPNs can help you access geo-restricted content by changing your iPhone’s location.

With so many VPN apps available for iOS, finding the right one can be difficult. So, I have done the research for you and curated a list of the best VPNs for iPhone and iPad. Take a look at the features, weigh the pros and cons, and pick one that meets your requirements.

Table of Contents
  • Surfshark VPN – Editor's Choice
  • ExpressVPN – Most trusted VPN for iPhone
  • Planet VPN – High Speed iPhone VPN
  • Proton VPN – Most secure VPN service for iOS
  • IPVanish – Connect unlimited devices
  • NordVPN – Advanced security with specialized servers
  • VPN by Private Internet Access (PIA) – Strong privacy commitment
  • CyberGhost – Complete privacy across Apple devices
  • Mullvad VPN – Most privacy-centered VPN service
  • Windscribe – Best free VPN for iPhone
  • Enjoy safe and secure browsing

1. Surfshark VPN – Editor’s Choice

Surfshark is one of the most affordable VPNs for iPhones. While many might think the affordability tag must affect its performance, the truth is that you won’t see any compromise in terms of performance and security features. That’s right! With 3200+ servers in 100 unique locations, you will enjoy blazing-fast speed across the globe.

Like me, if you use a VPN on multiple devices, Surfshark is definitely worth a try. It allows you to connect unlimited devices simultaneously under a single subscription. Further, you can browse the internet in peace because it follows a strict no-log policy, so the app won’t monitor, track, or store anything you do online.

Most importantly, it offers a super affordable two-year plan, using which you can access fast VPN servers on unlimited devices and get advanced security features like real-time email breach alerts and webcam protection.

Pros

  • Unlimited simultaneous connections
  • Strong security features 
  • Fast speeds 
  • Effective at unblocking geo-restricted content.

Cons

  • Occasional connection drops

Surfshark Pricing for Two-Year Plans:

  • Surfshark Starter: $1.99/month, includes 3 months free
  • Surfshark One: $2.49/month, includes 3 months free
  • Surfshark One+: $3.99/month, includes 3 months free

Download

2. ExpressVPN – Most trusted VPN for iPhone

When it comes to choosing a VPN app for your iPhone, you simply can’t go wrong with ExpressVPN – thanks to its unparalleled speed and robust security features. With its servers across 105 countries, ExpressVPN ensures seamless access to geo-restricted content, making it ideal for those who stream a lot of OTT content.

Moreover, its cutting-edge UDP, TCP, and IPsec encryption protocols guarantee that your online activity remains private and secure, shielding you from spyware and potential fraud.

ExpressVPN also has a no-log policy. It keeps no activity or connection logs, but it does collect a bare minimum of data, such as the amount of data transferred, connection dates, and VPN location, to keep your VPN connection running and improve our service. To learn more, you can check out our detailed review of Express VPN.

Pros

  • Excellent performance and speeds
  • User-friendly interface
  • Strong security features 
  • Reliable for streaming content

Cons

  • Relatively expensive 
  • Limited to 8 simultaneous connections

Price: 7-day free trial. Subscriptions start at $4.99/month for a 2-year plan, plus 4 months free

Download

3. Planet VPN – High Speed iPhone VPN

Planet VPN is a freemium VPN service. You can use its 11 servers free for a lifetime with no trial or credit card required, or upgrade to a low-cost Premium plan for extra features. On the free plan, there are no limitations on traffic, bandwidth, or usage time. Simply install the app and connect to your desired server.

With 1,260+ fast servers across 60+ countries, Planet VPN delivers high-speed connections, and its no-logs policy ensures your data remains secure. It uses robust protocols like OpenVPN, PlanetX, StarGuard, and IKEv2 for strong encryption, along with DNS and IP leak protection. If you’re looking for an easy, no-cost, and private VPN setup, Planet VPN is a solid choice.

Pros

  • Completely free with no sign-up required
  • Strong basic privacy tools built in
  • Easy to use across many devices

Cons

  • Slow and unstable connections on the free tier
  • Only 11 free server locations

Price: Free. Premium starts at $1.99/month for a 3-year plan, plus 1 year free

Download

4. Proton VPN – Most secure VPN service for iOS

Coming from the house of Proton Mail, ProtonVPN focuses on user privacy with a strict no-log policy under Swiss-based jurisdiction. While it does have a paid subscription plan, Proton Mail also offers a free version of its VPN service, and by free, I mean completely free with zero catches.

With its 4070 servers spanning 85 countries, it is one of the world’s fastest and most extensive networks, offering a truly global experience. When it comes to user security, Proton VPN uses proven AES-256 and ChaCha20 encryption protocols, along with cryptographically secure protocols like WireGuard and OpenVPN.

Pros

  • Strong focus on privacy and security
  • Offers a free plan with limited features
  • No logging policy

Cons

  • Speeds may be slower compared to some other VPNs
  • Limited server selection on free plan

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $79.99)

Download

5. IPVanish – Connect unlimited devices

IPVanish is known for its customizable security features, fast connection speed, and over 2400 extensive server networks with unlimited bandwidth. This extensive server infrastructure lets you easily bypass geo-restrictions and stream content from many countries.

Another exciting feature of IPVanish is that you don’t need to compromise the protection of one device for others, as there are no connection caps, thus securing all your devices simultaneously.

Along with the robust encryption protocols, including AES-256 encryption to secure your data from potential eavesdroppers, IPVanish VPN operates under a strict no-log policy.

Pros

  • Configurable apps 
  • Unlimited simultaneous connections
  • Secure access to media

Cons

  • Based in the US (potential privacy concerns),
  • Has had past controversies over logging policies.

Price: Free trial available. Subscriptions start at $2.19/month for a 2-year plan

Download

6. NordVPN – Advanced security with specialized servers

There cannot be a best VPN list without NordVPN in it. It allows you to connect to six different devices simultaneously and enjoy secure and private access to the internet on both private and public networks.

Unlike other VPNs, NordVPN offers unique double VPN servers, which encrypt data not once but twice, adding an extra layer of encryption.

So, whether you are concerned about safeguarding your online identity, accessing geo-restricted content, or secure browsing on public Wi-Fi networks, NordVPN has every tool and feature in its arsenal to effectively meet your needs.

Pros

  • Vast server network 
  • Strong security and privacy features 
  • Reliable for streaming and torrenting

Cons

  • Speeds can vary depending on server location
  • Occasional connectivity issues on some servers

Price: Subscriptions start at $3.39/month for a 2-year plan

Download

7. VPN by Private Internet Access (PIA) – Strong privacy commitment

Private Internet Access (PIA) is a renowned VPN service that prioritizes user privacy, security, and anonymity over anything else. All this is done with strong encryption protocols such as AES-256 and a strict no-log policy, ensuring maximum security and privacy protection.

It also comes with the Kill Switch capability, which automatically shuts down your internet connection in case the VPN connection suddenly drops, preventing data leaks or real IP address exposure.

If you are unsatisfied with or have any issues with the service, you can also take advantage of its 24/7 chat support and 30-day money-back guarantee.

Pros

  • Affordable pricing
  • Strong privacy features, including a no-logs policy,
  • Supports P2P and torrenting
  • Dedicated IP

Cons

  • The user interface may not be as intuitive for beginners
  • Occasional performance fluctuations

Price: Subscriptions start at $6.99

Download

8. CyberGhost – Complete privacy across Apple devices

The CyberGhost VPN offers the most user-friendly interface with one-click connectivity for all online privacy concerns. With its dedicated servers spanning over 100 countries, 126 locations, and 21 dedicated IP locations, you can enjoy uninterrupted streaming from apps such as Netflix, Hulu, YouTube, Crunchyroll, and more.

Moreover, you can connect up to seven different devices in your household with a single subscription and easily hop from one device to another. It also provides specialized servers for enhanced privacy and security, such as NoSpy servers in Romania.

Pros

  • User-friendly interface
  • Large server network
  • Strong security features
  • Specialized servers for streaming and torrenting

Cons

  • Inconsistent speeds on some servers
  • Occasional difficulty in connecting to certain streaming platforms

Price: Plans start at $2.19/month for a 2-year plan, plus 2 months free

Download

9. Mullvad VPN – Most privacy-centered VPN service

In my experience so far, I have found Mullvad VPN to be the best when it comes to user privacy. This is because, unlike other VPN apps, you don’t need to provide any personal information while creating an account. Instead, the app generates a unique account number for every user, eliminating the need for an email address or other personal information.

In addition, you get all the other VPN features, such as advanced encryption protocols, a no-log policy, the WireGuard protocol, and more. Moreover, it also accepts anonymous payment methods such as cash, Bitcoin, and other cryptocurrencies.

Pros

  • Focus on privacy and anonymity
  • No-logs policy
  • Accepts anonymous payments
  • Strong encryption

Cons

  • Limited server locations
  • Not as effective as others at unblocking geo-restricted content

Price: $5.95 for a 30-day subscription

Download

10. Windscribe – Best free VPN for iPhone

Windscribe offers the most intuitive and user-friendly interface, making it easier for users with little to no technical competence to access VPN services. The high rating on the App Store is proof of this.

Also, unlike any other top VPN apps for iPhone on this list, all Windscribe VPN services are free up to a generous 10GB monthly allowance, allowing you to test the service to its full extent before committing to a paid subscription.

In addition, Windscribe also offers a multi-hop feature, allowing you to route your internet traffic through multiple VPN servers.

Pros

  • Generous free plan with 10GB/month data
  • Strong security features
  • Supports unlimited connections

Cons

  • The free plan has limited server access and slower speeds

Price: Free (Subscriptions start at $3.99 per month)

Download

Enjoy safe and secure browsing

These were some of the best VPNs for iPhones and iPads. Always consider factors such as connection speed, server locations, privacy policies, and security protocols, and prioritize only the one with a proven track record of reliability and make a sound decision.

Which VPN are you going to pick? Do let me know in the comments below.

FAQs

Does VPN slow down iPhone?

No matter which VPN you choose, the connection speed will decline slightly due to the encryption process, which will be slightly burdensome on your iPhone’s battery and processor.

Does the iPhone have a built-in VPN?

Unfortunately, there isn’t a built-in VPN on iPhones.

Also read:

  • How to choose and use a VPN on Mac (Ultimate guide)

"The founder of iGeeksBlog, Dhvanesh, is an Apple aficionado, who cannot stand even a slight innuendo about Apple products. He dons the cap of editor-in-chief to make sure that articles match the quality standard before they are published."

About Dhvanesh

Ever since teenage years, gadgets and technology have held a special place in Dhvanesh's heart. This fascination with gadgets and their inner workings fueled a lifelong passion for exploration and troubleshooting. Disassembled electronic items scattered around the house became a familiar sight during his younger years, a testament to this insatiable curiosity.

From SEO Expert to Apple Evangelist

After completing his IT engineering diploma, Dhvanesh's professional journey began with a 4.5-year stint as an SEO executive, honing valuable digital marketing skills. However, the desire to share tech knowledge and connect with a like-minded community proved stronger. In 2012, Dhvanesh embarked on a new adventure, founding iGeeksBlog. This blog became a haven for Apple enthusiasts and tech aficionados seeking insightful and in-depth information about everything Apple.

A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge

In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. As the founder, he has steered the blog’s vision, ensuring it remains a trusted resource for Apple users worldwide. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development.

Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach

Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience.

Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem

Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. Currently, he also manages the iGeeksBlog+ weekly newsletter, delivering curated Apple news, gadgets, apps, tips and tricks straight to subscribers' inboxes. This unwavering commitment to Apple technology and a genuine desire to empower fellow users make him a valuable asset to the iGeeksBlog team.

title.rendered: How to silence your Apple Watch

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Silent Mode: Silent Mode, enabled in Control Center, mutes all notification sounds but still delivers haptic vibrations, so you can feel alerts without hearing them.
  • Theater Mode: For movies or dark rooms, Theater Mode silences all sounds and haptics and also keeps the screen from lighting up unless you tap it.
  • Do Not Disturb & Focus: Do Not Disturb and other Focus modes you set on your iPhone will automatically sync to your Apple Watch, silencing notifications based on your rules.
  • Cover to Mute Gesture: For immediate silence, use the “Cover to Mute” gesture by placing your palm over the watch face for three seconds when an alert sounds.
  • Your Options: Your watch offers multiple ways to silence alerts, from the basic Silent Mode to the comprehensive Theater Mode and synced Focus modes from your iPhone.

An Apple Watch is a perfect companion device for your iPhone, as it offers alerts for incoming calls, messages, and other notifications even if the iPhone isn’t nearby. While these alerts ensure you don’t miss anything important, they can sometimes get annoying, especially when you turn on Silent Mode on your iPhone but forget to do the same on the Apple Watch.

Knowing how to silence your Apple Watch is helpful in instances that require complete silence, such as during an important meeting or while sleeping. Read on to learn all the ways to silence an Apple Watch.

What does it mean to silence an Apple Watch?

Silencing your Apple Watch is a way to control how your Apple Watch behaves in terms of sound and vibration when an alert arrives. When you silence your Apple Watch, all sounds, including calls, messages, and app notifications, are muted. However, your Apple Watch still uses haptic feedback (gentle vibrations) to alert you so that you can stay updated without drawing attention in quiet environments.

When your watch is silenced, some features still function as normal:

  • Alarms still vibrate to alert you.
  • Timers will buzz on your wrist.
  • Depending on your health settings, you may still get heart rate and noise alerts.
  • Haptics for navigation (Maps) or workouts will still function unless turned off.

Simply put, silencing your Apple Watch is about how you are notified, not whether you are notified.

How to silence an Apple Watch

From enabling Silent Mode and using Theater Mode to covering your Apple Watch with your palm, Apple offers multiple ways to silence your watch, each designed for specific scenarios. Let’s take a look at each of them.

1. Enable Silent Mode

Unlike Focus modes, there is no option to mirror Silent Mode between your iPhone and Apple Watch. Thus, you must enable Silent Mode separately on your Apple Watch if you want to mute the incoming alerts for the time being. You can do this via the Settings app or the Control Center as shown below.

Via Settings:

  1. Open the Settings app and head to Sounds & Haptics.
  2. Here, toggle on the Silent Mode option.

Via Control Center:

  1. Press the Side button to bring up the Control Center.
  2. Here, locate and tap the bell icon to enable Silent Mode on your Apple Watch.

2. Use Theater Mode

Contrary to other Apple Watch features also available on iPhones, Theater Mode is an Apple Watch specific feature. When enabled, it silences all the alerts and dims the Apple Watch screen until you tap it or press the Digital Crown. Additionally, it also disables the Walkie Talkie and Raise to Wake Up functionalities, ensuring no distraction of any kind.

You can turn on Theater Mode on your Apple Watch like this:

  1. Press the Side button to access the Control Center.
  2. Here, locate and tap the Theater Mode button (with a double-mask icon) to put your Apple Watch into Theater Mode.

3. Turn on Do Not Disturb / Focus modes

While Apple, by default, mirrors the Do Not Disturb or Focus modes between the paired iPhone and Apple Watch, the automatic mirroring won’t work if it is turned off in the Watch app. If you have also done the same, you can manually enable the Do Not Disturb mode on your Apple Watch. Once enabled, your Apple Watch will remain silent until DND is turned off.

Here’s how you can turn on Do Not Disturb on your Apple Watch:

  1. Access the Control Center.
  2. Tap the Do Not Disturb icon (crescent Moon icon) and select Do Not Disturb from the available options.
  3. Finally, select the duration for how long you want your Apple Watch to be in that mode.

4. Mute specific app notifications

There are instances where you can’t put your Apple Watch on Silent Mode to avoid missing anything important, but you feel annoyed due to alerts from a specific app. If you are dealing with a similar situation, you can mute notifications from such apps entirely or temporarily. Here’s what you need to do:

  1. Swipe down on the watch face to access the Notification Center.
  2. Here, swipe right on the app notification you want to mute and tap the three-dot button that appears.
  3. Now, depending on the app, choose whether to mute the app notifications for the next hour or the rest of the day or turn them off altogether.

5. Use the Cover to Mute gesture

Imagine you are in a meeting but forget to enable Silent Mode on your Apple Watch, and an incoming alert arrives. Embarrassing, isn’t it? This is exactly where the Cover to Mute gesture can rescue you, allowing you to quickly silence incoming alerts on your Apple Watch. Mind you, this is a way to mute alerts in real-time, so you must act quickly as soon as an alert hits your watch to be able to silence it successfully.

All you need to do is cover your Apple Watch with your palm, and the incoming alert will get silenced. However, for it to work, you need the Cover to Mute gesture enabled on your Apple Watch. Follow these steps to do this:

  1. Open the Settings app and head to Gestures.
  2. Here, toggle on Cover to Mute.

Bonus tip: Prevent Siri from accidentally waking up on your Apple Watch

If you find that Siri wakes up too often by accident, you can easily adjust the settings to prevent it. Here’s how:

  1. In the Settings app, select Siri.

  2. If you want Siri to stop listening to the “Hey Siri” or “Siri” voice command, tap Listen for, then select the Off option on the subsequent menu.
  3. Otherwise, toggle off Raise to Speak and Press Digital Crown.

Signing off…

Those are all the ways to silence an Apple Watch. Whether you want to do it in advance or impromptu (using the Cover to Mute gesture), you can go with a method that best suits you and get control over how and when your watch alerts you.

Got any favorite Apple Watch tricks to stay distraction-free? Let us know in the comments!

FAQs

Does Silent Mode turn off haptic vibrations on an Apple Watch?

No, the Silent Mode does not turn off haptic vibrations on your Apple Watch. It simply disables audio alerts, allowing your watch to continue vibrating for notifications.

Will alarms still work when my Apple Watch is in Silent Mode?

Yes, alarms will still go off when your Apple Watch is in Silent Mode, but instead of making a sound, they will vibrate on your wrist using haptic feedback.

  • How to set a timer on an Apple Watch
  • How to set up cellular on your Apple Watch
  • How to type and enter text on your Apple Watch

@graph.name: How to Enable Silent Mode on Apple Watch via Settings
@graph.description: Turn on Silent Mode on your Apple Watch using the Settings app to mute sound alerts while still receiving haptic notifications.

step.name: Open Settings on Apple Watch
step.text: Press the Digital Crown, open the Settings app, and scroll to Sounds & Haptics.

itemListElement.text: Press the Digital Crown.
Open the Settings app.
Scroll down and tap Sounds & Haptics.

step.name: Enable Silent Mode
step.text: Toggle on Silent Mode to mute alerts while still getting haptic feedback on your Apple Watch.

itemListElement.text: Toggle on Silent Mode.

@graph.name: How to Enable Silent Mode on Apple Watch via Control Center
@graph.description: Quickly enable Silent Mode on your Apple Watch using Control Center to mute sound alerts while still receiving haptic notifications.

step.name: Open Control Center
step.text: Press the Side button to bring up the Control Center on your Apple Watch.

itemListElement.text: Press the Side button.
Wait for Control Center to appear.

step.name: Activate Silent Mode
step.text: Locate the bell icon in Control Center and tap it to enable Silent Mode.

itemListElement.text: Find the bell icon.
Tap the bell icon to toggle Silent Mode on.

@graph.name: How to Use Theater Mode on Apple Watch
@graph.description: Enable Theater Mode on your Apple Watch to keep the display dark and silent in low-light environments like cinemas or theaters.

step.name: Open Control Center
step.text: Press the Side button on your Apple Watch to access Control Center.

itemListElement.text: Press the Side button.
Wait for Control Center to open.

step.name: Enable Theater Mode
step.text: Tap the Theater Mode button, which has a double-mask icon, to activate it and keep your watch dark and silent until you turn it off.

itemListElement.text: Locate the Theater Mode button with a double-mask icon.
Tap it to enable Theater Mode.

@graph.name: How to Turn on Focus on Apple Watch
@graph.description: Enable Focus mode on your Apple Watch via Control Center to minimize distractions and silence notifications for a set duration.

step.name: Open Control Center
step.text: Access the Control Center on your Apple Watch by pressing the Side button or swiping up from the watch face.

itemListElement.text: Press the Side button or swipe up from the bottom.

step.name: Select Do Not Disturb
step.text: Tap the crescent Moon icon to open Focus options, then select Do Not Disturb.

itemListElement.text: Tap the crescent Moon icon.
Select Do Not Disturb from the list.

step.name: Choose duration
step.text: Select how long you want Focus mode to remain active on your Apple Watch.

itemListElement.text: Select a duration option like On, For 1 Hour, or Until This Evening.

@graph.name: How to Mute App Notifications on Apple Watch
@graph.description: Silence notifications from specific apps on your Apple Watch temporarily or permanently using the Notification Center.

step.name: Open Notification Center
step.text: Swipe down from the top of your Apple Watch face to access Notification Center.

itemListElement.text: Swipe down from the top of the watch face.

step.name: Select app notification
step.text: Find the app notification you want to mute, swipe right on it, and tap the three-dot button.

itemListElement.text: Swipe right on the notification.
Tap the three-dot button.

step.name: Mute notifications
step.text: Choose whether to mute notifications for the next hour, the rest of the day, or turn them off entirely for that app.

itemListElement.text: Select Mute for 1 Hour, Mute for Today, or Turn Off.

@graph.name: How to Use Cover to Mute Gesture on Apple Watch
@graph.description: Enable the Cover to Mute gesture on your Apple Watch to quickly silence incoming alerts by covering the display with your palm.

step.name: Open Gestures settings
step.text: On your Apple Watch, open the Settings app and scroll down to Gestures.

itemListElement.text: Press the Digital Crown.
Open the Settings app.
Scroll and select Gestures.

step.name: Enable Cover to Mute
step.text: Toggle on the Cover to Mute option to allow silencing alerts by covering the display with your palm.

itemListElement.text: Toggle on Cover to Mute.

keyPoints.title: Understanding Silence on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Silencing an Apple Watch mutes sounds and notifications but still allows haptic vibrations for alerts, enabling discreet updates without complete notifications.

keyPoints.title: Methods to Silence an Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: You can silence your Apple Watch through multiple methods such as Silent Mode, Theater Mode, Do Not Disturb, muting specific apps, and the Cover to Mute gesture.

keyPoints.title: Activating Silent Mode
keyPoints.explanation: Silent Mode can be enabled via Settings or Control Center, muting sounds for calls, messages, and app alerts while retaining vibrations for alarms and timers.

keyPoints.title: Using Theater Mode
keyPoints.explanation: Theater Mode silences all alerts, dims the screen, and disables features like Raise to Wake and Walkie Talkie to avoid distractions, activated through the Control Center.

keyPoints.title: Additional Silence Options and Tips
keyPoints.explanation: Other options include turning on Do Not Disturb/Focus modes, muting specific app notifications, or using the Cover to Mute gesture for quick, real-time silencing.

title.rendered: How to set a timer on an Apple Watch

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Using the App: The built-in Timers app on your Apple Watch lets you easily set custom timers or choose from a list of convenient presets like 1, 5, or 10 minutes.
  • Siri for Timers: For hands-free control, you can use Siri to quickly start, pause, resume, check, or even name a timer with just a simple voice command.
  • Watch Face Complications: For quick one-tap access, you can add the Timers app or a specific preset timer directly as a complication on your favorite watch face.
  • Running Multiple Timers: On watchOS 8 and later, you can run and manage multiple timers at the same time, each with its own label for easy identification.
  • Best Practices: To maximize efficiency, use Siri to set labeled timers for specific tasks and add your most-used presets as watch face complications for quick starts.

Staying on schedule often comes down to managing the little things in your day-to-day life, such as taking power naps that don’t turn into full-blown sleep sessions or pacing yourself during a workout. A timer can be your best friend for such moments, and it’s much more convenient if the timer lives on your wrist.

Instead of reaching for your iPhone, the Apple Watch lets you set and manage timers in seconds. You can stay on schedule without skipping a beat with just a few taps or a quick voice command to Siri. Let’s see how to set and manage timers on an Apple Watch.

2 ways to set a timer on an Apple Watch

There are two ways to set timers on your Apple Watch, each with its own advantage.

1. Set a timer on an Apple Watch using the Timers app

Similar to the Stopwatch app, your Apple Watch comes with a built-in Timers app that helps you stay efficient, organized, and on schedule. Here’s how to use it to set a timer:

  1. Open the Timers app on your Apple Watch.
  2. Choose one of the available presets or scroll down and tap the + button to create a new timer.

  3. Finally, select the Hours, Minutes, and Seconds tab and rotate the Digital Crown to set the duration.

Once set, tap the Start button to start the timer. You can then:

  • Tap the pause icon to temporarily stop the timer.
  • Tap the play icon to resume the timer.
  • Tap the X button to end the timer.

2. Set a timer on an Apple Watch using Siri

The quickest way to set a timer on your Apple Watch is to ask Siri to do it for you. All you need to do is summon Siri on your Apple Watch and ask, “Set a timer for X minutes.” Siri will confirm your voice command, and the timer will appear in your watch’s Smart Stack.

You can also use Siri on your Apple Watch to pause, resume, or cancel the timer in between or even ask how much time is left.

How to add a timer as a watch face complication

If you have a watch face that supports compilations, you can edit and customize it and add the Timers app or a preset timer compilation to it. This way, you can access the Timers app or start a preset timer with a single tap on your watch face.

Here’s how you can customize the watch face to add a timer compilation to it:

  1. Tap and hold the watch face to customize it.
  2. Here, tap the Edit button, then swipe right to the Compilations tab.
  3. Now, tap the empty compilation spot.
  4. Next, scroll down and select the Timers app.

  5. Finally, choose the desired Timer compilation. You can either choose the Timers app or a preset timer as the watch face compilation.

Once done, you can simply tap the Timer complication on the watch face to start or set a timer on your Apple Watch.

How to set multiple timers on an Apple Watch

Starting watchOS 8, Apple lets you set multiple timers on your Apple Watch at once. Here’s how to go about it:

  1. Open the Timers app and start the first timer as you would normally do.
  2. Once the first timer starts, tap the + button in the top-right corner.

  3. Choose one of the available presets or scroll down and tap the + button to create a custom timer.
  4. Use the Digital Crown to set the timer duration and tap the Start button.
  5. Repeat the process for the number of timers you want to set. All running timers will appear in a list view, and you can pause, resume, and cancel each separately.
  6. To cancel a timer, swipe left on it and tap the X button that appears.

Each timer will run independently, and you’ll receive separate haptic alerts when each one finishes.

Stay on track…

Those are all the ways you can set a timer on your Apple Watch. While every method is quite straightforward, using Siri to set a timer has an added benefit. With Siri, you can give a custom name (label) to each timer so you can easily identify them, which isn’t possible with the other two methods. However, if you often need a preset timer, adding it to the watch face as a compilation is the best approach.

Feel free to reach out to us via comments if you need further help.

You might also like:

  • How to set up cellular on your Apple Watch
  • How to type and enter text on your Apple Watch
  • How to use Water Lock on Apple Watch to eject water

@graph.name: How to Set Timer on Apple Watch using Timers App
@graph.description: Use the Timers app on your Apple Watch to quickly set countdowns with presets or custom durations for workouts, cooking, or reminders.

step.name: Open Timers app
step.text: Open the Timers app on your Apple Watch to begin setting a countdown.

itemListElement.text: Press the Digital Crown.
Open the Timers app.

step.name: Choose preset or create new timer
step.text: Choose one of the available preset timers or scroll down and tap the + button to create a custom timer.

itemListElement.text: Select a preset timer.
Or tap the + button to create your own.

step.name: Set duration
step.text: Select the Hours, Minutes, and Seconds fields, then rotate the Digital Crown to set the desired duration.

itemListElement.text: Tap Hours, Minutes, or Seconds.
Rotate the Digital Crown to adjust time.

step.name: Start and manage timer
step.text: Tap the Start button to begin the timer. Use the pause icon to stop temporarily, the play icon to resume, or the X button to end the timer.

itemListElement.text: Tap Start to begin.
Tap pause to temporarily stop.
Tap play to resume.
Tap X to end the timer.

@graph.name: How to Set Timer on Apple Watch using Siri
@graph.description: Quickly set and manage timers on your Apple Watch hands-free by using Siri voice commands for workouts, cooking, or reminders.

step.name: Activate Siri
step.text: Summon Siri on your Apple Watch by saying 'Hey Siri', holding the Digital Crown, or raising your wrist and speaking.

itemListElement.text: Say 'Hey Siri'.
Or press and hold the Digital Crown.
Or raise your wrist and speak.

step.name: Set a timer with Siri
step.text: Ask Siri to set a timer by saying 'Set a timer for X minutes'. Siri will confirm and start the timer, which will appear in your watch’s Smart Stack.

itemListElement.text: Say 'Set a timer for 10 minutes' or your desired duration.
Wait for Siri to confirm and start the timer.

step.name: Manage the timer with Siri
step.text: You can pause, resume, cancel, or check the remaining time by asking Siri, e.g., 'Pause timer' or 'How much time is left?'.

itemListElement.text: Say 'Pause timer' to stop temporarily.
Say 'Resume timer' to continue.
Say 'Cancel timer' to stop.
Say 'How much time is left?' to check the remaining duration.

@graph.name: How to Add Timer as Watch Face Complication on Apple Watch
@graph.description: Customize your Apple Watch face to add a Timer complication for quick access to countdowns and preset timers.

step.name: Enter watch face customization
step.text: Tap and hold your Apple Watch face until the customization menu appears, then tap Edit.

itemListElement.text: Tap and hold the watch face.
Tap Edit.

step.name: Go to Complications tab
step.text: Swipe right to the Complications tab to select which elements appear on your watch face.

itemListElement.text: Swipe to the Complications tab.

step.name: Select complication spot
step.text: Tap an empty complication spot where you want the Timer shortcut to appear.

itemListElement.text: Tap the empty complication slot.

step.name: Add Timer app
step.text: Scroll through the list, select the Timers app, and then choose your preferred Timer complication. You can select the Timers app or a preset timer.

itemListElement.text: Scroll down and select Timers.
Choose a Timer app shortcut or preset timer.

step.name: Save changes
step.text: Exit customization mode. You can now tap the Timer complication on your watch face to quickly start or set a timer.

itemListElement.text: Press the Digital Crown to save and exit.

@graph.name: How to Set Multiple Timers on Apple Watch
@graph.description: Run multiple countdowns at the same time on your Apple Watch by creating additional timers in the Timers app for cooking, workouts, or reminders.

step.name: Start the first timer
step.text: Open the Timers app and start your first timer as usual by selecting a preset or creating a custom one.

itemListElement.text: Open the Timers app.
Choose a preset or create a custom timer.
Tap Start.

step.name: Add another timer
step.text: Tap the + button in the top-right corner to set another timer.

itemListElement.text: Tap the + button.

step.name: Set duration for new timer
step.text: Choose a preset or scroll down and tap the + button to create a custom timer. Use the Digital Crown to set the duration, then tap Start.

itemListElement.text: Select a preset or create a custom timer.
Set the time using the Digital Crown.
Tap Start.

step.name: Repeat for more timers
step.text: Repeat the process to set as many timers as needed. All running timers will be listed, and you can manage them individually.

itemListElement.text: Repeat adding timers as needed.

step.name: Cancel a timer
step.text: Swipe left on the timer you want to stop and tap the X button to cancel it.

itemListElement.text: Swipe left on the timer.
Tap X to cancel.

keyPoints.title: Using the Apple Watch Timers App
keyPoints.explanation: The built-in Timers app allows users to set timers by choosing presets or creating new ones, with control options to start, pause, resume, or end the timer.

keyPoints.title: Setting Timers with Siri on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Users can quickly set a timer using voice commands with Siri, which can also be used to pause, resume, or check the remaining time of a timer.

keyPoints.title: Adding a Timer as a Watch Face Complication
keyPoints.explanation: You can customize your watch face by adding a Timers app or preset timer as a complication for quick access and one-tap timer starting.

keyPoints.title: Managing Multiple Timers on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Starting with watchOS 8, multiple timers can run simultaneously, each manageable individually with options to pause, resume, or cancel.

keyPoints.title: Tips for Efficient Timer Use on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Using Siri for naming timers and adding preset timers to the watch face are efficient methods for staying on schedule and managing time effectively.

title.rendered: Why you see sensitive content on Instagram and how to control it

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What is Sensitive Content?: Sensitive content on Instagram is material that doesn’t violate rules but may be upsetting or inappropriate, such as suggestive or violent posts from other users.
  • The Control Feature: Instagram’s “Sensitive Content Control” feature lets you manage how much potentially upsetting content you see in areas like Explore, Search, and suggested posts.
  • How to Adjust It: In your settings, you can choose between “Standard,” “More,” or “Less.” Selecting “Less” will show you the fewest posts with sensitive content from others.
  • Impact of a Change: Limiting sensitive content only affects posts from accounts you don’t follow; it does not impact what you see from the people you already follow.
  • The Main Benefit: Adjusting this setting helps create a safer and more predictable Browse experience, which is especially beneficial for younger users or those seeking a calmer feed.

Instagram is one of the most popular social media apps today. But with endless content flowing in, some posts can be upsetting or inappropriate. To give users more control, Instagram offers a Sensitive Content Control feature that lets you manage how much of this content appears in your feed.

In this guide, I’ll show you how to control sensitive content on Instagram and explain why such content might be showing up in your feed in the first place.

What is sensitive content on Instagram?

Sensitive content includes photos or videos that don’t violate Instagram’s Community Guidelines but could be considered disturbing or inappropriate by some users.

According to Instagram, this includes:

  • Sexually suggestive material such as people in see-through clothing, even if not explicit.
  • Graphically violent content, such as images or videos of injuries or fights.
  • Content promoting regulated substances such as vaping, drugs, alcohol, and weapons.
  • Posts with triggering subjects, like mental health challenges or destructive action.
  • Images or videos that illustrate or advertise cosmetic surgery.
  • Content that could be used to market goods or services with health-related claims, such as an advertisement for a weight-loss pill.

Instagram uses Recommendation Guidelines to filter such content, especially for younger users. Still, some posts might slip through. Let’s find out why

Why you’re seeing sensitive content on Instagram

Sometimes, your Explore tab may show stuff that makes you go, “Whoa, didn’t sign up for this.” Most of the time the culprit is the Instagram algorithm glitches. Recently, many users reported a surge in sensitive and NSFW content popping up in the Reels tab and feed. Later, Meta acknowledged the system error and fixed it.

Rather than this, here are some common reasons why sensitive content might be showing up in your feed or Explore page:

  • Your sensitive content settings allow it: If your settings are on Standard or More, Instagram will show you a mix of regular and possibly sensitive content. We will discuss these filter levels later in the post.
  • Your following: The accounts you follow also affect what you see. If you follow people or pages that often post edgy, bold or adult content, Instagram may also begin to show you other users posting similar kinds of content.
  • Your activity on Instagram: Instagram tracks your previous actions, such as the posts you like, save or comment on, to figure out what types of content to show you. If you’ve interacted with posts deemed sensitive, Instagram may presume you’re fine to see that type of content.
  • Explore, Reels, and Suggested Posts: Sensitive content is more likely to show up in these areas rather than in your regular feed. There Instagram tries to show you new content you might like, even from people you don’t follow.

The good news is that Instagram gives you the choice to manage your own experience and make it more comfortable and enjoyable.

Understanding Instagram’s Sensitive Content Control

Sensitive Content Control allows you to manage the level of sensitive content you see in:

  • Explore
  • Search
  • Reels
  • Suggested Posts
  • Accounts You Might Like
  • Feed Recommendations

However, it does not affect the content of the people you follow.

Instagram gives you three levels of control:

  • Standard (Default): Filters out some sensitive content but not all.
  • More: Allows more sensitive content to appear.
  • Less: Blocks most sensitive content—ideal for avoiding mature or triggering posts.

If you’re under 18, Instagram automatically sets this to Less and disables the “More” option.

How to limit sensitive content on Instagram

You can adjust your Sensitive Content settings through the mobile app or a web browser.

On iPhone and Android

  1. Open the Instagram app and tap your profile picture.
  2. Tap the menu (☰) at the top right.
  3. Go to What You See → Content preferences → Sensitive content.

  4. Select Less, then tap Confirm.

That’s all! The change kicks in right away—though I suggest restarting the app just to be sure. You may also clear the Instagram cache on your iPhone to get rid of old search history and pre-loaded media.

Using a web browser

  1. Visit instagram.com and log in.
  2. Click your profile picture → Settings (gear icon) → Choose Settings and Privacy.

  3. Select Content preferences, and click Sensitive content from the right side.

  4. Select Less and confirm.

Even after restricting sensitive content, if you are still unhappy with your feed, you can fix it. Check out our detailed guide to learn how to reset the Instagram algorithm.

What happens when you limit sensitive content on Instagram?

Limiting sensitive content on Instagram simply tells the app that you don’t want to view posts that you may find upsetting, disturbing or inappropriate. This doesn’t eliminate all sensitive content, but it minimizes your exposure to it—particularly from people or pages that you don’t follow.

Here’s what happens when you tweak your settings:

  • If you select the Less option in your Sensitive Content Control settings, Instagram will seek to not show you posts that feature topics I mentioned before. It has an impact on Explore, Search results, Reels, and Suggested posts in your main feed from people you don’t follow.
  • Sensitive Content Control only applies to accounts you don’t follow. So, if one of the people you follow shares something offensive, it can still appear in your feed or stories. You may report those inappropriate posts, or you can unfollow, mute or block the account.
  • Restricting sensitive content can create a healthier and more peaceful Instagram feed. This is particularly good for young users, users who want to avoid certain topics, and users who want safer browsing.

Keep in mind that while this feature limits your exposure to your content, it doesn’t necessarily guarantee the removal of every piece of sensitive material. That being said, you can reset your Instagram Explore page to customize it as you like.

Signing off

That’s how you can limit sensitive content on Instagram. It’s a powerful way to create a browsing experience that aligns with your comfort level and preferences. If you’ve been feeling overwhelmed by unwanted posts, give this setting a try—and let me know if it made a difference!

  • How to download Instagram reels on iPhone
  • Tips to use Instagram on iPhone like a pro

@graph.name: How to Limit Sensitive Content on Instagram on iPhone
@graph.description: Adjust Instagram settings on your iPhone to limit sensitive content by selecting the Less option under content preferences.

step.name: Open Instagram profile
step.text: Open the Instagram app and tap your profile picture in the bottom right corner.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Instagram app.
Tap your profile picture.

step.name: Access sensitive content settings
step.text: Tap the menu (☰) at the top right, go to What You See → Content preferences → Sensitive content.

itemListElement.text: Tap the menu icon.
Go to What You See.
Tap Content preferences.
Select Sensitive content.

step.name: Select Less option
step.text: Choose Less to limit sensitive content on Instagram, then tap Confirm to save your preference.

itemListElement.text: Select Less.
Tap Confirm.

@graph.name: How to Limit Sensitive Content on Instagram Web
@graph.description: Reduce the amount of sensitive content shown on Instagram when using the web version by adjusting content preferences in settings.

step.name: Open Instagram settings
step.text: Go to instagram.com, log in, click your profile picture, select Settings (gear icon), then choose Settings and Privacy.

itemListElement.text: Visit instagram.com and log in.
Click your profile picture.
Select Settings (gear icon).
Choose Settings and Privacy.

step.name: Access sensitive content settings
step.text: Select Content preferences, then click Sensitive content from the right-hand menu.

itemListElement.text: Select Content preferences.
Click Sensitive content.

step.name: Limit sensitive content
step.text: Choose Less to limit sensitive content on Instagram, then confirm your selection.

itemListElement.text: Select Less.
Confirm the change.

keyPoints.title: What is sensitive content on Instagram?
keyPoints.explanation: Sensitive content includes posts that don't violate guidelines but may be disturbing or inappropriate, such as sexually suggestive material, violent content, or posts promoting regulated substances.

keyPoints.title: Reasons for seeing sensitive content on Instagram
keyPoints.explanation: Sensitive content may appear due to your content settings, the accounts you follow, your activity, or in areas like Explore and Reels, often affected by algorithm glitches or your interaction history.

keyPoints.title: Instagram’s Sensitive Content Control features
keyPoints.explanation: This feature allows users to manage sensitive content in Explore, Search, Reels, and suggested posts through three levels: Standard, More, or Less, with the latter blocking most sensitive material.

keyPoints.title: How to adjust sensitive content settings
keyPoints.explanation: Users can change their preferences via the Instagram app or web browser, selecting Less to minimize sensitive posts, which takes effect immediately after saving the setting.

keyPoints.title: Impact of limiting sensitive content
keyPoints.explanation: Restricting sensitive content reduces exposure to upsetting posts from non-followed accounts, creating a safer browsing experience, particularly beneficial for young users and those seeking a more peaceful feed.

title.rendered: Tim Cook Teases Apple’s Most Exciting Product Roadmap Yet

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Tim Cook says Apple’s future pipeline is the most exciting ever, hinting at a burst of innovation not seen in years.
  • Apple is reportedly developing new iPhones, iPads, Macs, and AirPods, plus long-rumored products like foldables, Apple Glasses, and smart home hardware.
  • Despite lagging in generative AI, Apple is doubling down on hardware-led intelligence, including smarter Siri upgrades and ambient smart device features.
  • CEO excitement may signal major product shifts, not just upgrades, with new categories poised to reshape Apple’s long-term roadmap and public perception.
  • Big promises don’t guarantee breakthroughs, and Apple still needs to deliver on execution before this wave of products can be called revolutionary.

Tim Cook has made bullish statements about Apple before, but his latest remarks to employees suggest something more than the usual executive optimism. In an internal all-hands meeting held at the Steve Jobs Theater just a day after Apple’s earnings call and renewed scrutiny over its AI strategy, Cook said he has “never felt so much excitement and energy” around Apple’s product roadmap in his nearly 30-year tenure.

That’s a bold claim from the CEO who helped launch the iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods.

What’s Fueling the Hype?

While Cook stopped short of naming specific products, he emphasized the scope of what’s ahead. According to attendees, Apple is preparing its broadest hardware slate in years. That reportedly includes refreshed iPhones, iPads, Macs, and updated AirPods. More notably, speculation continues to swirl around foldable devices, long-rumored Apple Glasses, and new entries into the smart home category.

The comments appear timed to shift focus back to Apple’s core hardware strengths, as the company faces questions over its AI leadership. Cook didn’t ignore AI entirely, he called it “as big or bigger” than the internet or smartphone revolutions. Senior VP Craig Federighi also addressed internal concerns about Siri’s delay in adopting generative AI, explaining that a hybrid architecture had been abandoned in favor of maintaining “Apple quality.”

Strategic Pacing or PR Play?

Cook’s enthusiasm isn’t new, but this level of public internal confidence comes at a pivotal moment. Apple’s main hardware lines are aging, and investor patience is thinning as rivals push aggressively into AI and new form factors. A successful launch of Apple Glasses could establish a new category altogether. Fresh home devices might allow Apple to compete more directly with Amazon and Google in smart environments. And a rumored budget MacBook equipped with an iPhone-class chip could reset Apple’s pricing conversation.

Of course, CEO hyperbole doesn’t guarantee a breakthrough. Cook’s statements might just be aimed at energizing staff or reassuring stakeholders during a transition year. But given Apple’s careful approach to internal messaging, it’s notable when its CEO says the next chapter is unlike anything before.

If the coming hardware actually matches the anticipation Cook is cultivating, Apple could be on the verge of its most consequential product cycle in a decade.

Are you buying the hype, or waiting to see what ships? Drop your thoughts below.

keyPoints.title: Apple's Newfound Excitement Under Tim Cook's Leadership
keyPoints.explanation: Tim Cook expressed unprecedented enthusiasm about Apple's product pipeline during an all-hands meeting, indicating a significant boost in innovation and development activity.

keyPoints.title: Upcoming Apple Products and Innovations
keyPoints.explanation: Apple is developing a broad range of products including new iPhone models, iPad, Mac refreshes, updated AirPods, and potentially foldable devices, Apple Glasses, and new Home products.

keyPoints.title: Focus on Hardware and Artificial Intelligence
keyPoints.explanation: Despite criticism over lagging AI developments, Apple emphasizes its core strength in hardware, with plans to enhance AI integration, including work on Siri and other smart device features.

keyPoints.title: Significance of CEO's Enthusiasm and Potential New Markets
keyPoints.explanation: Cook's high level of excitement could signal major new product categories like Apple Glasses and expanded Home devices, aiming to rejuvenate Apple's innovation image and market reach.

keyPoints.title: Cautious Optimism About Apple's Future Releases

title.rendered: Future iPhones May Feature Image Sensor Rivaling Human Eye’s Dynamic Range

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple developing human-eye-level image sensor: A leaked prototype hints at breakthrough dynamic range tech for iPhone, aiming to match human visual perception.
  • New patent shows two-layer sensor design: Apple’s stacked architecture separates light capture and processing, promising sharper images with less noise.
  • 20 stops of dynamic range could rival cinema gear: If realized, this sensor would outpace most smartphones and challenge professional cameras in photo and video quality.
  • LOFIC tech and noise reduction built in: The sensor packs real-time memory circuitry and low-noise readout, improving highlights and shadows in harsh lighting.
  • Could reshape Apple’s camera supply chain: In-house sensor design would reduce reliance on Sony and enable faster, deeper camera innovation in future iPhones.

Apple appears to be working on a next-generation image sensor that could significantly boost iPhone camera performance, possibly reaching dynamic range levels comparable to the human eye. That’s according to a leak shared on Weibo, which suggests a prototype sensor is already under internal testing.

Apple Patent Suggests Major Camera Shift

A patent titled “Image Sensor With Stacked Pixels Having High Dynamic Range and Low Noise” was filed by Apple last month. The document outlines a two-layer sensor architecture combining stacked silicon dies, each responsible for a different stage of image capture and processing.

The upper layer the sensor die collects incoming light, while the lower logic die handles real-time image processing, including exposure control and noise suppression. The combination of both layers could deliver up to 20 stops of dynamic range, potentially rivaling or even exceeding current high-end cinema cameras.

For perspective:

  • The human eye typically achieves between 20 and 30 stops, depending on adaptation and light conditions.
  • Smartphone cameras today generally manage 10 to 13 stops.
  • Premium digital cinema cameras like the ARRI ALEXA 35 fall slightly below Apple’s claimed threshold.

Even if Apple’s sensor doesn’t fully hit its projected mark, the improvement could still position future iPhones well above the current mobile camera ceiling.

Technical Design: LOFIC and Real-Time Noise Reduction

The sensor die includes a key feature known as the Lateral Overflow Integration Capacitor (LOFIC). This tech enables each pixel to hold varying amounts of light in a single exposure, which helps retain detail in both highlights and shadows a common challenge in mobile photography.

Meanwhile, the logic die integrates memory circuitry within each pixel to measure and cancel thermal noise in real time, effectively minimizing grain before software even touches the image. In theory, this would lead to cleaner, more natural-looking results across difficult lighting environments.

From Patent Filing to Internal Testing

While the patent was just filed last month, the pace of development appears to be moving quickly. The Weibo account ‘Fixed Focus Digital‘ claims Apple already has a working prototype undergoing internal tests. If the timeline holds, this sensor could appear in iPhone 19 or iPhone 20 models, though no official plans have been confirmed.

Still, given the complex transition involved in replacing long-used Sony sensors, Apple may need multiple development cycles to finalize the hardware and production pipelines.

Implications for Apple’s Camera Strategy

All current iPhone models rely on Sony’s camera sensors, which also use a two-layer design. However, Apple’s proposed architecture introduces new elements and promises a more compact footprint. Building its own sensors could give Apple tighter control over the entire imaging pipeline, aligning with broader moves away from third-party component suppliers as seen in its shift from Intel to Apple Silicon, and its ongoing efforts to reduce reliance on Qualcomm.

If Apple succeeds, this would mark one of the most dramatic hardware leaps in iPhone camera history, potentially closing the gap between smartphone and professional-grade cinematography.

Would Apple designing its own high-dynamic-range sensor change how you view iPhone cameras? Let us know what you’d make of the shift below.

title.rendered: How to Set up Text Replacement on Your iPhone, iPad, and Mac

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What It Is: Text Replacement is a feature that lets you create shortcuts (like “omw”) that automatically expand into longer phrases, saving you time and reducing repetitive typing.
  • On iPhone/iPad: On an iPhone or iPad, you can create new shortcuts by navigating to Settings > General > Keyboard and then selecting the “Text Replacement” menu.
  • On Mac: On a Mac, you can add, edit, or delete your text shortcuts by going into System Settings and clicking on the “Keyboard” section.
  • Syncing Across Devices: Your custom text replacements will automatically sync across all your Apple devices as long as you are signed into the same Apple ID with iCloud Drive enabled.
  • Best Practices: For best results, create short shortcuts for frequently used email addresses, phone numbers, or common phrases to maximize your typing efficiency on all devices.

It can be frustrating to type the same thing, like your email ID, home address, or standard replies to messages or emails, over and over. But what if I told you that your Apple devices have a feature that can save you this repetitive typing?

It’s called text replacement, and with it, you can create shortcuts to replace long words or phrases. Read on to learn more about text replacement and find out how to set it up on your Apple devices.

What is text replacement on Apple devices?

Text replacement is a built-in feature on your iPhone, iPad, and Mac that lets you create shortcuts for longer phrases, words, or even emojis. It’s a simple yet powerful way to boost productivity and avoid repetitive typing.

Whether it’s emails, addresses, names, or your favorite emoji combos, text replacement speeds up everyday typing. Once set up, you only need to type the shortcut, and your device will automatically expand it to the full word or phrase you’ve assigned to it.

Here are a few examples of text replacement shortcuts:

  • gm: Good morning
  • addr: Platform 9 3/4, King’s Cross Station, London
  • email: abc@igeeksblog.com

The best part? Your text replacements automatically sync across all your Apple devices using iCloud. So once you set them up, they’re available and ready for use on your iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

How to set up text replacements on an iPhone or iPad

Text replacement is available on all Apple devices. However, the process to set it up is different on an iPhone or iPad compared to a Mac.

Create a text replacement shortcut

Speeding up your typing on your iPhone or iPad is just a few taps away. To create a text replacement shortcut on your iPhone and iPad, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Go to General > Keyboard > Text Replacement.

  3. Tap the + icon in the top-right corner.
  4. In the Phrase field, type what you want the shortcut to expand to. In the Shortcut field, enter the text you’ll type to trigger it.
  5. Tap Save, and you’re all set.

Now, whenever you type in the shortcut word, it will automatically be replaced with whatever you typed in the phrase field.

Edit or delete a text replacement shortcut

Mistyped a shortcut? Or no longer need one. You can edit your text replacement shortcuts to change the phrases and shortcut texts or even delete them entirely. Here’s how:

  1. Head to Settings > General > Keyboard > Text Replacement.
  2. Tap Edit in the bottom corner.
  3. Tap the – button beside the shortcut you want to delete, then tap Delete.

  4. To edit, tap the shortcut, make your changes, and hit Save.

How to set up text replacements on a Mac

The text replacement you set up on your iPhone or iPad automatically syncs with your Mac as well. However, if you want to set up text replacement on your Mac devices, follow these steps.

Create a text replacement shortcut

Creating a text replacement shortcut on a Mac is as easy as it is on an iPhone. Follow these simple steps:

  1. Open System Settings on your Mac.
  2. Select Keyboard from the sidebar, then under Text Input, click Text Replacements.

  3. Click the + button.
  4. Under Replace, enter your shortcut.

  5. Under With, enter the phrase you want it to expand to.
  6. Click Add, and you’re done.

Edit or remove a text replacement shortcut

If you want to update the shortcuts or clean up the lists, you can do it on your Mac like this:

  1. Go to System Settings > Keyboard.
  2. Under Text Input, click Text Replacements.

  3. Select the shortcut you want to edit, press the Return key on your keyboard, and make your changes.
  4. To delete, select the shortcut and click the – button below the list to remove it.

How to sync text replacements across Apple devices

Apple makes it seamless to keep your text replacement shortcuts synced across iPhone, iPad, and Mac. In fact, they sync across all your devices automatically. However, if they don’t, here’s how to make sure they do:

  1. Ensure you’re signed in with the same Apple Account on all your devices.
  2. On your iPhone, go to Settings, click your name at the top, and select iCloud. Ensure the Sync this iPhone toggle is turned on.

  3. Confirm that iCloud Drive is also enabled on your Mac: Go to System Settings, tap your name at the top, and select iCloud. Turn on sync for iCloud Drive by toggling on the Sync this Mac button.

Wait a few minutes for your shortcuts to sync automatically.

For more tips on syncing content across Apple devices, check out our guide on how to sync iPhone and iPad to Mac.

Signing off

Text replacement is one of those underrated Apple features that, once you start using, you’ll wonder how you lived without it. Whether streamlining work emails or texting that one boomer friend who hates short Gen-Z words, text replacement will replace the words easily for you in your chats and emails.

Go ahead, set up your shortcuts today, and let your Apple devices do the heavy typing for you!

step.name: Open Text Replacement settings
step.text: Open the Settings app, go to General, then Keyboard, and tap Text Replacement.

itemListElement.text: Tap Settings.
Go to General > Keyboard.
Tap Text Replacement.

step.name: Add a new shortcut
step.text: Tap the + icon in the top-right corner to add a new text replacement shortcut.

itemListElement.text: Tap the + icon.

step.name: Enter phrase and shortcut
step.text: In the Phrase field, type the full text you want the shortcut to expand to. In the Shortcut field, type the trigger text that will insert the phrase.

itemListElement.text: Type the phrase in the Phrase field.
Type the shortcut in the Shortcut field.

step.name: Save the shortcut
step.text: Tap Save to store the new text replacement shortcut on your iPhone.

itemListElement.text: Tap Save.

Tap Text Replacement.

step.name: Delete a shortcut

Tap Delete.

Tap Save.

@graph.description: Create a text replacement shortcut on your Mac by adding a custom shortcut and phrase in the Keyboard settings for faster typing.

step.name: Access text replacement settings
step.text: Open System Settings on your Mac, select Keyboard from the sidebar, then under Text Input, click Text Replacements.

itemListElement.text: Click System Settings.
Select Keyboard from the sidebar.
Click Text Replacements under Text Input.

step.name: Add a new shortcut
step.text: Click the + button to create a new text replacement shortcut.

itemListElement.text: Click the + button.

step.name: Enter shortcut and phrase
step.text: In the Replace field, type the shortcut you want to use. In the With field, enter the full phrase you want it to expand to.

itemListElement.text: Type the shortcut in the Replace field.
Type the phrase in the With field.

step.name: Save the shortcut
step.text: Click Add to save the new text replacement shortcut on your Mac.

itemListElement.text: Click Add.

@graph.name: How to Edit or Remove Text Replacement Shortcut on Mac
@graph.description: Edit or delete text replacement shortcuts on your Mac through the Keyboard settings for quick typing customization.

step.name: Open text replacement settings
step.text: Go to System Settings > Keyboard, then under Text Input, click Text Replacements.

itemListElement.text: Click System Settings.
Select Keyboard.
Click Text Replacements under Text Input.

step.name: Edit a shortcut
step.text: Select the shortcut you want to edit, press the Return key on your keyboard, make your changes, and press Return again to save.

itemListElement.text: Select the shortcut to edit.
Press Return and modify the text.
Press Return to save changes.

step.name: Delete a shortcut
step.text: Select the shortcut you want to delete, then click the – button below the list to remove it.

itemListElement.text: Select the shortcut.
Click the – button to delete.

@graph.name: How to Sync Text Replacements Across Apple Devices
@graph.description: Sync your text replacement shortcuts across iPhone, iPad, and Mac using iCloud so they stay updated on all your Apple devices.

step.name: Sign in with the same Apple ID
step.text: Make sure you’re signed in with the same Apple Account on all your devices.

itemListElement.text: Check that the same Apple ID is used on each device.

step.name: Enable iCloud sync on iPhone
step.text: On your iPhone, go to Settings, tap your name, and select iCloud. Ensure the Sync this iPhone toggle is turned on.

itemListElement.text: Open Settings.
Tap your name at the top.
Select iCloud.
Toggle on Sync this iPhone.

step.name: Enable iCloud Drive sync on Mac
step.text: On your Mac, go to System Settings, tap your name at the top, and select iCloud. Turn on Sync this Mac for iCloud Drive.

itemListElement.text: Open System Settings.
Tap your name at the top.
Select iCloud.
Toggle on Sync this Mac.

step.name: Wait for sync
step.text: Wait a few minutes for your text replacements to sync across all devices automatically.

itemListElement.text: Allow a few minutes for syncing to complete.

keyPoints.title: Introduction to Text Replacement on Apple Devices
keyPoints.explanation: Text replacement is a built-in feature on iPhone, iPad, and Mac that allows users to create shortcuts for longer phrases or words, boosting productivity by reducing repetitive typing.

keyPoints.title: Examples of Text Replacement Shortcuts
keyPoints.explanation: Common shortcuts include 'gm' for 'Good morning' and 'addr' for a specific address, which automatically expand into the full text when typed.

keyPoints.title: Setting Up Text Replacement on iPhone and iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Users can create shortcuts by navigating to Settings > General > Keyboard > Text Replacement, then adding new shortcuts and phrases manually.

keyPoints.title: Creating and Managing Shortcuts on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: On Mac, text replacements are set up via System Settings > Keyboard > Text Replacements, where new shortcuts can be added, edited, or deleted easily.

keyPoints.title: Syncing Text Replacements Across Devices
keyPoints.explanation: Text replacements automatically sync across all Apple devices using iCloud, but users should ensure they are signed into the same Apple ID and iCloud Drive is enabled on all devices.
