keyPoints.title: Instagram Blend Overview
keyPoints.explanation: Instagram Blend is a feature that creates a shared Reels feed within DMs by merging friends' viewing preferences, making Reel discovery more social and personalized.

keyPoints.title: How Instagram Blend Works
keyPoints.explanation: The feature functions by initiating a Blend in a chat, leading to a curated Reels feed based on mutual interests, which is refreshed daily and visible to participants.

keyPoints.title: Setting Up Instagram Blend
keyPoints.explanation: To set up a Blend, users send an invite in DMs, and once accepted by the other party, the shared Reels feed is automatically created.

keyPoints.title: Interacting with the Blend Feed
keyPoints.explanation: After activation, users can access the curated Reels by tapping the Blend icon in DMs, and they can interact with the content through liking, sharing, or chatting.

keyPoints.title: Leaving an Instagram Blend
keyPoints.explanation: Users can exit a Blend at any time by going to the specific Blend, tapping the settings, and confirming the leave action, thereby stopping the shared feed.

Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: How to screen record on your Mac (With or without audio)

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What It Is: Screen recording creates a video of your Mac’s screen activity, which is perfect for making tutorials, demonstrating software, or documenting issues for tech support.
  • Available Methods: You can use the built-in Screenshot Toolbar for quick captures, QuickTime for basic recordings, or third-party apps for professional features and more control.
  • The Easiest Method: For the easiest method, press `Shift+Command+5` to open the Screenshot Toolbar. From there, you can record the entire screen or a selected portion.
  • QuickTime’s Limitation: QuickTime Player offers basic screen recording but importantly, it cannot capture your Mac’s internal audio, only audio from an external microphone by default.
  • For Advanced Features: For professional results, use third-party apps like OBS Studio or ScreenFlow to record internal audio, edit your video, and add annotations.

A screen recording is more than just a tech trick—it’s a powerful tool for sharing tutorials, capturing issues, or documenting live events. Whether you’re walking someone through an app or saving a Zoom call for later, macOS makes it incredibly simple with built-in options like Screenshot Toolbar and QuickTime Player.

In this guide, I’ll explain how to record your Mac screen using native tools and when you might need a third-party app. Let’s get started.

What is Screen Recording on Mac?

Screen recording allows you to create a video of everything happening on your Mac’s screen. Unlike a screenshot, which freezes a single moment, screen recording captures the full experience in real time—ideal for walkthroughs, troubleshooting, or preserving digital events like webinars or video calls.

3 Easy ways to screen record on Mac

There are a few different ways to screen record on your Mac. I’ve discussed them all in detail below.

1. Using Screenshot Toolbar (macOS Mojave and later)

If you’re running macOS Mojave or newer, press Shift + Command + 5 to launch the Screenshot Toolbar.

Here’s how to get started:

  1. Choose what to record: Select either Record Entire Screen or Record Selected Portion.

  2. Click Options in the toolbar to customize your recording settings as follows:

    • Choose a location where your screen recording will be saved. By default, they are saved to your desktop.
    • Select a microphone if you want to record a voiceover or other audio with the screen recording.
    • Select a timer to delay the recording by five or ten seconds after you click Record.
    • Select Show Mouse Clicks to see a black circle around your pointer when you click during the recording.
    • After selecting your options, click Record to begin the screen recording.
  3. To stop screen recording, click the Stop button in the menu bar, or use the keyboard shortcut of Command + Control + Esc (Escape).

2. Using QuickTime Player

QuickTime Player is another built-in app perfect for quick recordings.

Steps to use QuickTime:

  1. Open QuickTime Player from the Applications folder.
  2. In the menu bar, click File > New Screen Recording.

  3. A small recording window will appear with a Record button in the center.
  4. Click the small arrow next to the Record button.
  5. Under Microphone, choose either:
    • Internal Microphone – to capture your voice or external sounds.
    • External Microphone – if you have a plugged-in or Bluetooth mic.



      If you don’t select a microphone, your screen recording will be silent. Since macOS doesn’t allow QuickTime to capture internal system audio by default, you’ll need third-party screen recording software to include it. We’ll cover those options in the next section.
  6. Click the red Record button to begin recording. You’ll see two options:
    • Click anywhere on the screen to record the full screen.
    • Or, drag to select a specific portion of the screen to record, then click Start Recording within the selection.

  7. To stop, click the Stop button in the menu bar or press Command + Control + Esc.

The recording will automatically open in QuickTime when done.

QuickTime doesn’t record internal audio. For that, you’ll need a third-party tool.

3. Use Third-Party apps (For Pro features)

Although macOS has built-in functionality for basic screen recording, you may want to use third-party apps when you need more control and features such as screen recording with audio. Some of the best apps tools such as:

  1. OBS Studio: Open-source, great for streamers and advanced setups
  2. ScreenFlow: Excellent editing tools and effects
  3. EaseUS RecExperts: Intuitive interface with internal audio recording

For a more advanced setup, check out our step-by-step guide on how to screen record on a Mac with audio using EaseUS RecExperts.

These are ideal for educators, gamers, YouTubers, or professionals creating high-quality tutorials or presentations.

Where do screen recordings save on Mac?

By default, screen recordings on a Mac are automatically saved to your Desktop. Once you stop recording, a video file with a name like Screen Recording [date] will appear. This makes it easy to find your recording right away without digging through folders.

If you’re using the Screenshot Toolbar (Command + Shift + 5), you can also click on Options before starting your recording to choose a different save location, such as Documents, Downloads, or a custom folder.

No matter which method you use, you can always move or rename the file later just like any other video on your Mac.

How to edit screen recordings on a Mac

For Quick Edits:

  • Use QuickTime Player: Open the video > Click Edit > Trim > Drag sliders to crop beginning or end.

For More Advanced Editing:

Try iMovie (free) to add:

  • Transitions
  • Titles
  • Music or Voiceover

For high-level editing, use third-party video editors like ScreenFlow or DaVinci Resolve give you even more control.

Pro tips for high-quality Mac screen recordings

Want your recordings to look polished and professional? Here’s how:

  • Record only what matters: Select the portion of the screen you need.
  • Close clutter: Quit unused apps and tabs to keep the screen tidy.
  • Use Focus Mode: Enable Do Not Disturb or Focus to block notifications.
  • Use an external mic: Better sound can elevate your recording quality.
  • Test before the real deal: Run a quick practice recording to catch any setup errors.
  • Watch your final cut: Always review before sharing.

Signing off

Screen recording on a Mac is easy, whether you’re using the Screenshot Toolbar, QuickTime Player, or advanced apps like OBS Studio. I hope this guide made it clearer for you to record what’s on your Mac screen like a pro.

Got questions? Drop them below—I’m happy to help!

Other interesting posts:

  • How to take a screenshot on Mac
  • How to take a screenshot on Apple TV using Mac
  • 3 Ways to share your Mac screen with another Mac
  • 3 Way to screen record on Windows 11

@graph.name: How to Record Screen on Mac Using Screenshot Toolbar
@graph.description: Record your Mac screen using the built-in Screenshot Toolbar in macOS Mojave or later. Choose full-screen or partial recording, customize settings, and save your video.

tool.name: Mac computer running macOS Mojave or newer

step.name: Open Screenshot Toolbar
step.text: Press Shift + Command + 5 to launch the Screenshot Toolbar on macOS Mojave or newer.

itemListElement.text: Press Shift + Command + 5.

step.name: Choose recording type
step.text: Select either Record Entire Screen or Record Selected Portion depending on what you want to capture.

itemListElement.text: Select Record Entire Screen.
Or select Record Selected Portion.

step.name: Open recording options
step.text: Click Options in the toolbar to customize your recording preferences such as save location, microphone input, timer, and mouse click visibility.

itemListElement.text: Click Options in the toolbar.
Select save location.
Select microphone if needed.
Set timer if required.
Enable Show Mouse Clicks if desired.

step.name: Start recording
step.text: Click Record to begin capturing your screen based on your selected settings.

itemListElement.text: Click Record.

step.name: Stop recording
step.text: Click the Stop button in the menu bar or press Command + Control + Esc to end the recording.

itemListElement.text: Click Stop in the menu bar.
Or press Command + Control + Esc.

@graph.name: How to Record Screen on Mac Using QuickTime Player
@graph.description: Record your Mac screen using QuickTime Player. Choose full screen or a selected portion, configure microphone settings, and stop recording with ease.

step.name: Open QuickTime Player
step.text: Launch QuickTime Player from the Applications folder on your Mac.

itemListElement.text: Go to Applications.
Open QuickTime Player.

step.name: Start a new screen recording
step.text: In the menu bar, click File > New Screen Recording to open the recording window.

itemListElement.text: Click File in the menu bar.
Select New Screen Recording.

step.name: Select microphone input
step.text: Click the arrow next to the Record button to choose your microphone: Internal Microphone for built-in audio or External Microphone for connected devices.

itemListElement.text: Click the arrow next to Record.
Select Internal or External Microphone.

step.name: Choose recording area
step.text: Click the red Record button. Click anywhere to record the full screen, or drag to select a portion and click Start Recording.

itemListElement.text: Click the red Record button.
Click anywhere for full screen recording.
Drag to select area and click Start Recording.

step.name: Stop recording
step.text: Click the Stop button in the menu bar or press Command + Control + Esc to end recording.

itemListElement.text: Click Stop in the menu bar.
Or press Command + Control + Esc.

keyPoints.title: Definition of Screen Recording on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: Screen recording on Mac creates a video of all activity on your screen, useful for tutorials, troubleshooting, or documenting live events, unlike static screenshots.

keyPoints.title: Methods for Screen Recording on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: There are three primary methods: using the Screenshot Toolbar, QuickTime Player, or third-party applications for more advanced features like audio recording.

keyPoints.title: Using the Screenshot Toolbar
keyPoints.explanation: Press Shift + Command + 5 on macOS Mojave or later to access the Screenshot Toolbar, where you can select recording options, customize settings, and start or stop recordings.

keyPoints.title: Using QuickTime Player
keyPoints.explanation: Open QuickTime Player, navigate to File > New Screen Recording, choose microphone options, and then start recording either the entire screen or a selected portion.

keyPoints.title: Third-Party Apps for Enhanced Recording Features
keyPoints.explanation: For added control and features such as internal audio recording, third-party apps like OBS Studio, ScreenFlow, or EaseUS RecExperts are recommended, especially for professional use.

title.rendered: Grok just got smarter Visual Intelligence on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What is Grok Vision?: Grok Vision uses your iPhone’s camera to identify objects and provide spoken, conversational AI responses about them.
  • vs. Apple’s AI: Unlike Apple’s static recognition, Grok Vision offers dynamic, voice-based AI conversations about what it sees.
  • Accessibility and Cost: The feature is free for all compatible iPhones, while Android users need a paid subscription for access.
  • The Bigger Picture: Grok’s conversational approach to visual AI is making advanced features more natural and universally accessible.
  • Key Advantages: Advantages include real-time analysis, multi-language support, and no new hardware requirements for iPhone users.

With its latest update, xAI’s chatbot can now see the world through your iPhone camera and talk to you about it in real time. It’s so good, this feels like what Apple’s Visual Intelligence should have been. But instead, we’re getting it through third-party apps like ChatGPT—and now, Grok. Here’s what Grok’s new vision capabilities look like and how they compare to Apple’s Visual Intelligence.

What exactly is Grok’s new vision mode?

Grok Vision turns your iPhone camera into a real-time AI lens. You can point it at anything—a product, a signboard, a plant, a document—and just ask, “What am I looking at?” Grok will talk back instantly. Not with a pop-up with some text, but with a natural-language reply, right out loud.

But it doesn’t stop there. You can have an ongoing conversation while the camera stays on. Ask follow-ups, switch topics, or even change Grok’s personality. There are built-in personas like Translator, Therapist, Storyteller, Conspiracy Theorist, and Motivator. It’s weirdly fun, and surprisingly useful.

And yes, it speaks multiple languages. You can talk to Grok in Hindi, French, Spanish, Japanese, and more. You can switch languages mid-convo, and it handles it smoothly. Also, it has memory, so it can remember things it has seen and heard in that conversation. 

This feels more like having a human companion who sees what you see and responds with context—not just a glorified scanner.

To access it, open the Grok app, tap on voice mode, and then on the camera icon. Now, you can talk to Grok and also let Grok see through either the back or front camera. You can either show your homework and ask it to provide answers or show a broken bike and ask it to explain the process of fixing it.

How it compares to Apple’s Visual Intelligence

Apple’s own Visual Intelligence (coming in iOS 18) works on a limited number of devices like the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 16. It uses image recognition to pull info about pets, objects, or places—but you only get static text responses. No voice. No memory. No personality.

And while Apple relies on integrations like Google Lens or ChatGPT to complete the task, Grok skips the middleman and gives you the answer, directly, with flair.

Grok works on every iPhone, not just Pro models

Unlike Apple’s Visual Intelligence, which is hardware-gated, Grok’s new vision mode works on any iPhone that can run the app. You don’t need an A17 chip or the latest iOS—just install, open, and explore.

Android users currently need the $30/month SuperGrok plan to unlock this feature, but iPhone users get it for free—no subscription required.

Why this matters

Grok is redefining what AI vision on smartphones should feel like: natural, responsive, and inclusive. Instead of limiting powerful features to premium devices, it makes them available to everyone. And while Apple’s version might catch up eventually, Grok is already miles ahead.

Don’t miss these related reads:

  • How to use Live Text on iPhone or iPad
  • Best ChatGPT apps for iPhone and iPad
  • How to create a memory movie with Apple Intelligence on your iPhone

title.rendered: Tired of your Mac’s wallpaper? Here’s how to change it

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Use Apple’s Wallpapers: Easily set a default wallpaper by choosing from Apple’s built-in options in your Mac’s System Settings.
  • Use Your Own Photos: Use your own pictures as wallpaper by adding a photo from your library in the System Settings.
  • The Quick Method: For a quick change, right-click an image in Finder, Photos, or Safari and set as wallpaper.
  • Create a Slideshow: Create an auto-rotating wallpaper slideshow by selecting an album or folder and setting a change interval.
  • For Multiple Displays: For multi-monitor setups, you can assign a unique wallpaper to each display in the System Settings.

Tired of staring at the same Mac wallpaper every day? Whether you’re looking to uplift your mood, personalize your setup, or just switch things up a bit, changing your wallpaper is an easy way to refresh your screen. And the good news? macOS gives you plenty of ways to do it—from built-in options, setting up custom photos, Live Wallpapers to even auto-rotating wallpapers that change automatically throughout the day. Here’s a complete guide to help you out with how to change wallpaper on mac:

Set a default Apple wallpaper on Mac

Follow these steps to pick a wallpaper from macOS’s built-in options:

  1. Click the Apple icon in the top-left corner of the screen and select System Settings. You can also launch System Settings by clicking its icon in the Dock.

  2. Scroll down and select Wallpaper in the sidebar. You will see wallpapers from Apple in various categories like Pictures, Landscape, Cityscape, Underwater, Earth, etc. You can also pick solid colors and dynamic wallpapers from here.
  3. Just click any image to instantly apply it to your desktop.

If you use virtual desktops, enable the toggle beside Show on all Spaces to set the same wallpaper for all virtual desktops. Otherwise, you can choose a different wallpaper for each space.

On macOS Monterey or earlier: Go to System Preferences > Desktop & Screen Saver, then select an Apple option from the sidebar to browse and apply wallpapers provided by Apple.

Change your Mac wallpaper to a custom image

If you want to apply your personal photo or any custom image as your wallpaper on your Mac, you can do so using these steps:

  1. Launch System Settings, scroll down, and click Wallpaper in the sidebar.
  2. Click the Add Photo option at the top and choose:
    • From Photos to browse and find a photo in the Photos app library.
    • Choose to pick an image from Finder.

  3. Beside the picture thumbnail at the top, you will see a bunch of options: Fill Screen, Fit to Screen, Stretch to Fill Screen, and Center. Try these to see how the wallpaper fits the screen.

To remove a custom wallpaper, apply a different wallpaper, hover over the custom one, and click the X (cross button).

Set a wallpaper from Finder, Photos, or Safari

Alternatively, you can also set a custom image as a wallpaper like this:

  • In Finder, find the image you want to set as a wallpaper, right-click it, and select Set Desktop Picture.

  • In the Photos app, select the photo you want to use as a wallpaper, click the Share button, and then select Set Wallpaper.

  • Apple also lets you set an image you find on Safari as your Mac’s wallpaper. In Safari, right-click on the image, and select Use Image as Desktop Wallpaper to set it without downloading it first.

Make your Mac’s wallpaper change automatically

Want your desktop to look different every time you see it? Here’s how to set up auto-rotating wallpapers:

  1. Go to System Settings.
  2. Scroll down and click Wallpaper in the sidebar.
  3. In wallpaper settings, click on Add Folder or Album.
  4. Click Choose Folder.

  5. Select a folder with multiple images. It will be added as a category.

  6. Click on the first image with rotating arrows on it.

  7. Choose how often you want the wallpapers to change with the appropriate option: Every Day, Every Hour, Every 5 Seconds, On Wake, or On Login).

This works great if you have a folder of travel photos, nature shots, or your own curated wallpaper collection. If you have an album in Apple Photos, you can directly select it from the drop-down.

Bonus: Set different wallpapers for different displays

If you’re using more than one display with your Mac, here’s how to set a unique wallpaper for each display:

  1. Go to System Settings > Wallpaper.
  2. Your screens will be listed separately at the top. Select the display you want to customize.
  3. Choose a different wallpaper for each one.

Changing your wallpaper might seem like a trivial thing, but it can make your Mac feel brand new. Whether you stick with Apple’s visuals or bring in your own, customizing your desktop is a great way to make your space your own.

Give your Mac a personal touch

A new wallpaper won’t speed up your Mac or boost its battery, but it will definitely change how it feels to use. It’s a small tweak that adds a personal touch to your daily setup. So go ahead, try out a few, rotate them, or set your own photo. Your desktop deserves a little makeover now and then.

FAQs

Why can’t I change wallpaper on my Mac?

You might be under admin restrictions (like in schools or offices), or the wallpaper might not have downloaded yet. Try waiting or restarting your Mac.

Can I use a video or Live Wallpaper as a wallpaper on my Mac?

macOS only supports animated wallpapers on the Lock Screen. To use videos, try third-party apps like iWallpaper or Paper.

How do I get high-quality wallpapers for my Mac?

Check out Unsplash, Pexels, or Wallhaven for high-quality wallpapers. You can also explore our curated collection of aesthetic Mac wallpapers.

Can I use different wallpapers for Light and Dark modes?

Yes! Apple’s Dynamic Wallpapers adapt based on Light or Dark mode—look for them in the Dynamic section.

What happens if I delete a wallpaper image?

macOS will switch to a default or blank wallpaper. You can always set a new one anytime.

@graph.name: How to Set Default Apple Wallpaper on Mac
@graph.description: Change your Mac desktop background to a default Apple wallpaper through System Settings. Choose from dynamic, still, or solid color options in Apple's wallpaper library.

step.name: Open System Settings
step.text: Click the Apple icon in the top-left corner of your screen and select System Settings. Alternatively, click the System Settings icon in the Dock.

itemListElement.text: Click the Apple icon in the top-left corner.
Select System Settings from the menu.
Alternatively, click the System Settings icon in the Dock.

step.name: Go to Wallpaper settings
step.text: Scroll down the sidebar and click Wallpaper to view available options.

itemListElement.text: Scroll down in the System Settings sidebar.
Click Wallpaper.

step.name: Choose and apply a wallpaper
step.text: Browse Apple’s wallpaper categories like Pictures, Landscape, Cityscape, Underwater, and Earth, or choose solid colors and dynamic wallpapers. Click an image to instantly apply it to your desktop.

itemListElement.text: Browse wallpaper categories.
Click an image to apply it.

@graph.name: How to Change Wallpaper on Mac
@graph.description: Customize your Mac desktop background by selecting images from the Photos app or Finder, and adjust how they fit your screen using System Settings.

step.name: Open Wallpaper settings
step.text: Launch System Settings on your Mac, scroll down the sidebar, and click Wallpaper to access wallpaper options.

itemListElement.text: Open System Settings.
Scroll down and click Wallpaper.

step.name: Add a new wallpaper
step.text: Click the Add Photo option at the top and choose one of the following: From Photos to select from your Photos app library, or Choose to pick an image from Finder.

itemListElement.text: Click Add Photo.
Choose From Photos to select from your Photos library.
Choose an image from Finder.

step.name: Adjust wallpaper fit
step.text: Beside the picture thumbnail at the top, choose from Fill Screen, Fit to Screen, Stretch to Fill Screen, or Center to adjust how your wallpaper is displayed.

itemListElement.text: Select Fill Screen for full coverage.
Choose Fit to Screen to maintain aspect ratio.
Select Stretch to Fill Screen to expand the image.
Choose Center to place the image in the middle.

@graph.name: How to Set Mac Wallpaper From Finder, Photos, or Safari
@graph.description: Quickly set an image as your Mac's wallpaper directly from Finder, the Photos app, or Safari without navigating through System Settings.

step.name: Set wallpaper from Finder
step.text: In Finder, locate the image you want to use, right-click it, and select Set Desktop Picture.

itemListElement.text: Open Finder and locate your chosen image.
Right-click the image.
Select Set Desktop Picture.

step.name: Set wallpaper from Photos app
step.text: In the Photos app, select the photo you want, click the Share button, and choose Set Wallpaper.

itemListElement.text: Open the Photos app and select a photo.
Click the Share button.
Select Set Wallpaper.

step.name: Set wallpaper from Safari
step.text: In Safari, right-click an image and select Use Image as Desktop Wallpaper to set it instantly without downloading.

itemListElement.text: Open Safari and find the image you want.
Right-click the image.
Select Use Image as Desktop Wallpaper.

@graph.name: How to Change Wallpaper on Mac Automatically
@graph.description: Set your Mac to automatically change wallpapers from a selected folder at custom intervals using System Settings.

step.name: Open Wallpaper settings
step.text: Go to System Settings, scroll down, and click Wallpaper in the sidebar to access wallpaper options.

itemListElement.text: Open System Settings.
Scroll down and click Wallpaper.

step.name: Add a folder or album
step.text: In Wallpaper settings, click Add Folder or Album, then click Choose Folder.

itemListElement.text: Click Add Folder or Album.
Click Choose Folder.

step.name: Select a folder of images
step.text: Choose a folder with multiple images from Finder. It will appear as a category in Wallpaper settings.

itemListElement.text: Navigate to the folder with multiple images.
Select the folder.

step.name: Enable automatic change
step.text: Click on the first image in the folder with rotating arrows to activate automatic wallpaper change.

itemListElement.text: Click the image with rotating arrows.

step.name: Set change interval
step.text: Choose how often wallpapers should change: Every Day, Every Hour, Every 5 Seconds, On Wake, or On Login.

itemListElement.text: Select a change interval from the options.

keyPoints.title: Set a Default Apple Wallpaper on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: You can select a wallpaper from macOS’s built-in options through System Settings, choosing from categories like Pictures or Landscape, and apply it instantly.

keyPoints.title: Customize Your Wallpaper with Personal Photos
keyPoints.explanation: To use your personal images as wallpaper, navigate to System Settings, click Add Photo, and select images from Photos or Finder, with options to fit them to your screen.

keyPoints.title: Set a Wallpaper from Finder, Photos, or Safari
keyPoints.explanation: Right-click images in Finder, Photos, or Safari to set them as your desktop wallpaper directly, allowing for quick customization from various sources.

keyPoints.title: Enable Auto-Rotating Wallpapers
keyPoints.explanation: Create a slideshow of images by adding a folder or album in System Settings, and set the interval for automatic changes, perfect for dynamic desktop backgrounds.

keyPoints.title: Assign Different Wallpapers to Multiple Displays
keyPoints.explanation: In System Settings, select Wallpaper, then choose individual displays at the top to assign unique wallpapers to each screen, enhancing multi-monitor setups.

title.rendered: How to Set up and Use Emergency SOS on Apple Watch

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What It Is: The Emergency SOS feature on Apple Watch helps you quickly call for help and share your location.
  • What Happens: Emergency SOS calls local emergency services, then texts your location to your designated emergency contacts.
  • Essential Setup: To prepare, you must add emergency contacts in the Health app and enable fall/crash detection features.
  • How to Activate: Activate SOS manually by holding the side button, or automatically via the watch’s fall and crash detection.
  • After a Call: If you call by accident, inform the dispatcher. You can stop location sharing after the emergency ends.

Apple’s Emergency SOS feature on the Apple Watch ensures that help is just a button press away. Whether you’re caught in an accident, experience a hard fall, or feel unsafe, your watch can alert emergency services and share your location instantly.

In this guide, I’ll walk you through how to set up and use Emergency SOS on Apple Watch, and how to manage its powerful features.

What is Emergency SOS on Apple Watch?

Emergency SOS is a built-in safety feature that lets you quickly contact emergency services and alert your emergency contacts. Depending on your model and region, it can either be activated manually or automatically during critical incidents like hard falls or car crashes.

What happens when Emergency SOS is triggered?

  • The Apple Watch dials local emergency services.
  • Sends your current location to your emergency contacts.
  • Updates them if your location changes.
  • Automatically calls for help if you can’t respond after a detected crash or fall.

How to set up Emergency SOS on your Apple Watch

Before using Emergency SOS, make sure it’s set up correctly on your iPhone and Apple Watch. While the Emergency SOS features are auto-enabled for your Apple Watch, you must manually add an emergency contact. You can add an emergency contact via the Health and Contact app.

Besides, you can head to the Watch app on your iPhone to check whether all Emergency SOS features are ON. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Watch app and ensure you are on the My Watch tab.
  2. Scroll down and tap Emergency SOS.
  3. Ensure that the Hold Side Button to Dial, Fall Detection, and Crash Detection toggles are green.

How to use Emergency SOS on your Apple Watch

Not only does your Apple Watch let you use Emergency SOS anytime you want, but it can also call emergency services automatically if a severe crash or fall is detected.

Manually trigger Emergency SOS:

  • Press and hold the Side button (Action button on Apple Watch Ultra) until the Emergency Call slider appears.
  • Drag the slider to the right to initiate the emergency call immediately.

Alternatively, you can keep holding the Side button until a countdown begins. Once the countdown ends, your Apple Watch will automatically initiate the emergency services.

Use Crash Detection and Fall Detection to call for help automatically:

These features work automatically once enabled:

  • The Crash Detection feature is available on the Apple Watch Series 8 and newer models, and the Fall detection feature is available on the Apple Watch Series 4 or newer models.
  • As the name suggests, the Crash Detection feature is designed to detect severe car crashes. The Fall Detection feature, on the other hand, detects a hard fall. In both cases:
  • Your Apple Watch taps on your wrist, chimes, and displays an alert on the screen.
  • You can use the alert to call emergency services right away or dismiss the alert by pressing the Digital crown.
  • If the Apple Watch finds out you’re unable to move, I will make the call automatically after a 30-second countdown in case a crash is detected and after a minute in case of fall.
  • Your Medical ID and location are shared with responders and emergency contacts.

How to cancel an accidental Emergency SOS call

If you accidentally initiate Emergency SOS:

  • Don’t hang up. Wait for the responder to answer.
  • Tell them the call was accidental.
  • Once the call ends, tap No when asked to send a message to your emergency contacts.

How to stop sharing location after an SOS Call

After an emergency call, your Apple Watch keeps updating your emergency contact with your location every 4 hours.

To stop this: Tap Stop Sharing from the notification that appears.

Signing off…

Emergencies are unpredictable. Thankfully, your Apple Watch makes it easy to call for help—even when your iPhone isn’t nearby. A few minutes of setup can give you peace of mind and might even save your life.

If you’ve got questions or need help setting this up, drop a comment below—we’d love to help!

FAQs

Can you call SOS on Apple Watch without iPhone?

Yes, you can. However, you must have a cellular Apple Watch with an active cellular plan, or your non-cellular Apple Watch must be connected to a Wi-Fi network, and Wi-Fi Calling is enabled with your carrier.

Can all Apple Watches detect falls?

Fall Detection is available on Apple Watch Series 4 and later. You must enable the feature manually in settings.

@graph.name: How to Set Up Emergency SOS on Apple Watch
@graph.description: Enable and configure Emergency SOS, Fall Detection, and Crash Detection on your Apple Watch using the Watch app on your iPhone.

step.name: Open the Watch app
step.text: On your iPhone, open the Watch app and ensure you are in the My Watch tab.

itemListElement.text: Open the Watch app on your iPhone.
Tap the My Watch tab if not already selected.

step.name: Access Emergency SOS settings
step.text: Scroll down and tap Emergency SOS to view safety features.

itemListElement.text: Scroll down in the My Watch tab.
Tap Emergency SOS.

step.name: Enable safety features
step.text: Ensure the toggles for Hold Side Button to Dial, Fall Detection, and Crash Detection are turned on (green).

itemListElement.text: Toggle on Hold Side Button to Dial.
Toggle on Fall Detection.
Toggle on Crash Detection.

@graph.name: How to Manually Trigger Emergency SOS on Apple Watch
@graph.description: Quickly initiate an emergency call from your Apple Watch by using the Side button or Action button to access the Emergency Call slider.

step.name: Press and hold the Side button
step.text: On regular Apple Watch models, press and hold the Side button. On Apple Watch Ultra, press and hold the Action button until the Emergency Call slider appears.

itemListElement.text: Press and hold the Side button.
For Apple Watch Ultra, press and hold the Action button.

step.name: Drag the Emergency Call slider
step.text: When the Emergency Call slider appears, drag it to the right to place the emergency call immediately.

itemListElement.text: Drag the Emergency Call slider to the right.

@graph.name: How to Cancel Accidental Emergency SOS Call on Apple Watch
@graph.description: If you accidentally trigger an Emergency SOS call on your Apple Watch, follow these steps to inform responders and prevent unnecessary alerts to your emergency contacts.

step.name: Wait for the responder to answer
step.text: Do not hang up. Allow the emergency responder to answer your call so you can explain the situation.

itemListElement.text: Keep the call connected until the responder answers.

step.name: Explain the accidental call
step.text: Tell the responder that the Emergency SOS call was triggered by mistake.

itemListElement.text: Inform the responder it was an accidental call.

step.name: Cancel sending alerts to emergency contacts
step.text: When the call ends, your Apple Watch may prompt you to send a message to your emergency contacts. Tap No to prevent sending alerts.

itemListElement.text: Tap No when asked to notify your emergency contacts.

keyPoints.title: Apple Watch Emergency SOS Functionality
keyPoints.explanation: The Emergency SOS feature on Apple Watch allows users to quickly contact emergency services and share their location in critical situations, enhancing personal safety.

keyPoints.title: Triggering and What Happens During Emergency SOS
keyPoints.explanation: When activated, Emergency SOS dials local emergency services, shares your location with contacts, updates them if your location changes, and can automatically call help if a crash or fall is detected.

keyPoints.title: Setting Up Emergency SOS on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: Users must manually add emergency contacts through the Health and Contact app, and verify that all Emergency SOS features—like fall detection and crash detection—are enabled in the Watch app.

keyPoints.title: Using Emergency SOS in Urgent Situations
keyPoints.explanation: Emergency SOS can be triggered manually by holding the side button or automatically through crash and fall detection, which alert emergency contacts and share your medical ID and location.

keyPoints.title: Cancelling and Managing Emergency SOS Calls
keyPoints.explanation: If an accidental call occurs, you should inform the responder, and after the emergency, you can stop sharing your location by tapping 'Stop Sharing' from the notification.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
"The founder of iGeeksBlog, Dhvanesh, is an Apple aficionado, who cannot stand even a slight innuendo about Apple products. He dons the cap of editor-in-chief to make sure that articles match the quality standard before they are published."

About Dhvanesh

Ever since teenage years, gadgets and technology have held a special place in Dhvanesh's heart. This fascination with gadgets and their inner workings fueled a lifelong passion for exploration and troubleshooting. Disassembled electronic items scattered around the house became a familiar sight during his younger years, a testament to this insatiable curiosity.

From SEO Expert to Apple Evangelist

After completing his IT engineering diploma, Dhvanesh's professional journey began with a 4.5-year stint as an SEO executive, honing valuable digital marketing skills. However, the desire to share tech knowledge and connect with a like-minded community proved stronger. In 2012, Dhvanesh embarked on a new adventure, founding iGeeksBlog. This blog became a haven for Apple enthusiasts and tech aficionados seeking insightful and in-depth information about everything Apple.

A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge

In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. As the founder, he has steered the blog’s vision, ensuring it remains a trusted resource for Apple users worldwide. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development.

Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach

Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience.

Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem

Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. Currently, he also manages the iGeeksBlog+ weekly newsletter, delivering curated Apple news, gadgets, apps, tips and tricks straight to subscribers' inboxes. This unwavering commitment to Apple technology and a genuine desire to empower fellow users make him a valuable asset to the iGeeksBlog team.

title.rendered: How to Take Macro Photos and Videos on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What is Macro Mode?: Macro mode uses the Ultra Wide lens to capture sharp, detailed close-up photos from as close as 2cm.
  • Device Compatibility: This feature is available on the iPhone 13 Pro and newer Pro models, and all iPhone 16 models.
  • Taking Macro Photos: To take a macro photo, simply move your iPhone close to a subject to trigger the mode automatically.
  • Recording Macro Videos: This automatic macro switching also works when recording videos, including in Slo-Mo and Time-Lapse modes.
  • For Older iPhones: For older iPhones without macro mode, use a third-party clip-on lens to achieve similar close-up results.

Ever spotted a tiny insect, water droplet, or texture and thought, “I wish I could capture that up close”? Well, good news—you don’t need a DSLR with a giant lens. Your iPhone already packs a powerful macro mode that lets you zoom in and shoot stunning close-up photos and videos. Whether you’re capturing nature, products, or textures, this guide will walk you through everything you need to know about using the macro mode on an iPhone.

What is the macro mode on iPhones?

The macro mode lets you shoot subjects up close using your iPhone without needing an external lens. It uses the Ultra Wide lens to capture sharp and detailed photos and videos of subjects as close as 2 centimeters from the lens.

This feature is great for shooting textures on leaves, insects, jewelry, food, or any tiny details you want to highlight. The Camera app automatically switches to macro mode when it detects you are close to a subject, but you can also control it manually if your iPhone has the option.

Which iPhones support macro mode?

Macro mode isn’t available on all iPhone models; only iPhones with an Ultra Wide camera can shoot in macro.

Back when it was introduced with the iPhone 13 Pro series, the macro mode was limited to the Pro models. However, starting with the iPhone 16 series, it’s available even on the standard models since they pack an Ultra Wide lens.

Here’s a full list of iPhone models that support macro photography:

  • iPhone 13 Pro
  • iPhone 13 Pro Max
  • iPhone 14 Pro
  • iPhone 14 Pro Max
  • iPhone 15 Pro
  • iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16
  • iPhone 16 Plus
  • iPhone 16 Pro
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max

Older iPhone models don’t support macro photography natively. However, there are workarounds—covered below—that you can use.

How to take macro photos on your iPhone

Taking a macro photo with your iPhone is easy:

  1. Open the Camera app.
  2. Set the mode to Photo.
  3. Move your iPhone close to the subject (within 2 cm), and the camera will automatically switch to the Ultra Wide lens and focus on the subject.
  4. Tap the Shutter button to take a photo.

Tip: If you see the Auto Macro button (flower icon), you can tap it to turn it off and use manual control instead.

How to record macro videos on your iPhone

For times when you need to capture a tiny subject in motion, you can record a macro video with your iPhone like this:

  1. Open the Camera app.
  2. Choose Video, Slo-Mo, or Time-Lapse based on your requirements.
  3. Tap .5x to switch to the Ultra Wide camera.
  4. Move close to the subject (within 2 cm).
  5. Tap the Record button to start recording. Hit it again to stop and save the recording.

Tip: If the video looks blurry, slightly back up or re-tap .5x to reset the focus.

Tips to capture better macro shots with your iPhone

While capturing macro shots is easy, here are a few things you can do to get the best results:

  • Use natural light or a ring light to brighten your subject.
  • Shoot in Apple ProRAW (if supported) for better editing control.
  • Hold your phone steady or use a tripod for sharper results.
  • Tap to focus if your subject is’t sharp.
  • Try different angles to avoid casting shadows from your iPhone.
  • Adjust the exposure by tapping and sliding up/down.
  • Edit later using apps like Snapseed or Lightroom to enhance the subject.

Can you take macro shots on unsupported iPhones?

Yes, you can take macro shots on any iPhone, even unsupported ones, with some help. Here are your options:

  • Clip-on macro lenses: Buy third-party lenses from brands like Moment or Apexel. These attach to your iPhone and mimic macro capability. This is the best option for high-quality macro photos and videos.
  • Third-party camera apps: Apps like Halide or Camera+ simulate macro mode using zoom techniques and AI. Mind you, most third-party camera apps that provide clean results are either paid or require a subscription.

You won’t get the same native quality, but it’s still a fun way to explore macro photography.

Bring the smallest details into focus

The macro mode lets you get closer to the smaller things around you—insects, textures, food, or anything with fine details. You don’t need a fancy setup; just your iPhone is enough to start exploring. And if your iPhone doesn’t support macro mode natively, there are still workarounds worth trying. Either way, it’s a fun way to experiment with close-up photography using whatever you already have.

  • How to use Photographic Styles on iPhone 16 series
  • Best iPhone camera settings for stunning photos
  • How to set timer on iPhone camera to take hands-free photos

keyPoints.title: What is the macro mode on iPhones?
keyPoints.explanation: Macro mode allows users to capture sharp, detailed close-up photos and videos using the Ultra Wide lens, focusing on subjects within 2 centimeters without external lenses.

keyPoints.title: Supported iPhone models for macro photography
keyPoints.explanation: Macro mode is available on iPhones with an Ultra Wide lens, starting from the iPhone 13 Pro series and included in all models from iPhone 16 onwards, with older models requiring workarounds.

keyPoints.title: How to take macro photos on an iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Activate macro mode by moving your iPhone close to the subject within 2 cm; the camera automatically switches to the Ultra Wide lens, and you can then tap the Shutter button to capture.

keyPoints.title: Recording macro videos on an iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Switch to Video, Slo-Mo, or Time-Lapse, then move within 2 cm of the subject, and start recording by tapping the record button, ensuring focus is sharp for a clear macro video.

keyPoints.title: Tips for better macro shots and workarounds for unsupported iPhones
keyPoints.explanation: Improve macro photos with natural light, steady holding or tripod use, and manual focus; for unsupported models, attach clip-on macro lenses or use third-party apps to simulate macro capabilities.

title.rendered: How to change the date and time on iPhone photos and videos

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iPhone photo metadata includes time, location, and camera info, which helps with sorting but can expose private details if shared.
  • You can manually change the date and time of any photo or video using the iPhone Photos app by tapping the info icon and selecting Adjust.
  • Batch edit timestamps for multiple files by selecting them, tapping the three-dot menu, and choosing ‘Adjust Date & Time’ to sync or shift metadata.
  • Third-party apps like Metapho offer deeper metadata editing, including the ability to strip, modify, or view EXIF data not editable in the Photos app.
  • Changing the timestamp won’t affect location data, but you can manually remove or edit location info from the same info screen for added privacy.

Recently, I was going through my photo library and realized all my vacation photos were saved with the wrong dates. If you’ve ever faced the same thing, don’t worry! Whether your iPhone’s clock was off or you crossed time zones without updating settings, you can easily change the date and time on iPhone photos and videos right from the Photos app. In this guide, I’ll walk you through it step by step.

What is Metadata on iPhone photos and videos?

When you take a photo or video on your iPhone, it saves more than just the image. It tags the file with additional data called EXIF metadata (Exchangeable Image File Format). This includes:

  • Date and time the photo or video was taken
  • Location data (if Location Services are enabled)
  • Camera settings – like aperture, ISO, shutter speed
  • File format and size
  • iPhone model and lens info

The Photos app uses this metadata to sort images by date, create Memories, and organize them into albums. It’s also helpful when you want to search iPhone photos by date or location. When you share a photo, the recipient may also see the timestamp and location unless you remove that data.

Sometimes, though, you might need to change or remove this metadata—especially if the timestamp is inaccurate or you want to maintain your privacy. Here’s how to fix it.

How to change the timestamp of a photo or video on your iPhone

Apple’s built-in Photos app makes it super easy to change the date and time metadata on iPhone photos and videos. Whether it’s a single image or an entire batch, here’s how you can do it.

Change the date and time of a single photo or video

  1. Open the Photos app on your iPhone.
  2. Find the photo or video you want to change and tap to open it.
  3. Tap the info (i) button below the image, or swipe up to view metadata.
  4. Tap Adjust next to the current date and time.
  5. Use the calendar and clock to set the correct timestamp.
  6. You can also adjust the Time Zone, if needed.
  7. Tap Adjust in the top-right corner to save.

After editing, the photo/video will move to its new spot in your photo library based on the updated date. So if you set an older date, it’ll appear earlier in your gallery.

Change the date and time of multiple photos/videos at once

If a bunch of your photos are off by the same date or time, you can edit them all together.

  1. Open the Photos app and go to your Library or an album.
  2. Tap Select in the top-right and choose multiple photos/videos.
  3. Tap the three-dot menu (•••) in the bottom-right corner.
  4. Choose Adjust Date & Time.
  5. Set the correct timestamp for all selected files.
  6. Tap Adjust to apply the change.

The time adjustment will apply relative to each photo’s original timestamp.

Bonus tip Sometimes, the location where a photo was taken is wrong—or maybe you just don’t want it there at all. You can adjust the location too.

Wrapping up

That’s it! Now you know how to edit date and time of iPhone photos and videos using the Photos app. Whether you’re fixing one file or organizing a whole album, it’s a great way to keep your media library neat and accurate. Give it a try—and if you run into any issues, feel free to drop a comment below!

FAQs

Are there apps that offer more control over iPhone photo metadata?

Yes, definitely! The iPhone’s native Photos app is handy for basic metadata edits like date, time or location, but there are third-party apps offering more control. Apps like Metapho, Exif Metadata, etc. let you view, edit, and even remove all kinds of photo metadata—like camera settings, file info, and more. These are especially helpful if you want to manage privacy or get super detailed with your photos.

Will changing the date and time affect location data?

Nope, changing the date and time of a photo or video won’t affect the location info. They’re stored separately, so updating one won’t change the other. If you want to change or remove the location too, you’ll have to do that separately—but it’s easy to do right from the same info screen on the Photos app. Go through our detailed guide on how to turn off geotagging for photos and videos on iPhone.

  • Best iPhone camera settings for stunning photos
  • How to recover deleted photos from iPhone or iPad
  • How to convert HEIC to JPG on iPhone, Mac, and PC

step.name: Access the Info panel
step.text: Tap the info button or swipe up to view metadata.

itemListElement.text: Tap the (i) icon below the image or swipe up on the screen.

step.name: Tap Adjust next to the timestamp
step.text: Find the date and time section and tap Adjust to begin editing.

itemListElement.text: Look for the current date and time field and tap Adjust beside it.

step.name: Set new date and time
step.text: Use the calendar and clock to enter the correct date and time.

itemListElement.text: Tap the calendar to pick a date and the clock icon to select a time.

step.name: Adjust time zone if needed
step.text: You can also change the time zone to match the location of the photo or video.

itemListElement.text: Tap Time Zone and enter the correct location if it’s different.

step.name: Save your changes
step.text: Tap Adjust in the top-right corner to confirm and save your edits.

itemListElement.text: Tap Adjust to save your updated timestamp and close the panel.

blockGraphs.question: Are there apps that offer more control over iPhone photo metadata?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes, definitely! The iPhone’s native Photos app is handy for basic metadata edits like date, time or location, but there are third-party apps offering more control. Apps like Metapho, Exif Metadata, etc. let you view, edit, and even remove all kinds of photo metadata—like camera settings, file info, and more. These are especially helpful if you want to manage privacy or get super detailed with your photos.
blockGraphs.label: FAQ (Block)

blockGraphs.question: Will changing the date and time affect location data?
blockGraphs.answer: Nope, changing the date and time of a photo or video won’t affect the location info. They’re stored separately, so updating one won't change the other. If you want to change or remove the location too, you’ll have to do that separately—but it’s easy to do right from the same info screen on the Photos app. Go through our detailed guide on how to turn off geotagging for photos and videos on iPhone.
blockGraphs.label: FAQ (Block)

keyPoints.title: Understanding Metadata in iPhone Photos and Videos
keyPoints.explanation: Metadata, or EXIF data, includes information like date, time, location, camera settings, and device details, which helps organize and sort your photos but can also raise privacy concerns.

keyPoints.title: How to Change the Date and Time of a Single Photo or Video
keyPoints.explanation: Use the Photos app to open the media file, tap info, select 'Adjust', and set the correct date, time, and time zone to update its metadata.

keyPoints.title: Batch Editing Date and Time for Multiple Files
keyPoints.explanation: Select multiple photos or videos, tap the three-dot menu, choose 'Adjust Date & Time', and set the desired timestamp to update all selected files simultaneously.

keyPoints.title: Additional Metadata Control with Third-Party Apps
keyPoints.explanation: For more advanced control over photo metadata, apps like Metapho and Exif Metadata allow viewing, editing, and removing detailed information beyond what the Photos app offers.

keyPoints.title: Effect of Changing Date/Time on Location Data
keyPoints.explanation: Adjusting the date and time does not impact location data, but you can separately modify or remove location info from the same info screen to enhance privacy.

title.rendered: Apple Builds AI Team to Reinvent Search Across Siri, Safari, and Spotlight

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple forms new AI group to revamp search tools including Siri, Spotlight, and Safari with smarter, privacy-focused tech led by the “Answer, Knowledge, and Information” team.
  • Focus is on on-device intelligence and privacy as Apple develops its own foundational AI to answer personalized queries using user documents and offline data.
  • AI reboot led by Robby Walker marks strategic reset after years of underwhelming Siri performance and search delays, with a new “Answer Engine” and standalone app in the works.
  • Still early in development with years to go as Apple is actively hiring for critical roles, though it’s already holding talks with several AI startups.
  • Competing against OpenAI and Google’s rapid gains means Apple’s new AI search will need to impress, but right now it’s a long-term play with cautious optimism.

Apple is staffing up for a major AI expansion, forming a new internal group focused on creating a smarter, privacy-minded search experience across its platforms. Dubbed the “Answer, Knowledge, and Information” team, the initiative is reportedly aimed at overhauling services like Siri, Spotlight, and Safari, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.

The company currently lists over a dozen open roles for this team across the U.S. and China, including a Staff Machine Learning Engineer tasked with advancing “Siri’s ability to answer personal questions” using documents stored on the device. The role description references large language models and a privacy-first approach, signaling that Apple may be building its own foundational AI system, rather than leaning entirely on partners.

After years of avoiding chatbot-style AI, Apple now seems to be shifting strategy.

What’s Driving Apple’s AI Reset

At WWDC 2024, Apple announced its new Apple Intelligence framework, complete with tools like Genmoji, Writing Tools, and Image Playground. Despite the rollout, few of these features have resonated widely. A major Siri upgrade, hyped internally and externally, was recently delayed by over a year, adding to frustration among employees and longtime users.

The new “Answers, Knowledge, and Information” unit appears to be Apple’s internal response to those stumbles.

A Team Built to Rebuild Search

Leading the new group is Robby Walker, a longtime Siri executive known for his blunt assessment of the team’s delays. According to internal reports, Walker described Siri’s repeated timeline slippages as “ugly and embarrassing” during a meeting earlier this year, a sentiment that may have earned him a mandate to rethink Apple’s AI services from the ground up.

Sources say the team’s early goals include:

  • A new “Answer Engine” capable of crawling the web and delivering general knowledge responses.
  • A standalone app distinct from Siri, Safari, or Spotlight.
  • Back-end systems built to support more advanced, context-aware search functions across Apple platforms.

How Soon Could It Launch?

With key roles still unfilled, the project remains in early development. A public rollout likely remains years away.

That said, Apple has been in quiet talks with AI startups focused on conversational search, hinting at a potential parallel track. While it’s unclear if any of those deals advanced, the discussions point to growing urgency inside Apple to close the AI gap with rivals.

Editorial Take: Apple Playing Catch-Up on Search

Apple Intelligence hasn’t yet delivered a breakthrough moment. If this new AI-powered search engine pans out, it could finally push Siri, Safari, and Spotlight beyond their current limitations and into the generative AI era.

But that’s assuming Apple ships it in time and with enough capability to compete with OpenAI and Google’s fast-moving tools. For now, it’s another early signal in Apple’s AI pivot, not a finished product.

Would a smarter Apple search engine actually replace your use of ChatGPT or Google? Sound off in the comments.

Apps like Metapho, Exif Metadata, etc. let you view, edit, and even remove all kinds of photo metadata—like camera settings, file info, and more. These are especially helpful if you want to manage privacy or get super detailed with your photos.

mainEntity.name: Will changing the date and time affect location data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, changing the date and time of a photo or video won’t affect the location info. They’re stored separately, so updating one won't change the other. If you want to change or remove the location too, you’ll have to do that separately—but it’s easy to do right from the same info screen on the Photos app. Go through our detailed guide on how to turn off geotagging for photos and videos on iPhone.

keyPoints.title: Apple's New AI Team and Goals
keyPoints.explanation: Apple has formed the 'Answer, Knowledge, and Information' team to develop smarter, privacy-focused search and AI features, including overhauling Siri, Spotlight, and Safari.

keyPoints.title: Focus on Privacy and Internal AI Development
keyPoints.explanation: Apple is building its own foundational AI system that emphasizes privacy, with roles aimed at enhancing Siri's ability to answer personal questions using on-device documents.

keyPoints.title: Strategic Shift Toward AI and Search Enhancement
keyPoints.explanation: In response to past delays and underwhelming AI features, Apple is internally rebooting its search and AI capabilities, led by Robby Walker, aiming to create a new Answer Engine and dedicated app.

keyPoints.title: Early Stage Development and Future Launch Timeline
keyPoints.explanation: With key roles still unfilled, the project is in the early stages, and a public launch is likely years away, although internal discussions with AI startups suggest growing urgency.

keyPoints.title: Potential Impact and Industry Positioning of Apple's AI Efforts
keyPoints.explanation: If successful, Apple’s new AI-powered search engine could surpass current limitations, but it faces competition from rapid advancements by OpenAI and Google, making Apple’s AI pivot a wait-and-see effort.

title.rendered: How to install Git on your Mac: Simple step-by-step guide

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What is Git?: Git is a free version control system that tracks file changes and helps teams collaborate on projects.
  • Check for Git: In the Terminal, run the command `git –version` to check if Git is already installed on your Mac.
  • Easiest Install Method: Run `git` in Terminal and accept the prompt to install Xcode Command Line Tools, which includes Git.
  • Homebrew Method: For more control, first install Homebrew, then run the `brew install git` command in your Terminal.
  • Essential Configuration: After installation, you must configure your user name and email using `git config` commands in Terminal.

If you are new to writing code or planning to collaborate on projects with other people, Git is an essential tool. It helps you organize your coding projects and reduces collaboration overhead to a great extent. Follow along, and I will show you how to download and install Git on your Mac.

What is Git?

Git is a free and open-source version control software that allows you to track changes in your source code. While primarily used by developers, you can use Git on macOS even for any project where managing versions would be useful—be it documents, design files, or personal notes.

Here’s how Git can prove helpful:

  • Saves snapshots (called commits) of your work over time
  • Records who did what and when in the project
  • Enables you to revert back to any past version of your project
  • Assists you develop new features or fixes in different branches and later merge with the main project
  • Enables multiple people to work in the same project without getting in each other’s way
  • Provides collaborators a full local copy of the project history, allowing work offline and better cooperation

Git is easy to download on a Mac and works really well with the Terminal, making it an amazing tool for managing your projects.

How to check if Git is already installed on your Mac

Before we get into installation, let’s check if Git is already present on your Mac. Some versions of macOS have Git installed, if you have used tools like Xcode. You can check if yours has it using these steps:

  1. Open the Terminal app. You can find it by searching Terminal in Spotlight or Launchpad.
  2. Type git --version and press Return.
  3. If Git is installed, you’ll see something similar to git version 2.49.0 on your screen. Make a note of the version number—it’s useful to know if it’s old.

  4. If you get an error like “No Developer Tools Were Found, Requesting Install,” it means Git isn’t installed on your Mac. You can proceed with installation as shown below.

You should always check the version first because it saves time and avoids unnecessary installations. If you have an older version, you might want to update it (we’ll cover that too later in the guide).

How to install Git on a Mac

There are two main ways to install Git on your Mac, and I’ll break each one down so you can choose what works best for you.

Method 1: Install Git using Xcode Command Line Tools

This is the easiest method if you don’t mind installing a small set of developer tools alongside Git. Xcode Command Line Tools include Git and are maintained by Apple, so you’ll get automatic updates through macOS.

  1. Open Terminal.
  2. Type git and press Return. Since Git isn’t installed, macOS will ask you to install the Xcode Command Line Tools.

  3. Click Install in the pop-up window.

  4. Now, select Agree on the License Agreement prompt window.

  5. If you’re not connected to power, click Continue on Battery Power. This starts downloading the tools, including Git. It may take a few minutes, depending on your internet connection.

  6. After installation, click Done on the dialogue box.

  7. Confirm it by typing git --version in Terminal. You should be able to see the installed version.

I love this method because there’s no extra hassle. Plus, if you’re planning to do any development on your Mac, these tools are super useful for other tasks.

Method 2: Install Git via Homebrew

Homebrew is a package manager for macOS that allows you to install tools such as Git via command line. So, first install Homebrew on your Mac if you don’t have it. Once Homebrew is installed, proceed with the instructions below:

  1. In the terminal, type brew install git
  2. Press Return and wait for the installation to complete. Homebrew will download and set up the latest version of Git on your Mac.
  3. Verify the installation by typing git --version. You should see the version number, like git version 2.48.2.

Homebrew is awesome because it keeps everything organized and makes updating Git a breeze (more on that later). If you use command-line tools, this method feels like a natural fit.

Note Previously, you could also download Git binary installer from the official website. However, as of writing, the installer has the older 2.33.0 version and is abandoned. So, you should go with any of the above methods.

How to configure Git on a Mac

Now that Git is installed, let’s configure it so it knows who you are. This is necessary because Git stamps your commits with your name and email, so it’s easy to see who changed what in a project. Open the Terminal app and run the following commands one by one:

  • To set your username, enter git config --global user.name "Your Name" Replace “Your Name” with your real name (e.g., git config –global user.name “Ava”).

  • Set your email address with the command git config --global user.email "you@example.com" Use the email you intend to use with your Git commits (e.g., git config –global user.email “ava.igeeks@example.com”).
  • You can also set your preferred text editor for Git. For instance, to use Visual Studio Code, use the command git config --global core.editor "code --wait" Or, to use nano (a simple Terminal editor), use the command git config --global core.editor "nano" Write any of your desired editor command instead of “code –wait”.
  • Verify your configuration by running git config --list This displays all your configurations, like your name, email, and editor.

That’s all! You must double-check your config to ensure that everything’s good. It’s a trivial step, but it prevents headaches down the line when you’re working on projects with people.

How to update Git on a Mac

It is important to keep Git up-to-date. New releases patch bugs, enhance performance, and introduce features that simplify your workflow. So, you should check the latest version on the official Git website at git-scm.com occasionally.

Once an update is available, follow the steps below depending on how you’ve installed Git.

If you used Homebrew:

  1. Launch Terminal.
  2. Type brew upgrade git and press Return. Homebrew will download and install the latest version of Git.
  3. Verify the update with git --version.

If you installed Git via Xcode Command Line Tools, updating macOS will also update these tools.

Signing off

Installing Git on your Mac is a great first step toward learning version control and working more efficiently on your projects. Each method I’ve described here is beginner-friendly and gets the job done. Now that Git is ready to go, you’re all set to harbor your skills. Happy coding!

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, definitely! The iPhone’s native Photos app is handy for basic metadata edits like date, time or location, but there are third-party apps offering more control. Apps like Metapho, Exif Metadata, etc. let you view, edit, and even remove all kinds of photo metadata—like camera settings, file info, and more. These are especially helpful if you want to manage privacy or get super detailed with your photos.

mainEntity.name: Will changing the date and time affect location data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, changing the date and time of a photo or video won’t affect the location info. They’re stored separately, so updating one won't change the other. If you want to change or remove the location too, you’ll have to do that separately—but it’s easy to do right from the same info screen on the Photos app. Go through our detailed guide on how to turn off geotagging for photos and videos on iPhone.

@graph.name: How to Check if Git is Already Installed on Your Mac
@graph.description: Quickly check if Git is installed on your Mac using Terminal. This guide shows how to verify the version or confirm if Git needs to be installed.

step.name: Open Terminal
step.text: Open the Terminal app on your Mac. You can find it by searching for Terminal in Spotlight or Launchpad.

itemListElement.text: Search for Terminal in Spotlight or Launchpad.
Open the Terminal app.

step.name: Check Git version
step.text: Type git --version and press Return.

itemListElement.text: Type git --version in Terminal.
Press Return.

step.name: Interpret the output
step.text: If Git is installed, you’ll see a message like git version 2.49.0. If you get an error such as 'No Developer Tools Were Found, Requesting Install,' it means Git is not installed.

itemListElement.text: If a version number appears, Git is installed.
If an installation prompt appears, Git is not installed.

@graph.name: How to Install Git on a Mac using Xcode Command Line Tools
@graph.description: Install Git on your Mac by using Xcode Command Line Tools. This guide walks you through the installation process using Terminal and Apple's built-in developer tools.

step.name: Open Terminal
step.text: Open the Terminal app on your Mac to start the installation process.

itemListElement.text: Search for and open the Terminal app.

step.name: Run the Git command
step.text: Type git and press Return. Since Git isn’t installed, macOS will prompt you to install Xcode Command Line Tools.

itemListElement.text: Type git in Terminal.
Press Return.

step.name: Start installation
step.text: Click Install in the pop-up window to begin downloading Xcode Command Line Tools.

itemListElement.text: Click Install when prompted.

step.name: Agree to the license
step.text: Select Agree on the License Agreement prompt window to continue.

itemListElement.text: Click Agree on the license prompt.

step.name: Continue on battery power if needed
step.text: If you’re not connected to power, click Continue on Battery Power to start downloading the tools, including Git. This may take a few minutes depending on your internet connection.

itemListElement.text: Click Continue on Battery Power.

step.name: Finish installation
step.text: Once the installation completes, click Done in the dialogue box.

itemListElement.text: Click Done when installation finishes.

step.name: Verify installation
step.text: Type git --version in Terminal to confirm Git is installed. You should see the installed version number.

itemListElement.text: Type git --version in Terminal.
Check the output for the version number.

@graph.name: How to Install Git on a Mac using Homebrew
@graph.description: Install Git on your Mac using Homebrew for the latest version. This quick guide covers the installation command, waiting for setup, and verifying the version.

step.name: Run Homebrew install command
step.text: In the Terminal app, type brew install git and press Return to start installing Git using Homebrew.

itemListElement.text: Type brew install git.
Press Return.

step.name: Wait for installation to complete
step.text: Homebrew will download and set up the latest version of Git. This may take a couple of minutes depending on your internet speed.

itemListElement.text: Allow Homebrew to finish downloading and installing Git.

step.name: Verify installation
step.text: Once done, type git --version in Terminal. You should see the installed version, for example git version 2.48.2.

itemListElement.text: Type git --version.
Check the output for the version number.

@graph.name: How to Configure Git on a Mac
@graph.description: Set up your Git username, email, and preferred text editor on a Mac. This guide also shows how to verify your configuration settings.

step.name: Set your Git username
step.text: In Terminal, type git config --global user.name "Your Name" replacing 'Your Name' with your actual name. For example: git config --global user.name "Ava".

itemListElement.text: Run git config --global user.name "Your Name".

step.name: Set your Git email
step.text: Run git config --global user.email "you@example.com" replacing the email with the one you’ll use for Git commits. For example: git config --global user.email "ava.igeeks@example.com".

itemListElement.text: Run git config --global user.email "you@example.com".

step.name: Set your preferred text editor
step.text: To set Visual Studio Code as your Git editor, run git config --global core.editor "code --wait". To use nano, run git config --global core.editor "nano". Replace with your preferred editor command.

itemListElement.text: Run git config --global core.editor "code --wait" to set VS Code.
Or run git config --global core.editor "nano" to set nano.

step.name: Verify your Git configuration
step.text: Run git config --list in Terminal to see all your current Git settings, including name, email, and editor.

itemListElement.text: Run git config --list.
Check name, email, and editor in the output.

@graph.name: How to Update Git on a Mac
@graph.description: Update Git on your Mac using Homebrew to get the latest version. This guide shows how to run the update command and verify the installed version.

step.name: Open Terminal
step.text: Launch the Terminal app on your Mac to run the update command.

itemListElement.text: Search for and open Terminal.

step.name: Run the Git upgrade command
step.text: Type brew upgrade git and press Return. Homebrew will download and install the latest version of Git.

itemListElement.text: Type brew upgrade git.
Press Return.

step.name: Verify the Git version
step.text: After the update completes, type git --version to confirm the latest version is installed.

itemListElement.text: Type git --version.
Check that the output shows the updated version.

keyPoints.title: What is Git?
keyPoints.explanation: Git is a free, open-source version control software that helps track changes, manage versions, and collaborate efficiently in various projects, including code, documents, and design files.

keyPoints.title: Checking if Git is already installed
keyPoints.explanation: Use the Terminal command 'git --version' to quickly verify if Git is installed on your Mac and to check its version, which can help determine if an update is needed.

keyPoints.title: Installing Git via Xcode Command Line Tools
keyPoints.explanation: This simple method involves opening Terminal, running the 'git' command, and accepting the prompt to install Xcode Command Line Tools, which includes Git and updates automatically with macOS.

keyPoints.title: Installing Git with Homebrew
keyPoints.explanation: First, install Homebrew, then run 'brew install git' in Terminal to install the latest Git version. This method makes updates easy and keeps your tools organized.

keyPoints.title: Configuring Git on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: Set your user name and email with 'git config' commands to identify your contributions accurately. Also, choose a default text editor for Git commands and verify settings with 'git config --list'.
